# Fulfillment — CI Java-21 mismatch + workflow_dispatch

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4).

## What was found

Two of the three acceptance criteria were **already true before this demand was
raised** (2026-07-11): commit `59d0362` (2026-07-07, "ci: build in temurin-21
sibling container; add workflow_dispatch") had already switched the sibling
build container from `maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17` to
`maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21` and added the `workflow_dispatch:` trigger. The
demand's own commit message even cites the failing run this fixed (`28787591773`,
"invalid target release: 21"). So by the time this session picked the demand up,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` already matched both criteria 1 and 2.

## What was actually broken and fixed here

While verifying criterion 1, I found a live, related defect the demand didn't
name: the workflow's "Checkout contracts at pinned tag" step still pinned
`ref: v0.3.0`, but this repo's own contracts pin was moved to `v0.11.0` in the
2026-07-13 hygiene/re-pin session (`validator/pom.xml`, `HEXAGON.md`). A CI run
would have checked out contracts `v0.3.0`, installed artifact
`io.platform:contracts:0.3.0` into the local `.m2`, and then failed resolving
`validator/pom.xml`'s dependency on `io.platform:contracts:0.11.0` — a fresh
blocker to the same "first green CI run" this demand exists to unblock. Fixed:
`ref: v0.3.0` → `ref: v0.11.0` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Acceptance criteria — how each was met

1. **temurin-21 image** — already true (commit `59d0362`, 2026-07-07), reconfirmed
   at HEAD.
2. **`workflow_dispatch` trigger** — already true (same commit), reconfirmed at
   HEAD.
3. **Green run verified next time the runner is online** — not verified live this
   session (no live self-hosted runner reachable from here); config-level
   verification only, per the demand's own fallback clause. The stale contracts
   pin fixed above was a config-level defect that would have blocked exactly this
   verification, so fixing it was necessary to make a future green run possible
   at all — flagging as the load-bearing change for whoever next has runner
   access.

## For the origin's loop-close

No further conventions-side work implied. If a self-hosted-runner CI run is
attempted next and fails on anything other than the two issues above (already-
fixed Java mismatch, now-fixed contracts pin), that's a new defect, not this one.

# Fulfillment — conventions' half: `vault-sync-handoff` + `brain-projection-equality` retirement-awareness (D075)

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4) — the coordinator
validates and delivers the summary; this report is the only output, nothing was
self-approved or notified directly to `platform-vault`.

**This report covers `conventions`' half of the demand ONLY.** The demand's `to:`
targets both `conventions` and `brain-toolkit` (`brain session close` stops
emitting the handoff block into a retired repo, sets the `progress_retired`
marker, writes the frozen-file header once, and enforces the >= 5-session
threshold). That half is a **separate fulfillment in `brain-toolkit`**, done by a
parallel session — not part of this report and not something this session touched
(this session made no edits outside `conventions`).

## What was asked (4 acceptance criteria, verbatim from the demand's own text —
`platform-vault/spec-agent-memory-system.md` Appendix A.3 point 5 / A.6)

1. A repo whose `.brain/config.yml` carries `progress_retired: <YYYY-MM-DD>` no
   longer FAILs `vault-sync-handoff` for a `PROGRESS.md` that has stopped growing
   — passes vacuously or with an advisory, the same disposition the fresh-adoption
   amendment (`14f3ae7`) already established for a zero-session `.brain/`.
2. `brain-projection-equality` SKIPS a retired repo entirely.
3. Eligibility is read from the `progress_retired` marker ONLY — no check may
   recompute "≥ 5 sessions?" by counting `.brain/sessions/` at run time (D075 A.3
   point 4).
4. A repo with NO `progress_retired` marker is completely unaffected — all 21
   non-retired `.brain` repos and the four D074-excluded repos keep today's exact
   behaviour (D063 untouched).

All four addressed below, in order.

## 1. `vault-sync-handoff` — advisory pass, mirroring `14f3ae7` exactly

Studied `14f3ae7` (`fix(validator): brain-session-file no longer FAILs a
freshly-adopted .brain/`) before writing anything, per the brief's own
instruction. That commit's disposition: `CheckResult.unverified(ID, "WARN — ...")`
— `UNVERIFIED`, not a new status, never flips the run to failing.
`VaultSyncHandoffCheck` now opens with a retired-repo branch, checked **before**
`PROGRESS.md` is even read:

```java
Path brainDir = repoPath.resolve(BRAIN_DIR);
Optional<String> retiredSince = Files.isDirectory(brainDir)
        ? SessionFileSupport.retiredMarkerValue(brainDir)
        : Optional.empty();
if (retiredSince.isPresent()) {
    results.add(CheckResult.unverified(ID,
            "WARN — PROGRESS.md retired " + retiredSince.get() + " (.brain/config.yml "
                    + "progress_retired marker, D075) — frozen in place, no further handoff "
                    + "blocks expected; not checked for growth"));
    return results;
}
```

Same status (`UNVERIFIED`), same `WARN —` message prefix, same "never fails the
run" guarantee as `14f3ae7`'s zero-session case — no new severity invented.
Checked first because retirement is a property of the repo, not of what's
currently on the `PROGRESS.md` page; a retired repo's frozen entry is never
re-validated against the normal `Vault-sync:`-line requirement once the marker is
confirmed.

## 2. `brain-projection-equality` — vacuous skip

Same "checked first" placement, before `sessionsDir`/`PROGRESS.md` are read:

```java
Optional<String> retiredSince = SessionFileSupport.retiredMarkerValue(brainDir);
if (retiredSince.isPresent()) {
    results.add(CheckResult.pass(ID,
            "skipped — PROGRESS.md retired " + retiredSince.get() + " (.brain/config.yml "
                    + "progress_retired marker, D075); no current handoff block is being "
                    + "generated to compare"));
    return results;
}
```

A vacuous `PASS` with a "skipped" message — this validator's own pre-existing
skip vocabulary (see the `.brain`-absent and no-`PROGRESS.md` branches
immediately below it in the same file), not a new one. Critically, this check
runs **before** the newest-session-file inference (explicit `Session:` pairing or
the mtime-based legacy fallback) is ever reached — a session file closed after
retirement is never consulted at all, so it can never be compared against the
frozen block. Regression-pinned by `brain-checks/retired-blocks-growing-fail`:
that fixture gives a v0.6-shaped, deliberately-mismatched, mtime-newest session
file the exact shape that would trigger the pre-existing legacy inference path
and FAIL — the test asserts `PASS`/"skipped" instead, proving the short-circuit
actually lands before the inference runs, not just that the final answer happens
to come out right.

## 3. Eligibility read from the marker only — no session-counting added

`SessionFileSupport.retiredMarkerValue(Path brainDir)` is the **only** place
either check consults for retirement status, and it does exactly one thing: read
`.brain/config.yml`'s `progress_retired` line. It never opens, lists, or counts
`.brain/sessions/`. Confirmed by inspection (both call sites — `git grep -n
"sessions" validator/src/main/java/.../VaultSyncHandoffCheck.java
ProjectionEqualityCheck.java` — the retired-repo branches in both files
reference no session-counting API; `ProjectionEqualityCheck`'s own pre-existing
`sessionsDir` read only happens **after** the retired-repo branch has already
returned for a retired repo, and only serves the *non*-retired equality
comparison that pre-dates this delta). No new method, field, or import touches
`.brain/sessions/` as part of retirement detection anywhere in this change.

## 4. Non-retired repos — byte-identical, both by code structure and by test

**By construction:** both new branches are `if (retiredMarkerValue(...).isPresent())`
early returns. For any repo with no `.brain/config.yml`, or one without a
`progress_retired` key, `retiredMarkerValue()` returns `Optional.empty()` and
execution falls straight through to the pre-existing method body, unmodified —
not a re-implementation that happens to produce the same answer, the literal
same code path.

**By test:** `nonRetiredReposKeepTodaysExactVaultSyncHandoffAndProjectionEqualityBehaviour`
re-asserts the pre-existing PASS/FAIL outcomes on three untouched, pre-existing
fixtures (`brain-checks/good`, `vault-sync-handoff/repo-without-line`,
`brain-checks/v06-good`). Every one of the 58 pre-existing `ValidatorCliTest`
tests covering these two checks (unmodified) still passes unchanged — the full
before/after suite run (below) is itself the regression proof, not just the one
new test.

**By real-fleet A/B jar comparison (the strongest evidence, not just fixtures):**
built the pre-change jar (`git stash` to the parent commit, `mvn clean package`)
and the post-change jar, ran both against `../agent-runner` and
`../media-generation` from the platform root, `diff`'d the full report output.
**Byte-identical, both repos, both directions.** Neither carries a
`progress_retired` marker (confirmed: `grep -n progress_retired
agent-runner/.brain/config.yml media-generation/.brain/config.yml` → no match in
either file).

```
agent-runner:      15 checks, 0 failed, 0 unverified — PASS (unchanged)
media-generation:  15 checks, 1 failed (theme-words, "Face"/Hugging Face —
                    pre-existing, unrelated), 1 unverified (brain-session-lessons
                    WARN — pre-existing) — unchanged
```

**Neither repo was given the marker** — the demand's own text explicitly reserves
each repo's actual retirement for its own later session ("neither repo retires
anything on its own initiative as part of this demand"), and this fulfillment
respects that.

## Malformed-marker decision (the brief's own open question — answered, not
skipped)

`retiredMarkerValue()` returns the raw date value **only** when the marker is
present **and** shaped like `YYYY-MM-DD`. A present-but-malformed value
(`progress_retired: yes`, an empty value, a typo'd non-date string) is treated
**exactly like an absent marker — NOT retired.**

Two alternatives were considered and rejected:
- **Trust any non-empty value as proof of retirement.** Rejected: a typo
  (`progress_retired: tru`) would then silently freeze a repo's `PROGRESS.md`
  advisory-pass and skip its own drift check without the repo ever having crossed
  the real ≥ 5-session threshold — the exact silent misclassification this whole
  delta exists to prevent, just moved one level up.
- **FAIL the run when the marker is malformed.** Rejected: a config typo unrelated
  to what these two checks actually verify (PROGRESS.md/session-file agreement) is
  not their defect to report — that would make an unrelated typo in
  `.brain/config.yml` break checks that have nothing to do with that file's other
  fields.

Fail-safe toward pre-delta (non-retired) behavior was chosen as the
least-surprising answer, and matches the demand's own framing: "Treat a
malformed/absent value as NOT retired." Pinned by two dedicated tests/fixtures:
`vaultSyncHandoffTreatsAMalformedProgressRetiredValueAsNotRetired`
(`progress_retired: yes`) and
`brainProjectionEqualityTreatsAMalformedProgressRetiredValueAsNotRetired`
(`progress_retired: not-a-date`) — both assert the check still FAILs on a real,
independent defect in the fixture, proving the malformed marker didn't cause a
skip/advisory, not merely that the status happened to differ.

## Reader implementation — looked before writing, per the brief

Read `brain-toolkit/bin/brain`'s existing `.brain/config.yml` consumer
(`_read_progress_standing()`, line ~361) before writing a parser, per the brief's
own instruction. It reads the file as plain text and applies
`re.search(r"^progress_standing:\s*(.*)$", text, re.M)`, then unquotes.
`SessionFileSupport.retiredMarkerValue()` mirrors that exactly: a single-key
regex line scan (`Pattern.compile("(?m)^progress_retired:\s*(.*)$")`), not a YAML
library — one minimal-reader convention for this file across both repos, rather
than `conventions` inventing a second parsing approach. Also consistent with this
same file's pre-existing `topLevelFields()`/`fieldValues()`, which scan
session-file frontmatter the same deliberately-not-a-full-YAML-parse way (a
session file's nested content legitimately contains characters a strict YAML
scanner rejects — the documented reason those methods exist).

## Tests

7 new tests in `ValidatorCliTest`, 4 new fixtures under
`validator/src/test/resources/fixtures/brain-checks/`:

- **`retired-clean`** — marker present, well-formed frozen 5-line handoff block.
  `vaultSyncHandoffAdvisoryPassesARetiredRepoInsteadOfFailing`,
  `brainProjectionEqualitySkipsARetiredRepoEntirely`, and
  `retiredRepoWhosePROGRESSStillHasAValidBlockIsStillFine` (the last of these
  covers the brief's fourth test requirement — "a retired repo whose PROGRESS.md
  still has a valid block → still fine" — and also asserts `brain-session-file`
  keeps passing unaffected, since that check is out of this delta's scope).
- **`retired-malformed-marker`** (`progress_retired: yes`) —
  `vaultSyncHandoffTreatsAMalformedProgressRetiredValueAsNotRetired`.
- **`retired-malformed-marker-projection-drift`** (`progress_retired: not-a-date`)
  — `brainProjectionEqualityTreatsAMalformedProgressRetiredValueAsNotRetired`.
- **`retired-blocks-growing-fail`** (marker present, a v0.6-shaped session closed
  after retirement carries a deliberately mismatched `vault_sync` and is given
  the mtime-newest filesystem position by the owning test via `touch()`) —
  `brainProjectionEqualitySkipBlocksAFailThatWouldOtherwiseGrowAfterRetirement`,
  the demand's own named worry made concrete and pinned.
- **`nonRetiredReposKeepTodaysExactVaultSyncHandoffAndProjectionEqualityBehaviour`**
  — regression pin against three untouched, pre-existing fixtures.

Two fixture-authoring bugs were caught and fixed during this session, not
shipped: (1) a first draft of `retired-malformed-marker/PROGRESS.md` used the
literal substring "Vault-sync:" inside its own explanatory prose, which
satisfied `VaultSyncHandoffCheck`'s substring-matching regex by accident and
produced a false PASS — reworded to avoid the string entirely; (2) the first
`retired-malformed-marker-projection-drift` session fixture used a legacy
filename shape, which `brain-projection-equality`'s legacy fallback path
correctly skips as "not v0.6-shaped" regardless of retirement — renamed to a
v0.6-shaped filename so the fixture actually exercises the comparison it's meant
to test.

**Suite: 65 → 72 tests.** Confirmed both counts via `git stash`/`stash pop`
(`mvn test`, not inferred from a diff): 65 green before this change, 72 green
after — 0 failures either side.

## Real-fleet verification (beyond the two acceptance-relevant repos above)

`mvn clean package` rebuilt `validator/target/conventions-validator-0.1.0.jar`
(shaded, 7.1 MB). Full A/B methodology and results are under "4. Non-retired
repos" above.

## What the origin (`platform-vault`) must know

- Both checks are retirement-aware as of commit `97472af`. Either pilot may now
  retire **once `brain-toolkit`'s own half of this same demand has also landed**
  — the sequencing note in the demand's own acceptance criteria ("the
  `conventions` half SHOULD land first or same-day") is satisfied; whether
  `brain-toolkit`'s half has landed in the same session is that session's own
  report to make, not this one's to claim.
- Neither `agent-runner` nor `media-generation` was given a `progress_retired`
  marker by this session — per the demand's explicit "neither repo retires
  anything on its own initiative" constraint. Retirement itself remains each
  repo's own later session, subject to `brain-toolkit`'s threshold enforcement.
- The `progress_retired` marker's accepted shape is exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`
  (matching `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, one regex line, no timezone/time component). If
  `brain-toolkit`'s marker-setting command emits a different shape (a full
  ISO-8601 timestamp, for instance), `conventions`' reader will treat it as
  malformed and NOT retired — worth a cross-check between the two fulfillments
  before either pilot actually retires, since this repo's session had no
  visibility into what `brain-toolkit`'s parallel session chose to write.

## Not done / caveats

- `brain-toolkit`'s half (marker setter, frozen-file header, generation stop,
  threshold enforcement) — explicitly out of scope for this session, per the
  task's own instruction not to touch that repo; a parallel session's own
  fulfillment.
- This report does not move the demand file in `platform-vault/demands/` to
  `archive/` — that is the origin's own action once the coordinator confirms
  both halves satisfied, per `DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §3 step 5, outside this repo's
  authority to do on `platform-vault`'s behalf.
- No governing-text contradiction found in Appendix A.3/A.6 against this brief —
  see the session's own report-back for the explicit confirmation.

   (`../DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §5).

   `job_class` (D047), explicitly said so in the entry itself: a repo-contents-only

   changes are process-visible. That's a judgment call for the shipping session,
   not a mechanical check derivable from HEXAGON.md, a dependency manifest, or file
   layout. The `descoped_reason` names what would change this (a future

   section surfaces the duty by name, not only via the imported block underneath.

   no edit made to `../platform-vault/CLAUDE.md` or any other `platform-vault`


The existing 23 entries were neither reordered nor otherwise touched (the two

the list names and pulls `functionalName`/`kind`/`side`/`status`/`deps` live from

- *`inventory.repos` includes `agent-runner`, no reordering of the others* —
  done. `application.yml` re-parses cleanly (PyYAML `safe_load`): 25 repos total
  (was 23), `agent-runner` present, no duplicates, prior order intact.
- *`GET /registry` lists it as a valid `hexagon.descriptor` entry parsed live* —
  verified read-only that `../agent-runner/HEXAGON.md` carries valid frontmatter
  with every required field: `functionalName: agent-runner` (matches
  `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$`), `kind: runtime`, `side: host`, `status: building`,
  `deps: [contracts, demand-coordinator, state-feed]` — exactly the values the
  demand's acceptance criteria name. `contracts` pin is `v0.14.0` (TypeScript
  binding). Nothing hand-entered on the control-plane side.

  `demand-coordinator`, and `state-feed`, no new edge for any other repo* —
  `deps` is exactly `[contracts, demand-coordinator, state-feed]`, so those are
  the only three edges the dependency map should gain from this entry; no other
  repo's row is affected.

Full `mvn test` under JDK 21 (Temurin 21.0.11, per the platform toolchain —

# Fulfillment — control-plane: send `X-Build-Secret` on `POST /build`

## What was done

`CiRunnerClient.triggerBuild()` (`src/main/java/io/platform/controlplane/shipping/CiRunnerClient.java`)
now builds the `POST /build` request with an `HttpRequest.Builder` and
conditionally adds an `X-Build-Secret` header — set to
`properties.buildSharedSecret()` whenever that value is non-null and
non-blank, omitted entirely otherwise. Nothing else about the request
changed.

`ShippingProperties` (a `@ConfigurationProperties` record) grew a fourth
component, `buildSharedSecret`, bound from
`control-plane.shipping.build-shared-secret`. `application.yml` sets it to
`${CONTROL_PLANE_SHIPPING_BUILD_SHARED_SECRET:}` — Spring relaxed binding,
so the env var name follows the same `SCREAMING_SNAKE` convention as every
other override in this file; blank default preserves exactly today's
behavior (no header). `DEPLOYMENT.md`'s env-var table documents the new var,
names the required match with ci-runner's own `BUILD_SHARED_SECRET`, and
flags it as a secret value for SOPS+age distribution, not a plaintext
default — consistent with the existing Postgres-credentials note in the same
file.

**No log/error leakage:** `CiRunnerClient`'s two failure paths —
`CiRunnerUnavailableException` for a non-202 response and for a connection
failure — interpolate the base URL and a truncated response body/status
code, never the header value or `properties.buildSharedSecret()`. Read the
whole file to confirm; the secret is referenced exactly once, at the
`requestBuilder.header(...)` call site.

## Read-only sanity check against the acceptance criteria

- *Sends `X-Build-Secret` whenever the secret is non-blank, omits it when
  blank* — done, and covered by two new unit tests
  (`triggerBuild_nonBlankSharedSecret_sendsHeader`,
  `triggerBuild_blankSharedSecret_omitsHeader`) that inspect the header a
  stub HTTP server actually received.
- *Settable per deployment without a code change, via Spring relaxed
  binding* — done: `CONTROL_PLANE_SHIPPING_BUILD_SHARED_SECRET` maps onto
  `control-plane.shipping.build-shared-secret` with zero code change,
  documented in `DEPLOYMENT.md`.
- *Never appears in logs or error messages* — confirmed by reading
  `CiRunnerClient` in full; also confirmed empirically during live
  verification below (the 401 error message from ci-runner names the header
  as missing/invalid but never echoes any secret value on either side).
- *Live verification with ci-runner's emitter, `BUILD_SHARED_SECRET` set: 202
  on match, 401 on mismatch* — done, see below.

## Live verification (real ci-runner `state-emitter`, real GitHub dispatch)

Ran against the actual persistent `ci-runner-state-emitter-1` container
(port 8083) and a locally-run instance of this repo's own jar (not the
shared `runtime-control-plane-1` container — kept that one untouched since
it's `runtime`'s to rebuild/restart, per standing convention), pointed at
the same Postgres the live container uses and at
`CONTROL_PLANE_SHIPPING_CI_RUNNER_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8083`.

1. Set `BUILD_SHARED_SECRET` in ci-runner's `.env` (gitignored, local-only)
   to a throwaway test value, `docker compose up -d state-emitter` to
   recreate the container with it.
2. **Match case:** started the local control-plane jar with
   `CONTROL_PLANE_SHIPPING_BUILD_SHARED_SECRET` set to the same value.
   `POST /ship {"repo":"elmoul/conventions","ref":"main"}` →
   **`202` / `status: PENDING`**. Emitter log:
   `[build-command] dispatched elmoul/conventions@main (corr=...)` — no
   `[build-auth]` rejection line. This created a real `workflow_dispatch` run
   on `elmoul/conventions` (`29862083828`); cancelled it immediately after
   (`gh run cancel`) since it was only a header-plumbing test, not a build
   this demand needed to complete.
3. **Mismatch case:** restarted the local jar with
   `CONTROL_PLANE_SHIPPING_BUILD_SHARED_SECRET=wrong-secret-value`.
   `POST /ship` (same body) → **`502`**, body
   `{"error":"ci-runner POST /build returned HTTP 401: {\"error\":\"Missing or invalid X-Build-Secret\"}"}`.
   Emitter log: `[build-auth] rejected /build: missing or invalid
   X-Build-Secret`. Confirms the emitter's own 401 propagates through
   `CiRunnerClient`'s existing non-202 handling — no new error path needed on
   this side. Neither the right nor the wrong secret value appears anywhere
   in either log or the HTTP response body.
4. **Cleanup, restored to prior state:** stopped both local jar instances;
   reverted ci-runner's `.env` to drop `BUILD_SHARED_SECRET` (it was blank
   before this session) and `docker compose up -d state-emitter` again to
   recreate the container back to blank-secret / in-network-trust mode —
   confirmed via `GET /health` → 200 and a log line showing normal restart.
   The shared, persistent `ci-runner-state-emitter-1` and
   `runtime-control-plane-1` containers are exactly as they were before this
   session; no lingering processes (`netstat` confirmed port 8079 free after
   both local jar instances were stopped).

## Test suite — GREEN

`mvn -B test`, JDK 21 (Temurin/Oracle 21.0.11, default on this box): **55
tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (2 new tests added to `CiRunnerClientTest`,
existing `ShippingProperties` call sites in `CiRunnerClientTest` and
`DeployRunnerTest` updated for the new constructor arity).

**Committed and pushed to `origin/main`**: `933cee7` (code + docs +
CHANGELOG), plus this report.

## Not done / caveats

- The live, shared `runtime-control-plane-1` container was **not** rebuilt
  or given a real `CONTROL_PLANE_SHIPPING_BUILD_SHARED_SECRET` — that
  container's rebuild/restart is `runtime`'s post-merge step (same posture
  as every prior control-plane demand touching the live container), and
  setting a *permanent* secret on both the live emitter and the live
  control-plane container is a paired operational rollout ci-runner's own
  PROGRESS already earmarked for itself once this demand is satisfied. This
  report proves the capability works end-to-end against the real emitter;
  turning it on in production on both sides is a follow-up outside this
  repo's own deploy surface.
- No SOPS+age secret material was created or distributed — the live
  verification above used a throwaway local value, reverted immediately
  after.

# Fulfillment — control-plane: CORS allow-list for the management console

## What was done

New `CorsConfig` (`src/main/java/io/platform/controlplane/config/CorsConfig.java`),
same pattern as state-feed's and treasury's — `WebMvcConfigurer`, constructor-injected
`@Value` allow-list, no blanket `@CrossOrigin("*")`:

- Property: `control-plane.cors.allowed-origins`, default `http://localhost:4200`
  (env-var overridable the standard Spring way:
  `CONTROLPLANE_CORS_ALLOWEDORIGINS` / `control-plane.cors.allowed-origins`).
- Grants exactly the five demanded endpoints:
  `GET /registry`, `GET /registry/dependencies` (via `/registry/**`, GET-only),
  `GET /ship/{correlationId}` (via `/ship/*`, GET-only),
  `POST /scaffold`, `POST /ship` (preflights included — Spring MVC's CORS mapping
  handles OPTIONS preflight automatically).
- `POST /ci/results` has **no** CORS mapping — ci-runner's server-to-server callback
  keeps zero browser grant, per the demand's explicit exclusion. `/registry/**` and
  `/ship/*` patterns do not cover `/ci/results`.
- Documented in `README.md` (What it does) and `HEXAGON.md` (inbound ports section).

## Acceptance criteria vs. what was verified

1. *Browser fetch from `http://localhost:4200` succeeds on the 3 GETs + 2 POSTs* —
   covered by the new `CorsConfigTest` (Spring Boot `RANDOM_PORT` + real HTTP
   preflights, one test per endpoint). See "Verification" for whether it executed here.
2. *`POST /ci/results` has no CORS grant* — asserted by
   `ciResultsCallbackGetsNoCorsGrantAtAll` (preflight from the allowed origin returns
   no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`).
3. *Non-allow-listed origins get no grant; origins configurable; documented* —
   `disallowedOriginGetsNoGrantOnRegistryGet` covers the negative case; property
   documented in README + HEXAGON.md.
4. *Era-I screens light up with no dashboard-side change* — expected once the live
   container is rebuilt; see below.

## Verification

`mvn` is absent on the host; tests ran inside Docker
(`maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21`, host `.m2` mounted, whole platform tree mounted so
sibling-repo-reading tests work). Result: **32 tests, 26 pass**. The 6 non-passing
are all environmental, none touch the CORS logic itself:

- 4 errors — every Testcontainers-based test (`CorsConfigTest`,
  `RegistryControllerTest`, `BuildTrackerRestartSafetyTest`, `ShipControllerTest`)
  errors on "Could not find a valid Docker environment" — the known
  Docker-in-Docker/Ryuk sandbox limitation. `CorsConfigTest` is among them because
  the app context needs Postgres to boot at all.
- 2 failures — `DeployRunnerTest`, pre-existing and unrelated: `runtime`'s
  `scripts/deploy.sh` carries CRLF line endings in this Windows checkout, so bash in
  the Linux container fails with `$'\r': command not found` before the test's
  expected error path is reached.

The new `CorsConfigTest` compiles cleanly and follows the exact shape of treasury's
green `CorsConfigTest`; a host-level Maven+Docker toolchain (or CI) should run it
green.

## For the origin / the architect

- **The live control-plane container does not pick this up by itself** — rebuilding
  and restarting it is the architect's post-merge step; nothing was done to running
  containers this session.
- After that restart, the Era-I screens should render live registry data with zero
  dashboard-side change; WU-108 can build on `POST /scaffold` / `POST /ship` +
  `GET /ship/{id}` polling as planned.
- Per `../DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4: done is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator/owner
  validates; dashboard archives its demand file only after approval.

# Fulfillment — wire `RegistryEntry.class` through `InventoryService.toRegistryEntry()`

## What we did

`InventoryService.toRegistryEntry()` now copies `descriptor.getClass_()` onto the
built `RegistryEntry` when present, converting `HexagonDescriptor.Class` to
`RegistryEntry.Class` via `.value()`/`RegistryEntry.Class.fromValue(...)` — the
same conversion pattern already used for `kind`/`side`/`status`. `GET /registry`
now serves `class: "low-stakes" | "health-class" | "kids-class"` for every app
hexagon whose own `HEXAGON.md` declares it.

Live-verified against the real fleet (`mvn spring-boot:run`, then `curl
localhost:8081/registry` via the full `RegistryControllerTest` MockMvc run, not a
separate manual boot — see Tests below): `plantpal`, `pregnancy`, and `portfolio`
each now carry `"class"` in their entry — `"low-stakes"`, `"health-class"`,
`"low-stakes"` respectively, matching their `HEXAGON.md` frontmatter exactly (the
same values the demand's acceptance criteria named).

## What we did NOT do (and why)

- **`appId` and `plan` were not wired.** The demand's own title says "if present"
  — checked directly against `contracts` v0.12.0's `hexagon.descriptor.json`
  schema (`contracts/schemas/control-plane/hexagon.descriptor.json`) and the
  generated `HexagonDescriptor.java`: neither `appId` nor `plan` exists on
  `HexagonDescriptor` at all. Both are `registry.entry`-only fields, documented
  in that schema/generated class as "populated when app.manifest registration
  arrives" — i.e. sourced from the *live app.manifest registration* port, not
  from a repo's static `HEXAGON.md`. That port isn't built yet (`control-plane`'s
  own `HEXAGON.md` lists "`app.manifest` self-registration" under "Not yet
  built"). There is nothing in this repo to copy them from yet; wiring them now
  would mean inventing a value, which the demand's own body explicitly didn't ask
  for (its dashboard-side workaround already treats this as an honest known gap,
  not something to fake).

  `descriptor.getClass_()` is `null` for every non-app repo (confirmed via the
  new `widget-b` assertion in `InventoryServiceTest`), so `entry.setClass_()` is
  simply never called for them, and `@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)` on the generated

  assertions: `widgetA.getClass_()` equals `RegistryEntry.Class.LOW_STAKES`, and
  `widgetB.getClass_()` (a `runtime`-kind repo with no `class` in its
  frontmatter) is `null`.

  `getRegistryReturnsEveryValidatedEntryWithNoErrors` already exercises the full

While getting to green, `RegistryControllerTest` had two pre-existing failures
against the live fleet, unrelated to either demand:
`treasuryUsedContractsMatchesItsHexagonMd` (treasury's `HEXAGON.md` had grown a
`dimension.event` entry since the test's hardcoded expectation was written) and
`dependencyMapShowsStateEventConsumedByItsDeclaredRepos` (`observability` now
also declares `state.event`, per its own recorded binding ruling). Reproduced
against the unmodified baseline (`git stash`) to confirm these predate this
session's changes, then updated the two hardcoded expectation lists in this
repo's own test file to match the live fleet — no sibling repo touched, no
contracts change, just this repo's own drift-tracking test catching up to
reality it's designed to track ("matched against the real fleet, not a frozen

# Fulfillment — control-plane: registry-gap follow-up

Not one of the demand's five explicit targets (`portfolio`, `pregnancy`,
`ci-runner`, `runtime`, `launcher`) — this closes the registry-gap side-effect
flagged when the demand-coordinator's dependency-order verdict couldn't compute
on 2026-07-11 because `portfolio` wasn't found in control-plane's registry.

## What was done

Investigated whether the gap is a genuine missing-registration bug in
control-plane or an intentional exclusion. It's neither, exactly:

- `control-plane.inventory.repos` (`application.yml`) has listed `portfolio`
  since 2026-07-09 (commit `3003793`, fulfilling
  `demand-coordinator-20260709-control-plane-registration`) — the walk list was
  never missing the entry.
- Reproduced the live behavior directly by running `InventoryService` against
  the real sibling checkouts (not the synthetic fixture `InventoryServiceTest`
  uses): `portfolio`'s `HEXAGON.md` frontmatter fails schema validation, so it
  lands in the visible `errors` array, not the `hexagons` entries `GET /registry`
  serves. Two problems in the frontmatter, first one masking the second:
  1. `status: built` — not in the schema's enum (`planned`/`building`/`active`/
     `deprecated`); Jackson throws constructing the enum, which is the first
     parse failure.
  2. `hosting: external-ok` — not a field `hexagon.descriptor` defines at all;
     this repo's parser deliberately fails on unknown properties rather than
     silently dropping them.
- This is control-plane's own documented invariant working as designed (see this
  repo's `HEXAGON.md`: "a repo whose frontmatter fails schema validation shows up
  as a visible error in the response, never a silent skip") — not a bug in this
  repo's registration mechanism or a case for a one-off insert into any registry
  store. There is no database here to hand-edit; the registry is computed live
  from every sibling's `HEXAGON.md` on each request (spec `spec-control-plane.md`
  §9's static-registry-first design, already past the "static registry file"
  phase into the live inventory reader).
- Per standing orders, did not edit `portfolio/HEXAGON.md` from this session (out
  of repo scope, same rule as the `contracts` one-line-fix rule, generalized to
  any sibling repo). Instead raised
  `demands/2026-07-13-portfolio-hexagon-descriptor-validation.md` (`to:
  [portfolio]`) with the exact reproduction above and the two concrete fixes
  needed, committed to `main` as its own coordination commit.

## Verification performed

Reproduced against the real `../portfolio` checkout (not asserted from memory or
docs): built a throwaway `InventoryProperties`/`InventoryService` call scoped to
`contracts` + `portfolio` only, ran it under `mvn test`, confirmed `portfolio`
appears in the response's `errors` list with the exact enum-construction failure
message quoted in the new outbox demand, then deleted the scratch test — nothing
committed from that probe.

Cross-checked `platform-vault/PLATFORM_STATE.md` (read-only, not edited): it
independently tracks the same `portfolio` `status: built` enum error under
"repo-side self-describing staleness (theirs to fix)" — consistent with this
report's diagnosis, and confirms the vault side already expects portfolio to be
the one to fix it, not control-plane.

## What the origin should do

No code or config follow-up needed in control-plane — nothing to change here.
Once `portfolio` fixes its `HEXAGON.md` (tracked via the new outbox demand this
repo raised, not this one), it will appear in `GET /registry` on the very next
request with no further action from this repo, since the registry is computed
live rather than cached or hand-maintained. Move
`platform-vault-20260711-port-reassignments` to `demands/archive/` once this
report (and the five explicit targets' reports) are approved — this repo does not
do that itself and will not notify the vault directly, per `../DEMAND_SYSTEM.md`
§4.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: model-policy settings panel [R4]

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. Full
build-notes trail: `PROGRESS.md`'s 2026-07-20 "Model-policy settings panel" entry.

## What shipped

Coded directly against the authoritative contract report
(`../ai-gateway/demands/fulfilled/agent-runner-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-store-report.md`),
read in full before writing anything, per the task's own instruction — no guessed shapes.

New files, all in `src/app/settings/`:

- `model-policy.model.ts` — `ModelFunction` (`extraction | tier3-classifier | embeddings`),
  `PolicyEntryDto` (`{repo, function, policy, explicit}`), `PolicyUpdateRequest` (`{policy}`), and
  a pure `parsePolicy(policy: string)` helper that splits `"force:<model>"` for the edit form's
  pre-fill — form mechanics only, never a resolution decision (mirrors
  `CeilingsCrudComponent`'s own number-string parsing).
- `model-policy-repos.ts` — the static list of `.brain`-enabled repos this panel manages
  (`agent-runner`, `media-generation`, per the demand's own acceptance criteria). Static
  deliberately: ai-gateway's store has no repo-enumeration endpoint (`GET /ai/policy` only lists
  *explicit overrides* — a repo entirely on defaults never appears there). Flagged in-code and
  in-render as the one thing on this panel that isn't itself sourced from a live call (design
  law 2).
- `model-policy.service.ts` — `forRepo(repo)` → `GET /ai/policy/{repo}`, `setPolicy(repo, fn, req)`
  → `PUT /ai/policy/{repo}/{function}`, both unwrapping the `ApiResponse<T>` house shape (same
  pattern `CeilingsService`/`KillSwitchService` already use). Deliberately never calls
  `GET /ai/policy/resolve` — the demand is explicit the panel doesn't need it (structurer-only);
  calling it would mean this panel silently making a resolution decision only the gateway is meant
  to make.
- `model-policy-error.ts` — `describeModelPolicyError`, same status-0-is-opaque posture every
  other direct-HTTP screen here already takes, but names the specific redeploy ambiguity in its
  message rather than a generic "ai-gateway down."
- `model-policy-table.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}` — presentational per-repo table (3 rows:
  extraction/tier3-classifier/embeddings), inline edit (`auto` radio / `force:` radio + model-id
  text input), a `Reset to default` control (only shown when `explicit: true`) that issues
  `{policy: 'auto'}` directly without opening the edit form — the documented reset path (no
  DELETE endpoint exists). Static R4/A.5 explanatory notes render under every `tier3-classifier`
  row (see below).
- `model-policy-panel.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}` — owns per-repo fetch/loading/error state via
  `StateShellComponent` (loading/unreachable/ready — `empty` isn't reachable here since
  `GET /ai/policy/{repo}` always returns exactly 3 entries per the contract), one shared class-2
  `ConfirmDialogComponent` (before→after diff, no typed word — a policy swap is reversible, not
  destructive, same class `CeilingsCrudComponent`'s edits use), and the session action-log append
  point (`SET_MODEL_POLICY` / `RESET_MODEL_POLICY`, class 2, screen `/settings`, target
  `<repo>/<function>`).
- `model-policy.model.spec.ts`, `model-policy.service.spec.ts`, `model-policy-error.spec.ts` — unit
  coverage for the parse helper, the service's HTTP shape, and the error classifier.

Modified: `settings-screen.component.ts/html` (adds `<app-model-policy-panel />`),
`settings-screen.component.spec.ts` (asserts the new panel renders), `README.md` (`/settings`
bullet gains the model-policy mention), `HEXAGON.md` (new outbound-port row + `ai-gateway`
dependency-list note), `CHANGELOG.md` (`### Added` entry).

## Placement decision

Embedded in the existing `/settings` screen rather than a new route. The demand's own title calls
it a "settings panel," it's owner-facing configuration (not an operational workflow like
Studio/Agents/Design), and `/settings` already satisfies D036 law 6 (deep-linkable) — no new route
was needed to meet that law. Follows `/settings`'s existing composition pattern (each concern is
its own presentational block appended to `settings-screen.component.html`, same as
`ConsoleConfigTableComponent`/`AvailabilityMatrixComponent`/`SettingsControlsComponent`).

## R4/A.5 semantics — what's live vs. static, and why

- **Effective policy + explicit/inherited distinction**: real, live, per-row (`entry.policy`,
  `entry.explicit` badge) — sourced directly from `GET /ai/policy/{repo}`, nothing computed.
- **Tier3-classifier never auto-downshifts**: a static note under every `tier3-classifier` row,
  always shown regardless of value — this is a fixed §9.0 rule (not repo/function-state-dependent
  data), so static is honest here, not a workaround.
- **Privacy-precedence caveat**: static note shown only when a `tier3-classifier` row is
  `force:<model>` — worded per the demand's own instruction, "as static explanatory text, since
  the panel cannot read repos' config.yml (absence is a state, not a blank)."
- **Self-defending-audit caveat**: same trigger (forced tier3-classifier), also static, for the
  reason in "Contract gap 1" below.

## Contract gaps found — flagged, not worked around

1. **Effective-policy shape carries no privacy/audit data.** The demand text (acceptance point 3)
   asks the panel to source the privacy-precedence note "from what the gateway API reports as the
   effective policy." But per the authoritative contract report, `PolicyEntryDto`
   (`GET /ai/policy/{repo}`'s response shape) is exactly `{repo, function, policy, explicit}` — no
   privacy field, no `selfDefendingAuditRequired`, no frontier-model name. Only
   `GET /ai/policy/resolve` carries `privacyEnforced`/`selfDefendingAuditRequired`, and this task's
   own brief is explicit the panel must not call it. Followed the brief's own stated fallback
   (static explanatory text) rather than either inventing data or silently calling `/resolve`
   anyway — flagging here because the demand's point-3 wording and the brief's fallback wording
   don't both fit the real DTO; a future session tightening this copy should know the effective-
   policy endpoint itself would need to grow a field (or the panel would need `/resolve`, contrary
   to today's brief) to make this genuinely live.
2. **New finding: no CORS grant exists for `/ai/policy/**` at all**, independent of the
   already-known redeploy gap. Read (not edited — never patch a sibling repo)
   `ai-gateway/src/main/java/io/platform/aigateway/config/CorsConfig.java`: it maps exactly
   `POST /ai/jobs`, nothing else, by explicit design (its own doc comment: grants are added "only
   once a real browser caller exists, never speculatively ahead of one"). This panel is that real
   browser caller now. Raised a new demand,
   `demands/2026-07-20-ai-gateway-model-policy-console-cors.md` (`to: [ai-gateway]`), asking for
   `GET`/`PUT` `/ai/policy/**` to be added to the allow-list — bundled with the redeploy this
   session already expected, since one container rebuild covers both.

## Degrades honestly today

Two stacked gaps stand between this panel and a live answer: (1) the live `runtime-ai-gateway-1`
container hasn't been redeployed onto ai-gateway's `/ai/policy/**` commits (`a9d079a`/`c088d77`) —
per ai-gateway's own fulfillment report, deliberately deferred until a live browser caller existed;
(2) the new CORS gap above. Until both land, every `GET /ai/policy/{repo}` call from the browser
fails (status 0, indistinguishable between "down," "no CORS grant," and "route doesn't exist yet"
from the browser's side alone) and `StateShellComponent` renders `unreachable` with a message
naming the specific probed endpoint (design law 3 — absence is a state, not a blank), never a
blank panel or a false "ready" state. `model-policy-error.ts`'s status-0 message says so explicitly
rather than implying a generic outage.

**Live end-to-end verification is pending both the ai-gateway redeploy and the new CORS grant** —
per the task's own agreed sequencing, this is not a gap this session needed to solve. Once both
land, the next session should re-verify a real read + a real edit (`force:<model>` and a reset)
against `agent-runner` or `media-generation` from `http://localhost:4200`, then this demand can be
considered closed end-to-end (today it's source/test-verified only).

## Tests / build

- `npx vitest run` (full suite): **905/905 green** (baseline 871 + 34 new: 3 `parsePolicy`, 5
  error-classifier, 5 service, 12 table-component, 9 panel-component). `settings-screen.component.spec.ts`
  updated (not counted as new) to assert the panel renders and to keep draining the now-larger set
  of on-init HTTP probes via its existing generic `httpMock.match(() => true)` teardown.
- `npx ng build`: clean, no warnings, no bundle-budget change (`/settings` was already an eagerly
  loaded route in this app's routing table — no new lazy chunk to budget).

## For the origin (agent-runner) / the architect

- Panel lives at `/settings` (not a new route) — `SettingsScreenComponent` composes
  `ModelPolicyPanelComponent` alongside the config table, availability matrix, controls, and
  action log.
- Nothing here computes a policy resolution or reads any repo's `config.yml` — every value shown
  is the gateway's own answer or explicitly-labeled static copy; every write is a real `PUT`
  gated behind the same class-2 confirm dialog every other reversible console write already uses.
- Two follow-ups now owed from ai-gateway before this closes end-to-end: redeploy
  `runtime-ai-gateway-1` onto `/ai/policy/**`, and fulfill
  `dashboard-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-console-cors`. Neither is blocking Phase 0/1 of the
  memory-system build per spec Appendix A.8 ("the store is a prerequisite for forcing, not for
  running"), same posture the sibling ai-gateway demand already established.
- Per `../DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4: `done` is a claim; the coordinator/owner validates and delivers
  this report to agent-runner. The origin demand file lives in agent-runner's own
  `demands/2026-07-20-dashboard-model-policy-settings-panel.md` (dashboard never held a copy, per
  the post-office model) — agent-runner archives it once the coordinator confirms this report.

## Addendum 2026-07-20 — live wiring verified end-to-end (container rebuilt, both gaps now closed)

Both gaps named above are closed: ai-gateway fulfilled `dashboard-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-console-cors`
(`../ai-gateway/demands/fulfilled/dashboard-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-console-cors-report.md`)
and redeployed `runtime-ai-gateway-1` onto both the CORS grant and the `/ai/policy/**` endpoints in
the same rebuild. This session closed the remaining link — `runtime-dashboard-1` itself was still
serving `fb42ed9` (pre-panel). Rebuilt and redeployed per this repo's own established precedent
(`docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml build dashboard && up -d dashboard` in `../runtime`,
same command WU-120/theme-c/every prior CORS fulfillment already used).

**Rebuild/redeploy, logged, generous timeout, only this repo's own container touched:**
- `docker compose build dashboard` → `BUILD SUCCESS` (image `runtime-dashboard`, ~6s app build
  inside a cached-layers image build).
- `docker compose up -d dashboard` → compose's own per-service log confirms every one of the other
  20 running containers stayed `Running` (never recreated); only `runtime-dashboard-1` went
  `Recreate → Recreated → Starting → Started`. Cross-checked with a `docker ps` name-set diff
  before/after (identical) and each container's own uptime after the fact (every sibling still at
  its pre-existing ~59-minute uptime; only `runtime-dashboard-1` reset to a fresh uptime).

**Served-bundle check:** `curl http://127.0.0.1:4200/` → `main-LW3RHC7I.js`; fetched that file
directly and grepped it — contains `app-model-policy-panel`, `model-policy-panel`,
`SET_MODEL_POLICY`, and `self-defending weekly audit` (the panel's own component selector, action
word, and static-caveat copy), confirming the rebuilt bundle is the one carrying this session's
code, not a stale cache.

**Live endpoint check (the CORS grant is browser-side; confirmed the endpoint itself answers too):**
```
curl -X OPTIONS http://localhost:8085/ai/policy/agent-runner -H "Origin: http://localhost:4200" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: GET"
→ 200, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:4200, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET

curl http://localhost:8085/ai/policy/agent-runner -H "Origin: http://localhost:4200"
→ 200 {"data":[{"repo":"agent-runner","function":"extraction","policy":"auto","explicit":false},
        {"repo":"agent-runner","function":"tier3-classifier","policy":"auto","explicit":false},
        {"repo":"agent-runner","function":"embeddings","policy":"auto","explicit":true}]}
```
Exactly the documented `PolicyEntryDto[]` shape, 3 entries, CORS header present on the real
response (not just the preflight).

**Real browser verification, not curl alone** (Browser pane navigated to `http://localhost:4200/settings`,
a fresh URL to force a real re-fetch past the tab's own HTTP cache — the tab had an older
`main-2JYNPCGT.js` cached from before either rebuild landed; a plain re-navigate reused it, a
cache-busted URL did not — noted here as a verification-tooling quirk of this session, not a defect
in the shipped app or its nginx config):
- The rendered page showed a real "Model policy" section with both pilot repos' live data
  (`read_page` accessibility-tree dump), matching the curl output exactly — including
  `agent-runner`/`embeddings` already showing `explicit: true` (a residue of ai-gateway's own
  verification session's force→reset cycle on that same row, correctly rendered as "an owner
  explicitly set this," not silently normalized away).
- Exercised a real write end-to-end through the actual rendered UI (clicked the real Edit/Save/
  Confirm controls, not a mocked call): set `agent-runner/extraction` to `force:claude-code` →
  confirm dialog showed `auto (inherited default) → force:claude-code` → confirmed → app showed
  "Saved." → a follow-up `curl .../ai/policy/agent-runner` confirmed the server-side store now had

  Then exercised the documented reset path the same way: clicked "Reset to default" → confirm

**No other repo or container touched.** Only `runtime-dashboard-1` was rebuilt/recreated this

# Fulfillment — dashboard: brain audit-queue screen

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.
Full build-notes trail: `PROGRESS.md`'s 2026-07-23 "Brain audit-queue screen" entry.

## Checked current state first

Before writing anything: a case-insensitive search across `src/` for `audit`/`pending-audit` and a
scan of `demands/fulfilled/` turned up nothing shaped like this capability — only the sibling
`brain-fleet-panel` work (a prior session, same demand family, `/brain` fleet-eligibility panel) had
shipped. This demand's own capability was not built by a prior session. Built fresh this session, on
the existing `brain/fleet-panel` branch.

## What shipped

Coded directly against agent-runner's real source (`../agent-runner/src/api/brainRoutes.ts`,
`domain/brain.ts`'s `parsePendingAudit`/`PendingAuditParsed`, and `brainRoutes.test.ts`'s own
fixture-driven HTTP assertions) — read in full before writing anything, no guessed shapes. The route
handler's real behavior: `exists: false` (no `pending-audit.md` yet) is a normal 200, never an
error; a 400 guards an unsafe repo segment before it ever reaches the filesystem; a 404 covers a
repo that doesn't exist or isn't `.brain`-enabled.

- **`agents/agent-runner.model.ts`** (existing file, extended) — `PendingAuditItem`
  (`{sessionId, unitId, lineRef, tier, classifierClass, context, humanClass}`, all `string | null`,
  field-for-field agent-runner's own parsed shape) and `PendingAuditResponse`
  (`{exists, generatedAt, items, filledCount, totalCount}`).
- **`agents/agent-runner.service.ts`** (existing file, extended) — `pendingAudit(repo)` (`GET
  /brain/{repo}/pending-audit`, on the existing `AgentRunnerService`, same "one service per owning
  hexagon" precedent the brain-fleet panel's own report already established — repo segment
  `encodeURIComponent`-escaped).
- **New `src/app/brain/audit/` folder:**
  - `brain-audit-dispatch-prompt.ts` — `buildBrainAuditFillPrompt(repo, selections)`, a pure
    text-template function (D036: the console renders and submits, it never writes a file itself).
    Names the exact file (`.brain/derived/pending-audit.md`), each item by its own identifying
    fields (`session_id`/`unit_id`/`line_ref` — matching the response's own `sessionId`/`unitId`/
    `lineRef`, snake_case to match the real `.md` file's own key names) and its chosen `human_class`,
    instructs the launched agent to set only those items' `human_class:` lines, commit, and touch
    nothing else (`context`/`tier`/`classifier_class` on any item, the structurer, the executioner).
  - `brain-audit-panel.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}` — presentational form. Renders every item's
    `sessionId`/`unitId`/`lineRef`/`tier`/`classifierClass`/`context` verbatim plus the response's
    own `filledCount`/`totalCount`. A `human_class` `<select>` per row offers exactly
    `applied`/`mentioned`/`deprecated` (a shared `HUMAN_CLASS_OPTIONS` const) plus a blank `(skip)`
    default — no other value is ever an `<option>`. Row selections reset via a constructor `effect()`
    keyed off `items()` array identity, so a repo switch or a refetch never leaks stale selections
    onto new rows. `exists: false` and `items.length === 0` (with `exists: true`) render two
    entirely separate template branches (`audit-no-sample` / `audit-zero-items` testids) — distinct
    messages, distinct markup, never reached simultaneously, and both only reachable once `state()`
    is `'ready'` (loading/error/unreachable stay owned by the shared `StateShellComponent`, exactly
    as the brain-fleet panel already does). Submit filters to only the rows with a non-blank
    selection before emitting — a skipped row is never present in the emitted array, not present
    with an empty-string `humanClass`.
  - `brain-audit-screen.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}` — the routed `brain/audit/:repo` screen. A live
    `ActivatedRoute.paramMap` subscription (same idiom `MissionDetailComponent`'s own doc comment
    explains: re-emits on every navigation to this route entry, including a param-only change on a
    reused component instance), fetches `pendingAudit(repo)` on each param change, computes
    `PanelState` (`loading`/`unreachable`/`error`/`ready` — no `'empty'`, since a 200 with `exists:
    false` or zero items is not itself an error/empty-request state, it's real content the panel
    itself branches on), owns the shared class-3 `ConfirmDialogComponent` (typed word `FILL`) and
    the actual `POST /dispatch` call (targeting `repo` — the audited repo itself, never
    `agent-runner`/`brain-toolkit`), and appends to the session action log (`FILL_AUDIT`, class 3,
    screen `/brain/audit`).
- **Modified:** `app.routes.ts` (new `brain/audit/:repo` route + doc-comment continuation),
  `brain-fleet-panel.component.{ts,html,spec.ts}` (new "Audit queue" `routerLink` per row, `+1`
  test), `brain-fleet-panel.component.spec.ts` / `brain-fleet-screen.component.spec.ts` (both needed
  `provideRouter([])` added to their `TestBed` config once `BrainFleetPanelComponent` started
  importing `RouterLink` — otherwise unchanged), `README.md` (routed-screens bullet gains the
  `brain/audit/:repo` mention), `HEXAGON.md` (new port-table row, `agent-runner` dependency note
  extended), `CHANGELOG.md` (`### Added` entry).

## Acceptance criteria — how each is met

1. **Per repo, renders every item from `GET /brain/{repo}/pending-audit`'s `items` array with
   `session_id`, `unit_id`, `line_ref`, `tier`, `classifier_class`, `context`, plus the response's
   `filledCount`/`totalCount`** — `BrainAuditPanelComponent` renders `sessionId`, `unitId`,
   `lineRef`, `tier`, `classifierClass`, `context`, `filledCount`, `totalCount` straight off each
   `PendingAuditItem`/the response body, no re-derivation; unit-tested (`brain-audit-panel.component
   .spec.ts`'s "renders every item field verbatim plus filledCount/totalCount") and screen-level
   (`brain-audit-screen.component.spec.ts`'s equivalent, against the real response shape).
2. **`exists: false` renders an explicit "no sample generated yet" state, distinct from and never
   conflated with a zero-item or error state** — two separate template branches
   (`audit-no-sample`/`audit-zero-items`), each asserted absent while the other is present, at both
   the panel level and the screen level (four dedicated tests total).
3. **`human_class` settable from exactly `applied`/`mentioned`/`deprecated`, or blank to skip** — a
   native `<select>` with exactly those four `<option>` values (three real values + the blank skip
   default) — asserted directly (`"the human-class select offers exactly the three allowed values
   plus a blank skip option, no other value"`), not merely documented.
4. **Submitting builds a dispatch prompt naming the exact file, the exact items (by
   `session_id`/`unit_id`/`line_ref`), and their chosen `human_class`, targeting the repo the audit
   belongs to; the console performs no file write itself** —
   `buildBrainAuditFillPrompt` is a pure string builder (six dedicated unit tests, including a
   null-identifying-field case rendering `(none)` rather than a fabricated placeholder), submitted
   through the existing `AgentRunnerService.dispatch()` with `repo: this.repo()` (the audited repo,
   confirmed by a dedicated screen test asserting `req.request.body.repo` equals the route's own
   repo param, not `agent-runner`/`brain-toolkit`) — this screen never opens, reads, or writes any
   file itself.
5. **Blank rows are excluded from the dispatch instruction entirely, never sent as an empty-string
   `human_class`** — the panel's `submit()` filters to `!!row.humanClass` before building the
   emission (a `''` selection is falsy and dropped); a dedicated test submits two rows with only one
   filled and asserts the emitted array contains exactly the one filled row, by exact shape (no
   second entry, no empty-string entry).

## Placement decisions

- **`brain/audit/:repo`, not a tab on `/brain` itself.** Detail-shaped content (one repo's own audit
  queue) reached via a link from the list (`brain-fleet-panel`'s new per-row "Audit queue" link) —
  the same list/detail split `design/:id`/`demands/:id` already established in this repo, not a
  drawer or tab bolted onto the fleet panel.
- **No new sidebar entry.** Consistent with every other `/x/:id`-shaped detail route in this repo
  (`design/:id`, `demands/:id`) — none of them get their own nav item either.
- **`pendingAudit()` added to the existing `AgentRunnerService`**, not a new service — same backend,
  same "one service per owning hexagon" precedent the brain-fleet panel's own report already
  established.
- **Dispatch targets the audited repo itself, not `agent-runner`/`brain-toolkit`.** Unlike the

   finds a disagreement with the server's own `summary`, displays the client re-parsed (raw-derived)
   counts instead and shows a visible mismatch banner. A dedicated test forces a deliberately-wrong
   server `ratifiedConventions.count` (5, against a real raw sample with 0 real entries) and asserts
   the wrong count (`5`) never renders, only the raw-derived `0` does.
2. **Proposed-conventions candidates as unit id + one-line description from `graph.md`'s `## Proposed
   conventions` section, explicitly named as needing iteration once real usage starts** —
   `parseProposedConventions` parses the real `agent-runner/.brain/graph.md` sample's `K-0152` entry
   into exactly `{unitId: 'K-0152', description: '"Two messages ...'}` (unit-tested against the real
   sample text verbatim, byte-for-byte, plus edge cases: no section at all, an empty section, a
   loosely-worded heading). The parser's own doc comment and this report both flag it as a
   provisional, iterate-with-agent-runner parse of prose — not a structured-contract guarantee.
3. **Batch selection of proposed unit ids — not all-or-nothing, not one-at-a-time-only** — a
   `Set<number>` of checked row indices; a dedicated test checks 2 of 2 candidates and asserts both
   emit in one `submitRequested`, a second dedicated test checks exactly 1 of 2 and asserts only that
   one row emits (proving neither "select all" nor "one at a time" is structurally forced).
4. **Submitting builds a dispatch prompt naming the exact unit ids selected, instructing the launched
   agent to append them under `.brain/overrides.md`'s existing `## ratified conventions` section
   (matching its current placeholder format, replacing `(none yet)` once real entries exist), and
   commit — the console performs no file write itself** — `buildBrainRatifyPrompt` is a pure string
   builder, unit-tested for every clause (naming the exact unit id/description, falling back to a
   bare unit-id line when description is empty, naming the `## ratified conventions` section and the
   `(none yet)` replacement instruction, instructing a commit, stating the console never writes the
   file itself) — 7 dedicated tests. Submitted through the existing `AgentRunnerService.dispatch()`
   with `repo: this.repo()` (confirmed by a dedicated screen test asserting `req.request.body.repo`
   equals the route's own repo param and `req.request.body.prompt` contains the exact selected unit
   id plus the section name) — this screen never opens, reads, or writes any file itself.
5. **An `exists: false` overrides response, or a graph response with no Proposed conventions section,
   renders an explicit empty/no-candidates state rather than an error** — three distinct testids
   (`ratify-no-overrides` for `overridesExists() === false`, `ratify-no-graph` for
   `graphExists() === false`, `ratify-no-candidates` for a real graph with zero parsed candidates),
   each asserted present with `state-error` absent, at both the panel level (dedicated unit tests) and
   the screen level (dedicated integration tests using real HTTP mock responses shaped exactly like
   `brainRoutes.test.ts`'s own missing-overrides.md / plain-graph.md fixtures).

## Placement decisions

- **`brain/ratify/:repo`, not a tab on `/brain` or a merge into `brain/audit/:repo`.** Detail-shaped
  content (one repo's own ratification queue) reached via a link from the fleet list, same
  list/detail split `brain/audit/:repo`/`design/:id`/`demands/:id` already established — audit-queue
  and ratification-queue are two independently-useful workflows over two different files
  (`pending-audit.md` vs. `overrides.md`+`graph.md`), not two views of the same data.
- **`overrides()`/`graph()` added to the existing `AgentRunnerService`**, not a new service — same
  backend, same "one service per owning hexagon" precedent every prior `/brain/*` addition in this
  repo already established.
- **Both endpoints fetched via `forkJoin`, not two independent state machines.** The ratification
  screen genuinely needs both together before it's meaningfully "ready" (candidates without knowing
  what's already ratified, or ratified-state without candidates to ratify, are each half a screen) —
  unlike the fleet panel's `/brain/fleet`+`/brain/repos` split (where a `reposDegraded` *secondary*
  signal made sense because the primary `/brain/fleet` answer is independently useful), there's no
  natural "primary" read here to degrade around, so a single combined `panelState` was the simpler,
  equally-honest choice. A hard failure on either request surfaces the same `error`/`unreachable`
  state via `describeAgentRunnerError`, same posture as `brain/audit/:repo`.
- **Candidate parsing lives entirely client-side (`parse-proposed-conventions.ts`), not requested as
  a new server-side structured field.** The demand body itself frames `graph.md`'s prose content as
  something "needing iteration with the fulfiller once real usage starts" rather than asking for a
  new agent-runner contract up front — building a small, explicitly-provisional client parser against
  the one real sample available, rather than raising a new demand for a server-side change nobody has
  validated the shape of yet, matches that framing. If/when a second differently-shaped `graph.md`
  breaks this parser's assumptions, that's the natural trigger for a follow-up demand asking
  agent-runner to parse and structure this section server-side instead.
- **Dispatch targets the repo whose own `.brain/overrides.md` is edited, not agent-runner or
  brain-toolkit** — same posture `brain/audit/:repo`'s fill-dispatch already takes (unlike the fleet
  panel's manual full-run trigger, which must run `bin/executioner` living in `brain-toolkit`):
  `.brain/overrides.md` is a file inside the ratified repo's own checkout.

## Degrades honestly today (not live end-to-end verified)

Same standing gap the brain-fleet-panel and brain-audit-queue reports already named and this session
did not close: agent-runner is host-native (not part of `runtime`'s Compose stack) and was not
started this session — starting a sibling repo's own service is that repo's action, not this one's to
take unprompted, and it wasn't named in this task's brief either. Every HTTP interaction shipped here
is verified against `HttpTestingController`-mocked requests whose route paths, methods, and body
shapes are cross-checked directly against agent-runner's real Express handler (`brainRoutes.ts`), its
own test fixtures (`brainRoutes.test.ts`), and this repo's own real `.brain/overrides.md`/
`.brain/graph.md` samples read this session — not against a live browser round-trip.

**Once agent-runner is confirmed live at `:8089`**, the next session (or this one, if re-engaged)
should: open `http://localhost:4200/brain`, follow a real repo's "Ratify" link, confirm the real
`GET /brain/{repo}/overrides` + `GET /brain/{repo}/graph` responses render (including the real
`K-0152` candidate for `agent-runner` itself), select a batch, confirm → `POST /dispatch` succeeds,
and check the launched Claude Code session's own transcript actually appended the entries under
`.brain/overrides.md`'s `## ratified conventions` section and committed. Separately, once a second or
differently-shaped `graph.md` sample exists in the wild, re-check `parseProposedConventions`'s
heading/line-shape assumptions against it — this is the explicitly-named "iteration with the
fulfiller" the demand body itself calls for, not a hidden gap. Neither gap blocks this demand's own
"done" claim — every acceptance criterion above is a testable statement about this console's own
behavior against agent-runner's documented contract and one real sample, none require agent-runner's
live uptime or a second sample to verify.

## Tests / build

- `npx vitest run` (full suite): **1245/1245 green** (baseline 1202 + 43 new: 5
  `parseProposedConventions`, 6 `parseOverridesSummaryFromRaw`/`overridesSummariesEqual`, 7
  `buildBrainRatifyPrompt`, 13 `BrainRatifyPanelComponent`, 11 `BrainRatifyScreenComponent`, 1
  `BrainFleetPanelComponent` new ratify-link test; no pre-existing test's assertions changed).
- `npx ng build`: clean, no errors. One bundle-budget WARNING (not an error) — 730.48 kB vs. a
  686.08 kB warning threshold (44.40 kB over, up from 29.99 kB over before this session), flagged here
  honestly rather than silently ignored, same class of caveat every prior brain-screen demand's own
  report already flagged for its own bundle growth.

## For the origin (agent-runner) / the architect

- `brain/ratify/:repo` composes: `BrainRatifyPanelComponent` (overrides summary/raw + candidate
  checklist + submit) + the shared `ConfirmDialogComponent` (class 3, typed `RATIFY`).
- Nothing here re-parses or re-derives `overrides.md`'s section counts server-authoritatively — the
  client-side re-parse (`overrides-raw-summary.ts`) exists purely as a disagreement check against the
  server's own `summary`, and always defers to `raw` on conflict, never the other way around. The one
  genuinely new client-side parsing surface is `parse-proposed-conventions.ts` (`graph.md`'s prose),
  explicitly flagged above and in the code itself as provisional.
- The one write path (the ratify-submit) is a real `POST /dispatch` gated behind the same class-3
  confirm dialog every other consequential console write already uses, and it never opens or writes
  `.brain/overrides.md` (or any file) itself — that happens inside the dispatched agent's own session,
  under its own write access to the ratified repo.
- No follow-up owed from agent-runner to close this — the read surface this screen depends on
  (`GET /brain/{repo}/overrides`, `GET /brain/{repo}/graph`) is already built, documented, and
  test-covered server-side (`brainRoutes.ts`, `brainRoutes.test.ts`'s own describe blocks for both
  routes). The only remaining gaps are live-environment verification and the explicitly-named
  graph.md-parsing iteration (see above), both this repo's own follow-ups, neither a blocker on any
  other repo.
- Per `../DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4: `done` is a claim; the coordinator/owner validates and delivers this
  report to agent-runner. The origin demand lives in agent-runner's own `demands/` (dashboard never
  held a copy, per the post-office model) — agent-runner archives it once the coordinator confirms
  this report.

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

## Checked current state first

Read the existing `/brain/audit/:repo` screen fully (`brain-audit-panel.component.ts`/`.html`,
shipped across two prior demands: `agent-runner-20260722-brain-audit-queue` for the base panel,
`agent-runner-20260724-dashboard-brain-audit-judgeable-context` for the per-row context block). Neither
prior session had shipped this demand's capability: every row rendered the identical blank fill
`<select>` regardless of whether `item.humanClass` already carried a saved value — the select's own
`selectionFor(i)` always starts at `''` and nothing in the row read `item.humanClass` at all — and there
was no `filledCount === totalCount` messaging anywhere in the panel or screen. Confirmed live against
agent-runner's real, running instance (`:8089`): `curl :8089/brain/agent-runner/pending-audit` returned
the real queue at `filledCount: 9, totalCount: 9`, all 9 items carrying a non-empty `humanClass`
(`applied`/`mentioned`) — exactly the state the demand names. Not a prior-session duplicate; built fresh
this session, continuing the session agent-runner's dispatch supervisor had already opened for this
task (`2026-07-24_0334_fulfill-demand-agent-runner-20260724-das`).

## What shipped

- **`brain-audit-panel.component.ts`**:
  - `isFilled(item)`: true iff `item.humanClass` is non-null and non-empty. Drives the per-row branch
    between the saved-verdict badge and the fill select.
  - `allFilled()` (computed): true iff `totalCount() > 0 && filledCount() === totalCount()`. Drives the
    completion banner and the submit-button omission.
- **`brain-audit-panel.component.html`**:
  - The "Human class" cell now branches: `isFilled(item)` renders a `saved: {{ item.humanClass }}`
    badge (`audit-item-human-class-saved`) — no `<select>` at all for that row, so there is no re-fill
    affordance to imply. An unfilled item is unchanged (the existing `<select>` with the blank "(skip)"
    default).
  - `allFilled()` renders an `audit-queue-complete` banner above the table stating the sample is
    complete and awaiting the next full structurer run to ingest it into `derived/audit.jsonl` — plain
    language, not a silently-unchanged queue view.
  - The submit button is **omitted entirely** (not merely `disabled`) once `allFilled()` — with every
    row's select gone, there is nothing left to select, and dispatching a second identical fill run is
    no longer the visible default at all, let alone the inviting one.
- **Tests**:
  - `BrainAuditPanelComponent`: filled row renders the saved badge and no select; an unfilled row is
    unchanged; the completion banner + button-omission fire exactly at `filledCount === totalCount > 0`;
    a partial fill (`filledCount < totalCount`) shows neither the banner nor an omitted button.
  - `BrainAuditScreenComponent`: one new end-to-end case built from the real live response's exact
    9 items (ids, session id, `humanClass` values verbatim from the `curl` capture below) — asserts all
    9 rows render saved badges, zero `<select>` elements, the completion banner naming
    `derived/audit.jsonl`, and no submit button, through the real HTTP-mock round trip.
  - Full suite (`npx vitest run`): 165 files, 1375 tests, all green — no regressions in the untouched
    partial-fill and submit-flow tests from the prior two sessions.
  - `npx ng build`: clean, 718.30 kB main bundle (+1.43 kB over the prior session's 716.87 kB), the
    same pre-existing bundle-budget WARNING, no new warning introduced.

## Acceptance criteria — how each is met

1. **A filled item (`humanClass` non-empty) renders visibly distinct from an unfilled one, saved
   verdict shown, no re-fill affordance implied** — the `audit-item-human-class-saved` badge replaces
   the `<select>` outright for that row; dedicated test (`a filled item renders its saved human_class
   verdict, not a re-fill select`) asserts both the badge text and the select's absence.
2. **`filledCount === totalCount` states plainly that the sample is complete and awaiting the next full
   structurer run to ingest into `derived/audit.jsonl`** — the `audit-queue-complete` banner, tested
   both at the panel level and end-to-end against the real live 9/9 response.
3. **The fill/dispatch affordance is disabled or repurposed once all items are filled** — repurposed:
   the submit button is not rendered at all once `allFilled()` (there is nothing to submit — every row
   already lost its select), so dispatching a second identical fill run is never the visible default,
   let alone the inviting one.
4. **Live-verified against agent-runner's real queue in its current 9/9-filled state** — `curl
   :8089/brain/agent-runner/pending-audit` (agent-runner live this session) confirmed
   `filledCount: 9, totalCount: 9`, all 9 items non-empty `humanClass`. The new screen-level test uses
   those exact 9 items (ids, `lineRef`s, `humanClass` values) verbatim, so the assertion that all 9 rows
   render saved badges + the completion banner + no submit button is checked against the real captured

## Not done / caveats

None. Both the UI-side capability this demand describes and its live-data precondition
(agent-runner's companion enrichment) are already met: agent-runner's own 9/9 queue already carries
non-empty `humanClass` on every item, so the owner sees the shipped-today filled-state UI against real
