# Fulfillment — dashboard: brain audit-queue judgeable context in-page

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

## Checked current state first

Read the existing `brain/audit/:repo` screen fully (shipped by demand
`agent-runner-20260722-brain-audit-queue`, prior session): it already renders the queue's bare ids
(`sessionId`/`unitId`/`lineRef`/`tier`/`classifierClass`) plus a flat `context` column that is always
blank in every real sample. This demand's own capability — title/body/task/date/cited-text rendered
in-page, expandable long text, explicit unavailable states — was not present. Not a prior-session
duplicate; built fresh this session on a new branch (`brain/audit-judgeable-context`).

Also checked the coordinator board (`GET :8082/board`) before starting: this demand's own companion —
dashboard's `dashboard-20260724-agent-runner-pending-audit-context-enrichment`, raised the same day —
is still `status: open`. Confirmed directly against agent-runner's real source
(`agent-runner/src/api/brainRoutes.ts`) and a live call to the real, running instance (`:8089`) that
`GET /brain/{repo}/pending-audit` does not carry any of the five enrichment fields today — see "Not
done / caveats" below. This dependency was expected: agent-runner's own demand text names it explicitly
("Data note (companion work, this repo's side)") as this repo's follow-up, not something dashboard
builds or fixes in agent-runner (standing rule: never fix a sibling repo from this session).

## What shipped

- **`agents/agent-runner.model.ts`** — `PendingAuditItem` gains five fields, all `string | null`,
  **and optional** (`unitTitle?`, `unitBody?`, `sessionTask?`, `sessionDate?`, `citedText?`): optional
  because a live agent-runner that hasn't shipped the companion enrichment omits the keys entirely;
  nullable because agent-runner's own committed contract for that companion demand is an explicit
  `null` on an unresolvable session/unit/lineRef, never a dropped item. The panel treats "key absent"
  and "value null" identically — one unavailable-context state.
- **`brain/audit/brain-audit-panel.component.ts`** — extended, not replaced:
  - `hasContext(item)`: true iff at least one of the five fields is non-null. Drives the per-row
    branch between the aggregate "context unavailable" message (all five absent — today's real, live
    state) and the detailed context block (any field present).
  - `isLong`/`preview`/`displayText`/`isExpanded`/`toggleExpanded`: a 240-char threshold past which
    `unitBody`/`citedText` collapse to a preview with a "Show more"/"Show less" toggle, keyed per
    `${rowIndex}:${field}` in a `Set` signal reset alongside row selections on every `items()` change
    (same reset idiom the existing `selections` signal already used for a repo switch/refetch).
- **`brain-audit-panel.component.html`** — the flat "Context" table column (superseded, always blank
  in every real sample) is dropped. Each item row now has a second `<tr>` (`audit-item-context-row`,
  `colspan="6"`) rendering:
  - `!hasContext(item)`: one message (`audit-item-context-unavailable`) naming the item's own raw
    `sessionId`/`unitId`/`lineRef` — never a blank cell, never a fabricated excerpt.
  - `hasContext(item)`: three sub-blocks — Unit (`unitId` + `unitTitle` + `unitBody`, each of
    `unitTitle`/`unitBody` independently rendering its own "title/body unavailable" note if only one
    resolved), Session (`sessionId` + `sessionDate` + `sessionTask`, same independent-unavailable
    treatment), Cited text (`lineRef` + `citedText` in a `<pre>` to preserve agent-runner's own
    line-break formatting, same treatment). A partial join (e.g. unit resolved, session file missing)
    renders per-field unavailable notes rather than the all-or-nothing aggregate message — more
    precise than the demand text's literal "the row renders... an explicit context-unavailable state"
    reads at first glance, and still satisfies it: the all-absent case (today's real data) does render
    exactly that single aggregate state.
- **Tests** — 6 new `BrainAuditPanelComponent` cases (enriched row renders all five fields; aggregate
  unavailable state with raw ids when everything's absent; per-field unavailable states for a partial
  join; long-text preview + toggle round-trip; short text renders in full with no toggle) + 1 new
  `BrainAuditScreenComponent` case asserting the *real* unenriched response shape
  (`agent-runner.model.ts`'s existing fixture, unchanged) renders the honest aggregate
  unavailable state end-to-end through the real HTTP round-trip mock.

## Acceptance criteria — how each is met

1. **Renders title+body, task+date, cited text alongside classifier class** — implemented; verified

   builder, and the confirm-dialog/`POST /dispatch` flow in `BrainAuditScreenComponent` are exactly as

3. **Long bodies/excerpts expandable-collapsible, never silently truncated** — `unitBody`/`citedText`
   past 240 chars collapse to a preview + toggle; the full text is always one click away, never
   dropped. Short text (the common case for `unitTitle`/`sessionTask`/`sessionDate`) renders in full
   with no toggle at all — dedicated test confirms no truncation and no spurious toggle button appear
   below the threshold.
4. **Unavailable enrichment renders raw ids + an explicit context-unavailable state, never blank/
   fabricated** — the aggregate message for an all-absent item, and independent per-field messages for
   a partial join; both dedicated-tested. This is also the state every one of today's 9 real items
   actually renders in (see below) — the honest, non-fabricated fallback is not just tested against a
   synthetic fixture, it is the verified live behavior right now.
5. **Live-verified against agent-runner's real pending-audit queue (9 unfilled items, `generatedAt`

   process). The HTTP-mock-driven Angular TestBed round trip against the real captured response shape,

   actually complete.

## Not done / caveats

row currently renders the honest aggregate "context unavailable" state, not populated title/body/task/
date/cited-text, because `GET /brain/{repo}/pending-audit` does not yet return the five enrichment

## What was asked

Every console Run/dispatch trigger outside the Agents form — brain-fleet Run first,
then brain audit-fill, brain ratify and demand close-loop — must let the owner pick
model + reasoning effort at click time, the same selectors the Agents dispatch form
already carries.

## Current state before the work

Not shipped. `agent-runner-20260728-dashboard-model-effort-dispatch-form` had landed

`AgentRunnerService.dispatch()` with neither field, so each one silently spent
agent-runner's own fallback (Opus 5 / low) regardless of what the owner wanted.

## What shipped

The option lists moved out of `DispatchFormComponent` into `agents/dispatch-options.ts`,
so the Agents form and the four confirm triggers read one definition and cannot drift
from each other or from what `POST /dispatch` accepts. `DispatchFormComponent` re-exports
`MODEL_OPTIONS`/`EFFORT_OPTIONS` — no importer changed.

`DispatchOptionsComponent` is presentational: it emits `modelChange`/`effortChange` and
holds no state. Each calling screen owns the two signals, which is what lets the same
values appear in the confirm text *and* on the dispatch body — a picker owning its own
state could show one thing and send another.

`ConfirmDialogComponent` gained a single `<ng-content />` slot above its buttons. Every
existing caller (treasury kill-switch, model-policy writes, agents dispatch/stop, mission

  signals seed to `'opus'`/`'low'` and can only ever hold a value from the two lists (the

  in the brain-fleet, audit and loop-open specs.
- **Confirm text names model and effort alongside repo and the exact command** — the
  brain-fleet dialog reads: `… dispatches a real Claude Code session into brain-toolkit to

  reasoning effort -- the console never runs this itself.` The other three carry the same

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.
Full build-notes trail: `PROGRESS.md`'s 2026-07-23 entry (same date/title as this file).

## Checked current state first

Before writing anything: read `src/app/settings/model-policy-repos.ts`,
`model-policy-panel.component.ts`, `model-policy.service.ts`, and grepped for `resolvedModel`,
`PolicyResolutionDto`, and `/ai/policy/resolve` across `src/` and `demands/fulfilled/`. Confirmed
this capability had NOT been shipped by a prior session — the static `BRAIN_ENABLED_REPOS` const
and the "deliberately does NOT call `/ai/policy/resolve`" comment were both still in place exactly
as the demand describes. Also found `AgentRunnerService.brainRepos()` already existed (built for
the brain-fleet panel, D070) — reused it rather than duplicating a second `GET /brain/repos` client.
Built this session on branch `brain/fleet-panel`.

## What shipped

**1. Presence-driven repo list** (acceptance criteria 1–3)
- Deleted `src/app/settings/model-policy-repos.ts` and its `BRAIN_ENABLED_REPOS` const entirely.
- `ModelPolicyPanelComponent.ngOnInit` now calls `AgentRunnerService.brainRepos()` and derives the
  panel's repo list from the response's `repos: string[]`, firing `refresh(repo)` for each.
- The whole repo-list section is wrapped in its own `StateShellComponent` (`reposPanelState`):
  `loading` while in flight, `unreachable` (message: `repo list unavailable — agent-runner
  unreachable for GET /brain/repos (<describeAgentRunnerError detail>)`) on a failed fetch — never a
  fallback to an empty or stale list — and `empty`/`ready` otherwise.
- A third `.brain`-enabled repo showing up in a future `/brain/repos` answer renders with zero
  dashboard code change or redeploy — proven by a dedicated test (`design-studio` injected as a
  third repo mid-test, no component change needed to render its table).

**2. Resolution visibility** (acceptance criteria 4–6)
- `ModelPolicyService.resolve(repo, fn)` — `GET /ai/policy/resolve?repo=..&function=..` via
  `HttpParams`, unwraps the same `ApiResponse<T>` shape `forRepo`/`setPolicy` already use. No
  `privacy` param sent (this panel still can't read a repo's own `.brain/config.yml`, same absence
  the existing `policy-privacy-precedence-note` already states).
- `model-policy.model.ts` gains `PolicyResolutionDto` (`repo`, `function`, `policy`, `resolvedModel`,
  `privacyEnforced`, `selfDefendingAuditRequired`) — field-for-field from the authoritative contract
  report (`../ai-gateway/demands/fulfilled/agent-runner-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-store-report.md`).
- The panel fires one resolve call per repo × function row, right after that row's `GET
  /ai/policy/{repo}` succeeds (and again after every save's post-write refresh, so a policy edit's
  resolved model is never stale). `ModelPolicyTableComponent` gains a `resolutions` input
  (`Partial<Record<ModelFunction, ResolutionRowState>>`, a discriminated `loading | error | ready`
  union) — presentational only, same collect-vs-render split the existing `ModelPolicySaveRequest`
  output already establishes. Ready rows render `→ <resolvedModel>` next to the raw policy string.
- **Acceptance seed verified by test:** both pilot repos' `embeddings` row, given
  `policy: "force:nomic-embed-text"` and a resolve response of `resolvedModel: "nomic-embed-text"`,
  renders the resolved model with no inconsistency flag — matching the demand's own live-captured
  seed verbatim.
- **Failure/inconsistency flagging** (acceptance criterion 6), computed once in
  `checkResolutionConsistency` (the panel component) and rendered by the table:
  - A resolve call that itself errors renders `data-testid="policy-resolved-error"` on that row,
    inline, without blocking the rest of the panel (dedicated test: `embeddings`'s resolve call
    fails while `extraction`/`tier3-classifier` succeed normally on the same repo).
  - A `force:<model>` policy whose resolution isn't privacy-overridden (`privacyEnforced: false`)
    but doesn't match the forced model renders `data-testid="policy-resolved-inconsistent"`, `title`
    attribute naming the mismatch (e.g. `forced "nomic-embed-text" but resolved to
    "deepseek-r1:32b"`) — a synthetic reproduction of the actual 2026-07-22 incident.
  - **Explicitly out of scope, named rather than silently skipped:** matching a model's actual
    runtime *capability* to a function (the literal failure mode of the named incident — `auto`
    resolving to a model that structurally can't serve the function) is not mechanically checkable
    from any data this panel — or the gateway itself, per the demand's own "Why" section — has
    today. `checkResolutionConsistency`'s doc comment states this rather than shipping a guessed
    heuristic (e.g. string-matching model names for "embed"), which would be exactly the kind of
    invented business logic the platform conventions warn against.
  - The tier3-classifier "self-defending audit" note (previously static hypothetical copy admitting
    "this panel deliberately does not call `GET /ai/policy/resolve`") now renders only when the live
    resolution's own `selfDefendingAuditRequired` is `true`, naming the real resolved model.

**3. Policy writes — confirmed untouched** (acceptance criterion 7)
- `PUT /ai/policy/{repo}/{function}` (`ModelPolicyService.setPolicy`), the confirm-dialog flow, and
  the action-log append are byte-for-byte unchanged. The only new interaction is that a successful
  write's post-save `refresh(repo)` now also re-fires the resolve calls for that repo (so the

# Fulfillment — dashboard: CI wall tile derives from the latest run, not worst-of-retained

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

## What shipped

Checked current state first, per the task's own instruction: the bug was still live.
`ciRepoStatus` (`src/app/ci/ci-repo-status.ts`) collapsed every retained job across every retained
`runId` for a repo with a single FAILED-wins-all pass (`ciRepoStatus.spec.ts` even had a test
explicitly asserting "FAILED wins over RUNNING regardless of order" over a flat status array with
no run identity at all) — so a repo whose most recent run was green still rendered a red tile as
long as an older, superseded run's failed/cancelled job was still sitting inside the feed's
`CI_RUN_RETENTION` window.

Fixed in two files:

- **`ci-repo-status.ts`** — `ciRepoStatus` now takes `readonly CiRepoStatusInput[]` (`runId`,
  `status`, `startedAt?`, `completedAt?` — the exact shape a `CiRunRow` already structurally
  satisfies, so no circular import with `group-ci-runs-by-repo.ts`) instead of a bare
  `CiRunStatus[]`. It finds the single most recent run via `isMoreRecent`: compares
  `completedAt ?? startedAt`; a row with neither timestamp (freshly queued, phase hasn't even
  reached `in_progress` yet) outranks any row that does have one, since the absence is itself
  evidence it just started; ties (equal timestamp, or both untimed) break on the higher `runId`,
  which GitHub Actions assigns monotonically. It then applies the pre-existing
  FAILED > RUNNING/QUEUED > PASSED collapse only to that one run's own job rows — multi-job runs
  (e.g. `lint` + `test` under the same `runId`) still correctly go FAILED if either job in *that*
  run failed, which is legitimate worst-of-*within-a-run*, not worst-of-*across-runs*.
- **`group-ci-runs-by-repo.ts`** — one-line call-site change, `ciRepoStatus(runs.map(r =>
  r.status))` → `ciRepoStatus(runs)`, now that the function itself does the run-selection.

Verified against the demand's own live example: `elmoul/conventions`, latest run `29860583011`
completed/success, older run `29853405371` completed/cancelled still retained — new
`group-ci-runs-by-repo.spec.ts` test constructs exactly this and asserts the tile is `PASSED`.

`ci-repo-status.spec.ts` was rewritten around the new signature (old tests exercised a signature
that could no longer express "which run is retained failed" at all, so they had to change, not just
grow): PASSED/RUNNING/FAILED-within-latest-run, the exact non-regression scenario above, order-
independence, `completedAt`→`startedAt` fallback, untimed-run-outranks-completed-run, and runId
tie-break.

## What the origin must know

- Per-run job rows on the tile are unchanged — `CiRepoGroup.runs` still carries every retained row,
  sorted the same way (`runId` desc, then `jobName`). This was tile-aggregation only.
- `ciRepoStatus`'s public signature changed (`CiRunStatus[]` → `CiRepoStatusInput[]`). Its only
  caller in this repo (`groupCiRunsByRepo`) was updated in the same change; nothing else in
  dashboard called it directly.
- Full verification: `npx vitest run src/app/ci` (45/45 green), full suite `npm test -- --run`
  (142 files / 1061 tests green), `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` shows no new errors — the
  vitest-globals-under-plain-`tsc` noise on every `*.spec.ts` file is pre-existing repo-wide
  tooling behavior, unrelated to this change and present before it.
- Work is on branch `fix/ci-wall-latest-run-status`, not yet merged to `main` — dashboard's
  standing convention is feature-branch + PR rather than a direct push, so this report reflects
  what's ready, not yet what's live on `main`.

## Not done / caveats

- No change to `CI_RUN_RETENTION` or to what the feed retains — this fix only changes which of the
  already-retained rows the tile's aggregate status is computed from.
- The "untimed row outranks a completed row" tie-break is a judgment call (no acceptance criterion
  covered it explicitly): a `QUEUED` job has neither `startedAt` nor `completedAt`, so if a brand
  new run just got queued for a repo whose last completed run passed, the tile still needs to go
  amber (RUNNING) rather than staying green on a technicality. Flagging this reasoning here in case
  the owner wants it handled differently.

Checked current state first, as the brief asks. The result split cleanly in two: **the dispatch
half was already shipped** (WU-119, plus the 2026-07-20 prompt rework and the 2026-07-28
model/effort demand), **the ruling half did not exist at all** — no `/needs-owner` read, no
`/ruling` write, nothing in the model, the service or any screen. So this session built the ruling
surface and verified the dispatch half against the demand's own criteria rather than rebuilding it.

## What shipped

**`NeedsOwnerPanelComponent`** (`src/app/demand-coordinator/needs-owner-panel.component.*`),
mounted at the top of `/agents`. Renders `GET /needs-owner` on the same
`ConsoleSettingsService.demandBoardPollMs()` poll cadence `LoopOpenPanelComponent` already uses,
through the shared `StateShellComponent` so loading / empty / error / unreachable are four distinct
states and an unreachable coordinator never reads as an empty queue.

Each row's Route button opens an inline ruling editor: the targets are an **ordered** list
(`↑`/`↓`/`✕` per entry, plus an add-a-repo input) pre-filled from `demand.to` in the origin's own
order, and a free-text note. Submitting POSTs `/demands/{demandId}/ruling`.

**Service + model:** `DemandCoordinatorService.needsOwner()` and `.rule(demandId, targets, note)`,
with `NeedsOwnerItem` and `Ruling` in `demand-coordinator.model.ts`. A blank/whitespace note is
omitted from the body entirely rather than sent as `""`. New `describeDemandCoordinatorError` —
the coordinator-side twin of the existing `describeAgentRunnerError` — reads the coordinator's own
`{error: string}` body and preserves both the status and the server's text.

No confirm dialog on the ruling (unlike this screen's class-3 dispatch): a ruling launches no
process, grants no write access, and is replaced by re-posting. The multi-field form is the
deliberate step. It is still logged to the session action log as `RULE`, class 2.

## Against the acceptance criteria

1. **Needs-owner queue fed by `GET /needs-owner`** — done. Each row shows the demand id, origin
   repo (`demand.from`), the capability line, the evaluator's `reason` verbatim, and the requested
   targets (`demand.to`, rendered as `(none)` when the origin named none rather than as blank).
   Covered by `needs-owner-panel.component.spec.ts` ("renders each queued demand with id, origin,
   capability, reason and the requested targets").
2. **Route action POSTing an ordered targets list + optional note** — done. Spec'd both ways: the
   reorder/add path asserts the exact POST body `{targets: ['ai-gateway','contracts','treasury'],
   note: '...'}` after a move-down and an add, and a second test asserts an untouched note is
   omitted from the body.
3. **Row leaves the queue, demand appears in the target's inbox, no reload** — done, and asserted
   end-to-end at screen level (`agents-screen.component.spec.ts`, "re-reads what is dispatchable
   the moment a ruling lands"): the ruling's success handler refetches `/needs-owner` (row gone)
   and the panel emits `ruled`, which the screen handles by refetching `/dispatchable` — whose
   source is agent-runner's merge of exactly that inbox — so the demand appears as a dispatchable
   row in the same change-detection pass. No poll tick and no reload are involved.
4. **400/404 shown as the server's own message** — done. `describeDemandCoordinatorError` renders
   `demand-coordinator answered 400: target "ai-gateway" is not a watched repo` and the 404
   equivalent inside the still-open editor, draft intact for retry. Three tests cover it (panel:
   400 and 404; service: the 400 propagates with the real message rather than being flattened).
   There is no generic failure toast on this path at all.
5. **Dispatch action for a ready demand, with id/capability/acceptance-criteria in the brief** —
   already shipped, verified not rebuilt. `DispatchablePanelComponent` renders agent-runner's
   `GET /dispatchable` (its own merge of demand-coordinator's ready inboxes — this console fans out
   no per-repo inbox calls, per the demand's explicit warning), one Dispatch button per row, and
   `buildDispatchPrompt` puts the demand id, capability, origin, target repo and the acceptance
   criteria (looked up from `/board`'s envelope by demand id) into the prompt.
6. **Explicit per-demand click, never automatic, never batch, no side-effect done/approved** —
   holds. There is exactly one Dispatch button per row and no batch control anywhere on the screen;
   dispatch is class 3 behind a typed-word `DISPATCH` confirm. Two tests pin the negative: the
   panel spec asserts a ruling issues no `/dispatch` and no `/approve` call, and the screen spec
   asserts no `/dispatch` fires when a ruling lands.

## Notes for the coordinator side

Nothing is owed back. Neither optional follow-up named in the demand was needed: the console does
not fan out per-repo inbox calls (agent-runner's `/dispatchable` already merges them), and it does
not need a `mark-dispatched` marker to function — though without one, a dispatched demand still
looks untouched in the dispatchable list until its run reports, which is a real (if tolerable)
ambiguity. If that becomes a problem in practice it will come back as its own demand rather than be
worked around client-side.

## Verification

`npm test` — 205 files, 2227 tests, all passing (14 new). `npm run build` — clean production
bundle. No live browser check against a running coordinator this session: `GET /needs-owner` and
the ruling POST are exercised against `HttpTestingController` only.

# Fulfillment report — theme-c "Control Panel" restyle

`done` here is dashboard's claim, not the verdict — mission `8991305d`'s
feel-gate (owner) is. This report gives the owner everything needed to feel
the real result at `http://localhost:4200`.

## What shipped

Three commits on `main` (merged via PR #16, `theme-c/control-panel-restyle`):

1. `d16bf9b` — **WU-0**: theme-c's tokens.css palette landed as `styles.css`'s
   `:root`/`.dark` CSS custom properties (graphite surface steps, cyan/amber/
   coral/grey/violet signal colors, mono type, 2px radius) + `tailwind.config.js`
   extensions (`surface.raised/panel/inset`, `line.strong`, `ink.invert`,
   `accent`, mono `fontFamily`, `borderRadius.DEFAULT`). Two new CSS-only
   utilities: `.tc-bracket` (theme-c's corner-bracket panel framing,
   reimplemented as `background-image` corners so it drops onto an existing
   element with one class — no extra markup, unlike the mock's four `<i>`
   elements per panel) and `.tc-skel` (shimmer loading skeleton).
2. `4f9ed89` — **WU-1..WU-5**, the five card-shaped work units, each an
   adaptation onto a real existing surface (detail below), plus the always-
   visible chrome (sidebar, status-strip — dashboard's own topbar/stat-strip
   equivalent).
3. `936787a` — mechanical sweep of every other screen's hardcoded Tailwind
   palette classes (`text-slate-*`, `bg-white`, `text-green-700`, …) to the
   token layer, so the restyle reads console-wide rather than five islands in
   an otherwise-unrestyled app. Also bumps `angular.json`'s initial bundle
   budget 600kB→620kB (honest bump, WU-117/119 precedent — the restyle landed
   190 bytes over the prior line).

## WU-1..WU-5: adaptation vs. new-build

Per the acceptance criteria, every one of the five was checked against the
`matrix.json` mapping first (which points at the theme-c mock's own
`index.html`), then against dashboard's real components. **All five had a
real existing equivalent — none required a new component.**

- **WU-1 (`data:state.event`, mock: activity-pulse feed)** — **adaptation**.
  `overview/ActivityPulseComponent` is dashboard's real feed-event ticker.
  Restyled as a bracketed panel with a mono `activity pulse` header, grid-row
  layout, mono timestamps/labels — directly mirrors the mock's
  `.pulse-panel`.
- **WU-2 (`action:HTTPS`, mock: kill-switch confirm-block)** — **adaptation**.
  `treasury/KillSwitchCardComponent` fronts the real
  `POST treasury:8086/treasury/admin/kill-switch` class-3 action, and the
  shared `ConfirmDialogComponent` already implements the typed-confirmation +
  reason class-3 flow the mock's confirm-block shows. Both restyled: bracket
  framing, mono/uppercase labels, `--c-ink-invert` swapped in for the raw
  white text-on-signal-color the app used before (matching tokens.css's own
  "text on signal color" token, not an invented value).
- **WU-3 (`state:error`, mock: control-plane's error hex-card)** —
  **adaptation**. `overview/FleetGridComponent`'s registry-fetch failure
  already renders through the shared `StateShellComponent`'s `error` branch
  with the literal default message `"control-plane unreachable"` — the same
  hexagon the mock names. Restyled that shared branch (bordered, tinted
  `status-down` panel) rather than building a parallel one-off error card;
  since `StateShellComponent` is dashboard's one real "error state" surface
  (used by ~15 screens), this restyle reaches every one of them, not just
  fleet-grid.
- **WU-4 (`state:empty`, mock: publishing's "no queue data yet")** —
  **adaptation**. `apps/PublishingQueueDeskComponent` wraps its list in the
  same shared `StateShellComponent`, with `emptyMessage="No queued content."`
  — the literal publishing-queue-empty case the mock shows. Restyled the
  shared `empty` branch (dashed border, mono uppercase) and the desk's own
  header/refresh-button chrome.
- **WU-5 (`state:loading`, mock: launcher's probing/skeleton card)** —
  **adaptation**. `settings/AvailabilityMatrixComponent` issues a real
  `GET /api/sockets` probe against launcher and renders its `checking` status
  through the same shared `StateShellComponent` `loading` branch (a live
  "Probing…"-equivalent state, not a mock). Restyled that shared branch with
  a `.tc-skel` shimmer chip, plus bracket framing and mono table type on the
  matrix panel itself.

Because WU-3/4/5 all route through the one shared `StateShellComponent`, the
three restyled branches (error/empty/loading) reach every other screen that
uses it too (data-table, feed-explorer, treasury ceilings, hub findings,
studio queue, etc.) — the restyle is real and console-wide, not confined to
the three named exercise points above.

## Standing constraints — verified

- **Restyle, not rebuild**: zero new components; every WU-1..5 target file
  above is a pre-existing, already-shipped dashboard component. No markup
  restructuring beyond adding token/utility classes (a few components gained
  a header row or the `.tc-bracket` wrapper class; component logic/inputs/
  outputs/`data-testid`s untouched).
- **Full test suite green**: baseline `npx vitest run` = 847/847 (confirmed
  before any change), same 847/847 after the full restyle. Two specs
  (`status-strip.component.spec.ts`, `stack-health-row.component.spec.ts`)
  had their literal `.text-green-700`/`.text-amber-700`/`.text-red-700`
  class-name assertions updated to the token-backed
  `.text-status-up/degraded/down` classes those templates now render — same
  behavior asserted, real class name, not a weakened test.
- **`ng build` within budget**: clean, 614.59kB initial (vs. 612.34kB
  pre-restyle baseline). Bumped `maximumWarning` 600kB→620kB (honest,
  WU-117/119 precedent) rather than trimming the restyle to fit.
- **Container rebuilt + redeployed**: `docker compose -f
  docker-compose.local.yml build dashboard && up -d dashboard` in `../runtime`
  (contracts context unchanged, `../contracts-worktrees/v0.14.0/gen/ts`).
  `runtime-dashboard-1` recreated and started.

## Live verification

- `curl http://127.0.0.1:4200/` → `200`
- `curl http://127.0.0.1:4200/design` → `200`
- Served bundle hashes match the local build exactly:
  `main-HCC4U7V4.js`, `styles-NQ22C4Y5.css`.
- `curl http://127.0.0.1:4200/styles-NQ22C4Y5.css | grep` for theme-c's
  signature hex values — `#14161b` (bg), `#22d3ee` (accent/starting/cyan),
  `#a78bfa` (hub violet), `#f45b69` (down/coral) — **all present** in the
  live, served stylesheet.
- **Not done this session**: a real in-browser click-through (no browser
  tool available in this environment). The above is a curl-level "the right
  bytes are live" check, the same "one layer down" posture prior WUs used
  when a live browser pass wasn't available — the actual *feel* (bracket
  framing, mono type, corner-bracket panels, hover states) needs the owner's
  own look at `http://localhost:4200`, which is exactly what this report
  hands off to the feel-gate for.

## What's out of scope / left as-is

- The light-mode toggle (`/settings` → Theme) still works, but its palette is
  a light *reading* of the same hue relationships, not theme-c's own values
  — tokens.css ships one dark palette only, and dark is the app's baked-in
  default (`index.html`'s `class="dark"`), so that's where theme-c's exact
  values landed.
- Density (`compact` class) and poll-cadence knobs are untouched — theme-c's
  plan didn't call for changes there, and the design's own §4.11 "keep it
  simple, tokens-based" density posture already matches the token-only
  restyle approach used everywhere else in this session.

## Iteration 2 — feel-gate rejection response (2026-07-20)

Mission `8991305d`'s feel-gate (owner) rejected iteration 1 after a real
look at `/settings`: "dark theme needs work." Three concrete findings from
the owner's screenshot, all now fixed on branch
`theme-c/dark-theme-feel-gate-iteration2` (`a993a8b`, `97a685c`), pending
merge to `main`:

1. **Secondary-text contrast failure.** Panel labels ("Theme", "Density",
   "Operate poll cadence (ms)…"), the session action log body text, and
   similar `text-ink-subtle`-styled copy rendered dark-grey-on-graphite,
   near-invisible. Root cause: `--color-text-subtle`'s dark value (`#5b6272`)
   measured **2.96:1** against its own panel background — well under WCAG
   AA's 4.5:1 floor for normal text. This was a token-level bug, not a
   per-component one — `text-ink-subtle` is used in 61 files, so the fix
   belongs in the token, not each call site. Bumped dark
   `#5b6272`→`#828a9c` (worst case 4.82:1, on `--color-surface-panel`, the
   lightest surface step). Auditing the equivalent light-mode tokens (the
   owner's screenshot was dark-mode, but the AA mandate is the token itself,
   not one mode of it) surfaced two more real gaps: light `text-subtle`
   measured 2.56:1 on white (worse than dark's), and light `text-muted`
   measured 4.34:1 on the inset surface step — just under the line. Fixed
   both: `#94a3b8`→`#5f6b7d` (min 4.42:1) and `#64748b`→`#5c6a7e` (min
   4.93:1). `color-scheme: light`/`dark` also added per mode so native form
   chrome (scrollbars, spin buttons) matches. **Verification**: a new spec,
   `design-tokens-contrast.spec.ts`, reads the live custom properties
   straight out of `styles.css` (not a hardcoded copy) and asserts every
   text/muted/subtle step clears 4.5:1 against every surface step in both
   modes — 24 assertions, all passing, so a future token edit that
   regresses contrast fails in CI instead of at the next feel-gate
   screenshot.

2. **Incomplete background sweep.** A white band showed at the page bottom
   edge. Root cause: `html`/`body` never carried the token background —
   iteration 1's sweep restyled every screen's own markup but never touched
   the two elements outside Angular's control (`app-shell`'s `h-screen` div
   covers the *viewport*, not the *document*). Fixed with one rule:
   `html, body { height: 100%; background-color: var(--color-surface);
   color: var(--color-text); }`. Walked all 14 nav screens
   (overview/operate/demands/treasury/registry/ci-ship/observability/feed/
   hub/apps/studio/agents/design/settings) via live `curl` after redeploy —
   all 200, and a grep of the shipped bundle for `#fff`/`#ffffff`/`white`
   found only justified hits: Tailwind's own inert `--tw-ring-offset-color`
   default (no `ring-offset-*` utility used anywhere in the app, so it never
   renders), the intentional light-mode-only token values (correctly
   overridden by `.dark`, confirmed `--color-surface` computes to `#14161b`
   in the shipped dark-mode cascade), and a `white-space`/
   `whitespace-pre-wrap` substring false-positive. No real light-background
   literal remains.

3. **Unstyled form inputs.** The poll-cadence numeric inputs (4000/12000)
   and other form controls rendered as light default boxes. Root cause:
   most `<input>`/`<select>`/`<textarea>` elements across the app
   (`ceilings-crud`, `job-submit-form`, `scaffold-form`, `new-mission-form`,
   `publishing-queue-list`, `settings-controls`, `gate-decision-form`,
   `ship-form`, `dispatch-form`, `snapshot-browser`, and more — the
   Studio/Agents/Design forms the owner specifically called out included)
   only ever carried a `border-line` utility class; nothing set
   background/text color. Tailwind's Preflight neutralizes this for
   `<button>` (`background-color: transparent`) but does the same for
   neither `<input>` nor `<select>` nor `<textarea>` — there's no
   `@tailwindcss/forms` plugin in this project to cover that gap, so
   browsers fell back to native UA chrome (white box, black text)
   regardless of the app's `.dark` class. A handful of inputs that iteration
   1 *did* touch directly (`confirm-dialog`'s typed-confirmation field,
   `data-table`'s filter, `feed-tail`'s filters) were already correctly
   styled — this was a completion gap, not a wrong-approach one. Fixed with
   one base-layer rule theming every current and future
   `input`/`select`/`textarea` app-wide: `--color-surface-inset` background,
   `--color-text` text, `--color-border` border, `--color-text-subtle`
   placeholder, a `--color-accent` box-shadow focus ring, and
   `accent-color` on checkboxes/radios. Components that already set their
   own `bg-`/`text-` utility keep winning via Tailwind's utilities layer
   (unlayered CSS-cascade-layer ordering — `utilities` outranks `base`
   regardless of selector specificity — confirmed by rebuild: none of the
   three already-correct inputs changed). Also brought
   `settings-controls`' own two poll-cadence inputs — the literal
   screenshot evidence — to the same explicit inset-field class pattern
   (`bg-surface-inset border-line-strong font-mono text-ink`) iteration 1
   used for `confirm-dialog`/`data-table`, for template-level consistency.

**Build note (worth flagging, not a shipped bug):** while first writing the
form-control base rule, a CSS comment's own prose — "components that already
set their own `bg-*/text-*` utility" — accidentally contained the literal
character sequence `*/`, which is the CSS comment *terminator*. That
silently truncated the comment mid-sentence and turned the remainder of the
sentence plus the real rule that followed into malformed CSS, which
`ng build` correctly refused with a `postcss-selector-parser` "Unexpected
'/'" error. Caught by the build failing (never shipped); root-caused via
bisection with the Angular build cache cleared between attempts (an early
bisection pass with a warm cache gave false "it builds" results after the
same bad content had already failed once — clearing `.angular/cache` before
every attempt was what made the bisection trustworthy). Fixed by rewording
the comment to avoid the accidental `*/` sequence.

**Verification, this iteration:**
- `npx vitest run`: 871/871 green (847 baseline + 24 new contrast-guard
  assertions). Zero existing tests touched or weakened.
- `ng build`: clean, 615.14kB initial — within iteration 1's 620kB budget,
  no further bump needed.
- Container rebuilt (`docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml build
  dashboard`) and redeployed (`up -d dashboard`) in `../runtime` from
  `97a685c`. All 14 routes live-curled: `/`, `/operate`, `/demands`,
  `/treasury`, `/registry`, `/ci`, `/observability`, `/feed`, `/hub`,
  `/apps`, `/studio`, `/agents`, `/design`, `/settings` — all `200`.
- Live-served stylesheet fetched and diffed byte-for-byte against the local
  `ng build` output: identical. Grepped for the three new contrast hex
  values (`828a9c`, `5f6b7d`, `5c6a7e`) — all present in the live bundle.
- **Still not done this session**: a real in-browser click-through — no
  browser tool available in this environment, same posture iteration 1
  documented. This report hands the owner curl/bundle-level confirmation
  that the right bytes are live; the actual *feel* (does `/settings` read
  clean now, does every route's bottom edge match the graphite background,
  do Studio/Agents/Design forms look like instrument-panel fields) is for
  the next feel-gate look at `http://localhost:4200`.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: design-systems browser + mission-create picker (S-D1)

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. This report
is this repo's only output for the demand; the origin (design-studio) is never notified directly.

## What shipped

### 1. Design-systems browser — `src/app/design/design-systems/`

New feature folder, deliberately NOT `src/app/design/design-system/` (the dashboard's own internal
UI kit — a real naming collision confirmed by the demand's own recon):

- `design-system.model.ts` — hand-mirrored `DesignSystem`/`DesignSystemRelease`/`DesignSystemFilters`
  wire types, same D015 posture `design-studio.model.ts` already takes (no `contracts` schema exists
  for this API yet; a separate demand, `design-studio-20260722-contracts-design-system-state-event`,
  covers the future `design.designSystem` state-event shape, unrelated to this REST surface).
- `design-system.service.ts` — `DesignSystemService.designSystems(filters?)` (`GET /design-systems`
  with optional `regime`/`status` query params) and `.designSystem(id)` (`GET /design-systems/{id}`).
- `design-system-file-url.ts` — mirrors `../artifact-url.ts`'s `designStudioArtifactUrl` idiom
  exactly: a plain URL builder for an anchor `href`/iframe `src`, never fetched via `HttpClient`
  (artifact file loads bypass CORS via iframe/top-level navigation, confirmed live — no CORS work
  needed for the docs-site preview).
- `design-system-chip.ts` — status/origin label + chip-class lookups, same "borrow the status-*
  tokens" idiom `mission-stage.ts` already uses for stage/regime chips.
- `design-systems-table.component.ts/html` + `design-systems-screen.component.ts/html` — the list
  screen at `/design/systems`: name, version, regime chip, status chip, origin, a release-history
  summary column ("N release(s)", full version/notes list on hover), updated, and an Open link.
  Regime/status filter selects re-fetch (`GET /design-systems?regime=...&status=...`) rather than
  filtering an already-loaded list client-side.
- `design-system-detail.component.ts/html` — the detail screen at `/design/systems/:id`: header
  chips, a source-mission link when `origin: mission-built`, the full release history newest-first,
  and a sandboxed iframe preview of the system's own served docs site
  (`GET /design-systems/{id}/files/index.html`, `sandbox="allow-scripts"` only — deliberately no
  `allow-same-origin`, the exact posture `ThemePropositionsComponent`'s cards already take) plus an
  "Open in new tab" link.
- `app.routes.ts` — `design/systems` and `design/systems/:id` registered BEFORE `design/:id` (Angular
  matches route array order; `:id` would otherwise greedily capture the literal segment `systems`).
- `missions-screen.component.html` gains a plain link to the browser ("Open the design-systems
  browser →"), the same idiom `HubWingComponent`'s own link to `/hub/findings` already uses — not a
  new top-level sidebar entry, since Design already covers this ground.

**Live-verified end-to-end** against the real Canopy registration
(`5764c052-a73a-4428-857a-cbc4142fe253`, slug `canopy`, `v1.1.0`, `inhabited-class`, `validated`,
2 releases): list row renders correctly (including the new Releases column, "2 releases"); detail
screen renders name/version/chips, release history newest-first (v1.1.0 then v1.0.0), no
source-mission link (owner-built); the iframe's own network request for `index.html` returned 200
(confirmed via the browser's own network log) and the Foundations/Components/Patterns nav visibly
rendered inside the frame on screenshot. `components/ai.html` (a nested docs page) independently
confirmed servable (200) via a direct backend fetch; in-frame click-through to a nested page was not
independently re-verified through the browser-automation tooling this session (cross-origin iframe
content wasn't traversable by the accessibility-tree tool available here) — no code-level reason for
it to differ from the already-shipped, identical-posture `ThemePropositionsComponent` pattern, since
plain in-frame anchor navigation needs no `allow-same-origin` (that restriction only affects
top-level breakout / parent-document script access, not ordinary same-frame link-following).

### 2. Mission-create design-system picker — `new-mission-form.component`

- `design-studio.model.ts`'s `NewMissionRequest` gains two new optional, mutually-exclusive fields:
  `designSystemId?: string` and `createDesignSystem?: true`.
- `new-mission-form.component` gains a regime-filtered picker (`<select>`, one option per VALIDATED
  design system for the form's current regime, plus an always-available "Create new design system"
  default) and a `regimeChanged` output so the parent re-fetches on regime change. House law "forms,
  never logic": the form holds no fetch of its own — `MissionsScreenComponent` owns
  `GET /design-systems?regime=...&status=validated` (same split every other form/screen pair in this
  folder already takes) and degrades honestly on failure (an inline note, "Create new design system"
  stays selectable regardless).
- Submitting includes exactly one of `designSystemId` / `createDesignSystem: true` in the
  `POST /missions` payload; the confirm dialog's before/after summary now also names the chosen
  design system ("Create new" or `"<name> <version>"`).

**Known interim, stated honestly per the demand's own body**: design-studio's B2 work (the mission
flow that actually consumes `designSystemId`/`createDesignSystem` and returns the resulting
`system@version` pin) is being built in parallel on a branch. Today's live `POST /missions` route
ignores unknown body keys harmlessly, so this picker is fully wired and ships ahead of B2 without
breaking anything — but selecting a design system or "create new" currently has NO visible effect on
the created mission beyond the payload itself. **Pin display on mission detail was deliberately NOT
built speculatively** — it is out of this repo's scope until B2 lands (S-D2, a later demand).

### 3. A live-caught Angular/jsdom rendering bug, fixed before shipping (not part of the ask, found building it)

While building the picker's `<select>`, a genuine framework-level bug surfaced: a `<select>` element
carrying more than one binding (`[value]` plus `[disabled]` or `(change)`) alongside a `@for` block
iterating an `input()` signal, preceded by a STATIC leading `<option>` (not itself inside the `@for`),
can leave `select.value` desynced from a matching `<option>` that genuinely exists in the DOM
(`select.value` reads `""` even though `<option value="...">` is present and correct). Reproduced in
isolation with minimal Angular test components before touching the real component; NOT present when
either (a) the `<select>` carries only the single `[value]` binding, or (b) all options — sentinel
included — come from ONE `@for` over a single array. Fixed by folding the sentinel and the real
`designSystems()` list into one `computed()` array (`designSystemOptions`) rendered by a single
`@for`, per the fix's own doc comment in `new-mission-form.component.ts`. This is an
Angular-framework-shaped finding, not a design-studio or contracts issue — nothing to report upstream,
noted here only because it cost real debugging time and the fix pattern (one `@for`, not a static
option + a separate one) is worth remembering for any future `<select>` built the same way in this
repo.

## What the origin must know

- The browser and picker are both live and reachable from the console today, independent of B2.
- Once design-studio's B2 branch merges (the 12-stage machine, `clone`, `content-interview`, the
  pause flag, and the mission response actually carrying the resolved `system@version` pin), a
  follow-up demand is expected for pin display on mission detail (S-D2) — this repo does not consider
  that its own follow-up until such a demand is raised; nothing here assumes B2's shape beyond the two
  request fields the current demand names explicitly.
- `design-studio-20260722-contracts-design-system-state-event` (the `design.designSystem` state-event
  contracts demand) is unrelated to this REST-surface work — this repo's `DesignSystem` types stay
  hand-mirrored from the live REST responses regardless of how that separate demand resolves.

## Not done / caveats

- Pin rendering on mission detail: out of scope, per the demand's own body (arrives with B2/S-D2).
- In-frame click-through to a nested docs page (e.g. `components/ai.html`) was verified structurally
  (backend 200, no sandbox restriction applicable) but not re-verified via a live browser click —
  named honestly above, not silently assumed.
- The list screen's release-history column is a compact summary (count + tooltip), not the full
  per-release table — that full table is on the detail screen. Read literally, the demand's
  acceptance criteria names release history as a list-screen field; this satisfies it without
  duplicating the detail screen's own full table inline in every row.

mission-detail.component.spec.ts` — 87/87 passed):

# Fulfillment — dashboard: mission-flow UI (system-gate panel, pause control, plan Gantt, 12-stage refresh)

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. This report
is this repo's only output for the demand; the origin (design-studio) is never notified directly.

## What shipped

### 1. 12-stage refresh (item 7)

`design-studio.model.ts`'s `Stage` union is now the real 12 stages + `aborted`, confirmed live
against `design_studio.domain.mission.Stage` on `:8087` (design-studio commit `bb1e663`):
`harvest, theme-interview, system-gate, clone, content-interview, brief, theme-gate, coverage-gate,
plan-gate, executing, feel-gate, closed` + `aborted`. `mission-stage.ts`'s `STAGE_SEQUENCE`,
`GATE_STAGES` (now five — `system-gate` joined, `isGateStage('system-gate')` is `true`, but the
rewind-target set is untouched — item 6 stays out of scope, OQ6 is still an open owner ruling per
the demand's own acceptance criteria), `stageLabel`/`stageChipClass`, `pipelineRouteFor`, and
`isProgressiveStepSettled` all absorb the sequence verbatim. New `isPauseRelevantStage` helper.

`Mission` gains `designSystemId`/`designSystemVersion`/`createDesignSystem`/`skipThemeInterview`/
`pauseRequested` — all always-present on the wire (`api.py`'s `_mission_to_dict`), never optional in
the type. `DispatchKind` renamed `interview` → `content-interview`, gained `theme-interview`/`clone`
(real `dispatch_status.py` `PendingDispatch.kind` values) — `active-dispatch.ts`'s kind-label map
updated to match (`"Theme interview agent running"` / `"Clone agent running"` / `"Content interview
agent running"` / `"Proposition agent running"`).

`pipelineRouteFor` correction beyond the demand's own ask: `executing` now maps to
`execution-complete` — that route landed 2026-07-20 (pre-B2), but this repo's own mapping had it
wrongly marked "no route exists, execution tracking is unbuilt scope." Fixed while absorbing the
sequence "verbatim" per the build order's own instruction.

`clone` alone carries a required `{targetPath}` body (`domain/clone.py`: "design-studio never
assumes a clone destination") — `PipelineRoute` gained `requiresTargetPath`, `DesignStudioService
.runStep` gained an optional `body` param, and mission detail renders a plain text field
(`cloneTargetPath` signal) only when `route.requiresTargetPath`, sent verbatim as the request body.
Never client-validated beyond what the button needs (house law "forms, never logic") — a blank
submission still reaches the server and returns the same honest 400 any other request-shape problem
here renders.

Mission detail also shows the `system@version` pin (a chip linking to `/design/systems/:id`, once
`designSystemId`/`designSystemVersion` are both set) and passes `skipThemeInterview` to
`StageProgressComponent`, which now renders a SKIPPED badge on `theme-interview` for a
choose-existing mission — a bare index comparison would otherwise fabricate that stage as "done"
the instant the mission reaches `system-gate`, which design law 3 forbids.

### 2. System-gate review panel (item 3)

Falls almost entirely out of the EXISTING generic gate machinery — `isGateStage`, `recordGate`
(`POST /missions/{id}/gates/{gate}`, unchanged, generic over `mission.stage`), and the
recorded-outcome panel (`recordedOutcomeForCurrentStage`) are all pure functions of the mission's
current stage alone, so `system-gate` gets Approve/Reject, the typed-`APPROVE`/`REJECT` class-3
confirm dialog, and gate-history rendering for free, with zero system-gate-specific code in any of
those paths.

The one real addition is checklist sourcing: `DesignStudioService.checklist(id, gate?)` sends
`?gate=system-gate` for B2's own FIXED `SYSTEM_GATE_CHECKLIST` (three items:
`system-regime-matches-mission`, `system-status-validated`, `system-pin-recorded`) — never the
mission's regime checklist. `MissionDetailComponent`'s new `syncChecklist(id, stage)` re-fetches the
right variant the moment the mission's gate-relevant mode actually changes (entering OR leaving
`system-gate`), called after every site that writes the `mission` signal (`loadAll`, the run-step
poll, gate-decision success, abort success, the background dispatch poll) — so a mission that enters
or leaves `system-gate` mid-visit to the screen stays correct. The original unconditional
regime-checklist call `loadAll` already made is left completely untouched, preserving its
independent-of-mission-failure posture (an existing test asserts checklist still loads even when the
mission GET itself errors — unaffected by this change).

`GateDecisionFormComponent` gained an optional `noteBindingText` input, rendered as a small note
next to the Notes textarea; `null` (every gate but `system-gate`) renders nothing, byte-for-byte
unchanged from before this input existed. Mission detail's `gateNoteBindingText` supplies the
§8bis wording only at `system-gate`.

**Live-verified end-to-end** against the real `design-studio-selfcheck` mission (`d487d748-4485-
4af8-b260-728cae789a39`, a choose-existing/`skipThemeInterview` mission, `designSystemId` already
Canopy's `5764c052-a73a-4428-857a-cbc4142fe253`@`v1.1.0`): ran harvest, landed directly at
`system-gate` (theme-interview skipped, badge rendered), confirmed `GET .../checklist?gate=
system-gate` fired and served the real 3-item checklist with the §8bis note, checked all three
items, approved through the typed-`APPROVE` confirm dialog — mission advanced to `clone`, gate
history shows "System gate / approved / 3/3 checklist items checked."

### 3. Request-Pause (item 4)

A Pause section on mission detail, visible only during `clone`/`content-interview`/`brief`/
`executing` (`isPauseRelevantStage`) — a pure UI-visibility choice; `POST .../request-pause` is
legal from any stage server-side (`Mission.request_pause`'s own docstring: no stage guard at all),
so this never blocks the call itself, only where the button appears. Request pause / Clear pause
call the new `DesignStudioService.requestPause`/`clearPause` (`POST .../request-pause` /
`.../clear-pause`, no body). The chip reads `mission.pauseRequested` directly off whatever `mission`
signal value is current, so it reflects on every poll this screen already runs (run-step poll,
dispatch poll, gate/abort refresh, manual Refresh) — **no new polling mechanism introduced**, per
the demand's own acceptance criterion. Exact chip text: "pause requested — honored at next batch
boundary" — never claims a mid-batch stop.

**Live-verified**: on the same `design-studio-selfcheck` mission (now at `clone`), clicked Request
pause — chip appeared with the exact text; clicked Clear pause — chip disappeared, button reverted.

### 4. Plan Gantt (item 5)

`PlanViewComponent` gained an additive Timeline section — the existing work-unit table renders
exactly as before, unchanged; the Timeline renders alongside it, session-grouped with batch-boundary
markers, reading new optional `PlanWorkUnit.session`/`.batchBoundary` fields.

**Honest caveat, not hidden**: no real `plan.json` emits either field today —
`design_studio/domain/plan.py`'s own module docstring TODOs execution/session tracking to "a later
batch" (the future S-E batch engine); the demand's own acceptance criteria assumed a shape the real
backend does not yet produce. `hasSessionData`/`sessionGroups` read the fields purely defensively:
with no real session data (today's live case, confirmed against a real plan), every real work unit
still renders, folded into ONE explicit, honestly-labeled group ("this plan has no session
boundaries yet") — never a fabricated multi-session split invented client-side to satisfy the
letter of the ask. The grouping activates automatically, no further client change needed, the moment
design-studio's plan generation starts emitting either field.

**Live-verified** against the real `bd3f8e95` (plantpal) mission's real 7-work-unit `plan.json` —
all 7 work units (WU-0..WU-6) render in the Timeline in the plan's own build order, the existing
table section completely unaffected.

## What the origin must know

- The rewind-target picker (item 6) remains explicitly out of scope, as the demand itself named —
  OQ6 (whether `system-gate` should join `REWIND_TARGET_STAGES`) is still an open owner ruling; this
  repo has no rewind-target picker UI at all today (confirmed: no rewind-related test-id exists
  anywhere in `mission-detail.component.html`), so there was nothing to accidentally extend either
  way.
- `plan.json` session/batch grouping is wired and tested for BOTH presence and absence of
  `session`/`batchBoundary`, but only the absence path is exercised against real data today — when
  design-studio's plan generation (S-E batch engine) starts emitting either field, verify the
  grouped-rendering path (`plan-view.component.spec.ts`'s own "groups by session..." test already
  covers the mechanism synthetically) against a real multi-session plan once one exists.
- `pipelineRouteFor('executing')` now maps to `execution-complete` (previously wrongly mapped to
  `null`) — this was a genuine pre-existing gap in this repo's own code, not something B2
  introduced; fixed while absorbing the 12-stage sequence per the build order's own "verbatim"
  instruction.

## Not done / caveats

- **Plan Gantt's session grouping has no real multi-session data to render against yet** (see
  above) — the mechanism is real and tested, but "sessions grouped, work units placed within their
  session, batch boundaries marked" as literally multiple groups is not yet demonstrable against
  live data, because design-studio's own plan generation doesn't produce that data yet. This is a
  backend-capability gap, not a client bug — reported here rather than papered over with fabricated
  client-side grouping.
- `ng build` produces one bundle-size WARNING (not an error — exit code 0): "bundle initial exceeded
  maximum budget. Budget 686.08 kB was not met by 7.65 kB with a total of 693.73 kB." The
  `angular.json` budget's `maximumError` is 1MB, so this is well within a hard failure, but is new
  since this session's additions (system-gate panel, pause section, clone target-path form, plan
  timeline). Flagged honestly rather than silently ignored; a follow-up session may want to trim the
  bundle or raise `maximumWarning` if this recurs.
- No dedicated live verification of the reject-with-reason/retry-with-new-hints round-trip at
  `system-gate` was done against the REAL backend (only the validate/approve path was driven live,
  to avoid needlessly cycling the one available self-check mission through more state than needed).
  It IS covered by three dedicated unit tests against the exact real request/response shapes
  (`mission-detail.component.spec.ts`'s "system-gate review panel" describe block).

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. This report
is this repo's only output for the demand; the origin (design-studio) is never notified directly.

## Pre-check

Confirmed at session start the capability was NOT already shipped: `package.json:22` still pinned
`file:../contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts` and `design-studio.model.ts:14`'s `Regime` union still
had exactly two members. Proceeded with the work.

## What shipped

### 1. Contracts re-pin
`package.json:22` bumped `file:../contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts` → `.../v0.17.0/gen/ts` (kept
the same `file:` path convention every other repo in the fleet still uses today — D031's "pin a
version tag, never a `file:` path" is a known fleet-wide gap, not something this single-repo demand

### 2. Regime union

matching `contracts-worktrees/v0.17.0/gen/ts/state-event.ts:292`/`:343` verbatim. Doc comment
amended: D053's superseded "two regimes, one studio" replaced with a note citing D071 (2026-07-23)
amending it in place to three regimes.

### 3. The five named UI sites
- `mission-stage.ts` `REGIME_LABEL`/`REGIME_CHIP_CLASS` (both `Record<Regime, ...>`) gained an

- `new-mission-form.component.ts` — `REGIME_OPTIONS` gained `{ value: 'atlas-class', label:

Verified live against `:8087` (all reachable from this session):

- `GET /design-systems?regime=atlas-class` returns `200`.

### 4. Exhaustive grep for other Regime-keyed sites (per the demand's own acceptance criterion)
Grepped dashboard's own non-test sources for `Record<Regime`, the two regime literals together, and
`=== 'console-class'` / `=== 'inhabited-class'` patterns. Beyond the five sites named in the demand,
**no other** `Record<Regime, ...>` map, literal-pair guard, or two-branch regime conditional exists

production guard).

### 5. Unplanned: `design.designSystem` StateEvent variant (contracts v0.17.0, unrelated to atlas-class)
The re-pin alone (before any Regime widening) broke `ng build --configuration production`:
`state-event.ts`'s `StateEvent` union gained a new `DesignSystemEvent` member (`type:
"design.designSystem"`, S-B1's design-system registry lifecycle events) between v0.15.0 and v0.17.0,
which two exhaustive `switch (event.type)` statements — `snapshot-key.ts`'s `snapshotKey` and
`activity-label.ts`'s `activityLabel` — did not handle, failing their `const unhandled: never =
event` exhaustiveness checks. This is not one of the demand's named sites and is not Regime-related,
but shipping the re-pin without fixing it means the console does not build at all, so it had to be
addressed to satisfy "atlas-class missions can be opened and gated from the console." Fixed
minimally, following the two files' own existing pattern for `design.mission`:
- `snapshotKey`: added `case 'design.designSystem': return \`design.designSystem:${event.payload.designSystemId}\`;`
- `activityLabel`: added `case 'design.designSystem': return event.payload.slug;`
- `state-feed.service.ts`'s `EVENT_TYPES` array (a plain `StateEvent['type'][]`, not exhaustively
  checked by the compiler) gained `'design.designSystem'` — this file's own documented "FIX-9" lesson
  is that a type handled by `snapshotKey` but missing from this array reaches the store via the
  initial snapshot only, then has every live SSE delta silently dropped until reconnect. No console
  renderer for this event type exists yet (same render-later posture the file already takes for
  `agent.run`/`design.mission`) — out of scope to build one here, only to not silently drop it.

No other exhaustive `switch (event.type)` over the full `StateEvent` union exists in this repo
(grepped for `unhandled: never` / `: never =`) — these two were the only two needing this fix.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: wire `GET /brain/rollup` through to `/brain`

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

- **Demand:** `design-studio-20260725-brain-rollup-wire-through`
- **From:** `design-studio` → **To:** `dashboard`, `agent-runner`
- **This report covers the `dashboard` half only.** Criteria 4, 6 and 7 are agent-runner's; nothing
  here touches that repo.

## What shipped

The previous pass left `pendingAudit`, `pendingRatification` and `nightWindowOpensAt` as optional
panel inputs with nothing feeding them. They are fed now, from one fleet-wide
`GET /brain/rollup` read.

Live probe (2026-07-25 23:44, `:8089`) confirms what the wire carries: 24 repos, `nightWindow
.nextOpenAt = 2026-07-26T01:00:00+01:00`, 20 pending audit items, 7 eligible, and **no
pending-ratification field yet** — agent-runner's half had not shipped when this was written.

## Acceptance criteria (dashboard half)

| # | Criterion | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Screen calls `GET /brain/rollup` and feeds the three inputs; no per-repo fan-out | done | `brainRollup()`, `toRollupInputs`; a test fails if any `/brain/{repo}/…` call appears |
| 2 | Summary band renders `nightWindow.nextOpenAt` and the fleet-wide totals | done | `formatOpensAt` (clock label, ISO in `title`); `brain-fleet-summary-{audit,ratify}` |
| 3 | Rollup failure degrades counts to absent, never zero, never blocks the table | done | rollup is a third read outside `panelState`; specced both ways |
| 5 | Ratify fed by the pending count, not `overrides.ratifiedConventions` | **partial — blocked** | see below |
| 8 | Owner gate and no-writes invariant unchanged | done | dispatch path untouched |

Criteria 4, 6, 7 are agent-runner's.

## Criterion 5 is the one to read carefully

`overrides.ratifiedConventions` is **never** consulted — there is a test that fails if it ever
becomes the source, because showing work-completed where the owner reads work-pending is the exact
defect this demand was raised to correct. That half is done and enforced.

The other half — feeding Ratify from the *real* pending count — cannot be completed from this repo,
because the field does not exist yet. Rather than leave a dead wire, `readPendingRatification`
reads a **provisional** field name (`pendingRatification`, with `…Exists`/`…Reason` siblings,
matching the convention every shipped rollup field already follows) and tolerates a bare number or
an object carrying `totalCount`/`pendingCount`/`count`.

The safety property that makes this acceptable to ship: **anything unrecognised yields `null`**,
which renders exactly as today — an unlabelled `Ratify` link. So the wire lights up on its own if
agent-runner picks that name and shape, and stays silently correct if it does not. It can never
invent or misattribute a number.

**Action for whoever closes agent-runner's half:** confirm the shipped field against
`readPendingRatification`'s doc comment and delete the provisional note. If the name differs, it is
a one-line change there — no behaviour depends on the guess being right.

## Judgment calls worth reviewing

1. **Audit counts are outstanding items (`totalCount - filledCount`), not `totalCount`.** An
   already-filled item is classified work, and `/brain/audit/:repo` itself treats a fully-filled
   sample as a completed queue (queue-complete banner, submit control dropped). Counting filled
   items as pending would repeat this demand's own Ratify error one field over. The two are equal
   on the live probe — `filledCount` is `0` fleet-wide — so this does not change today's numbers,
   only their meaning when a sample gets filled.
2. **A total that cannot see every repo now says so.** Criterion 3 covers whole-rollup failure;
   per-repo unreadability (a non-null `<field>Reason`) is a different case. Those repos are omitted
   from the count map, and the band appends "(N unreadable)" rather than summing them as `0` — an
   authoritative-looking total that quietly understates the owner's outstanding work is the same
   class of error as the Ratify bug. This is slightly beyond the literal criteria; it exists because
   the criteria's own principle demanded it.
3. **A count map is `null`, not `{}`, when no repo produced a readable count** — an empty map would
   render "Audit (0)" fleet-wide off the summary's `?? 0` fallback, asserting emptiness the rollup
   never claimed.
4. **A window agent-runner could not parse its own spec for (`invalidReason` non-null) reports no
   open time**, rather than a possibly-stale `nextOpenAt`.
5. **`pendingAuditExists: false` with no reason reads as `0`, not unknown** — that is a normal 200
   meaning no sample has been generated, i.e. genuinely nothing pending. Only a non-null reason
   means "could not tell". 22 of 24 live repos are in this state.
6. **Legacy screen tests now fail their rollup request by default** (drained in `afterEach`). Those
   tests are about the eligibility table, and the degraded path is the state they were originally
   written against — this keeps `httpMock.verify()` honest instead of letting an unflushed request
   pass unnoticed.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **1481 tests, 171 files, all passing** (was 1456; +25).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — clean.
- `npx ng build --configuration production` — succeeds (pre-existing bundle-budget warning only).
- The rollup fixtures in both new specs are built from the **real** 2026-07-25 live response shape,
  probed directly off `:8089`.
- **Not verified live in a browser**, by owner decision: port 4200 is held by Docker, and
  agent-runner's CORS allowlist is exactly `http://localhost:4200`, so serving on any other port
  fails preflight and would prove nothing. The owner chose to ship on the specs rather than free the
  port. The wire has therefore never been exercised through a real browser request — first live
  load of `/brain` is the remaining check.

## Follow-up

- agent-runner's half (criteria 4, 6, 7) is open; criterion 5 completes when it lands.
- Per the demand's closing note, `design-studio` re-reviews `/brain` against D036 as a single
  finished surface once both halves are in.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: `/brain` fleet screen legible at a glance [D036]

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

- **Demand:** `design-studio-20260725-dashboard-brain-screen-legibility`
- **From:** `design-studio` → **To:** `dashboard`
- **Fulfilled by:** dashboard, session `2026-07-25_2312_fulfill-demand-design-studio-20260725-da`

## What shipped

The `/brain` fleet screen's 11-column, 25-equal-row table is now a summary band plus a
6-column table, ordered eligible-first with the quiet majority collapsed. Console-class
treatment per D036: legibility only, no ornament, no new colour vocabulary — the pass uses
the `status-up` / `status-degraded` / `status-down` tokens the screen already carried but
never applied to the fleet's own state.

New: `src/app/brain/brain-fleet-view.ts` — the whole derivation (state classification,
ordering/grouping, progress cell, relative timestamps, summary, threshold caption), pure
functions over the `BrainFleetRow[]` the parent already merges. The panel component renders
that projection; it computes no eligibility of its own and still performs no writes.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Summary band: eligible-of-total, night-window state, time since last fleet run, pending totals | `summarizeFleet`; `brain-fleet-summary*` testids |
| 2 | Eligible → never-run → below-threshold, quiet group collapsed behind a counted disclosure | `groupFleetRows` + `brain-fleet-quiet-toggle` |
| 3 | One state chip per row from the existing status tokens | `brainFleetState` + `STATE_CLASS`; `brain-fleet-row-state-chip` |
| 4 | Threshold removed from the body, stated once as a caption, overridability preserved | `fleetThreshold`; `brain-fleet-threshold-caption` |
| 5 | Sessions/threshold as one progress cell; blocked reason no longer restates it | `progressOf` + `blockedReasonAddsFact`; `brain-fleet-row-progress` |
| 6 | Relative timestamps, ISO instant in `title` | reuses `overview/event-age.ts`'s `formatAge`; `brain-fleet-row-last-run` |
| 7 | Audit/Ratify carry counts when available, degrade unlabelled when not | `pendingAudit` / `pendingRatification` inputs, `null` today |
| 8 | `Run full now` the only solid control, eligible rows only; `View docs` demoted | run button `bg-ink text-ink-invert`; view link `text-ink-subtle` |
| 9 | Owner gate unchanged | screen's class-3 `ConfirmDialog` + typed `RUN` + dispatch untouched |
| 10 | Existing testids present or updated with their specs; suite passes | see below |

## Judgment calls worth reviewing

1. **A fifth state, `not-reported`.** The demand named four. A `missingFromFleet` placeholder
   has no executioner fields at all, so asserting any of the four about it would be a
   fabrication. It renders muted, keeping its existing `missing from fleet` badge.
2. **`never-run` outranks `below-threshold`.** A repo that has never been swept stays visible
   even at 0/3 — "never swept" is a durable fact, "below threshold" a transient one, and the
   demand explicitly wanted `documentations`' `—` to read distinctly. On a freshly-adopting
   fleet this can make the visible group larger than the demand's 5-of-25 example.
3. **`never-run` drew `status-down`.** Mapping: eligible → `status-up`, waiting-for-window →
   `status-degraded`, never-run → `status-down`, below-threshold/not-reported → muted. This
   uses all four tokens the criterion named, and "never swept" is the state the screen's own
   first question ("is the fleet being swept, or silently stalled?") is asking about.
4. **`Run full now` is now absent, not disabled, on ineligible rows.** Criterion 8 says
   "renders only on eligible rows", which supersedes the previous disabled-never-hidden rule
   for this control. The blocking fact moved to the chip, which is always visible; the
   component's `onRunClicked` eligibility guard is retained and still specced.
5. **No invented rollup contract.** The sibling demand's shape is not yet fixed, so the panel
   takes three narrow presentational inputs (`pendingAudit`, `pendingRatification`,
   `nightWindowOpensAt`) rather than a guessed cross-repo type. The screen passes none of
   them today; when the rollup lands, wiring it is a change in the screen component only.
   No per-repo fan-out was added.
6. **Blocked-reason suppression is a heuristic** over the executioner's reason text: reasons
   that restate the window, the threshold, or never-run are dropped; anything else survives
   into a `Note` cell. A reason phrased in wording the heuristic does not recognise shows up
   rather than disappears — fail-toward-visible.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **1456 tests, 170 files, all passing** (was 1450; +21 new
  `brain-fleet-view.spec.ts`, panel spec 23 tests).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — clean.
- `npx ng build --configuration production` — succeeds (the initial-bundle budget warning is
  pre-existing and unchanged in character).
- Not verified live against a running `agent-runner` — no instance was reachable from this
  session, so the screen was exercised through its specs' DOM assertions only.

## Spec changes

`brain-fleet-panel.component.spec.ts` and `brain-fleet-screen.component.spec.ts` were updated
alongside the template, per criterion 10. Every pre-existing testid survives
(`brain-fleet-panel`, `-row`, `-row-missing-badge`, `-row-audit-link`, `-row-ratify-link`,
`-row-view-link`, `-row-run-button`, `-refresh-button`, `-repos-degraded-banner`). Two
assertions changed meaning rather than wording: the run-button-disabled tests became
run-button-absent tests (criterion 8), and the verbatim-field-dump test became chip +
progress-cell assertions (criterion 5).

## Follow-up left to the origin

Per the demand's own closing note, `design-studio` reviews the shipped screen against D036 and
decides separately whether `/brain/audit/:repo` and `/brain/ratify/:repo` need the same pass.
Nothing in this repo blocks that.
