# Fulfillment — dashboard: one source of truth for ratification candidates

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

- **Demand:** `design-studio-20260726-brain-ratify-single-source`
- **From:** `design-studio` → **To:** `dashboard`, `agent-runner`
- **This report covers `dashboard`'s leg only.** agent-runner's leg (criteria 2, 3, 5, 7) was already
  shipped and reported before this session opened; I read their report for the endpoint contract and
  built against the live endpoint, and touched nothing in that repo.

## What shipped

`/brain/ratify/:repo` reads `GET /brain/{repo}/ratification-candidates` — the same
`scanRatification()` call whose count the fleet row's Ratify badge shows via `/brain/rollup`. The
badge and the queue are no longer two readings that happen to agree; they are one scan read twice.

**`parse-proposed-conventions.ts` was deleted outright**, taking agent-runner's own recommendation
over the demand's "retired or reduced to a fallback" wording: any fallback reading `graph.md` *can*
disagree with the badge, and that is the defect rather than a mitigation of it. `graph.md` is still
read by `/brain/view/:repo`, which shows the file as itself and makes no claim about pending work.

## Acceptance criteria — dashboard's leg

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Badge count and listed candidates derived from the same source, equal for every repo | done — live 24/24, zero mismatches |
| 4 | Ratified-but-not-yet-applied surfaced distinctly (rendering half) | done — its own read-only section, never a candidate |
| 6 | Client-side `graph.md` parser retired or reduced to a non-disagreeing fallback | done — deleted |
| 8 | Dispatch still submits unit ids, screen performs no writes, owner gate unchanged (dashboard half) | done — untouched |

Criteria 2, 3, 5 and 7 are agent-runner's.

## Live verification

Criterion 1 asks for equality *for every repo in the fleet*, which no unit test can assert. I ran the
dashboard's **own** projection logic — `readPendingRatification` transcribed verbatim from
`brain-rollup.ts`, plus the ratify screen's own `candidates`/`count` reads — against the real
`:8089` fleet:

```
agent-runner         badge=46  listed=46  servedCount=46  rnya=0  AGREE
dashboard            badge=0   listed=0   servedCount=0   rnya=3  AGREE
demand-coordinator   badge=0   listed=0   servedCount=0   rnya=2  AGREE
media-generation     badge=63  listed=63  servedCount=63  rnya=0  AGREE
… 20 more, all AGREE
repos checked: 24 | mismatches: 0
```

Both owner-reported cases now resolve correctly:

- **`agent-runner`: badge 44, queue 0 → badge 46, queue 46.** (46 not 44 because the gated set moved
  since the demand was written.) The queue was empty because `graph.md`'s projection was stale; the
  screen no longer reads it.
- **`dashboard`: badge 0, queue 3 → badge 0, queue 0, with 3 shown as ratified-not-yet-applied.**
  Those three were `ratifiedConventions: 3` in `overrides.md` *and* offered as candidates. They are
  now visible as their own state and cannot be selected, so the owner is no longer invited to ratify
  what they have already ratified — and a dispatched agent can no longer rewrite existing entries.

## Judgment calls worth reviewing

1. **Unknown is not empty, and the screen says so.** `candidates: null` (agent-runner could not read
   the unit files) renders an explicit unknown notice carrying agent-runner's own `reason`, with no
   submit control at all — not an empty queue. Conflating those two is the same class of error as the
   badge/queue split this demand exists to close.
2. **A served count that disagrees with its own served list raises a visible banner.** It should be
   structurally impossible — one scan produces both — so this is a guard on an invariant, not a
   reconciliation. Same posture the panel's existing `summaryMismatch` banner already takes for the
   overrides summary. The alternative is discovering the invariant broke by watching an owner stop
   trusting the screen, which is how this demand started.
3. **`ratifiedNotYetApplied` is deliberately NOT added into the badge number.** It is work already
   done; adding it would both inflate the pending count and break the badge/queue equality criterion
   1 asks for. It has its own count in its own section instead.
4. **The dispatch prompt's `description` now comes from the candidate's `title`, not `body`.** Title
   is the one-line summary an `overrides.md` entry wants; the fuller `body` is rendered on screen for
   the owner to judge by but would bloat the file. Unit ids — the part that actually identifies the
   work — are unchanged, so the prompt shape needed no change at all.
5. **The previous session's provisional `pendingRatification` type is now the real one.** That guess
   turned out to match what agent-runner shipped (`{count, ratifiedNotYetApplied, unreadableUnits}`),
   confirmed against the live endpoint; the tolerant multi-shape parse and its provisional note are
   gone, replaced by a read of `.count`.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **1486 tests, 170 files, all passing** (was 1481/171: +14 new, −4 from the deleted
  parser's own spec, −5 rewritten).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — clean.
- `npx ng build --configuration production` — succeeds (pre-existing bundle-budget warning only).
- Both new specs' fixtures are shaped after the real live response, probed directly off `:8089`.
- **Not verified in a browser.** Port 4200 is held by Docker and agent-runner's CORS allowlist is
  exactly `http://localhost:4200`, so any other port fails preflight and would prove nothing — the
  same constraint as the previous session, and the owner's standing decision was to ship on the
  specs. The live fleet check above exercises the real endpoints and the real projection logic, but
  not the rendered DOM.

## Note back to the origin

agent-runner's closing note — that a number is only as good as the queue it links to — applies to
this repo too, and more directly: the wire-through session shipped the badge and never opened the
screen it links to. The count and the queue were one click apart and nobody looked. Worth carrying
into the D036 re-review as a check on the surface rather than on either endpoint.

# Fulfillment report — design-studio-20260728-dashboard-artifact-readers

## State before this session

Not shipped. A prior session (`2026-07-28_1413`) opened against this same demand and closed
`status: partial` with an empty `changes:` list — no code from it exists; the working tree was clean
apart from the untracked demand file itself. The capability was built from scratch here.

## What shipped, against each acceptance criterion

**1. Harvest reader.** `HarvestViewComponent` renders `harvest.json`'s descriptor (identity,
contracts pin, and `deps`/`infra`/`decisions`/`contracts.used` as chip rows), the
`exposed.inbound` and `exposed.outbound` tables with their real column sets (inbound:
port/contract/sync-async; outbound: the same plus callee), and `contractsSchemas.resolved` next to
`unresolved` as its counterpart rather than as a red list.

`gaps[]` is the section that leads, styled as an open-question block (`status-starting`, not
`status-down`), with an explicit note that these are not errors — they are what harvest could not
answer from documents and they become the interview questionnaire verbatim. The unresolved-contracts
block says the same thing one level down and points back at the questionnaire, which is why
`e8e4b3e5`'s first five gaps are one per unresolved contract id.

**2. Interview reader — `answer` as formatted markdown.** `InterviewViewComponent` renders the
`answer` field through `renderMarkdownToHtml` (the same renderer the brain doc panel and the
Documentations screen already use — escapes the whole source before recognizing any syntax, emits
only its own fixed tag set), as the panel's primary content. Verified against `bd3f8e95`'s real
`answers.json`, whose 7624-character answer is numbered markdown with bold and inline code: the
spec asserts the list is a real `<li>` list, the bold a real `<strong>`, the backticked id a real
`<code>`, and that no literal `\n` survives into the DOM.

`questions[]` renders as the asked list. One honesty note the demand's wording invited a guess on:
neither answers file carries a per-question answer — the agent answers all questions in the one
markdown body — so the reader renders the questions as the asked list and names the answer body as
their single joint answer, rather than inventing a split. The genuine per-question match exists only
in `brief.json`'s `answeredQuestions`, made server-side by numbered-marker extraction, and
`BriefViewComponent` is what renders it as a real Q&A list.

**3. Both namings.** `interview-artifacts.ts` holds `INTERVIEW_NAMINGS` — the content pair
(`questionnaire.json`/`answers.json`) and the theme pair (`theme-interview-*.json`) — and
`MissionDetailComponent.loadInterview` resolves which one a mission carries by asking for each
pair's answers file in turn and taking the first non-404. The mission's stage is deliberately not
used to predict it: a mission can carry either, both or neither, and the artifact on disk is the
only honest answer. A non-404 error stops the walk and is reported as the real failure it is, never
retried against the other naming and mislabelled "not run yet". Specs cover both legs end-to-end
(`bd3f8e95`'s pair and `e8e4b3e5`'s), plus the case where the content pair answers and the theme
request is therefore never issued.

**4. `transcriptTail` never leads.** It sits behind a disclosure that is closed by default. The
label's line count reads `transcriptTail.length` only — no line body is touched — and
`transcriptLines()` returns `[]` until `transcriptExpanded()` is true, so the 262,091 bytes are
never in the DOM on first paint. The spec asserts both halves: the answer renders fully with the
disclosure closed and `transcriptLines()` empty, and the bodies appear only after the click.

**5. Brief reader.** Every section renders — `dataToExpose`, `actions`, `forms`, `validation`,
`states`, `volumes`, `priorities` — plus `answeredQuestions` as an expandable Q&A list whose answers
are rendered as markdown. `synthesisNote` renders inside the open-questions block as a standing
caveat headed "What this brief did and did not invent".

**6. `openQuestions` prominent.** It is the first section in the reader, above every other, in its
own bordered block, with a note that these are addressed to the owner rather than to the next
pipeline step. A spec asserts the DOM ordering directly rather than trusting the template's reading
order.

**7. Empty vs absent.** Distinguished at two levels. A brief whose `forms`/`validation`/`volumes`/
`priorities` are genuinely empty (that is `bd3f8e95`'s real shape) renders each section with its
honest `(0)` count and an "empty, on purpose" line naming why — that is the artifact being correct,
not incomplete. An artifact that does not exist yet is a 404, classified as the `empty` `PanelState`
and rendered by the state-shell's not-yet branch — never a blank region, never an error. A real
non-404 failure is that one reader's `error`/`unreachable` state and never suppresses the other two;
a spec covers exactly that mix (harvest 500, brief 200, interview absent, all three rendering
their own truth simultaneously).

**8. The flat list survives.** `ArtifactsPanelComponent` is now titled **All files** and collapsed by
default, stating its file count while closed. Contents, sizes and the open-in-a-new-tab anchor are
unchanged — the escape hatch for everything without a reader (proposal mocks, `tokens.css`,
`state-material-mapping.json`, `design-system-build.json`), none of which this demand touched. One
deliberate detail: the four non-ready states render whether or not the disclosure is open, so a
closed list can never be the reason an error or an unreachable design-studio goes unseen.

**9. Fetched as JSON over the existing CORS grant, no design-studio change.** All three reuse
`designStudioArtifactUrl`'s route through `HttpClient`, generalising the `plan()`/`matrix()` idiom
already in `DesignStudioService` into `artifactJson<T>(id, file)` plus named `harvest()`/`brief()`
wrappers. Re-verified live this session from the console origin against the running service:
`brief.json` 200 in 13.7 ms; `answers.json` 200, 274,904 bytes, in 10–24 ms across three runs;
`theme-interview-answers.json` 200, 88,746 bytes, in 9 ms; `harvest.json` 200 in 12 ms — each with
`access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200` and `content-type: application/json` on the
response. No design-studio-side change was needed or made.

**10. A large artifact does not block first paint.** Every artifact fetch is independent and fired in
parallel inside `loadAll`; nothing awaits anything else, and each reader owns its own state. Within
the interview reader, the answer renders without the transcript bodies existing at all (point 4).

**11. Existing primitives, existing idiom.** Each reader is a `state-shell`-wrapped section in the
same `rounded border border-line bg-surface p-3` idiom as `PlanViewComponent`/`MatrixViewComponent`,
with the same `h2` uppercase heading and `title` attribute naming its source route, the same
`h3` section sub-headings, the same expand-on-click row pattern for long content, and the same
defensive `?? []` reading of every wire collection. No new component primitive and no new styling
vocabulary was introduced. (`wall-panel` and `data-table` were deliberately not used: the trust wall
is not what these panels are about, and the port/contract tables are small, fixed, order-significant
projections of the artifact — sortable/filterable generic tables would let the reader reorder rows
away from the artifact's own order.)

**12. System-build minor.** `SystemBuildPanelComponent` now renders "pages not yet declared" for a
batch the server reported with `pagesTotal: 0` that has not consolidated — the R9 shape where
batches 1 and 2 start a fresh build with empty page lists until batch 0 (the constitution)
consolidates and declares their pages. `0/0 pages` stated the opposite of what is true there. A
batch that reports `0/0` and *is* consolidated keeps the plain count, and a batch the server never
reported at all still shows no pages claim of either kind.

**13. Test hooks and suite.** Every pre-existing `data-testid` is still present and unchanged;
`artifacts-list`/`artifact-row`/`artifact-open-link` moved behind the new `artifacts-toggle` and
their specs were updated in the same commit. New hooks: `harvest-view`/`interview-view`/`brief-view`
and their sections, `artifacts-toggle`, `system-build-batch-pages-undeclared`.

Suite: **180 files, 1618 tests, all green** (baseline 176/1580 — +4 files, +38 tests).
`tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build` succeeds with the same pre-existing initial-bundle budget
warning as before, unrelated to this work.

## Not touched, deliberately

`state-material-mapping.json` and `tokens.css` have no reader — R5's job, per the demand. The
proposal mocks keep the plain-URL/`iframe` idiom `ThemePropositionsComponent` already uses.

## Follow-ups for design-studio

None blocking. One observation worth having on the record: `answers.json`'s `transcriptTail` is
95.3% of the file and its `result` entry duplicates `answer` byte-for-byte, so every console load of
that artifact transfers ~262 KB it renders nothing from unless the owner expands the disclosure. If
design-studio ever wants to split it (`answers.json` + `answers-transcript.json`, or a
`?include=transcript` query), this console would need only a second fetch behind the same
disclosure. Not requested, not required — the current shape is fast enough live (measured above).

# Fulfillment — dashboard: keep the complete unit body on audit/ratify dedup, not the truncated title

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

- **Demand:** `design-studio-20260728-dashboard-brain-dedup-kept-truncated-text`
- **From:** `design-studio` → **To:** `dashboard`

## What shipped

Before starting, I checked `git log`, `demands/fulfilled/`, and this repo's own `.brain/sessions/`
for prior work on this exact demand. Found `.brain/sessions/2026-07-28_0236_fulfill-demand-design-studio-20260728-da.md`
— a dispatch-supervisor session opened against this identical task, `status: partial`, empty
`changes` — abandoned before any code was written. So this was live work, not a re-do; that stray
session file is committed alongside this fix as the honest record of the earlier attempt.

**Root cause.** The prior demand (`design-studio-20260728-dashboard-brain-subscreen-legibility`)
shipped a correct `titleDuplicatesBody(title, body)` predicate but wired both templates backwards:
on a duplicate, each template kept rendering `title` (the served field, allowed to be a truncated
lead-in) and suppressed `body` (the complete text) entirely. Live, this read as "the fix broke the
screens" rather than "fixed" them — 43 of 46 ratify rows and 8 of 10 audit items showed only a
truncated title ending in `…` with no way to reach the rest.

**The flip.** Both `BrainAuditPanelComponent` and `BrainRatifyPanelComponent` now render `body`
unconditionally whenever it's present — in full, or as a preview with a "Show more"/"Show less"
toggle once it passes `LONG_TEXT_THRESHOLD` (240 chars) — and render `title` only when
`!titleDuplicatesBody(title, body)`. `title` disappearing on a duplicate is not a loss: it was
never anything but a redundant (and possibly lossy) restatement of the same text `body` now shows
in full.

**Shared preview mechanism.** `src/app/brain/long-text.ts` (new) extracts
`LONG_TEXT_THRESHOLD`/`isLongText`/`previewText` out of the audit panel, which already had this
machinery for `unitBody`/`citedText`. The ratify panel gets the identical mechanism for
`candidate.body` for the first time — before this fix it rendered a non-duplicate body in full with
no truncation at all, so a long non-duplicate candidate body had no collapse/expand either. This is
what satisfies the acceptance criterion that ratify offer "equivalent access to a long candidate
body": not just on the duplicate path, but for every long body, matching audit's existing behavior.

**Quote/escaping normalization.** `titleDuplicatesBody` now strips one leading quote character
(`"`/`'`) and unescapes backslash-escaped quotes (`\"`, `\'`) on both sides before comparing —
covers the three named live candidates (K-0058, K-0097, K-0131) whose served title differs from
its body only by that serialization artifact, which the exact-equality/truncated-prefix rule alone
did not catch and which would otherwise still render twice.

**Contract, not just detection.** `titleDuplicatesBody`'s doc comment now states explicitly: on
`true`, the caller renders `body` and suppresses `title`, never the reverse — the exact inversion
this demand exists to fix, now written into the function's own contract so it can't recur silently.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ratify: every candidate's complete unit text reachable (full or truncated+expander) | `ratify-candidate-body` always renders when `candidate.body` is present; `ratify-candidate-body-toggle` past threshold |
| 2 | Audit: every item's complete unit body reachable on the same terms | `audit-item-unit-body` always renders when `item.unitBody` is present; existing `audit-item-unit-body-toggle` |
| 3 | Text still renders once, not twice | `title`/`description` suppressed via `!titleDuplicatesBody(...)` guard whenever `body` renders |
| 4 | Surviving string on duplicate is the complete one (body), not the truncated lead-in | template guard direction flipped on both panels |
| 5 | Audit's Show more/Show less restored; ratify offers equivalent access | audit: unconditional on `unitBody` presence (previously gated behind non-duplicate); ratify: new `displayBody`/`isBodyExpanded`/`toggleBodyExpanded` |
| 6 | Regression test: no rendered unit text ends in a truncation marker without an expand control | `brain-audit-panel.component.spec.ts` / `brain-ratify-panel.component.spec.ts`, "no rendered ... text ends in a truncation marker ..." |
| 7 | K-0058/K-0097/K-0131-style candidates render once, not twice | `titleDuplicatesBody`'s quote/backslash-escape normalization + dedicated tests in both component specs and `duplicate-text.spec.ts` |
| 8 | `titleDuplicatesBody`'s contract/doc comment states which string survives | `src/app/brain/duplicate-text.ts` doc comment |
| 9 | Owner gate, dispatch payload, integrity banner, no-writes invariant unchanged; suite passes | none of `submit()`'s payload shape, the confirm-dialog gate, or any HTTP-calling code was touched — see Verification |

## Judgment calls worth reviewing

1. **Ratify's new expand/collapse applies to every long body, not only duplicate-triggered ones.**
   The acceptance criteria's own wording ("equivalent access to a long candidate body") reads as
   general, not duplicate-scoped, and audit's own existing mechanism is likewise unconditional on
   duplication — a long, non-duplicate body was already collapsible on audit before this fix. Ratify
   previously had no truncation at all for a non-duplicate body; this fix gives it the same shape as
   audit rather than a narrower one that only fires on the duplicate path.
2. **Quote/escape normalization strips only one leading quote character, not internal or trailing
   ones.** The demand's named cases (K-0058/K-0097/K-0131) are described as differing by "a leading
   quote character or a backslash-escaping difference" — leading-only, so that's what's implemented.
   Backslash-unescaping applies wherever `\"`/`\'` appear in the string, not just at the edges, since
   a backslash-escaping difference is plausibly anywhere in the text, not just the start.
3. **`long-text.ts` is a new shared module rather than duplicating the threshold/preview logic a
   second time into the ratify panel.** Not required by the acceptance criteria directly, but the
   demand's own framing ("the ratify screen offers equivalent access") reads as "the same mechanism,"
   and the codebase already has one precedent (`duplicate-text.ts`) for factoring exactly this kind
   of shared audit/ratify logic out rather than forking it.
4. **`citedText` is still outside `titleDuplicatesBody`'s scope**, same judgment call the prior
   report flagged — this demand's acceptance criteria are scoped to unit title/body (audit) and
   candidate title/body (ratify), not the cited-source-text field, so it was left untouched.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --run` — **1525 tests, 173 files, all passing** (was 1509/172: +1 file —
  `long-text.spec.ts` (6 tests) — and net +16 tests total: `duplicate-text.spec.ts` (+4),
  `brain-audit-panel.component.spec.ts` (+3 net: 2 tests rewritten to the corrected direction, 3
  new), `brain-ratify-panel.component.spec.ts` (+3 net: 2 rewritten, 3 new), `long-text.spec.ts`
  (+6, new file)).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — clean.
- `npx ng build --configuration production` — succeeds (the pre-existing initial-bundle budget
  warning is unchanged in character from the prior report, not a new regression).
- Every pre-existing testid this fix touches survives unchanged: `audit-item-unit-title`,
  `audit-item-unit-title-unavailable`, `audit-item-unit-body`, `audit-item-unit-body-unavailable`,
  `audit-item-unit-body-toggle`, `ratify-candidate-description`, `ratify-candidate-body`. New
  testid: `ratify-candidate-body-toggle` (mirrors audit's existing `-toggle` naming).
- **Not verified live against a running agent-runner.** No instance was reachable from this
  session — the same standing constraint the prior two brain-screen demands' reports already
  noted. The "43 of 46" / "8 of 10" counts from the acceptance criteria were taken as given rather
  than re-measured; this fix is exercised through the specs' DOM assertions only, including the two
  rewritten tests that directly assert the corrected suppress/render direction and the new
  regression sweep asserting no truncated text renders without an expander.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: `/brain` audit and ratify sub-screen legibility

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

- **Demand:** `design-studio-20260728-dashboard-brain-subscreen-legibility`
- **From:** `design-studio` → **To:** `dashboard`

## What shipped

Before starting, I checked `git log`, `demands/fulfilled/`, and this repo's own `.brain/sessions/`
for prior work on this demand. The related `design-studio-20260725-dashboard-brain-screen-legibility`
report explicitly scoped itself to the `/brain` fleet screen and deferred `/brain/audit/:repo` and
`/brain/ratify/:repo` to a later demand; `design-studio-20260726-brain-ratify-single-source` fixed
the ratify queue's data source but didn't touch rendering. Neither shipped any part of this demand.
A dispatch-supervisor session (`.brain/sessions/2026-07-28_0212_...`) had opened against this exact
task and gone `partial` with an empty change list — no code had been written. So this was live work,
not a re-do.

**Double-rendering.** A new shared predicate, `titleDuplicatesBody(title, body)`
(`src/app/brain/duplicate-text.ts`), covers exact equality (what the ratify template's guard already
caught) plus the case it missed: `title` is a truncated lead-in of `body`, with or without a trailing
ellipsis marker. Both `BrainAuditPanelComponent` (which had no guard at all) and
`BrainRatifyPanelComponent` now call the same function. Tested standalone (9 cases) rather than only
through the two components that consume it.

**Raw overrides.md.** The `<pre data-testid="ratify-overrides-raw">` block is now wrapped in a
`<details data-testid="ratify-overrides-raw-details">`, collapsed by default (no `open` attribute).
The parsed summary counts (`ratify-summary-counts`) render above it, outside the disclosure, so they
stay visible without expanding anything. The displayed raw text has its `<!-- ... -->` authoring
comments stripped by a new `stripHtmlComments()` — the underlying `overridesRaw()` input is untouched,
so the client-side summary re-parse (which already has its own comment-skip logic) keeps reading the
real file.

**Batch affordances.** The candidate list gained a free-text filter
(`ratify-candidate-filter`, matching unit id / title / body) plus `ratify-select-all` /
`ratify-clear-all` buttons. Both bulk actions — and the filter itself — operate on
`filteredIndexedRows()`, the currently-*listed* set: selecting or clearing while filtered leaves rows
hidden by the filter untouched, so toggling the filter back and forth never silently discards a
selection made under a different filter. `ratify-candidates-filtered-count` ("Showing X of Y") makes
the scope unambiguous next to the buttons. The dispatch button's existing `Ratify N unit(s)` label
already stated the selected count and needed no change.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ratify: no candidate renders its text twice (exact-eq + truncated-prefix) | `titleDuplicatesBody`; template guard at the candidate body `@if` |
| 2 | Audit: unit title/body under the same rule | same predicate, `brain-audit-panel.component.html`'s unit-body block |
| 3 | Rule is a shared, tested predicate, not duplicated | `src/app/brain/duplicate-text.ts` (+9 tests), imported by both panels |
| 4 | Raw overrides.md collapsed by default; summary counts stay visible | `ratify-overrides-raw-details` (no `open`); summary `dl` sits outside it |
| 5 | Authoring comments not rendered when expanded | `stripHtmlComments()` applied before display |
| 6 | Select-all / clear-all over currently-listed candidates | `selectAllListed()` / `clearAllListed()`, scoped to `filteredIndexedRows()` |
| 7 | Text filter over id/text; select-all scoped to filtered set; count unambiguous | `filteredIndexedRows()`; `ratify-candidates-filtered-count` |
| 8 | summaryMismatch banner, dispatch unit-id payload, owner gate, no-writes invariant unchanged | none of `submit()`'s payload shape, the screens, or the confirm-dialog gate were touched |
| 9 | Existing testids present/updated with specs; suite passes | see Verification |

## Judgment calls worth reviewing

1. **Comments are stripped from the data shown, not just visually hidden.** The demand's own
   capability line said "stripped"; the acceptance criteria's alternative ("or the disclosure makes
   clear it's shown verbatim") was there as a fallback if stripping proved impractical. It wasn't, so
   stripping was taken as the primary instruction.
2. **Select-all/clear-all scope to the filtered set symmetrically.** An alternative reading had
   clear-all wipe the *entire* selection regardless of filter. I chose the symmetric behavior — both
   bulk actions act only on what's currently listed — because it's the one that never destroys a
   selection made under a different filter state without the owner seeing it happen.
3. **The audit panel's body block disappears entirely on a duplicate, not a "hidden" placeholder.**
   When `unitBody` is a duplicate of `unitTitle`, no `-unavailable` message renders either — the body
   *is* available, it's just redundant with text already shown, which is a different fact from "not
   resolved" and gets no unavailable-style treatment.
4. **Cited text was left out of the dedup rule.** The acceptance criteria named only unit title/body;
   `citedText` is a different field (quoted source text, not a unit summary) and was not brought under
   the predicate. Flagging this as a judgment call in case design-studio wants it included later.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **1509 tests, 172 files, all passing** (was 1486/170: +14 for the two new pure-function
  files' specs, +7 in `brain-ratify-panel.component.spec.ts`, +2 in `brain-audit-panel.component.spec.ts`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — clean.
- `npx ng build --configuration production` — succeeds (the pre-existing initial-bundle budget warning
  is unchanged in character).
- Every pre-existing testid this demand touches survives: `ratify-overrides-raw`,
  `ratify-candidate-body`, `ratify-candidate-checkbox`, `ratify-submit-button`,
  `ratify-summary-mismatch-banner`, `ratify-summary-counts`, `audit-item-unit-body`. New testids:
  `ratify-overrides-raw-details`, `ratify-overrides-raw-summary`, `ratify-candidate-filter`,
  `ratify-candidates-filtered-count`, `ratify-select-all`, `ratify-clear-all`,
  `ratify-candidates-filtered-empty`.
- **Not verified live against a running agent-runner.** No instance was reachable from this session
  (same standing constraint noted in the two prior brain-screen demands' reports) — the "44 of 46
  candidates currently duplicate" fact from the acceptance criteria was taken as given rather than
  re-measured, and this fix is otherwise exercised through the specs' DOM assertions only, including a
  fixture explicitly modeled on the truncated-prefix case the criteria describes.

## Follow-up left to the origin

Judgment call 4 above (`citedText` on the audit panel) is a candidate for a future demand if
design-studio wants the same rule extended there — nothing in this repo blocks it.

# Send back at a gate — the console half

## State before this session

Not shipped, and checked first. Nothing in this repo mentioned `sendBack`/`send-back` in any form:
`Mission` carried `gateRecords` and `rewinds` only, `DesignStudioService` had no caller for the
route, and the gate decision form offered exactly two controls. The capability was built here for
the first time.

design-studio's half **was** already live (its own fulfilment of the paired demand
`dashboard-20260728-design-studio-gate-send-back`, raised from this repo on 2026-07-28): verified in
`../design-studio/src/design_studio/api.py` — `POST /missions/{id}/send-back` reading a required
non-empty `note` (400 otherwise) and reading no `checklist` field at all, and `_mission_to_dict`
projecting `sendBacks: [{gate, note, sentBackAt}]` on every route's response.

## What was built

### Wire + service
`SendBackRecord` (`gate`/`note`/`sentBackAt`) and `SendBackRequest` (`note`, and nothing else) in
`design-studio.model.ts`, plus `Mission.sendBacks` as a required always-present field — the same
posture `rewinds` already has, matching the real wire shape (`[]`, never an absent key). The model's
doc comment records what a send-back is NOT, so no later reader has to re-derive it: not a verdict,
not a stage change, not a dispatch, not a consumed round, and never binding direction.

`DesignStudioService.sendBack(id, {note})` → `POST /missions/{id}/send-back`. The body is the note
alone; the service spec asserts that `checklist` and `outcome` are absent from the request body, not
merely unused.

### The third control
`GateDecisionFormComponent` gains a `sendBackRequested` output and a **Send back** button beside
Approve and Reject, styled as a neutral outline rather than an up/down colour — it must not read as
a third verdict. It is:

- disabled until the Notes field is non-empty (whitespace-only does not arm it), with the reason
  said out loud next to it rather than left as a dead button;
- never gated on checklist completeness — "I cannot evaluate this" has to stay reachable exactly
  when the boxes cannot be ticked;
- emitting the **trimmed note only**, never the tick state, which would imply an assertion the owner
  did not make.

Approve's own arming is untouched, including its existing "no client-side completeness rule"
posture (design law 1) and the `approveBlockedReason` path.

Not labelled *Retry*, per the demand's naming note; a test asserts the word "retry" appears nowhere
in the form.

### On the gate, in place
`MissionDetailComponent.onSendBackRequested` calls the service directly — **no confirm dialog**.
The shared class-3 typed-word dialog guards actions that move something (a gate decision advances or
binds, an abort is terminal); a send-back moves nothing, and the ceremony would misrepresent it. The
action is logged to the action log as `SEND_BACK_GATE`, class 2.

On success the mission is replaced from the response and the page re-renders in place: same stage,
same form, no recorded-outcome card, no gate-history decision row, no progress indicator moved.
`recordAnotherRequested` is deliberately left alone (no decision was recorded, so there is nothing
to collapse), and no checklist/dispatch/artifact resync fires, because none of them can have
changed. A refusal renders design-studio's own message verbatim and leaves the gate exactly as it
was.

Above the form, a **"Sent back — recorded, not decided"** panel lists every send-back recorded at
the gate the mission is sitting at, newest first, each with its timestamp and note. Deliberately not
rewind-aware, unlike `recordedOutcomeForCurrentStage`: that computed answers "is this gate already
decided for THIS visit", where a pre-rewind verdict is actively misleading; this one answers "what
has the owner said they could not evaluate here", which stays true across a rewind.

### Chronology, Now panel, queue
`GateHistoryComponent` takes a third input and renders a third row kind — dashed border, neutral
`sent back` badge, `Sent back at <gate> — not decided` — interleaved chronologically with decisions
and rewinds, and carrying no outcome badge of any kind.

`selectNowState`'s `waiting-on-you` now carries the most recent send-back recorded **at that gate**
(scoped on purpose: a note left at an earlier gate is not why the current one is stuck). The state
itself is unchanged — a sent-back gate is still waiting on the owner — and the panel appends the
reason. A send-back never changes precedence: a running dispatch still wins the panel.

`designMissionNeedsYouItems` needed no change at all: it keys off the gate stage, which a send-back
does not touch, so the mission continues to appear in the queue. A test now pins that, per the
demand's criterion.

A mission with no send-backs renders exactly as it did before: no panel, no rows, no empty state
anywhere — there is no claim to make about a gate nobody has sent back.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Third control labelled "Send back", not "Retry" | `gate-decision-form.component.html`; spec asserts the label and that "retry" appears nowhere |

# Fulfillment report — design missions in the needs-you queue

## State on arrival

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. **Not shipped, and not partially shipped.**
`NeedsYouService` had exactly five sources and no reference to `DesignStudioService` anywhere;
`Mission.designSystemBuild.failure` and `Mission.pauseRequested` were modelled and rendered on
`/design/:id` but read by nothing on the overview. All of R7 was open.

## What shipped

### The rule module (`src/app/overview/design-mission-needs-you.ts`)

A pure `designMissionNeedsYouItems(mission): NeedsYouItem[]`, kept out of the service so the
judgement about design-studio's state machine can be read and tested without an HTTP poll or a
signal graph around it. Three reasons, each its own item — a mission can legitimately be at a gate
AND paused AND carrying a dead build unit, which is three distinct owner actions and so three rows:

| condition | key | message |
|---|---|---|
| stage ∈ the five gate stages, `activeDispatch === null` | `design-gate:{id}` | `{repo} · {Gate label} is waiting on your decision` |
| `designSystemBuild.failure !== null` | `design-build-failure:{id}` | `{repo} · design-system build attempt failed on {unit} (batch {n}) — needs an owner` |
| `pauseRequested` | `design-paused:{id}` | `{repo} · mission is paused and waiting to be resumed` |

All three link to `/design/{id}`. Keys are `reason:id` — the same `key:id` shape the five existing
sources use, stable across polls, so a mission sitting at a gate never churns the badge.

Gate membership and terminality are read from `mission-stage.ts`'s existing `isGateStage` /
`isTerminalStage`, which already mirror design-studio's own `GATE_STAGES` — no second copy of the
set was invented here.

Two exclusions, both deliberate:

- **Terminal missions** (`closed`, `aborted`) produce nothing, whatever else is set on them — a
  terminal mission is a record and no owner action is outstanding on it.
- **A gate with a dispatch in flight** produces no gate item: at `system-gate` a design-system
  build genuinely runs under the gate, and an agent working is not the owner being blocked. The
  failed-build item is deliberately *not* gated on `activeDispatch` — design-studio does not report
  a dead run as an active dispatch, and clears `failure` itself the moment a retry dispatches, so
  the two fields are read independently exactly as its own model docs describe.

### The judgement call, stated in the code

The demand asked for one decision to be made deliberately and written down: whether a mission
merely READY TO RUN a mechanical step (`harvest`, `brief`, `coverage`, `plan`) counts. It is
**EXCLUDED**, per the demand's lean, and the reasoning is in the module docstring rather than a
commit message: the badge is defined as "the count of things waiting on you" and is only useful
while every row is something the owner must *decide*, not something anyone could press. Including
runnable steps would make a mission contribute an item at nearly every stage of its life and the
count would stop meaning anything. The docstring also names the revisit condition — if missions are
observed idling at a runnable step for long stretches, the honest fix is to add it here, or better,
to make the step self-drive server-side.

### The service wiring

A sixth source in `NeedsYouService`: its own `timer(0, this.consoleSettings.demandBoardPollMs())`
over `DesignStudioService.missions()`, with its own `missions` / `missionsSettled` /
`designStudioError` signals. No new cadence knob — this is the same `demandBoardPollMs()` and the
same per-source independent-timer idiom the board and pending-approval polls already use. The
source is read-only: one `GET /missions`, no writes to design-studio, and a spec asserts every
request the queue makes to the design-studio origin is a `GET`.

Independence matches the service's existing posture exactly: a failed missions poll keeps the last
known missions rather than dropping to zero, sets `designStudioError`, and never touches the other
five sources' signals. `state()` now reads a new `sourceError` (`coordinatorError ?? design-studio`),
so a design-studio outage caveats the queue the same way a coordinator outage always has — and
still renders `error` rather than a dishonest "Nothing needs you." when it is the *only* thing that
could have produced items.

### The badge

Nothing was needed: `StatusStripComponent`'s needs-you slot already reads
`NeedsYouService.count`, which is `items().length`. The new items are in the badge by construction.

### Testids

`data-testid="needs-you-queue"` and the `state-*` hooks are untouched. One new hook,
`data-testid="needs-you-caveat"`, was added alongside its spec — the caveat line now names which
service is unreachable ("Some items may be missing — design-studio is unreachable right now")
instead of always saying `demand-coordinator`, which would have been a lie once a sixth source
could fail.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **186 files, 1796 tests, all green** (baseline was 185 / 1781; +1 file, +15 tests).
- `ng build` — clean (the pre-existing initial-bundle budget warning is unchanged).
- Three sibling specs (`status-strip`, `overview`, and the queue's own) had their
  `httpMock.verify()` flushes extended for the new request; no assertion in any of them was
  weakened or removed.

## Not done / worth knowing

- Not verified live against a running design-studio. Everything here is covered by specs against
  design-studio's documented response shape (`Mission`, `DesignSystemBuild.failure`,
  `ActiveDispatch`), and the demand states CORS is already granted and verified for that origin —
  but the first real poll against the live service is still unobserved from this session.
- The queue does not order design items relative to the other five; they append after the existing
  sources, matching how each source already appends in turn. If the queue ever grows long enough
  that ordering matters, that is a separate design question for the whole widget, not this source.

# Fulfillment report — the phase spine and the Now panel

**Not previously shipped.** The state check at session start found R3 (the artifact readers) as the
newest design work on `main` (`c083444`, archived `a413372`); nothing in the repo carried a phase
spine, a Now panel, a scope clamp or a demoted Kill mission. This is new work.

## One thing the owner should know first

**This branch contains PR #27.** Two acceptance criteria of this demand — the `build` dispatch kind
and `designSystemBuild.failure` — name shapes that exist on `main` nowhere: they live on
`demand/build-dispatch-visibility-followup` (PR #27, open since 2026-07-28 08:34), this repo's own
owed follow-up on its own already-approved demand
`dashboard-20260728-design-studio-build-dispatch-visibility`. The Now panel's "an attempt died"
state cannot be written without `failure`, and its "waiting on an agent, kind `build`" state cannot
be written without the kind.

Rather than re-mirror those two shapes in a second commit (which would have conflicted with #27 on
sight), this branch **merges #27** (`151b950`) and builds R4 on top (`bab6955`). Merging this PR
therefore lands #27 as well. If that is not wanted, #27 should be merged first and this branch
rebased — the two commits are cleanly separated either way.

## Against each acceptance criterion

1. **Three phases with the doc's labels** — `MISSION_PHASES` in `mission-phases.ts`: *1 · the design
   system* (harvest, theme interview, system gate, clone), *2 · the propositions* (content interview,
   brief, theme gate, coverage gate, plan gate), *3 · the build* (executing, feel gate, closed). The
   stage ORDER is never re-declared: `mission-phases.spec.ts` asserts `phasedStages()` equals
   `STAGE_SEQUENCE`, so a stage added server-side surfaces as a failing test, not a silent omission.
2. **One-line subtitles** — quoted verbatim from the overview diagram's own second text line
   (`harvest` → *mechanical repo scan*, `clone` → *pinned system@version*), rendered under every
   stage in the spine and in the Now panel's header. Never paraphrased: the doc is owner-validated
   wording and this repo is not its author.
3. **Kind, never colour alone** — `StageKind` is `mechanical | agent | gate | terminal`, read off the
   diagram's own `c-gray`/`c-purple`/`c-coral`/`c-teal` groups one box at a time (two readings worth
   noting: `brief` is gray, and `executing` is purple — only `closed` is teal). It is carried by a
   distinct shape per kind (`▪ ◆ ▲ ●`) paired with the kind's NAME in the element's accessible name
   and its title, with the token only reinforcing. The four-way legend renders on the page, with what
   each kind means for the reader ("a dispatched session — wait", "moves only on your recorded
   decision — act").
4. **Console tokens, not diagram hex** — `stageKindClass` maps the four meanings onto the tokens this
   console already uses for the same meanings (`ink-muted`, `status-starting`, `status-degraded`,
   `status-up` — the same "borrow the status-\* tokens for a non-health chip" idiom `stageChipClass`
   already uses). A spec asserts no `#rrggbb` ever appears and that the four are distinct.
   `diagram-conventions.md` §1's rule is honoured literally: the four meanings are preserved, the
   values differ, and no semantic colour was changed.
5. **Current stage by position, not colour** — a `▸` marker in a reserved gutter (so nothing shifts
   between rows), a "now" badge, and `aria-current="step"`, asserted to appear on exactly one stage.
   The collapsed narrow reading deliberately does NOT carry a second `aria-current`.
6. **Readable narrow** — a fixed `md:grid md:grid-cols-3` (one column per phase, one stage per row):
   the columns narrow, the row count never changes, so the ragged `flex-wrap` at ~976px cannot recur.
   Below `md` (~768px) it collapses to three phase rows with per-phase progress and the current stage
   named. A spec asserts both halves and that `flex-wrap` is gone.
7. **One state at a time** — `selectNowState` returns a discriminated union; the panel spec renders
   seven differently-shaped missions and asserts exactly one state element is present each time.
8. **Waiting on an agent, `build` included** — kind label, run id, dispatch state, and elapsed. One
   honest deviation worth naming: **`ActiveDispatch` carries `{runId, kind, state}` and no timestamp
   of any kind**, so a true run age does not exist client-side. `observedElapsedLabel` reports how
   long THIS page has SEEN the run in flight, labelled as such ("seen running ~4m on this page"), and
   returns nothing below one minute rather than implying precision it lacks. Inventing a start time
   from the first poll that happened to observe the run would have been exactly the invented run
   state design law 2 forbids.
9. **A dispatched unit died** — a non-null `designSystemBuild.failure` is its own state, ranked above
   "an agent is working", naming the batch, the unit, the run id (or saying none was recorded) and
   what to do: press Build design system to retry, and nothing restarts by itself.
10. **Paused** — its own state, ranked above a running dispatch, worded to `design-mission.md` §2's
    two halves as corrected by the pause-semantics doc-sync: new spending stops right away, the
    background advancer starts nothing further (not even the next page inside a batch already in
    progress), a hand-driven call comes to rest at a batch boundary and never mid-batch, and anything
    already dispatched runs to completion. At the four stages with no server-side consumer of the
    flag it says exactly that instead — never a claim the console cannot support.
11. **Waiting on you** — at a gate the panel leads with the decision, and the page order was changed
    so the gate-decision form is the very next section (asserted: it now precedes plan/matrix,
    artifacts and history, and Kill mission).
12. **Ready to run** — every step named in plain language ("Assemble the interface brief from the
    harvest and the interview answers"); a spec asserts no step action contains `POST`, `GET` or a
    leading `/`. The raw route is not deleted — it stays as the small print on the run-step section
    where it always was.
13. **Terminal** — closed and aborted each render a summary (gate decisions, rounds, rewinds, pinned
    system, or the recorded abort reason) and offer no action; the panel contains zero buttons in
    that state, and the footer still reports honestly that a closed mission cannot be aborted.
14. **Kill mission demoted** — moved to a `<footer>` below every panel that carries actual work
    (asserted against five of them by DOM order), visually quieter, with the class-3 typed-`ABORT`
    confirmation, the optional reason field and the honest `runStop` rendering untouched.
15. **Scope clamped** — out of the meta line into its own block, clamped to three lines with a
    "Show full scope (N characters)" toggle. **Clamped, never truncated**: the whole string stays in
    the DOM, so find-in-page and screen readers reach every word either way. A short scope gets no
    affordance; an empty scope renders nothing at all.
16. **No capability removed** — the gate decision form and its checklist, plan, coverage matrix,
    rounds and theme propositions, the three R3 artifact readers, the system build panel, gate
    history, abort, pause, the rewinds display and the run-step action all still render and still
    work. A spec asserts the section list; the pre-existing 108 mission-detail cases pass unchanged.
17. **No console-side policy** — `selectNowState` reads `stage`, `pauseRequested`, `activeDispatch`
    and `designSystemBuild.failure`, plus `mission-stage.ts`'s existing pure lookups. It decides
    which fact to say first; it never decides what the pipeline may do next, and every action it
    names is one the page already offered.
18. **Testids and suite** — every pre-existing `data-testid` on the touched surfaces is still present
    (`stage-progress`, `stage-progress-step`, `stage-progress-gate-badge`,
    `stage-progress-skipped-badge`, `abort-mission-*`, `run-step-*`, `gate-*`, `pause-*`,
    `system-build-*`). **1683/1683 green**; production build clean. That is the 1618 baseline + 8
    from the merged PR #27 + 57 new.

## Two small things changed beyond the letter of the demand

- **`headerDispatch` now also requires a non-null `designSystemBuild`.** PR #27 suppressed the header
  tag for a `build` dispatch at `system-gate` on the grounds that the build panel renders it — but
  that panel's liveness section only exists once the build projection has landed, so a build dispatch
  arriving before it would have shown nowhere at all. Tightened, with the reasoning in a comment.
- **Every mission write now goes through one `setMission`**, which timestamps the dispatch
  observation feeding the elapsed reading. It records nothing else and derives no state.

## Not in scope, per the demand's own exclusions

Gate workspaces (R5), a rewind trigger (R6 — the rewinds *history* still renders), and any change to
`NeedsYouService` (R7) were left alone.

A Rewind panel on /design/:id beside the gate history: target picker, optional direction free-text with its synthetic-record note, class-3 typed REWIND confirmation, verbatim refusal rendering, and a recorded-rewind confirmation read back from design-studio's own response
NowPanelComponent.gateFormVisible -- the gate copy now names the recorded-outcome card and its Record another decision button when that, not the form, is what renders below

Artifact JSON reads (plan/matrix/harvest/brief + the interview naming walk and its questionnaire half) gated on GET /missions/{id}/artifacts, with an unconditional fallback when the listing itself cannot be read

# Fulfillment report — the rewind control, coverage gaps, and three honesty fixes

## State on arrival

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. One of the three parts was **already shipped**:

- **§2 — the coverage gate renders `matrix.json`'s `gaps`: ALREADY DONE.** `MatrixViewComponent`
  carries `gaps()`, the template renders `matrix-gaps` / `matrix-gaps-heading` / `matrix-gap`, and
  `matrix-gaps-covered` renders an **empty** array as *"No gaps — every item in the brief is covered
  by a mock."* — full coverage, not an empty region — with an **absent** `gaps` field claiming
  nothing at all. Landed by the session that fulfilled
  `design-studio-20260728-dashboard-theme-gate-workspace` (§4 of that demand), and covered by
  `matrix-view.component.spec.ts`'s own `MatrixViewComponent — gaps` block. Nothing was redone.

Everything else was genuinely absent: `DesignStudioService` had no `rewind` method at all, the Now
panel's gate copy was unconditional, and `loadAll` fired every artifact read blind.

## What shipped

### 1 · The rewind control

`POST /missions/{id}/rewind` now has a console caller. The rules are design-studio's, mirrored:

- **Targets are strictly-earlier gate stages** from `REWIND_TARGET_STAGES` (`theme-gate`,
  `coverage-gate`, `plan-gate`, `feel-gate`), resolved by index in `STAGE_SEQUENCE`. From
  `plan-gate` the picker offers `theme-gate` and `coverage-gate`; from `feel-gate`, three; never the
  stage the mission already sits at.
- **`system-gate` is never offered, from any stage.** It is in `GATE_STAGES` and deliberately not in
  `REWIND_TARGET_STAGES`, because D069's **OQ6 is still an open owner ruling**. A test asserts this
  across every member of `STAGE_SEQUENCE`, so a future edit cannot quietly pre-empt the ruling.
- **No control at all** from `theme-gate` (the earliest target has no earlier one), from `closed` or
  `aborted`, or from any stage before `theme-gate`. Each case renders its own honest sentence rather
  than a disabled control or a blank — `rewindUnavailableReason`.
- **Class 3.** The existing `ConfirmDialogComponent`, typed word `REWIND`, whose title states that
  the mission moves **BACKWARD**, that nothing is deleted, and that *every gate between the target
  and where it stood must be approved again individually, exactly as the first time through*.
- **The optional `direction`** is a free-text box carrying a permanent note that a direction given
  for a **theme-gate** rewind ALSO lands as a synthetic REJECTED theme-gate record which the next
  propose round consumes as binding §8bis law (D067, "zero new machinery"). The confirmation repeats
  that sentence for exactly the one request shape that produces one — a theme-gate target with a
  non-empty direction — and never for any other, which would be a false claim about the write.
  A blank direction is **omitted from the body entirely**, never sent as `''` or `null`.
- **All four refusals render verbatim.** A forward target, the current stage itself, a non-gate
  target (including the distinct "a gate but not a rewind target" wording) and any target from a
  terminal stage all come back as one 409 `RewindRefusedError` whose `{error}` string
  `describeDesignStudioError` passes through unchanged, naming `currentStage`/`to`/`reason`. The
  dialog closes, the control re-arms, and the rest of the page keeps rendering.
- **The history rendering is untouched.** `GateHistoryComponent` and `rounds.ts` were not modified;
  a rewind recorded through the new control appears in the existing history, and
  `isRewindSyntheticRecord` continues to keep the synthetic theme-gate record from being counted a
  second time as an independent owner verdict — asserted directly in the new end-to-end test.

The panel sits next to the gate history it complements, above the footer's Kill mission: rarer than
a gate decision, not as final as an abort. The success line is read back from design-studio's own
response (`mission.rewinds.at(-1)`), never the request echoed.

### 2 · Coverage gaps

Already shipped — see *State on arrival*. Verified live against the existing tests, not re-derived.

### 3 · The three honesty fixes

- **The Now panel no longer over-promises at a decided gate.** `NowPanelComponent` takes
  `gateFormVisible`, `MissionDetailComponent`'s own signal, passed in rather than re-derived (it
  depends on the page-local `recordAnotherRequested`, which the panel cannot see). When the form is
  what renders, the copy is exactly what it always was; when the recorded-outcome card is what
  renders, the panel names that card and its **Record another decision** button instead. Both
  wordings still say the stage moves only on a recorded decision — the fix is the pointer, not the
  rule.
- **Artifact readers ask only for listed files.** `loadAll` now issues `GET /missions/{id}/artifacts`
  first and hands the resulting name set to `loadArtifactReaders`, which fires `plan.json`,
  `matrix.json`, `harvest.json`, `brief.json` and the interview naming walk (plus its questionnaire
  half) only for files the listing actually names. An unlisted file goes straight to the same
  `absent` state a 404 produced, so the rendering is byte-for-byte what it was without the round
  trip. Driving `e8e4b3e5`'s exact shape — a mission at `theme-interview` with an empty listing —
  now issues **zero** artifact reads where it previously issued five.
  **Fail-safe:** when the listing itself fails (unreachable, 5xx), every read fires unconditionally,
  exactly as before. A page that cannot read the listing must not silently claim every artifact is
  absent. The 404 branch of the naming walk is kept unchanged for the stale-listing case.

### 4 · Test hooks and the suite

Every pre-existing `data-testid` is still present. One test changed premise rather than assertion:
`'rewind-target picker (item 6, out of scope) is unaffected'` asserted that **no** rewind testid
existed anywhere, which was true only while the picker did not exist. It is rewritten to assert what
now actually holds and is the point of the criterion — at `system-gate` no target select renders and
the honest unavailable note does, i.e. `system-gate` is not offered as a rewind target.

The `mission-detail` spec harness (`flushInitial`, `flushArtifactReaders`,
`flushInitialAtSystemGate`) was updated once, centrally, to answer the artifact listing before the
reads and to expect a read only for a listed file — deriving the listing from whatever bodies the
call site passed, so all 114 `flushInitial` call sites keep asserting exactly what they did.

New tests: 8 in `mission-stage.spec.ts` (target set, strict-earlier, never-system-gate across the
whole sequence, terminal/theme-gate/pre-theme-gate unavailability), 3 in
`design-studio.service.spec.ts` (body shape with and without `direction`, the 409 left as a real
error), 3 in `now-panel.component.spec.ts` (both copies, and the rule that survives both), and 14 in
`mission-detail.component.spec.ts` (picker contents, unavailability, the POST behind the typed
confirm, the direction + synthetic-record confirmation, history without double-counting, four
verbatim refusals, cancel, disabled-until-chosen, and three artifact-gating cases).

```
Test Files  185 passed (185)
Tests       1781 passed (1781)
```

# Fulfillment report — drive the create-new design-system build from the console

## State before this session

Verified first, per the demand's own "check current state" instruction: `grep -rn
'designSystemBuild\|build-system'` over `src/app` returned nothing, and `pipelineRouteFor('system-gate')`
still returned `null`. Nothing had been shipped by a prior session — the capability was built from
scratch here.

## What shipped, per acceptance criterion

**1 — the action exists for a create-new mission at system-gate.** `/design/:id` renders a
`system-build-section` whenever the mission is at `system-gate` with `createDesignSystem: true`. Inside
it, a **Build design system** button (`data-testid="build-system-button"`) is shown exactly when
`canBuildDesignSystem` holds — design-studio's own three server-side preconditions mirrored for
*visibility only* (at `system-gate`, create-new, not yet pinned). It is a client-side visibility
choice, never a gate on the POST: any mission that fails a precondition still gets the server's honest
409 rendered verbatim if the call is issued. Mission `e8e4b3e5-ef0c-46b1-8a76-57c4126f219d` is exactly
this shape and is now drivable from the console with no curl step.

Deliberately kept OUT of `pipelineRouteFor`/"Run next step": that button's whole contract is "advance
the mission", and `build-system` never advances the stage. It is its own action, in its own panel,
labelled so it does not read as a next-step.

**2 — no body, progressive, re-renders from the response.** `DesignStudioService.buildSystem` POSTs
`{}` and returns the full `Mission`. The component writes that response straight into the `mission`
signal; the spec asserts `httpMock.expectNone(missionUrl(...))` after a settle, so a follow-up GET is
mechanically excluded, not just intended.

**3 — same poll cadence, no double-POST.** The build uses the identical `timer(0, POLL_MS)` self-driving
idiom `onRunNextStep`'s progressive branch already uses (`POLL_MS = 3000`, unchanged, no second
mechanism introduced). `buildSystemPending` disables the button for the whole flight and swaps its label
to `Building…`; a mid-flight click is a no-op (asserted). The poll stops when `isSystemBuildSettled`
holds — `done`, `paused`, or a `null` projection in the response — the three states in which a further
POST provably does no work (`run_build`'s own early returns). Once settled the label becomes
`Continue build`, since a second run genuinely continues rather than starts.

**4 — the exact projection.** `DesignSystemBuild` carries `designSystemId`, `slug`, `name`,
`currentBatch`, `done`, `paused`, `batches[{batch, name, status, pagesTotal, pagesConsolidated}]`,
`reentry`, mirrored field-for-field from `design_system_build_projection`
(`domain/design_system_build.py:942-982`). Two deliberate typing choices, both documented in the model:
`status` is `string`, not a `'pending' | 'consolidated'` union, because the projection's own docstring
says the underlying tracking shape may change and an unknown value must render itself back honestly
(design law 3); `reentry` is typed as its real `{rejectionsSeen, enteredAtBatch, directionExcerpt, at}`
object, read from `_apply_reentry_if_needed`.

**5 — the progress panel.** `SystemBuildPanelComponent` renders all four batches by name (0
constitution, 1 components, 2 patterns-guidelines, 3 assembly-qa) with per-batch status and
`pagesConsolidated/pagesTotal`, marking `currentBatch` (`data-current="true"` + a `current` badge). A
`null` projection renders an explicit not-started body — the four batches greyed, status "not started",
no fabricated page counts — never a blank region and never an error. The fixed four are a scaffold only:
wherever the server reported a batch, the server's own name and status win, and a projection reporting
fewer than four batches renders the reported ones and leaves the rest honestly statusless (covered by a
spec).

**6 — paused and reentry.** `paused` renders its own chip plus an explanatory note ("stopped at a batch
boundary, not mid-batch; further calls do no work until the pause is cleared") and is mutually exclusive
with the done/in-progress chips. `reentry` renders as its own §8bis block: the batch it was rewound to,
how many rejections were consumed, the timestamp, and the `directionExcerpt` verbatim.

**7 — Request-pause at the stage that honors it.** `system-gate` added to `PAUSE_RELEVANT_STAGES`. The
four existing stages are kept, as the demand asked, but the panel no longer lets one button imply the
same effect in both cases: a new `isPauseHonoredStage` (true for `system-gate` alone —
`DesignSystemBuildService` at `design_system_build.py:667`/`:806` is the only `pause_requested` reader in
the service) drives two different notes and two different chip texts. At `system-gate`: "the
design-system build reads this flag at every batch boundary". At the other four: "Nothing at this stage
reads this flag yet… it is recorded honestly, but no work here stops because of it."

**8 — all three 409s.** `describeDesignStudioError`'s existing uniform `{error}` handling already renders
design-studio's error text verbatim, and all three of this route's 409s use that same body shape
(`DesignSystemBuildImmutableError` additionally carries `designSystemId`, which is not needed beyond the
message). A parameterized spec covers all three and asserts the page stays usable afterwards: the panel
still shows the last good progress, the gate panel is intact, the action is re-armed, and the poll has
stopped rather than retrying into the same error.

**9 — the gate itself is untouched.** No change to the system-gate checklist fetch, its 3 items, or the
binding-direction note; a spec pins both.

**10 — suite.** Baseline was 173 files / 1532 tests. Now **176 files / 1580 tests, all green**
(`npm test -- --run`), plus a clean `npm run build`. No existing `data-testid` was removed. Three were
deliberately changed in meaning and updated together with their specs: `pause-requested-chip`'s text is
now stage-dependent, and `pause-honored-note`/`pause-unhonored-note` are new siblings in the same panel.

## Honest limits

- **Not live-driven.** The console path is unit-tested end to end against mocked HTTP, but no real build
  was run against design-studio for mission `e8e4b3e5` from this session. Driving that build — and
  recording the real `design-system-build.json` and populated payload — is the demand's own "what we do
  once closed", design-studio's step, and it dispatches billable agent work that is not this repo's to
  trigger unasked.
- **`activeDispatch` still cannot show a running build** (`find_pending_dispatch` has no `system-gate`
  branch). The panel therefore never claims "no agent running" on the strength of it — per-batch status
  and page counts are the only progress signal it renders, exactly as the demand's own scope note
  requires. That is design-studio's R2, a separate raise.
- **Batch-3 semantics not specially rendered.** `assembly-qa` is mechanical (no dispatch, no LLM); the
  panel renders it with the same status/count row as the others, since the projection reports it
  identically (`pagesTotal: 1`). No claim is made either way about how it does its work.

`done` is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates.

# Fulfillment report — the theme gate as a review workspace

**Not previously shipped.** The state check at session start found R4 (the phase spine and the Now
panel) as the newest design work on `main` (`bab6955`, archived `6e8bca7`). Nothing in the repo
rendered `state-material-mapping.json` at all (it appeared only as a row in the artifacts list), no
binding direction rendered anywhere near the gate form, `ChecklistItem` carried no group, and
`Matrix.gaps` was typed and rendered nowhere. This is new work.

## What shipped, against each criterion

**1. Each theme card is paired with that theme's own mapping entry.** `state-material-mapping.ts`
parses the file; `ThemePropositionsComponent` renders one table per card — one row per domain state,
columns `visualProperty` / `inspectionReveals` / `nonVisualTwin` — beneath the theme's own iframe.

**2. Scoped to the SELECTED round.** The fetch is `<selectedRoundDir>/state-material-mapping.json`,
where `selectedRoundDir` is the existing `Mission.rounds.roundDirs[n - 1]` the theme cards themselves
are already scoped by: `proposals/` for round 1, `proposals-round-N/` after. It re-fetches the moment
the round selector moves, and a response arriving for a round the owner has since left is discarded
rather than rendered (`loadedMappingDir` guard). Covered by a test that switches rounds and asserts
round 3's "Comet Field" is gone and round 1's own theme is in its place.

**3. Name + signature/technique with the card.** Both render above the meta line. The descriptor key
is `signature` in round 2 and `technique` in round 3 of the real `bd3f8e95` artifacts and absent
entirely in round 1 — all three shapes are read, the third rendering the name alone.

**4. Whatever state keys the file carries.** Any object-valued key that isn't `name`/`signature`/
`technique` and carries at least one of the three judged fields is a row, in the file's own key
order. Nothing in this repo names `error`/`empty`/`loading`/`dimension.event`/`state.event` — they
come out of the file, which is what makes it work for a mission whose brief yields a different set.

**5. A round with no mapping.** A 404 (and a file that parses to no usable theme entry) renders the
theme cards unchanged plus one sentence saying the round has no mapping. A real read failure says
that instead, naming the error. Neither is a blank region and neither is an error state on the round
view.

**6. Binding direction at the point of decision.** At `theme-gate`, `BindingDirectionComponent`
renders above the gate form: every earlier round's rejection notes plus every rewind direction,
merged and numbered oldest-first — the order design-studio's own §8bis fold-in consumes them in —
each attributed ("Round 1 rejected …", "Rewound from plan-gate …"). `bindingDirections` reads rewinds
from `Mission.rewinds` rather than from the synthetic `GateRecord` that `Mission.rewind()` appends at
the same instant, so `bd3f8e95`'s "use particle js, and start from theme-c, and use green in palette"
appears exactly once. A rejection attributed to the LATEST round is excluded: that is a decision
already recorded on this round, not direction that shaped it — it keeps rendering in the round
selector's note and in the gate history, both untouched.

**7. Source per checklist item.** Already rendered before this demand; now carries its own
`data-testid` and is asserted in both the grouped and the flat branch.

**8. Grouping is conditional on the data.** design-studio's `ChecklistItem` now carries `group` and
`groupLabel` in source (`domain/regime.py`, `api.py`) — but its LIVE deployment on `:8087` does not
yet serve them (verified this session: `GET /missions/bd3f8e95-…/checklist` returns
`key`/`text`/`source` only). So the console renders flat today and will render grouped the moment
that deployment catches up, with no further change here. No section boundary is held in this repo;
the heading is the API's own `groupLabel`, falling back to the slug rather than titlecasing it; and a
response where only SOME items carry a group renders flat rather than orphaning the rest.

**9. Coverage gate gaps.** Rendered under the matrix table. `bd3f8e95`'s live `matrix.json` carries
`gaps: []`, which now reads "No gaps — every item in the brief is covered by a mock." rather than
nothing at all. A non-empty array lists the tags; an absent field renders nothing, claiming neither
coverage nor holes.

**10. Submission unchanged.** No change to `GateDecisionSubmission`, the notes field, the approve and
reject actions, the class-3 typed confirmation, or the system-gate binding note. A test asserts the
emitted payload is the same flat `key -> boolean` map when the checklist is grouped.

**11. Existing behaviour preserved.** The round selector, the iframes and their open-in-new-tab
links, the recorded-outcome card and "Record another decision", and the R4 spine and Now panel all
keep their existing tests, unmodified.

**12. Tests.** Every existing `data-testid` is still present and unchanged. The suite: **185 files,
1727 tests green** (baseline 183/1683 — two new spec files, +44 cases). `npm run build` is clean
(the pre-existing initial-bundle budget warning is unchanged).

## Live checks run this session (read-only)

- `GET /missions/bd3f8e95-…/artifacts/proposals-round-3/state-material-mapping.json` → `200`,
  `application/json`, and with `Origin: http://localhost:4200` it answers
  `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200` — the console can read it from the browser
  today, no design-studio change needed.
- `GET /missions/bd3f8e95-…/checklist` → items without `group` (see criterion 8).
- `GET /missions/bd3f8e95-…/artifacts/matrix.json` → `gaps: []`.

No live browser click-through was run: the mapping and gaps paths are exercised against fixtures
trimmed verbatim from the real artifacts on disk, and the one thing a browser session would have
added — that the artifact reads work cross-origin — is the CORS check above.

## Notes for design-studio

- The `group`/`groupLabel` fields of demand `dashboard-20260728-design-studio-checklist-groups` are
  in design-studio's source but not in its running deployment. The console is ready for them; nothing
  further is owed here once that deployment ships.
- `state-material-mapping.json` has no schema and two live namings for the theme descriptor
  (`signature`, `technique`) plus a round-1 shape carrying neither. This console reads all three and
  will keep doing so; if a canonical key is ever chosen, that is a design-studio decision, not a
  reason for a demand back.

## Out of scope, as the demand states

No rewind trigger control (R6), no `NeedsYouService` (R7), and no change to how a gate decision is
submitted or recorded.

# Fulfillment report — let the owner unblock a build that has given up

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. Nothing had been shipped by a prior session: a grep
for `unblock`, `qaOverride` and `blocked` as *data* across `src/app/design` and `src/app/overview`
returned only prose in comments, exactly as the demand said. `DesignSystemBuild` carried
`designSystemId`/`slug`/`name`/`currentBatch`/`done`/`paused`/`batches`/`reentry`/`failure` and
neither of the two projection fields. This was full build work.

## What shipped, against each acceptance criterion

**Mission model mirrors both fields.** `DesignSystemBuildBlocked` and `DesignSystemBuildQaOverride`
are typed exactly as the projection ships them, each `| null` on `DesignSystemBuild`, with the
failure-vs-blocked distinction written into the doc comment rather than left tribal.

**Blocked is its own terminal state, textually and visually distinct.** The chip reads
`blocked — nothing retries` in the terminal (status-down, filled) styling, next to the existing
done/paused/in-progress chips it now sits beside as a fourth mutually exclusive case. The body block
says the build *has given up*, that nothing retries it, and that only the owner can restart it. The
existing failure rendering — whose own last line is "run the build again to retry that unit" — is
deliberately **suppressed** while blocked rather than rendered beside it: the two carry opposite
instructions, and two readings with one of them wrong is worse than either alone.

**The blocked rendering names unit, batch, attempts and reason** — all four plus the `at` timestamp,
read straight off the projection, nothing derived.

**Unblock calls the endpoint and is offered only while blocked is non-null.** The buttons live
*inside* the panel's blocked block, so they structurally cannot exist in any other state; a spec
asserts their absence on a non-blocked build.

**Both shapes, as an explicit owner choice.** Two buttons, never one: *Unblock — retry this unit*
(`acceptQaFindings` omitted from the body entirely) and *Unblock — accept the QA findings*
(`acceptQaFindings: true`). A line under them states each one's meaning in the demand's own words —
"I fixed the underlying problem, or it was transient" / "I have READ the QA report and accept these
findings as they are" — and says the retry gets a full fresh attempt budget.

**The note is offered and sent on both.** On the class-3 path it is the dialog's own optional reason
field. The class-2 dialog has no reason field, so the note textarea is projected into the dialog's
existing `ng-content` extra slot (the same mechanism the brain dispatch pickers use) rather than
adding a class-2 reason mode to the shared component. An empty/whitespace note is not sent at all —
an empty string is not a record of anything.

**Accepting QA findings is class 3 with the existing typed-confirmation dialog.** Typed word
`ACCEPT`. The confirmation title states plainly that it records a DURABLE owner override accepting
known-failing QA findings on this design system, that it is written into its `qa-report.json`, that
the system will be pinned and cloned into a product repo, and that nothing is fixed by it.

**A recorded qaOverride is rendered afterwards**, with its timestamp and note (and an honest "no note
was recorded" when there is none). It renders whatever the build's current state is — including a
`done: true` build, which is exactly what an owner sees at system-gate — because it is a durable fact
about the system being judged, not a transient banner.

**The QA report's own `ownerOverride` is not contradicted.** The console reads no `qa-report.json`
today (no reader exists), so there is nothing to contradict; the override rendering asserts only what
the projection says and explicitly names the report as carrying the same override. It never claims QA
passed, and the build's own chips continue to describe batch consolidation, never QA verdicts.

**The needs-you queue distinguishes the two.** `designMissionNeedsYouItems` gains a
`design-build-blocked:` source that names unit, batch, attempts and "nothing retries until you unblock
it" — and it **suppresses** the `design-build-failure:` row for the same build, since the same dead
unit is usually behind both and two rows would double-count one problem while the weaker of them
understated it. A failing-but-not-blocked build produces the failure row exactly as before.

**Refusals render verbatim and leave the page usable.** The write goes through the shared
`describeDesignStudioError` classifier into its own alert region under the panel; a spec drives the
"not actually blocked" 409 and asserts the message text, the dialog closing, the blocked block still
being there from the last good response, and the buttons still enabled.

**Existing behaviour preserved.** Progress panel, batch rendering, paused state and note, 8bis
reentry display, and the R11 validate-and-pin flow are all untouched and still covered by their own
unmodified specs.

**Testids.** All existing hooks are unchanged. New: `system-build-blocked`, `-chip`, `-headline`,
`-reason`, `-at`, `system-build-unblock-retry-button`, `system-build-unblock-accept-qa-button`,
`system-build-unblock-note`, `system-build-unblock-error`, `system-build-qa-override`, `-headline`,
`-note`, `-no-note`, `unblock-retry-note-input`.

## One judgement call worth flagging

`isSystemBuildAdvancing` (the read-only poll's arming condition) now also returns `false` for a
blocked build — polling it would be watching for an event that by construction cannot arrive, since
design-studio's `_is_carryable` skips the mission entirely. Both that guard and the panel read the two
new fields with `?? null`, never `=== null`, so a projection predating either field reads as "not
blocked" rather than blocked-by-absence.

## Verification

`npm test`: **186 files, 1815 tests green** (baseline 1796 + 19 new). `npm run build`: clean, with
only the pre-existing initial-bundle budget warning. Not exercised against a live blocked build —
none exists yet, which is the demand's own point; every state is driven from the projection shapes
design-studio documented.
