# Fulfillment report — let a create-new mission be validated, pinned and approved from the console

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. Nothing had been shipped by a prior session:

- `grep -rn "retire" src/app` matched only status *labels*/*filters* and unrelated decision-code links;
  the string `/validate` appeared nowhere as a call.
- `DesignSystemService` had exactly two methods, both `GET`.
- `GateDecisionRequest` was `{outcome, notes, checklist}` — no `designSystemId` field existed, so the
  console could not send one.
- `mission-detail.component.ts:577`'s `systemPin()` was still guarded on `mission.designSystemId !== null`,
  and was the only link to a design system anywhere on the mission page.

The capability was built from scratch here.

## What shipped, per acceptance criterion

**1 — the system is reachable while the mission is still unpinned.** `builtSystemId()` resolves from
`designSystemBuild.designSystemId` — populated the moment the build STARTS — and is non-null exactly
while `Mission.designSystemId` is still `null`. It renders a `built-system-link` to
`/design/systems/:id` inside the system-build section, i.e. at the gate, at the moment the review
happens. `systemPin()` is untouched and takes over unchanged once the approval lands (verified by test:
after approval the pin link shows `v1.0.0` and `built-system-link` is gone).

**2 — the link reaches the rendered documentation.** A second link, `built-system-docs-link`, points at
`GET /design-systems/{id}/files/index.html` via the existing `designSystemFileUrl` helper —
`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, the same posture the design-systems screen's own
open-in-new-tab link already takes. The registry row and the docs are both one click away.

**3 — validate at the gate.** A `validate-built-system-button` in the same panel calls
`POST /design-systems/{id}/validate` behind a class-3 typed `VALIDATE` confirmation. It never navigates:
a test checks a box and types notes BEFORE validating, and asserts both survive the round-trip, with
the status chip flipping `Draft → Validated` and Approve arming — from the response, never a re-fetch.

**4 — validate and retire on the design-systems detail screen.** A new
`design-system-transitions-section` offers Validate (draft only) and Retire (draft or validated); a
retired entry offers neither and says so rather than rendering an empty row. Both re-render from the
POST response.

**5 — class-3 with the existing typed-confirmation dialog.** Both screens use the shared
`ConfirmDialogComponent` with `[dialogClass]="3"` and typed words `VALIDATE` / `RETIRE`, and both append
a class-3 `ActionLogService` entry (`VALIDATE_DESIGN_SYSTEM` / `RETIRE_DESIGN_SYSTEM`) on success and on
refusal alike. Tested: the POST does not fire until the exact word is typed.

**6 — the OPTIONAL `designSystemId`.** `gateRequestFor()` adds the field on exactly one shape of
request: `outcome === 'approved'` AND `stage === 'system-gate'` AND a non-null `builtSystemId()` (which
is itself null for any already-pinned or choose-existing mission). Everything else sends the byte-identical
body it always did — the field is ABSENT, not null. Four tests pin this: approval carries it; rejection
at system-gate does not; another gate does not; a choose-existing mission does not (and issues no
registry read at all).

**7 — after approval.** The gate response advances the mission to `clone` and the header renders the
resolved `system@version` pin through the untouched `systemPin()`.

**8 — all three refusals render verbatim.** A parameterised test drives
`SystemGateUnpinnedError`, a regime mismatch and a not-validated status through the real
`describeDesignStudioError` classifier: each renders its server text verbatim in `gate-decision-error`,
the dialog closes, the stage stays at `system-gate`, and Approve is pressable again. The validate call's
own refusal gets the same treatment (`validate-built-system-error`, status untouched, button re-armed).

**9 — the ordering is made obvious.** `approveBlockedReason()` disables Approve and states why while the
system is still `draft` ("… is still draft — design-studio pins only a validated system. Validate it
first, then approve."), or when there is nothing to pin at all. It is deliberately NARROW: only the two
states that make approval *definitionally* impossible and that this console can see with certainty. A
regime mismatch is rendered honestly (`built-system-regime-mismatch`) but does NOT block — that refusal
stays design-studio's to make. An unloaded or unreadable registry entry blocks nothing at all. Reject,
the checklist and the notes are never affected.

**10 — the three checklist items are answerable.** The panel renders the pin the approval would record
(`plantpal-e8e4b3e5@v1.0.0`), the status chip, and an explicit regime match/mismatch line — read live
from `GET /design-systems/{id}`, not inferred.

**11 — nothing else changed.** Same checklist payload (asserted key-for-key against the system-gate
checklist), same notes, same approve/reject actions, same binding-direction note, R5b grouped rendering
untouched. `GateDecisionFormComponent`'s new input defaults to `null`, which is byte-for-byte the
previous behaviour.

**12 — the suite.** `npm test`: **185 files, 1753 tests green** (baseline 1727 after R5b; +26 new).
`npm run build` clean (the pre-existing bundle-budget warning is unchanged). Every pre-existing
`data-testid` is present and unchanged.

## Implementation notes worth carrying forward

- **The registry read is driven from `setMission`**, idempotent per id, the same posture
  `syncStateMaterialMapping` already takes — the built system's id is only ever knowable from a mission
  response, and it can appear (build start) or disappear (the pin landing) on any one of them. The
  mission-detail spec gained a `flushBuiltSystem` drain in `afterEach`, mirroring the existing
  state-material-mapping drain, so unrelated tests do not have to spell out a request they do not care
  about.
- **No client-side copy of design-studio's transition rules.** Both screens decide only what to OFFER
  (a transition with nothing to do is not shown); whether a transition is legal stays server-side and is
  rendered verbatim if refused.

## Nothing was raised to another repo

Every endpoint this needed already existed; no `contracts` change, no design-studio change, no vault-
relevant fact. Console-only work, as the demand predicted.

# Fulfillment report — reference imagery attaches to a rejection and shows on the record

## State before this session

**Not shipped.** Checked first, as instructed: `referenceImages` appeared nowhere in `src/`,
`GateRecord` had no such field, and the gate decision form had no file control of any kind.

Pre-work baseline: **1854 passing, 186 files**; `ng build` already over its bundle budget
(948.18 kB vs 686.08 kB) before this work — pre-existing, verified by building a stashed tree.

## Wire format

Taken verbatim from design-studio's own fulfilment report for the paired demand
`dashboard-20260729-design-studio-reference-imagery-in-direction` — base64 in the same JSON body,
not multipart:

```json
{ "outcome": "rejected", "notes": "...", "checklist": {},
  "referenceImages": [ { "filename": "map.png", "dataBase64": "<no data: prefix>", "contentType": "image/png" } ] }
```

`contentType` is optional there and always sent here: design-studio decides the real type from the
file's magic bytes and 400s when a declared `contentType` contradicts them, so sending it makes an
honest mismatch surface as a refusal instead of being silently ignored.

## What shipped

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `design/reference-images.ts` | new — the caps, the accepted types, the per-file refusal message, the `data:` strip, the size caption |
| `design/design-studio.model.ts` | `ReferenceImageUpload`; `GateDecisionRequest.referenceImages?`; `GateRecord.referenceImages?` |
| `design/gate-decision-form.component.*` | the attach block (input, previews, per-image Remove, refusal line, upload-failure state); attachments ride `requestReject()` alone |
| `design/gate-history.component.*` | `missionId` input; per-record thumbnail strip on the existing artifact route |
| `design/mission-detail.component.*` | `gateReferenceUploadError`; the image count in the reject confirmation; `[missionId]` on the history |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Unreleased/Added entry |

### Three decisions worth stating

**"Reject path only", with no reject *mode* to hang it on.** This form has three buttons and one
shared Notes field; there is no state in which the owner has "chosen Reject" before pressing it. So
the control is a bordered block inside the reject-consequence group, headed *"Reference imagery for a
rejection — optional"* and stating outright that Approve and Send back carry none — and the code
enforces exactly that: `request()` attaches only when `outcome === 'rejected'`, and `requestSendBack()`
never reaches it at all. Making the control appear and disappear would have meant inventing a mode
this form does not have.

**Client-side validation is the form's own field check, not orchestration.** Design law 1 forbids
duplicating design-studio's pipeline rules here. These are not pipeline rules: they are upload limits
the server refuses identically with a 400 regardless, and checking them here only means the owner
learns about a 12 MB screenshot before spending a round-trip — *with the limit stated*. The one place
the client is deliberately weaker: the server sniffs magic bytes and catches a lying extension; the
browser check is the reported MIME type (falling back to the extension when the browser reports
none), so the server keeps the last word on the dishonest cases.

**Base64 is read once, at selection.** The preview `src` and the wire `dataBase64` are literally the
same bytes from the same `FileReader` result, so what the owner previewed is what gets posted — there
is no second read at submit time that could diverge.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Attach control on the REJECT path only | `gate-decision-form.component.spec.ts` — *offers the attach control…*, *never sends attachments on Approve, and never on Send back* |
| Attaching optional; no-image rejection posts as today | *a rejection with no images posts exactly the body it does today — no empty array*; `mission-detail` — *a rejection with no attachments posts and confirms exactly as it did before* |
| Type + size validated with the SAME limits, stated in the message | `reference-images.spec.ts` (9 tests, incl. the 5 MB / 6-image messages); form spec — *refuses a wrong type by name…*, *refuses past the 6-image cap…* |
| Previewable and individually removable before submit | *previews each selected image and removes one individually, before anything is submitted*; *clears the file input so the same file can be re-attached* |
| Thumbnails → full size, existing artifact route, never base64 in the payload | `gate-history.component.spec.ts` — *renders each reference as a thumbnail opening to full size…* (asserts the exact artifact URL and that the `src` is not a `data:` URL) |
| References on PRIOR rounds too | *renders references on PRIOR rounds too, not only the newest record* |
| No references → renders exactly as today | *a record with no references renders exactly as it did before — no strip, no placeholder*; plus the no-mission-id case |
| Upload failure preserves the typed note | form spec — *an upload failure is an explicit state that keeps the typed note and every selected image*; `mission-detail` — *a failed upload keeps the typed note and the selected images, and says so explicitly* |
| testids present/updated with specs; suite green with baseline | every pre-existing hook untouched; **1880 passing** (baseline **1854**, +26) |

## Not verified live

**No live end-to-end round-trip was performed this session.** design-studio's own counterpart report
records that its single real-dispatch verification is still outstanding (blocked by agent-runner's
one-live-session-per-repo lock), so the server side of this pair is not itself end-to-end confirmed
yet. Everything above is verified by the unit/integration suite against the documented wire format —
no browser was pointed at a live `:8087`, and this report does not claim otherwise. The natural live
check, once design-studio's own script has run: reject `theme-gate` on a real mission at
`http://localhost:4200/design/<id>` with a mockup attached (design-studio's CORS grant is scoped to
that exact hostname), then confirm the thumbnail on the recorded row loads from `:8087`.

# Checklist item `detail` — the doctrine's own words, on demand

## State before this session

Not shipped. `ChecklistItem` mirrored `key`/`text`/`source`/`group`/`groupLabel` only, and
`gate-decision-form.component.html` rendered exactly those. Nothing in the repo read, dropped or
displayed a `detail` field. The capability was built here for the first time.

## What was built

`GET /missions/{id}/checklist`'s optional per-item `detail` — the verbatim doctrine prose the item's
assertion label was transcribed from — is now offered beside each checklist item on the gate decision
form, behind a collapsed native `<details>` disclosure labelled `doctrine`.

- **Model** (`design-studio.model.ts`): `detail?: string | null` added to `ChecklistItem`, optional
  and nullable for the same reason `group` is — the console must render correctly against a
  design-studio deployment that predates the field, and against an item nobody has traced back to a
  paragraph yet. `DesignStudioService.checklist()` passes the response through untyped-untouched
  (`http.get<ChecklistResponse>`), so no mapping layer needed a change.
- **Component** (`gate-decision-form.component.ts`): one presentational helper, `detailOf(item)`,
  returning the trimmed prose or `null`. Absent, `null` and whitespace-only collapse to the same
  answer deliberately — an empty expander reads as prose that failed to load rather than prose that
  was never traced. It derives no rule: ticking, completeness and the submitted payload never consult
  it.
- **Template** (`gate-decision-form.component.html`): the disclosure is rendered inside the shared
  `#checklistItem` `ng-template` — the same one both the grouped and the flat branch already use via
  `ngTemplateOutlet` — so it appears identically under either branch with no per-gate or per-regime
  special case. It sits at `text-xs text-ink-subtle`/`text-ink-muted` under the `text-sm` label,
  indented `ml-6` to hang beneath the text rather than beside the checkbox.

### The one design decision worth naming

The `<summary>` is rendered **outside** the item's `<label>`, as a sibling within the `<li>`, not
inside it. A `<summary>` nested in a label is a label-associated click target: every open and every
close of the disclosure would toggle the checkbox. That would have broken "reading a detail never
alters the tick" in the exact way the demand names, silently and only in the browser. A spec now
pins it (`opening a detail never ticks its box`).

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it is met |
| --- | --- |
| Item can show its `detail` in addition to `text` | `data-testid="gate-checklist-detail"` disclosure per item carrying prose |
| `text` stays primary, never replaced/truncated/outranked | `text` untouched at `text-sm` inside the label; detail is `text-xs`, muted, below, collapsed |
| Presented on demand, not inline by default | Native `<details>`, closed by default — the console's existing disclosure idiom (`connector-vocabulary`, `brain-ratify-panel`) |
| Null/absent renders exactly as today | `detailOf` returns `null` for absent, `null` and whitespace-only; the `@if` renders no element at all — no summary, no box |
| Ticking unchanged: binary, keyed by `key`, unaffected by reading | Summary outside the label; `toggle`/`checked`/payload untouched; specs assert both the box state and the emitted map |
| Approve's all-items-checked requirement unchanged; an unopened detail never gates | No change to `requestApprove`/`approveBlockedReason`; spec approves with every detail unopened |
| Grouping by `group`/`groupLabel` and item order unaffected | Rendered inside the shared item template; spec asserts group membership counts and `data-key` order across both groups |
| Every regime + the system-gate checklist, no per-gate special case | The component is regime- and gate-agnostic (it receives `items` from `MissionDetailComponent` for both the regime checklist and `?gate=system-gate`); the disclosure is data-conditional only |
| Existing `data-testid` hooks intact | No existing hook removed or renamed. New: `gate-checklist-detail`, `gate-checklist-detail-summary`, `gate-checklist-detail-text` |

## Verification

- **Pre-work baseline:** `npm test` → **186 files / 1815 tests, all passing** (17:42).
- **After:** `npm test` → **186 files / 1821 tests, all passing** — the 6 new tests in
  `gate-decision-form.component.spec.ts` ("per-item doctrine detail"), no existing test changed.
- `npx ng build` succeeds. The initial-bundle-budget warning is pre-existing and unrelated.

## Notes for design-studio

- The console renders `detail` verbatim, with `whitespace-pre-line` — paragraph breaks in the prose
  survive; no truncation, no markdown interpretation.
- An item may send `detail` with or without `group`; the two are fully independent here.
- Nothing is sent back: `detail` is display-only and never appears in the gate decision body.

# Report — the gate decision form says what it does with the owner's note

Commit: `bb4fe14` (branch `feat/gate-action-consequences`).

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. Partly shipped, and the split matters:

- **Already shipped** — the send-back capability itself (demand
  `design-studio-20260728-dashboard-gate-send-back-control`) and its rendering. A recorded
  send-back has had its own history row since then (`gate-history-send-back-row`: dashed
  border, neutral `sent back` badge, "Sent back at \<gate\> — not decided"), deliberately
  styled as neither a verdict nor a rewind, plus a `gate-send-backs` panel above the form
  listing this gate's own send-backs under "Sent back — recorded, not decided". **AC 5 was
  therefore already met and needed no work** — it is documented here rather than redone.
- **Not shipped** — everything else. The Notes field was labelled `Notes`, full stop, with
  three controls underneath sending it to three different destinations. `system-gate` alone
  carried a §8bis binding-direction note (`gate-note-binding-text`), and only at that one
  gate. Nothing anywhere said a send-back note reaches no agent. And after a rejection the
  panel read "A new proposition round will consume this direction when /propose is re-run" —
  true, but phrased as a thing already in motion, with the control that actually starts it
  living in a different section further down the page.

## What shipped

### 1. Two destinations, stated where the owner is typing (AC 1, 2)

`gate-decision-form.component.html` — the Notes label is now "Notes — where this text goes
depends on which control you press", and directly beneath the textarea sits
`gate-note-consequences`, two plain lines in the form itself (no `title`, no tooltip, no
help link):

- `gate-note-consequence-reject` — "**If you Reject:** your note becomes binding direction
  for the next round — the next agent run reads it as law."
- `gate-note-consequence-send-back` — "**If you Send back:** your note is recorded on the
  mission and sent to no one — no agent reads it, and nothing is dispatched."

**Approve is untouched** — no third line. The demand says "Approve — unchanged", and a
third entry would dilute the exact contrast the block exists to draw.

`system-gate`'s existing §8bis sentence was *folded into* the reject line rather than left
standing above the textarea as a second paragraph: it is the same destination said more
precisely for one gate, and saying it twice on one screen is the noise this demand is
against. The `gate-note-binding-text` hook is unchanged and still present at `system-gate`
and absent everywhere else — all four pre-existing assertions on it pass untouched.

### 2. "Recording a rejection started nothing" (AC 3, 4)

`mission-detail.component.ts` — new `rejectionAwaitingNextRound`, a computed over mission
data only:

- the current visit's recorded outcome is a rejection (`recordedOutcomeForCurrentStage`,
  already rewind-aware — a pre-rewind verdict is not this visit's), **and**
- `mission.activeDispatch` is null (a running agent *is* the answer; that branch renders the
  run, unchanged), **and**
- at `theme-gate`, the rejection is not one a later round already answered.

That last clause is AC 4's "a rejection newer than the latest consolidated round".
design-studio's API carries neither a per-round timestamp nor a round↔gate-record link
(`_mission_to_dict`/`rounds_summary` cross-reference nothing), so the honest derivation is
the structural attribution `rounds.ts`'s `buildRoundViews` already performs: a rejection
attributed to a **non-latest** round is one a later `/propose` was generated to answer, and
only that case is excluded. A mission with no rounds at all is correctly still awaiting one.
Every other gate has no round concept and nothing to exclude.

No client-side flag exists anywhere in this path — there is nothing to lose on refresh,
which is precisely when an owner comes back to check whether anything happened.

`mission-detail.component.html` — inside the existing `gate-recorded-outcome` card, the
rejection branch gains a middle case between "an agent is running" and the plain fallback:

> No new round has started. Recording this rejection dispatched nothing — your direction is
> stored and waits here until you start the next round.

…followed by the run-step action **from that same card** (`gate-run-next-step-button`,
calling the existing `onRunNextStep()`), labelled with the existing `runStepButtonLabel()`
and annotated "→ POST /propose — starts the next round and consumes your direction". Its
error renders inline (`gate-run-next-step-error`). At a gate with no pipeline step of its own
(`system-gate`, `feel-gate`) the sentence still appears and `gate-next-step-no-route` says so
honestly rather than inventing a button that would POST nothing.

### 3. What did NOT change (AC 6)

No route, no request body, no checklist behaviour, no payload field. The offered button
issues the byte-identical POST the run-step section already issued — asserted directly
(`expect(req.request.body).toEqual({})` against `stepUrl('m1', 'propose')`). Approve/Reject/
Send back all emit exactly what they emitted before. This demand changed what the console
says, not what it does.

## Tests (AC 7)

Every pre-existing `data-testid` is still present. Two existing assertions changed *text*
(not hooks) because the sentence they asserted is the sentence this demand replaced — both
updated in the same commit as the template:

| Spec | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "theme-gate rejection with nothing dispatched" | asserted "new proposition round" / "/propose" | asserts "No new round has started", "dispatched nothing", the button, and `POST /propose` |
| "a non-theme-gate rejection with nothing dispatched" | asserted "No regeneration running yet" | asserts the same new sentence, naming `POST /plan` |

Added: 3 tests on the form (two distinct destinations rendered under the textarea and in the
DOM not a `title` attribute; Approve left with no line of its own) and 5 on mission-detail
(same POST/body as the run-step section; the state reproduced across a full component reload;
a rejection a later round already answered is *not* awaiting anything; a routeless gate says
it without inventing a button; an approved record produces no such state at all).

- **Pre-work baseline:** `npm test -- --run` → **186 files, 1846 tests, all passing.**
- **After:** `npm test -- --run` → **186 files, 1854 tests, all passing** (+8).
- `npm run build` clean (the initial-bundle budget warning is pre-existing and unrelated).

## Notes for design-studio

Nothing is owed back. One thing worth knowing on your side: the "was this rejection already
answered by a later round" question is answered here by a *structural approximation*, not by
data. If `rounds_summary` ever grew a per-round `generatedAt` (or a round↔gate-record link),
this console would drop the approximation for an exact comparison the same day. Raised as
context, not as an ask.

# Report — the theme-gate approval names which theme it approves

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. **Not shipped, at all** — `approvedTheme` did not
occur anywhere under `src/`. The gate request body the console posted was
`{outcome, notes, checklist}` (plus `designSystemId` on one system-gate shape and `referenceImages`
on a rejection), so every approval made through this console went in without a named theme.
`themePropositions()` existed but was scoped exclusively to `selectedRoundDir` — the round being
VIEWED — and was used only to render the propositions cards. Nothing in design-studio was touched or
needed; its side has accepted and validated the field since 2026-07-30.

## What shipped, against each acceptance criterion

**1. The round's themes are an explicit choice, and APPROVE posts the chosen slug.**
`GateDecisionFormComponent` gains `themeChoices: string[]` and renders a radio group
(`gate-approved-theme-picker` / `-option` / `-radio`, each option carrying `data-slug`). The chosen
slug is put on the submission as `approvedTheme`, which flows unchanged through
`MissionDetailComponent.gateRequestFor` into the `POST /missions/{id}/gates/theme-gate` body. Typed
on both `GateDecisionSubmission` and `GateDecisionRequest`.

**2. Choosing is REQUIRED to approve.** `themeChoiceMissing()` disables the Approve button, sets its
title, and renders `gate-approved-theme-needs-choice` naming the consequence ("an approval without
one degrades the coverage matrix and the build plan"). `request()` also refuses to emit in that
state, so the guard is not the button's disabled attribute alone. Where no choices were supplied
(every other gate, and a theme-gate mission with no propositions on disk) the picker does not exist
and Approve behaves exactly as before — the console is stricter than the API only where it actually
has a choice to offer.

**3. The slugs come from the LATEST propose round.** `MissionDetailComponent.approvedThemeChoices`
runs `themePropositions(artifacts, latestRoundDir)` — `roundDirs[roundDirs.length - 1]`, deliberately
NOT `selectedRoundDir` — and only at `stage === 'theme-gate'`. `themePropositions()` itself is
untouched: the propositions cards keep their viewed-round scoping, which is correct for what they
show. The two questions ("which round am I looking at" and "which round can I approve from") now have
two separate answers instead of one wrong shared one.

**4. A viewed/approved round discrepancy is made visible.** `approvedThemeRoundNotice` is non-null
exactly when the selected round dir differs from the latest, and states it in full: you are viewing
Round N, an approval always names a theme from the LATEST round (Round M), the choices below are
Round M's. Rendered as `gate-approved-theme-round-mismatch`. The form only renders the string; the
parent owns round selection, so it owns the derivation (design law 1).

**5. Approve-scoped.** `approvedTheme` is attached inside `request()` under
`outcome === 'approved'`, and send-back never reaches that method at all. Covered by two tests at the
form level and two through the parent (the reject body and the send-back body are asserted whole,
with a theme picked).

**6. A 400 is legible and costs nothing.** `describeDesignStudioError` already reads design-studio's
`{error}` body, so the refusal renders verbatim in `gate-decision-error`. Nothing on the error path
clears the notes, the ticks or the pick — asserted explicitly, both in the form's own spec and end to
end through the component, which is the same R15b rule the failed image upload follows.

**7. Every other gate untouched.** The picker renders only on a non-empty `themeChoices`, which the
parent supplies at `theme-gate` alone; `system-gate`'s `designSystemId` resolution in
`gateRequestFor` is unchanged. A test approves at `coverage-gate` and asserts no picker and an armed
Approve.

**8. A decided theme-gate renders unchanged, and shows the recorded theme.** `GateRecord` gains
optional `approvedTheme`. It renders on the recorded-outcome card
(`gate-outcome-approved-theme`) and on the history row (`gate-history-approved-theme`); absent — every
rejection, every other gate, every pre-field record — draws nothing at all.

**9. Hooks and suite.** No existing `data-testid` was removed or renamed; all new ones are listed
above. Baseline before the change: **190 files / 1987 tests passing**. After: **190 files / 2002
tests passing** (+15), plus a clean `ng build`.

**10. Test coverage.** Form spec (`gate-decision-form.component.spec.ts`): posts the chosen slug;
Approve blocked with no choice made (and emits nothing if clicked anyway); reject/send-back carry no
`approvedTheme`; no choices renders no picker and the pre-existing approve body; the notice renders
verbatim; a pick the round has stopped offering is dropped rather than left arming Approve; form state
survives a failure. Component spec (`mission-detail.component.spec.ts`): the latest round's slugs are
offered while round 1 holds a different one; the posted body carries `approvedTheme`; Approve blocked
with no pick and no request issued; the discrepancy notice on an older round tab; reject and send-back
bodies whole; the 400 surfaced with note/ticks/pick preserved; no picker at `coverage-gate`; a decided
gate showing its recorded theme.

## Judgement calls

- **Stale pick defence.** The picked slug is read through `chosenTheme()`, which only returns it while
  it is still one of the offered slugs. A mission poll (or a decision that starts a new round) can
  change the choices underneath the owner; without this, a slug the server would now 400 stays armed
  behind an enabled Approve, and the owner never sees the set change.
- **No client-side round policy in the form.** The form receives slugs and a sentence; it derives no
  notion of "latest". Everything round-shaped stays in the parent, which is where round selection
  already lives.
- **The confirm dialog names the theme.** Which theme is being approved is the most consequential fact
  about a theme-gate approval, so it belongs in the last line read before typing APPROVE. Empty string
  wherever no theme was named, so every other gate's dialog text is byte-identical.

## Nothing raised

No demand raised. Nothing in design-studio needed changing (confirmed by the demand itself), no
contract pin moved, no port or layout changed. `Vault-sync: none`.

# Fulfillment report — a mission that has stopped forever stops looking idle

## State before

Not previously shipped. Verified on `main` before any edit: `grep -rn "blockedDispatch\|dispatch/unblock" src/`
returned nothing at all. The field was on the wire and no line of the console read it.

The existing blocked-BUILD work (demand `design-studio-20260728-dashboard-unblock-a-blocked-build`)
was present and is the register this work deliberately reuses rather than inventing beside.

## What shipped

`blockedDispatch` is typed once on `Mission` and read from the payload — both list and detail, since
both routes carry it and both now render it. Nothing derives it, and nothing derives *around* it: the
console still makes no health claim from `activeDispatch` alone, which is exactly the ambiguity the
new field exists to resolve (a dead dispatch, a blocked one and a healthy idle mission all report
`activeDispatch: null`).

Three surfaces:

1. **The mission list** — a `blocked — nothing retries` chip under the stage chip, in the same
   `border-status-down` / `text-status-down` / `bg-status-down/10` register as the blocked system
   build's own chip. Not a bespoke treatment; the chip's `title` names the stage, the attempt count
   and the recorded reason so the row is legible without opening anything.
2. **The needs-you queue** — reason `2ter` in `design-mission-needs-you.ts`, its own row alongside
   the blocked-build row rather than folded into it: different stage, different cause, a different
   unblock route.
3. **Mission detail** — `BlockedDispatchPanelComponent`, rendered above the stage spine, stating the
   blocked stage, the attempts, the recorded reason and the time, and carrying the single unblock
   button.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it is met |
| --- | --- |
| `blockedDispatch` read from both routes and typed as `null` or `{stage, attempts, reason, at}` | `BlockedDispatch` + `Mission.blockedDispatch` in `design-studio.model.ts`; a service spec asserts the field survives `missions()` and `mission(id)` |
| Distinguished IN THE MISSION LIST, in the blocked-build register, not bespoke | `mission-blocked-dispatch-chip` in `missions-table.component.html`; specs assert the chip, its stage/attempts/reason title, and that its classes are the same status-down pair |
| Detail states stage, attempts, reason, at | `blocked-dispatch-headline` / `-reason` / `-at`; asserted individually |
| `POST /dispatch/unblock` offered ONLY on a blocked mission | The button lives inside the panel, and the panel renders only under `@if (blockedDispatch())`. Spec: with `blockedDispatch: null` neither panel nor button exists. `onUnblockDispatch()` also returns early if the field is null |
| On 200, re-render from the returned body, no follow-up GET | `setMission(updated)`; spec asserts the panel is gone and `httpMock.expectNone(missionUrl('m1'))` |
| 409 handled without breaking the page: show `error`, refresh, no spinning button | Refusal rendered verbatim via the shared classifier; a **targeted** `GET /missions/{id}` replaces the stale payload (not `refreshMission()`'s full reload, which would drop the page to its loading state and take the refusal off screen with it); pending cleared on every path. The refusal is rendered OUTSIDE the panel's condition, so the refresh that clears `blockedDispatch` cannot delete the explanation of why the button vanished. All asserted |
| A non-blocked dispatch failure is NOT surfaced as needing attention | No new surface reads `designSystemBuild.failure`-style "died once" state for dispatches, and there is no client-side attempt counting at all. Specs assert: no list chip and no needs-you row when `blockedDispatch` is null on an idle mission. The 422 hint says out loud that nothing is owed by the owner |
| 409 vs 422 distinguishable on the stage routes | `classifyDispatchStepError` — 422 → `attempt-died` ("the next call retries it, within ~30s"), 409 carrying `stage`/`attempts`/`reason` → `blocked` ("the retrying is over"), anything else → `other` with the message it always had. Rendered under both run-step error sites (`run-step-attempt-died`/`run-step-blocked` and the gate-card pair). Unit-tested per status, including that a plain `StageMismatchError` 409 stays `other` |
| `activeDispatch` handling unchanged; no health inferred from it | `active-dispatch.ts`, `active-dispatch-tag.component.*`, `headerDispatch()` and `mission-now.ts` are untouched. The blocked panel and chip read `blockedDispatch` only, and the chip renders independently of whether a dispatch tag is present |
| Blocked-BUILD affordance keeps working, own route | `unblockBuildSystem` / `designSystemBuild.blocked` / `system-build-panel` untouched; their 8 existing specs pass unmodified. The two unblock routes are separate methods on the service, and the model comment records that `dispatch/unblock` covers the other four stages and 409s at `system-gate` |
| Tests: blocked mission in the list, detail rendering, successful unblock re-render, 409-on-stale | All four, plus the 422-vs-409 pair, the only-when-blocked case, and the needs-you rows |

## Deliberate judgement calls

- **No confirmation dialog** on `dispatch/unblock`, unlike the build's two-shape unblock. There is
  exactly one thing this action can mean, it is reversible, it records no durable override, and the
  mission is already stopped dead — a dialog in front of the only button that unsticks the page is
  ceremony. The demand's own words ("the one-click unblock") were read as intentional.
- **The 409 refresh is a targeted mission re-read**, not the page's full reload. The full reload
  clears the mission signal and drops the screen to its loading state, which would remove the refusal
  text at the exact moment it is the only thing worth reading.
- **`stage` typed as `string`**, exactly as the demand specifies, and rendered verbatim rather than
  mapped through `stageLabel` — the field is design-studio's own name for the blocked stage and this
  console does not re-derive it.
- **The Now panel was not given a new state.** It has no state for the blocked *build* either (that
  build has its own panel), so adding one only for the blocked dispatch would have made the two
  terminal give-up states inconsistent in the one place they are most likely to be compared. The
  blocked-dispatch panel sits above the spine instead — higher on the page than the Now panel.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **188 files, 1934 tests, all passing.** No test deleted; the pre-existing
  blocked-build and `activeDispatch` specs pass unmodified.
- `npx ng build --configuration production` — clean (only the pre-existing bundle-budget warning).
- Not verified in a live browser: this needs a design-studio actually reporting a non-null
  `blockedDispatch`, which requires a mission whose dispatches really have burned their budget.
  Every claim above is asserted against the payload shape the demand specifies.

## No cross-repo change

Console-only. No `contracts` change, no design-studio change, no new request shape beyond the route
the demand named.

# Wrong-address notice — one honest explanation instead of thirteen wrong ones

## State before this session

Not shipped. `git grep` for `canonicalOrigin`, `OriginGuard`, `origin-guard`, `wrong address`
and any `window.location` read outside specs returned nothing across `src/`. No config entry
named a canonical console origin; nothing in the shell compared the address bar to anything.
An owner at `http://127.0.0.1:4200` got exactly the symptom the demand describes: every
cross-origin panel rendering its own honest `unreachable`, none of them able to say why.

The gap itself was already *documented* — `console-config.ts`'s `designStudioBaseUrl` comment
records the live-verified fact that design-studio answers the `127.0.0.1:4200` preflight with
400 "Disallowed CORS origin" while granting `localhost:4200`. That note was the evidence; this
session turned it into something the browser tells the owner.

## What shipped

**The canonical origin, declared once.** `consoleConfig.canonicalConsoleOrigin =
'http://localhost:4200'`, first entry in `core/console-config.ts`, alongside the existing base
URLs. No component holds the literal — `OriginNoticeComponent` reads the config, and both spec
files assert against `consoleConfig.canonicalConsoleOrigin` rather than re-typing the string
(one spec pins its value explicitly, so a change to it is a deliberate edit, not a silent one).

**`core/window-location.ts` — a `WINDOW_LOCATION` injection token** over the four address-bar
facts the notice needs (`origin`, `pathname`, `search`, `hash`), defaulting to the real
`window.location`. Same shape as the existing `EVENT_SOURCE_FACTORY` token, and for the same
reason: a real `window.location` cannot be reassigned in a spec, so without the seam neither
origin is testable.

**`shell/origin-notice.component.ts` + `.html`**, mounted once in `AppComponent` as the first
child of the shell root — above the status strip, so it is the first thing on the page and, as
the shell is on every route, present on **every** screen rather than only `/design`. When
`window.location.origin` differs from the canonical origin it renders a persistent
`role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"` bar that:
- names the current origin (`data-testid="origin-notice-current"`),
- names the canonical one (`data-testid="origin-notice-canonical"`),
- states that the platform's services grant the canonical origin **only**,
- and carries a real `<a href>` to the *same* path on the canonical origin —
  `pathname + search + hash` preserved, so `/design/abc-123?tab=checklist#gate` moves in one
  click with nothing retyped (`data-testid="origin-notice-link"`).

**What the notice deliberately does not claim.** It asserts only what the address bar proves —
that this origin is not the granted one — and says panels *may* read as unreachable "whatever
their services are actually doing". It never says a request was blocked, never says CORS,
never says preflight: the browser withholds the reason for a blocked fetch from script (a
blocked request is indistinguishable from a dead service), which is precisely why an
address-bar-level notice is the only honest way to say this at all. That constraint is
enforced, not just intended — a spec asserts the rendered text contains none of `cors`,
`blocked`, `preflight`.

**Absent when the origin is canonical, and byte-identically so.** The whole template is inside
a single `@if (mismatched())`, so on `http://localhost:4200` there is no wrapper element and no
whitespace-bearing node — the spec asserts `textContent.trim() === ''` on the component and a
null `[data-testid="origin-notice"]` at five routes through the real shell.

## Untouched, on purpose

- **Every per-panel `unreachable` state.** Not one panel, service, probe or error path was
  touched. A genuinely down service, seen from the canonical origin, still reads exactly as it
  reads today — the shell spec re-asserts the status strip and all 16 sidebar links are intact
  with the notice showing, and confirms the notice *precedes* them rather than replacing
  anything. This notice is an additional higher-level explanation, layered above the honest
  per-panel readings, never a substitute for them.
- **No service change, no CORS allow-list change, no `contracts` change, no `runtime` compose
  change.** One repo, as the demand specified. `designStudioBaseUrl` still points at
  `http://127.0.0.1:8087` (the service's own loopback address — unrelated to which hostname the
  console is opened at, and the demand did not ask for it to change).
- **Existing `data-testid` hooks.** All present and unchanged; the four new ones are additive.

## Tests

Baseline before this session: **187 files / 1880 tests, all passing.**
After: **188 files / 1898 tests, all passing** (`npm test -- --run`) — +1 file, +18 tests, zero
pre-existing tests modified beyond the shared `beforeEach` gaining a canonical-origin
`WINDOW_LOCATION` provider so every existing shell expectation describes the app as the owner
actually sees it.

Both origins are covered at both levels:
- `origin-notice.component.spec.ts` (7): canonical → renders nothing; `127.0.0.1:4200` → both
  origins named; link preserves path + query + fragment; `role="alert"`; no CORS/blocked/
  preflight claim; a port-only difference (`localhost:4201`) counts as a different origin.
- `app.component.spec.ts` (+11): at `/`, `/design`, `/treasury`, `/settings`, `/agents` — notice
  present and correctly addressed on a non-canonical origin, wholly absent on the canonical one
  — plus the shell-integrity check above.

`npx ng build` succeeds. The bundle-budget warning it prints is pre-existing and unrelated
(present before this change).

## Follow-ups for the origin repo

None required — this demand was scoped to one repo and needed nothing from design-studio.

Worth knowing, though: the notice explains the mismatch, it does not resolve it. If the owner
would rather `http://127.0.0.1:4200` simply *work*, that is a CORS allow-list change in each
granting service (design-studio's own grant is the one this repo has live-verified as
`localhost`-only) — a separate demand per service, deliberately not made here.

src/app/design/missions-table.component.spec.ts, src/app/design/mission-detail.component.spec.ts — both render sites asserted to carry the fix through the shared component

# Fulfillment report — a finished agent stops saying it is running

## State before

Not previously shipped. `active-dispatch.ts` still carried the defect verbatim as the demand
described it: `DISPATCH_KIND_LABEL` baked the word "running" into each of the five kinds, and
`activeDispatchKindLabel(kind)` never saw `state`. Verified on `main` before any edit.

## What shipped

The label is now two halves, composed:

```ts
const DISPATCH_KIND_AGENT: Record<DispatchKind, string> = {
  'theme-interview': 'Theme interview agent', clone: 'Clone agent',
  'content-interview': 'Content interview agent', propose: 'Proposition agent',
  build: 'Design system build agent',
};

const DISPATCH_STATE_PHRASE: Record<DispatchState, (agent: string) => string> = {
  launched: (a) => `${a} running`,
  finished: (a) => `${a} finished — run this step again to read its output back`,
  failed:   (a) => `${a} failed — nothing was read back`,
  stopped:  (a) => `${a} stopped before finishing — nothing was read back`,
  unknown:  (a) => `${a} dispatched`,
};

export function activeDispatchLabel(dispatch: ActiveDispatch): string { ... }
```

The verb is no longer a property of the kind. The old kind-only export is gone rather than left
beside the new one — a signature that cannot see the state is exactly what the demand named as the
defect, so leaving it callable would have left the defect available.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How it is met |
| --- | --- |
| Text derived from BOTH kind and state | `activeDispatchLabel(dispatch: ActiveDispatch)`; `activeDispatchKindLabel(kind)` removed entirely |
| `launched` byte-for-byte unchanged | All five launched strings asserted literally in `active-dispatch.spec.ts`; the pre-existing tag/table/now-panel specs that assert the old wording pass untouched |
| `finished` contains no form of "running" | Asserted `.toLowerCase()).not.toContain('running')` across all five kinds, plus at both render sites |
| `finished` names the read-back | `"… finished — run this step again to read its output back"`, asserted for all five kinds. Stated unconditionally on the demand's own reasoning: `find_pending_dispatch` bails to `None` once consolidated, so `activeDispatch` + `finished` already means "done, not read back" |
| `failed`/`stopped` read as neither running nor finished | Own phrases; asserted absent of "running" and of "agent finished" for all five kinds |
| `unknown` keeps note + helper as-is | `DISPATCH_STATE_UNKNOWN_NOTE` and `isDispatchStateUnknown` untouched; the label states only "… dispatched" and leaves diagnosis to the existing note |
| `DISPATCH_STATE_TO_DOT` unchanged | Not edited; its spec passes unmodified |
| Tag not hidden when finished | The `@if` structure is untouched — the tag renders for every state. Asserted explicitly at both render sites |
| Both render sites, one implementation | Verified, not assumed: `mission-detail.component.html` (×2), `missions-table.component.html` and `system-build-panel.component.html` all render `<app-active-dispatch-tag>`; new finished-state assertions added to `mission-detail.component.spec.ts` and `missions-table.component.spec.ts` prove the shared component carries it. `now-panel.component.html` is deliberately not a second tag (one dispatch, one tag) but was calling the same helper, so it was moved to `activeDispatchLabel` too |
| `active-dispatch-kind` testid present, specs updated not deleted | testid unchanged in the template; every existing spec kept and extended |
| Unit-tested per state | `launched`, `finished`, `failed`, `stopped`, `unknown` in `active-dispatch.spec.ts`; `finished` asserts both the absence of "running" and the presence of the read-back instruction |
| No design-studio / contracts / API / HTTP change | Console-only. No service, model, or request touched — every input comes from the `activeDispatch` payload already on screen |

## Verification

`npm test` — **188 files, 1906 tests, all passing.** No test was deleted.

## Not in scope (per the demand)

No "read the output back" button was added, and the dot vocabulary is untouched.

# Report — the console renders the gate review surface

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. **Not shipped, at all**: `gateContext` appeared
nowhere in `src/` — not in the model, not in a template, not in a test. Every one of the five
acceptance criteria was open. The console read the mission payload's other fields and dropped this
one silently, which is exactly the shape a purely additive server change takes on a console that
ignores it.

Two adjacent things WERE already shipped and were deliberately left alone rather than rebuilt:
`MatrixViewComponent`/`PlanViewComponent` (the JSON readers over `matrix.json`/`plan.json`, demand
`…-artifact-readers`) and the rejection-consequence block under the Notes field (demand
`…-gate-action-consequences`). The second is what this demand corrects rather than replaces — see §3.

## What shipped

### 1. The rendered review view, beside the JSON (AC 1)

`mission-detail.component.html` — a new `gate-review-views` block at the top of the gate panel,
rendered whenever `gateContext.reviewViews` is non-empty. Each path is both **linked**
(`target="_blank"`) and **embedded** (an iframe, `sandbox="allow-scripts"`, the same defense-in-depth
idiom `ThemePropositionsComponent` already uses for agent-authored mock pages). URLs come from the
existing `designStudioArtifactUrl` — the same `GET /missions/{id}/artifacts/{path}` route this console
already calls, no design-studio change and no new CORS surface (an anchor/iframe load needs no grant).

The paths are **design-studio's**, never a map in this repo: nothing here knows that `coverage-gate`
means `matrix.html`. A third view at a third gate renders the day design-studio emits it. `matrix.json`
/`plan.json` are untouched — still listed in Artifacts, still rendered by their own readers, asserted
directly (`matrix-view` still present alongside the new block).

One thing that needed care rather than a one-liner: `bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl` returns a fresh
wrapper object per call and an `[src]` binding re-navigates on identity change, while this screen
replaces its whole mission object every poll tick. Naive wiring would reload the embedded matrix every
few seconds under the owner's eyes. `trustedFrameUrl` memoizes by URL string — the same defect
`ThemePropositionsComponent` was live-caught with in WU-120 and documents at length.

### 2. The producing step, offered before the refusal (AC 2)

`gateArtifactMissing` reads `artifactPresent`/`canDecide` and, where either is false, the new
`gate-artifact-missing` block names `requiredArtifact`, prints `producedBy` verbatim
(`→ POST /missions/{id}/coverage`), and offers a **Produce it** button that issues the byte-identical
`POST /missions/{id}/{step}` the run-step section already issues (asserted: same URL, `{}` body).

`approveBlockedReason` — the existing input that greys Approve for an unpinnable `system-gate` — now
covers this case too, and is checked first because it applies at whatever gate design-studio says it
applies to. This is not the client-side completeness logic design law 1 forbids: it is read from the
server's own `canDecide`, for a state `record_gate_outcome` will refuse outright. Reject is
deliberately unaffected, and the checklist/notes keep working.

### 3. Reject labelled per gate (AC 3)

`GateDecisionFormComponent` gains one presentational input, `rejection`:

| `startsNewRound` | Button | Consequence line under Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `true` (theme-gate, system-gate) | `Reject — starts a new round` | unchanged: "your note becomes binding direction…" (+ system-gate's §8bis refinement) |
| `false` (coverage/plan/feel-gate) | `Reject — advisory only` | "advisory only — recorded for you, no pipeline step reads it", then `effect` and `remedy` verbatim |
| `null` (design-studio predating the field) | `Reject` | unchanged |

The pre-existing line said the *iterating* gates' truth at all five gates — false at three of them.
That is the correction, not an addition beside it, which is why `gate-note-consequence-reject` is now
absent (not merely supplemented) at an advisory gate.

Two places the same falsehood also lived, fixed with it:
- the reference-imagery hint ("the next agent run is told to open and study them") now carries
  `gate-reference-attach-advisory` where there is no next run;
- the typed-`REJECT` confirm dialog gains `advisoryRejectionClause()` — the owner is told before they
  commit, not only after.

### 4. The `notice`, verbatim (AC 4)

`Mission.notice` is now typed (`AdvisoryRejectionNotice`), read off the `POST /gates/{gate}` response
into `gateAdvisoryNotice`, and rendered as `gate-advisory-notice` at the top of the gate panel:
`effect` and `remedy` printed as design-studio sent them, no paraphrase. Cleared when a new decision is
composed and on every mission load — it is a statement about one call, not a property of the mission.

### 5. `gateContext: null` (AC 5)

`?? null` at a single point (`gateContext` computed) collapses all three producers of "no context" —
no mission loaded, a non-gate stage (design-studio's own `null`), and a design-studio predating the
field (absent, `undefined`) — into one answer, and every consumer renders exactly what this screen
rendered before. Asserted both ways: a **gate** stage with `gateContext: null` still offers a full,
unqualified decision (approve armed, plain `Reject`), and a non-gate stage renders none of it.

## Tests

- **Pre-work baseline:** `npm test -- --run` → **188 files, 1934 tests, all passing.**
- **After:** `npm test -- --run` → **188 files, 1946 tests, all passing** (+12: 9 on mission-detail,
  3 on the form). `npm run build` clean — the initial-bundle budget warning is pre-existing.

No pre-existing test changed. Every prior assertion on `gate-note-consequence-reject`,
`gate-note-binding-text` and `gate-reject-button` still passes untouched, because a mission fixture
without a `gateContext` takes the `null` branch — which is the same fact as AC 5, checked by the whole
existing suite rather than only by the two tests that name it.

## Notes for design-studio

Nothing is owed back. Two observations, as context rather than asks:

1. `producedBy` is rendered verbatim with its literal `{id}` placeholder (`POST /missions/{id}/coverage`)
   — correct as documentation of the route, and the console does not substitute the mission id into it
   because that would be inventing a URL out of prose. The button next to it calls the real route through
   this repo's own `pipelineRouteFor` mapping, which already had `coverage-gate → coverage` and
   `plan-gate → plan`. If `gateContext` ever grew a machine-readable step name, the console would drop
   its own mapping for it the same day.
2. `feel-gate` declares `startsNewRound: false` with a `remedy`, but has no `requiredArtifact` and no
   review view — it renders the advisory reject label and remedy, and no artifact/review block. That
   reads correctly; noted only so you know the console handles the "listed for completeness" gate
   exactly as the table intends.

src/app/design/rounds.ts — `buildRoundViews`'s `isLatest` is now positional (`index === roundDirs.length - 1`), no longer `rounds.latestRound === index + 1`; this alone repairs `bindingDirections` and `mission-detail`'s `rejectionAwaitingNextRound`, both of which filter on `!view.isLatest`

# Fulfillment report — round selection survives an abandoned round

## State before

Not previously shipped. Verified against `main` before any edit: `rounds.ts` carried both defects
exactly as the demand describes them.

```ts
isLatest: rounds.latestRound === index + 1,            // false for EVERY view on a gapped mission
...
return rounds.latestRound ?? rounds.roundDirs.length;  // a round NUMBER, guarded against a POSITION
```

`MissionDetailComponent`'s lookup is `roundDirs[n - 1]`, so on a mission whose round 4 was abandoned
(`latestRound: 5`, four surviving dirs) the default selection resolved to `5`, `roundDirs[4]` was
`undefined`, and the propositions panel rendered empty but for its tabs — with no tab current, since
`isLatest` was false everywhere at once.

## What shipped

One numbering space for rounds in the console: the 1-based POSITION in `roundDirs`. That is already
what `RoundView.roundNumber`, the `round` query param and the `roundDirs[n - 1]` lookup speak;
`latestRound` — design-studio's own round number — is the only value that ever disagreed, and it now
takes part in neither decision.

```ts
isLatest: index === rounds.roundDirs.length - 1,
...
return rounds.roundDirs.length;
```

Both `isLatest` consumers are repaired by that one line, because both were reading the same wrong
flag:

- `bindingDirections`'s `.filter((view) => !view.isLatest)` again excludes the latest round's own
  rejection, exactly as its docstring already specified. With `isLatest` universally false it
  presented a round's own rejection as direction that SHAPED it — the panel's meaning inverted.
- `mission-detail`'s `rejectionAwaitingNextRound` (the computed reached from
  `recordedOutcomeForCurrentStage`) no longer treats the latest round's own rejection as "answered by
  a later round", so a rejected latest round again offers the *No new round has started* affordance.
- `roundLabel` reads `(current)` for the last round, and `RoundSelectorComponent`'s note picks
  `Round N rejected — awaiting a new proposal round` over `Why round N was superseded` again — both
  were already derived from `isLatest` and needed no change of their own.

Deliberately NOT done, per the demand: no round number is decoded out of a dir name
(`proposals-round-4` -> 4). `design-studio.model.ts` states the dir naming is "never assumed
client-side, always read from this array"; parsing it would trade one coupling for a worse one. On a
gapped mission the console therefore shows its own consistent ordinal (`Round 4 (current)` for
`proposals-round-5`) rather than a number it cannot honestly derive. The doc comments on
`RoundView.roundNumber` and `.isLatest` now say this in full, so the next reader does not re-litigate
it.

No design-studio change, no `contracts` change, no new API field — `roundDirs` carried everything
this needed.

## Verification

`npm test` (full suite, Vitest 1.20.0): **188 files, 1914 tests, all passing** — the baseline before
this work adds 8 tests (5 in `rounds.spec.ts`, 3 in `mission-detail.component.spec.ts`) and deletes
none. One existing test *title* was corrected in place (`rounds.spec.ts`: "latest flagged from
rounds.latestRound" -> "latest flagged positionally (the last roundDir)"); no existing expectation
changed.
`npm run build` succeeds (the pre-existing initial-bundle budget warning is unchanged).

Existing `data-testid` hooks `rounds-section`, `round-selector` and `round-selector-tab` are all
still present and are asserted directly by the new end-to-end test.

New coverage:

- `rounds.spec.ts` — gapped fixture `{proposalRounds: 4, latestRound: 5, roundDirs: [proposals,
  proposals-round-2, proposals-round-3, proposals-round-5]}`: `isLatest` is `[f, f, f, t]`;
  `resolveSelectedRound(_, null) === 4` and indexes to `proposals-round-5`; `?round=2` honored;
  `?round=5` (a round number, not a position) falls back to the last round rather than rendering
  nothing; the latest round's own rejection stays out of `bindingDirections`. A same-size CONTIGUOUS
  mission is asserted alongside it as the control.
- `mission-detail.component.spec.ts` — the same gapped mission driven through the component: no
  `round` param selects round 4, exactly one tab is `aria-selected`, its label is `Round 4
  (current)`, its own mock renders (`proposals-round-5/theme-a/index.html`); `?round=2` overrides and
  re-scopes the mocks; a rejected latest round shows `Round 4 rejected — awaiting a new proposal
  round` (never "superseded") and the still-unanswered next-step note.

One expectation was corrected while writing the tests rather than forced through: on the gapped
fixture with a single rejection on record, `buildRoundViews` attributes it to round 3 — the confirmed
trigger for the round after it, per that function's own backward-fill rule. That attribution is
pre-existing, unrelated to this fix, and correct; the test asserts the real behaviour.

# Report — the console shows how old a mission's inputs are, and offers the refresh

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. **Not shipped, at all** — no occurrence of
`harvestGeneratedAt`, `refreshes`, `refreshed` or `refresh-inputs` anywhere under `src/`. The
service side, by contrast, was fully landed and read directly out of `../design-studio` rather than
guessed at: `_harvest_generated_at` / `harvestGeneratedAt` on every mission response (`api.py:459`),
`RefreshRecord` and `Mission.refreshes` (`domain/mission.py:463`), `RefreshInputsService`
(`domain/refresh_inputs.py`), the `POST /missions/{id}/refresh-inputs` route with its hoisted
`refreshed` block (`api.py:1357`), and `RefreshRefusedError` → 409 (`domain/errors.py:187`,
handler at `api.py:805`). Nothing was implemented in that repo; it was read only.

## What shipped, against each acceptance criterion

**1. `mission.harvestGeneratedAt` on the mission screen, called out when materially old.**
`input-staleness.ts` is the whole derivation, tested independently of the DOM. It measures the
snapshot against the mission's own `updatedAt` — **not wall-clock `now`**, which was the obvious
alternative and the wrong one: it would escalate a long-closed mission's callout forever, reporting
inputs as increasingly urgent when nothing will ever be used from them again. The materiality
threshold is 3 days, and the constant carries its own reasoning: tighter (hours) fires on the
ordinary multi-day mission and teaches the owner to skip past the callout, which would cost exactly
the reading this demand buys; looser (a week) is the age that already went unnoticed. It is a
display threshold only — design-studio never sees it, and crossing it changes what the console
*says*, never what the mission may do.

`null` renders as **nothing at all** — no row, no error, no zero date. Same for a blank or
unparseable timestamp, which is the honest reading: design-studio's own field returns `None` both
before harvest has run and for an artifact it cannot read, and both mean "nothing is known". A
harvest newer than the last activity (clock skew, or the refresh that produced `updatedAt`) clamps
to zero rather than reporting negative age. Tested against mission `e8e4b3e5`'s real numbers:
harvested `2026-07-23T09:35:03Z`, active `2026-07-30` → `7 day(s) behind`, material.

**2. The refresh offered at `coverage-gate` and `plan-gate`, with a required, owner-typed reason.**
`REFRESH_OFFERED_STAGES` is deliberately **narrower** than what design-studio accepts (any
non-terminal stage past `brief`). This console never offers a refresh the service would refuse; it
does decline to offer some the service would accept, which is a UI judgment and is written down as
one rather than left implicit. Notably `theme-gate` is a gate and is *not* offered — a stale brief
costs nothing where the thing being judged is the round's own mocks.

The reason is required and is the owner's own words, trimmed. No placeholder, default or generated
string is ever sent: a recorded reason nobody wrote is worse than none, because it reads as an
account of why the inputs changed while being an account of nothing — on the one act that must
never be silent. The submit button is disabled until the field has content, and that is stated as a
courtesy, not the guarantee; the server's 400 remains the guarantee.

**3. What a refresh does and does not do, stated before the confirm.** Three static blocks, not
behind a toggle and not below the fold, on screen alongside the submit button: what it does
(re-derives harvest+brief against the target as it stands today); what it does not (moves no stage,
reverses no gate decision, erases nothing — the superseded inputs are kept); and what genuinely
follows (items the refreshed brief no longer carries disappear from the matrix and the plan; items
it adds are genuinely uncovered, because the approved mocks were built against the old brief, and
will show as **real gaps at the next coverage run — that is the coverage gate doing its job, not a
regression**). The copy is static on purpose: these are design-studio's own documented invariants,
true of every refresh, and deriving them per mission would invent a claim this repo has no basis
for. Each sentence is asserted in the spec, so the copy cannot silently drift out of the panel.

**4. The `refreshed` block surfaced.** Rendered as the added and removed `category:key` tags,
separately, with the reason and timestamp — the owner reads what changed without diffing two JSON
artifacts. Added items are labelled as the gaps they will become, never softened. When a refresh
changed nothing, the block says so in words rather than rendering two empty lists. The result block
leads with "the mission has not moved" — a result panel sitting next to gate controls must not read
as though something advanced.

**5. `mission.refreshes` in the mission-history view.** Folded into `GateHistoryComponent` as a
fourth list and a fourth row kind beside `gateRecords`/`rewinds`/`sendBacks`, interleaved
chronologically. Its label states out loud that it moved no stage and reversed no decision — a row
sitting among verdicts would otherwise read as one by association. It belongs there for the reason
the other three are separate lists: "the owner re-derived the inputs" is a genuinely different event
from a verdict, a jump backwards, or a refusal to judge, and it is the one event that can change
what a *later* decision is even about, so a reader tracing why a covered row became a gap has to
find it in order beside the gates it sits between.

**6. The superseded inputs are reachable.** Three ways, all through the existing artifact route
(`designStudioArtifactUrl`, which already encodes path segments individually so nested paths
survive): linked from the refresh result block, linked from the history row, and listed by the
artifacts panel, which reads `GET /missions/{id}/artifacts` recursively and therefore picks up
`superseded/*.json` with no change at all. The two link sites assert the exact built URL
(`…/artifacts/superseded/harvest-before-refresh-1.json`).

**7. Both refusals handled honestly.** The 409 (terminal, or not yet past `brief`) renders
design-studio's own sentence verbatim, leaves the typed reason exactly where the owner put it, and
returns the button to usable rather than leaving it spinning.

The 400 exposed a **real pre-existing gap, now fixed**: `describeDesignStudioError` only read
`{error}`, the shape every *domain* error arrives in via an `@app.exception_handler`. A refusal a
**route** raises directly does not use that shape — FastAPI's own `HTTPException` serialises as
`{detail}` — so `refresh-inputs`' empty-reason 400 rendered as the bare "design-studio answered HTTP
400.", discarding the one sentence saying what was wrong with the request. `POST /send-back`'s blank-
note 400 had been doing the same thing since 2026-07-28, unnoticed. The describer now falls back to
a **string** `detail`; `error` still wins where both are present, and a non-string `detail` (FastAPI
validation errors are an array of per-field objects) is ignored rather than stringified into noise
dressed as an explanation. Every existing message is byte-identical.

## Verification

- **Full suite green: 1987 tests / 190 files** (was 1985/190 before this session's own additions —
  baseline confirmed green on a stash before any assertion was written, so no pre-existing failure is
  being carried).
- **41 new tests**: 9 (staleness derivation), 10 (the panel), 7 (the fourth history row kind), 10
  (mission-detail integration end to end), 2 (the service's request/refusal shapes), 3 (the `detail`
  fallback).
- `ng build` completes with **no warnings** — including the NG8102 the first pass surfaced, which was
  a genuine signal: `refreshes` is always-carried on the wire, so the defensive `?? []` was dead and
  was removed rather than silenced.
- Nine fixture files across `design/` and `overview/` gained the two new always-present mission
  fields, keeping every fixture honest against the real wire shape.

## Not done, and why

**No live browser verification.** Exercising this end to end means POSTing a real refresh against a
real mission — it rewrites `harvest.json` and `brief.json` on disk and appends a permanent record.
That is a live mutation on owner data and needs its own explicit, specific ask; it is not covered by
authorization to fulfil this demand. Everything above is verified against design-studio's actual
source (read directly, not assumed) and through the HTTP-level test harness. **If the owner wants a
live run, mission `e8e4b3e5` is the natural subject and the one this demand was written about — say
so and it can be driven on `:4200`** (agent-runner/design-studio CORS is port-specific).

## Vault-relevance

None from this session. The console-side work changes no port, no layout, no pin, and cuts no tag.
design-studio's own stage-machine change (a mission's inputs are no longer fixed after `brief`) is
genuinely vault-relevant, but it is that repo's to report — its demand said as much and flagged the
`spec-design-studio.md` amendment as following from its own landing, not from this console wiring.

# Report — coverage-gate becomes a scope negotiation, and the console says so

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. **Not shipped**: `coverage-scope`, `matrixStale`,
`briefAdditions`, `ownerAdded` and `scopeRounds` appeared nowhere in `src/`, `ChecklistGateMode` was
`'regime' | 'system-gate'`, and `rejectionAwaitingNextRound` derived "a round is waiting" from stage
plus `activeDispatch` alone, exactly as the demand describes.

Two things WERE already shipped and were built on rather than rebuilt: `GateRejectionSemantics`
(`startsNewRound`/`effect`/`remedy`, from demand `…-render-the-gate-review-surface`) was already
modelled and already drives `GateSurfaceComponent`'s reject-button label and note destination — what
was missing was the post-rejection panel consulting it — and `rounds.ts`'s positional round
machinery, which the scope axis now reuses unchanged.

## What shipped, criterion by criterion

**1. The fix that came first, independent of everything else.** `rejectionAwaitingNextRound` now
returns `null` wherever `gateContext.rejection.startsNewRound === false`. Where it is false the
panel renders the gate's own `effect` and `remedy` strings verbatim
(`workspace-gate-next-step-advisory` / `-remedy`, and `gate-next-step-advisory` / `-remedy` on the
pre-D088 page, which shares the controller) and offers no run-step button. Deliberately `=== false`,
not falsy: a design-studio predating `gateContext` renders exactly as before. This is wrong at
`plan-gate` and `feel-gate` today for the same reason, and is fixed there by the same change.

**2. No run-step button for a route that cannot consume direction.** Falls out of (1): the button
lives inside the `rejectionAwaitingNextRound` branch, which is now unreachable at an advisory gate.
`pipelineRouteFor` itself is untouched — the button is still correct for producing a missing gate
artifact, which is a different question from consuming a note.

**3. Unchanged when coverage-gate flips.** Nothing in this repo lists which gates iterate. When
`startsNewRound` becomes true the same surface renders the next-round copy and the button again;
asserted directly (`gate-surface.component.spec.ts`, `mission-detail.component.spec.ts`).

**4. The scope-round surface.** New `ScopeRoundComponent`, rendered at coverage-gate in the
workspace's decision column: the round's proposal from `coverage-scope.json` with the per-round
ordinal as the FIRST column, the round number and the brief's `generatedAt` in the header, previous
rounds through the same `RoundSelectorComponent` the propose rounds use, `activeDispatch` of the new
kind `scope` through the same `ActiveDispatchTagComponent`, `blockedDispatch` stated as fact (the
unblock stays with the parent's existing panel — one code path to that call, not two), and an
abandon control behind a class-2 confirmation posting `POST /missions/{id}/coverage/abandon-round`.
`mission.scopeRounds` is read as a PEER of `rounds`, with its own `scopeRound` query param; the
selection, the round labels and the abandoned-round gaps are `rounds.ts`'s existing positional
machinery, reused rather than re-derived.

**5. Per-round ordinals never travel.** The ordinal is computed at render from the rows of the round
currently on screen and is held in no state, so switching rounds renumbers by construction (asserted
by switching the artifact under the component and reading the numbers back). Separately, when the
artifact's own `briefGeneratedAt` differs from the mission's current one, the surface says the brief
grew after this round was scoped and that direction written against these numbers does not carry —
rather than letting a stale numbering stand silently. Both stamps absent ⇒ nothing claimed.

**6. Two visually distinct note boxes.** The gate's own note box is titled *Reject with direction* at
coverage-gate and carries a fourth destination row naming what it cannot deliver and pointing at the
other box. The other box (`BriefAdditionsFormComponent`, its own inset panel) states *this grows the
brief itself* and why a rejection structurally cannot.

**7. Required note, optional structured items.** `growBrief` sends `{note}` alone for a note-only
submission (legal, and the button arms on the note alone), and `{note, items}` when rows are given —
rows the owner left blank are dropped rather than sent as empty assertions. The two item fields are
`category` and `item`, the first two columns of the table on screen.

**8. `matrixStale` banner.** Rendered at coverage-gate from the server-computed field, beside the two
stamps so the owner can see the gap themselves. Never re-derived from the stamps (asserted: stamps
that disagree while `matrixStale: false` render no banner), and **nothing consumes it to disable
Approve** — D088's rule is respected exactly.

**9. `briefAdditions` in mission history.** Fifth row kind in `GateHistoryComponent`, interleaved
chronologically, with its own badge, its note, the tags it created (or the honest "no brief item
created" of a note-only addition) and the tags the brief already carried.

**10. `owner-added` badge.** On scope rows, and on matrix rows as an `Owner` column that appears only
when the brief actually carries owner additions — so a mission with none renders exactly the table it
always did.

**11. The coverage-gate checklist.** `ChecklistGateMode` gained `'coverage-gate'`;
`syncChecklist`'s ternary is now a pass-through over a `GATE_SCOPED_CHECKLIST_STAGES` set, so every
non-regime mode IS the `?gate=` value. No item key is written anywhere in this repo — asserted by
serving two invented scope keys from the route and reading them back off the DOM.

**12. The pre-existing type drift.** `MatrixRow.mappedScreen`/`mappedComponent` are now
`string | null`. Nothing rendered wrong (readers already defended with `|| '—'`), but the type
asserted a guarantee `domain/coverage.py` never made.

## Two things design-studio should know

1. **A wire-naming discrepancy in the demand itself, resolved toward the acceptance criterion.** The
   demand's prose (batch A) names the brief-addition item pair `{category, key}`; acceptance
   criterion 7 names it `{category, item}`. This console sends **`item`**, because the criterion is
   what it is measured against and `item` is what the matrix column it mirrors is called. At the time
   this shipped, `POST /missions/{id}/brief-additions` did not exist yet in `design-studio` (the
   domain record, the error class and `brief.py`'s `ownerAdded` merge point are present;
   `brief_growth.py` and the route are not), so nothing is broken either way — but the route should
   accept `item`, or say so and this repo will change one line.

2. **Every new field is read optionally and additively.** `briefAdditions`, `briefGeneratedAt`,
   `matrixGeneratedAt`, `matrixStale`, `scopeRounds`, `brief.ownerAdded` and the `scope` dispatch
   kind are all absent-tolerant: against today's design-studio the console renders precisely what it
   rendered yesterday, plus the criterion-1 fix, which needs only `gateContext` (live since
   2026-07-30). Nothing waits on batches A–C to be correct.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **204 files, 2210 tests, all passing** (2165 before; +45, of which 12 are the
  new scope-round surface, 6 the brief-additions box, 12 the controller's coverage-gate behaviours,
  6 the gate surface's advisory/two-box rendering, 6 the history's fifth list, 3 the matrix badge
  and null mappings).
- `npx ng build` — clean.
- Not verified live against a running design-studio: the routes and artifacts three of these
  criteria consume (`coverage-scope.json`, `POST /brief-additions`, `POST /coverage/abandon-round`,
  `?gate=coverage-gate`) do not exist there yet, by the demand's own staging. The criterion-1 fix
  and the type-drift fix are the two that are live-checkable today and are covered by tests against
  the exact `gateContext` shape design-studio publishes.
- One gap named honestly: the `matrixStale` BANNER's markup lives in
  `mission-workspace.component.html`, which has no spec of its own in this repo (only its
  sub-components do). The banner's data path — `matrixStale()` read, never derived — is tested at the
  controller.
