# design-studio-20260804-dashboard-design-screen-list-and-regime-legibility — fulfilment report

**Not already shipped.** Checked first, per the demand's instruction: of the six acceptance criteria,
exactly one was partially in place before this session — the list already rendered a
`blockedDispatch` chip and the running-agent tag (demands `...20260730-dashboard-blocked-dispatch-
visibility` and the 2026-07-21 owner commission). Ordering, all four filters, `pauseRequested`,
`gateContext`, the explained regime field, the design-system explanation and the abort-reason column
did not exist. All six criteria are now met.

## What was built, per criterion

### AC1 — a stable, explicit ordering the console controls

`mission-list-view.ts`. Six orderings (opened oldest/newest, updated newest/oldest, target repo,
pipeline stage), chosen from a visible control, applied on a copy of the payload — the array behind
the signal is never mutated.

Two decisions worth stating, because both are the demand's own reasoning carried one step further:

- **The default is `created-asc`, not `updated-desc`.** The demand names most-recently-updated as the
  obvious operator default and, in the same breath, names why the server refuses to sort by it: a
  mission jumps to the top the moment a gate is decided, moving out from under the person reading it.
  That argument does not stop being true when the console is the one sorting. `createdAt` never
  changes for the life of a mission, so `created-asc` is the one ordering under which a row's
  position is a function of nothing that can move — which is exactly the acceptance criterion
  ("rows never change position without a user act"). `updated-desc` is one click away, and choosing
  it IS the user act that makes rows movable.
- **Every comparator breaks ties on `id`**, so the order is total: two missions created in the same
  millisecond, or at the same stage, have exactly one legal arrangement, and re-sorting the same
  payload twice cannot produce two different screens. Tested directly.

This is on top of design-studio's own `ORDER BY` fix, not instead of it — F1's note that "a stable
payload order is the floor, not the feature" is the reason this exists at all.

### AC2 — filters by regime, stage, target repo, and a hide-terminal toggle

All four, client-side over the snapshot in hand (`GET /missions` takes no query parameters — unlike
`/design/systems`, whose two filters are real query params and therefore a re-fetch). The option
lists are derived from the payload, so only regimes/stages/repos that really have a mission are
offered: no filter on this bar can produce an empty table by construction. `hideTerminal` defaults
OFF — hiding rows by default would mean an owner's first look at the screen silently omits most of
it.

Two things the bar does that the criterion did not ask for and the screen needs anyway: a
"Showing N of M" count (with four filters on one bar, a narrowed list and a genuinely short one look
identical), and an empty state that says *which* emptiness it is — "No mission matches these filters
— 4 exist" versus "No design missions yet". The bar itself renders outside the state shell, so it
stays reachable while the table is empty; clearing a filter is precisely what an owner staring at an
empty table needs to do.

### AC3 — BLOCKED / ACTIVE / PAUSE-REQUESTED on the row

A labelled **Status** column, driven by `mission-markers.ts`: `blocked` → `active` →
`pause-requested` → `gate` (`NEEDS YOU`, from a non-null `gateContext`) → `matrix-stale`, in that
fixed severity-first order, each carrying the full sentence on its `title`. The running-agent tag
stays below the chips — `ACTIVE` says *that* something runs, the tag says *which* agent, in what
state, with the link to its run.

Rules the module holds to, all tested:

- every marker comes from a field design-studio really sends; **no marker is inferred from another's
  absence** (`activeDispatch: null` means three different things, per the wire's own documentation);
- `matrixStale` is read as `=== true`, so an absent field claims neither staleness nor freshness;
- `gateContext` absent and `null` render identically — an older design-studio sends no such key;
- a mission with none of them set gets an explicit em-dash, not a blank cell. "Nothing is claimed" is
  not the same as "healthy", and the screen does not say the second.

Two more of the demand's "available, unused" fields got columns while the table was open, because
both were named as making otherwise-identical rows distinguishable: **Pinned system**
(`designSystemVersion`) and **Rounds**. Rounds renders the two axes separately (`P11 · S2`) and never
folds them into one number — reading `latestRound` off the wrong axis is the worse failure the
coverage-gate demand already warned about.

### AC4 — a regime choice the owner can actually make

The `<select>` of slugs is gone. The field is a radio list rendered from `GET /regimes`, walked in
the doctrines' own `order`, each option carrying its `thesis`, its `discriminator` as "Choose it
when:", its `doctrine`, its `checklistSection`/`checklistSize` ("26 checklist item(s) to review at
each gate"), and its `avoidWhen` behind a "Do NOT choose it when…" disclosure on the option itself.

**Nothing in this repo carries a list of regimes any more**, which was the point of F2's closing
instruction. Confirmed by test: a fourth profile (`guided-turn-class`) added to the route's response
renders, selects and submits with no code change here. Two supporting changes made that true rather
than merely claimed:

- `NewMissionRequest.regime` and `DesignSystemFilters.regime` widened to `RegimeId`
  (`Regime | (string & {})`). A picker that can *display* a fourth regime but not *submit* it would
  be a worse failure than not rendering it. The previous `setRegime` guard was a three-way string
  check — itself a copy of the enum — and would have silently refused a regime the route had just
  offered; it now guards emptiness only.
- `regimeLabel`/`regimeChipClass` tolerate an unrecognized regime (render it back verbatim; neutral
  chip) instead of returning `undefined`, which rendered a blank cell and the literal string
  "undefined" in a `[class]` binding respectively.

The route ordering is applied client-side rather than trusted: the live payload confirms it, since
`GET /regimes` on `:8087` currently returns atlas(2), inhabited(3), console(4) — arrival order and
`order` are not the same list.

**Honest degrade.** A 404/unreachable `/regimes` falls back to the three named slugs *plus a visible
line saying they cannot be explained here and why*. Silently falling back to the unexplained list the
route was added to fix would reintroduce the defect invisibly. The form still submits — the regime is
a legal enum value on `POST /missions` whether or not the explaining route answers.

### AC5 — the Design system field says why it is empty or short

The `status=validated` half of the fetch moved client-side; the screen now reads the whole regime
list and splits it. The picker still offers validated systems alone (`_resolve_chosen_design_system`
refuses anything else), but the ones held back are now *counted*, which is what makes the sentence
possible:

- nothing at all for the regime → "No validated console-class design system exists yet — a new one
  will be built during this mission."
- something exists but is not validated → "…1 exists for this regime but is not validated, so it
  cannot be pinned at system-gate", with a link to `/design/systems`.
- a short-but-non-empty list gets the same treatment — the demand's `Rhizome` case, where switching
  to atlas-class surfaces `Herbarium` and correctly hides the draft, was unexplained too.
- a complete list says nothing at all.

A failed registry fetch is kept strictly apart from a correctly-empty one: an unreadable registry is
a different fact, and letting a fetch failure borrow this explanation would be the same defect in
the other direction.

### AC6 — the abort reason has a column

`Reason (aborted)`, its own labelled column, truncated with the full text on the cell's `title`. It
is out of the Stage cell entirely (asserted by test: the stage cell no longer contains the reason
text). A non-aborted row renders an em-dash there rather than a ragged blank.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **2280 tests pass, 207 files**, all green. 1008 of them under `src/app/design`,
  including the two new pure-logic suites (`mission-list-view.spec.ts`, `mission-markers.spec.ts`)
  and the three rewritten/extended component suites.
- `npx ng build` — clean.
- `GET /regimes` and `GET /missions` on `:8087` both answer 200 as of this session (the demand warned
  the instance was still serving the previous build; it has since been restarted), and the live
  `/regimes` payload matches the mirrored `RegimeProfile` shape field-for-field.
- No live browser pass was run for this change; every behaviour above is covered by component tests
  against the real DOM under jsdom.

## Flagged for design-studio, not acted on

- **`Regime` stays narrow on the READ side.** `Mission.regime`, `DesignSystem.regime` and the
  `Brief`/`Plan`/`Matrix` artifact types still declare the three-member union. That is correct today
  and will be *drift* the moment `guided-turn-class` is adopted and a mission carries it — the exact
  "the type says a guarantee the wire never made" class this repo's own model file warns about.
  Runtime is already safe (the label/chip helpers fall back honestly), so nothing renders wrong; the
  types are what will lie. Widening them fleet-wide is a separate change this demand does not ask for
  and it should land with the adoption, not ahead of it.
- **`GET /missions` still takes no query parameters.** Filtering is client-side and that is fine at
  today's volume, but the four filters here are exactly the four a server-side filter would take if
  the ledger ever outgrows one payload.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: launcher staleness read-only badge (D077)

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. This report
is this repo's only output for the demand; the origin (platform-vault) is never notified directly.

## Pre-check

Checked current state before starting, per the demand's own instruction. Grepped `src/` for
`stale`/`isStale` — zero hits — and confirmed `SocketSummary` (`src/app/launcher/socket-summary.ts`)
had no `stale` field yet. The companion `to: [launcher]` demand
(`platform-vault-20260723-launcher-stale-rebuild-restart-build`) was already fulfilled this session
window (commit `81241f8` on launcher's `main`, report at
`../launcher/demands/fulfilled/platform-vault-20260723-launcher-stale-rebuild-restart-build-report.md`),
so the `stale` object this demand consumes already exists on the wire — read launcher's `server.js`
and its fulfillment report directly to get the exact shape rather than guessing it. Not previously
shipped on this side; proceeded with the work.

## What shipped

### 1. Types (`socket-summary.ts`)
Added `SocketComponentStaleness` and `SocketStaleness`, matching launcher's `socketSummary()` /
`computeComponentStaleness()` output field-for-field: `{ isStale, checkedAt, components: [{ id,
label, isStale, runningCommit, mainHead, imageBuiltAt, checkedAt }] }`. `SocketSummary.stale` is
`SocketStaleness | null`, and made **optional** (`stale?:`) rather than required — an older launcher
build's response simply omits the field, and every other consumer of `SocketSummary` in this repo
(operate-screen's poll loop, start-fleet-macro, existing spec fixtures) constructs the type without
it, so making it required would have forced unrelated test-fixture edits across the codebase for a
field those call sites never touch.

### 2. Read model (`socket-row.component.ts`)
Two computed signals: `isStale()` reads `socket().stale?.isStale ?? false` (absent field, `null`
field, and `isStale: false` all fall through to `false` identically — the "degrades cleanly" criterion
is structural, not a branch that can be forgotten); `staleComponentLabels()` joins the labels of just
the stale components, for the badge's tooltip. No new component state, no HTTP call, no dashboard-owned
data — both signals are pure derivations of the `SocketSummary` the parent screen already polls via
the existing `GET /api/sockets` call in `launcher.service.ts` (untouched).

### 3. Badge (`socket-row.component.html`)
A `Stale build` badge renders next to the existing socket-type badge only when `isStale()` is true,
styled with the same `status-degraded` token the row's conflict-warning text already uses (a stale
build is an attention-worthy-but-not-broken signal, the same severity tier as a socket conflict, not
a `status-down` fault). `title` attribute names which components are stale. No button, link, or any
other affordance was added — verified by re-reading the finished template that the only new markup is
the `<span>` badge itself, nothing interactive.

### 4. Tests (`socket-row.component.spec.ts`)
Four new cases: no `stale` key at all (older launcher build), `stale: null` (socket with no tracked
components — the common case today, per launcher's report, for every socket but `platform-stack`/
`plantpal`), `stale.isStale: false`, and `stale.isStale: true` (asserts the badge renders and its
title lists the stale component's label, not the non-stale one). All 13 tests in the file pass; full
suite run afterward: 165 files / 1364 tests green (was 1360/165 immediately before this session per
the prior fulfillment report in this same repo).

## Confirms against acceptance criteria

- **Additive-field read, no new channel**: only `launcher.service.ts`'s existing `sockets()` call is
  used; nothing new was added to `LauncherService`.
- **Read-only, no rebuild/restart surface**: grepped the finished diff for `rebuild`/`restart` —
  zero hits outside this report's own prose. The badge has no click handler.
- **Degrades cleanly**: absent field, `null`, and `isStale: false` are all one code path (`?? false`),
  not three. Launcher being unreachable entirely is already handled upstream by the existing poll-error
  path in `operate-screen.component.ts` (`staleWarning`/`pollError`, unrelated naming coincidence with
  this demand's "stale" — pre-existing, not touched) — a row simply never renders without socket data,
  same as today.
- **No new dashboard-owned state/admin API surface**: confirmed — everything added is derived,
  read-only, computed-signal state scoped to a single row component; no service, store, or new HTTP
  call was introduced.

## Not done / caveats

- Only `SocketRowComponent` renders the badge. `StartFleetMacroComponent` (`start-fleet-macro.component.ts`)
  also reads `SocketSummary` but for the fleet-wide start/stop macro, not a per-socket detail view — the
  demand's acceptance criteria named "the console's existing launcher-socket panel" (singular, §2/§4),
  which is the Operate screen's socket list this session targeted. Left the macro component untouched;
  a future demand can extend badge visibility there if the owner wants it surfaced in more than one place.

# Fulfillment — dashboard: fix broken production build (unresolved `@platform/contracts` import)

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. This report
is this repo's only output for the demand; the origin (platform-vault) is never notified directly.

## Pre-check

Found an orphaned, unclosed `.brain` session record from an earlier dispatch of this exact demand
(`.brain/sessions/2026-07-24_0027_...md`, untracked, `status: partial`, empty `changes`/`decisions`/
`lessons`) — no actual work had been done under it. Confirmed the capability was NOT already shipped:
`npm run build` passed locally (see below, this is the local/container split that is the actual root
cause), but `docker compose build dashboard` — the path the demand names as authoritative — still
failed with the exact reported error. Proceeded with the work under a fresh session.

## Diagnosis

**`CostTickEvent` still exists, unchanged, under that name in contracts v0.17.0**
(`node_modules/@platform/contracts/state-event.ts:73`, `dist/state-event.d.ts:60`) — this is not an
upstream rename or removal. No `contracts` check is needed.

**Root cause is local to this repo: a stale Dockerfile path, not a tsconfig/import-path issue.**
`package.json:22` already pins `@platform/contracts` to
`file:../contracts-worktrees/v0.17.0/gen/ts` (bumped in `ad14bbf`, the atlas-class-regime session,
2026-07-23). But `Dockerfile:4` still read:

```
COPY --from=contracts . /contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts
```

— the Dockerfile's own half of that re-pin was never moved. Inside the container the `npm ci` step
resolves the `file:` dependency against `/contracts-worktrees/v0.17.0/gen/ts` (per package.json), but
the COPY had only ever populated `.../v0.15.0/gen/ts`, so that directory never existed in the build
image. This is exactly the "a pin lives in three places, move all three" failure mode
`runtime/docker-compose.local.yml`'s own header comment documents for the four Java services and
warns dashboard is exempt from ("dashboard stays v0.15.0/gen/ts... not moved this wave") — except it
was in fact half-moved (package.json only), which is worse than not moved at all: locally `npm
install` (not `ci`, and against a node_modules already populated from before the bump) papered over
it, so `npm run build` passed on a workstation with pre-existing `node_modules`, while a clean
containerized `npm ci` build failed outright. This matches the demand's own framing exactly: found by
the launcher's rebuild path (D077), which does a real containerized rebuild, not a workstation-cached
one.

**Confirmed via a fresh `docker compose build dashboard`, as the demand required — reproduced,
partially fixed, and the remainder isolated to a different repo:**

1. **Pre-fix repro**: `docker compose -f runtime/docker-compose.local.yml build dashboard` failed with
   `TS2307: Cannot find module '@platform/contracts' or its corresponding type declarations` at every
   one of this repo's five import sites (`wing.ts`, `status-strip.component.ts`,
   `job-progress-merge.ts`, `cost-concentration.ts`, `cost-history.service.ts`) — the whole module was
   unresolvable, not just `CostTickEvent`; the demand's report undersold the blast radius by naming
   only the one file it happened to hit first.
2. **Dockerfile fix applied**: `COPY --from=contracts . /contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts` →
   `.../v0.17.0/gen/ts` (matches package.json exactly; the only in-repo change this fix required).
3. **Post-fix rebuild**: the `Cannot find module '@platform/contracts'` errors are gone — module
   resolution now works. But the build **still fails**, on a different error:
   `TS2339`/`TS2322`/`TS2678` around `design.designSystem` / `DesignSystemEvent` in
   `snapshot-key.ts`, `state-feed.service.ts`, and `activity-label.ts` — the exhaustive
   `StateEvent`-union handling `ad14bbf` added for v0.17.0's new `design.designSystem` variant.
   Confirmed why: `contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts` has no `DesignSystemEvent` at all (grepped,
   zero hits) — the container is still building against **v0.15.0 contract content**, despite my
   Dockerfile fix, because `runtime/docker-compose.local.yml:307-308` (a different repo) still points
   this service's `contracts` build context at
   `additional_contexts: contracts: ../contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts`. My Dockerfile fix changed
   only the *destination* directory name the COPY writes to inside the image — the *source* content
   Docker copies from is decided by that `runtime` compose file's `additional_contexts` mapping, which
   nothing in this repo controls.

## What did NOT ship, and why

The `runtime/docker-compose.local.yml` half of this fix. Per this platform's standing rule (CLAUDE.md
"you work in ONE repo per session"), `runtime` is a sibling repo this session must not edit even for a
one-line, obviously-correct-looking fix — same posture as the `contracts`-repo escalation rule, just
for a different sibling. Flagging back to platform-vault rather than touching it:

**Needed in `runtime/docker-compose.local.yml`, lines 301-308** (the `dashboard` service's `build`
block): bump `additional_contexts.contracts` from `../contracts-worktrees/v0.15.0/gen/ts` to
`../contracts-worktrees/v0.17.0/gen/ts`, and update that block's own header comment (lines 301-306,
which currently says "dashboard/package.json + Dockerfile re-pinned together... this alias is the
host-side half of the same re-pin" — no longer true post-`ad14bbf` until this line itself moves).
Until that lands, `docker compose build dashboard` will keep silently building against stale v0.15.0
contract content even though every file inside this repo (`package.json`, `Dockerfile`) already says
v0.17.0 — the exact "half-repin" failure mode that file's own header comment already names and warns
about for the Java services, now confirmed to also apply, currently unfixed, to dashboard.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (`ng build`) — exits 0, clean (pre-existing 80KB bundle-budget warning only,
  unrelated).
- `npm test -- --run` — 165 files / 1364 tests green.
- `docker compose -f runtime/docker-compose.local.yml build dashboard`, pre-fix — reproduced the
  reported failure exactly (unresolved `@platform/contracts` import).
- Same command, post-fix — the reported failure is gone; a distinct, pre-existing, cross-repo
  half-repin failure remains and is reported above rather than worked around from here.

## Vault-sync

None from this repo's own state — no owner ruling made, no version tag cut, no port/service/layout
change in `dashboard`. The `runtime/docker-compose.local.yml` gap above is the substantive
vault-relevant fact from this session; reporting it here (rather than raising a second demand) since
this report already routes to platform-vault as the demand's origin, and the report explicitly says
routing further checks is platform-vault's call, not this repo's.

fulfillments.body: # Fulfillment — dashboard: console-wide clickable decision codes (D079) "Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary. ## Addendum — 2026-07-24, second session: anchor map re-derived from `documentations`' verified index The demand was amended before this second session's dispatch: `documentations/reference/decisions.md` now exists (github.com/elmoul/documentations) and carries all 81 decisions with real GitHub-rendered heading anchors, "verified against GitHub's own rendered anchors, not guessed" (that file's own words) — explicitly instructing a future session to derive the D-number → anchor map from that file rather than re-deriving slugs locally. **Current-state check (before working, second session):** the capability itself was already fully shipped — `git log` showed `feat(core): console-wide clickable decision codes (D079)` (`dab4b33`) on branch `feat/decision-code-links` (open PR #23) and a fulfillment report already on `main` (commit `93d4a80`, this file). Re-reading `src/app/core/decision-links.ts` on that branch confirmed it still used the *original* mechanism — a locally-snapshotted GitHub blob-view line anchor (`#L` into `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md`), pre-dating the amendment and not yet consuming `documentations`' index. So: not a no-op, and not a from-scratch build — closed the specific gap the amendment named. **What changed.** `DECISION_ANCHORS` (`core/decision-links.ts`) replaces the old `DECISION_LINES` line-number map: same shape (`Record`), but each value is now the real GitHub heading-anchor fragment copied verbatim from `documentations/reference/decisions.md`'s "All 81, by number" table (extracted programmatically from that file — 81 rows, no conflicts, D001..D081), instead of a line number into the raw file. `decisionUrl(code)` now builds `.../PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md#` (a rendered-markdown-view heading anchor) rather than `.../PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md#L` (a blob/raw-view line anchor) — both still resolve into the same vault file, but the new form deep-links to the *rendered* entry a reader actually reads, not a raw source line. The fallback behavior (a code with no map entry resolves to the bare vault file, never a broken link) is unchanged. Chose **not** to re-derive slugs from `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md` locally even now that this repo could attempt it — the whole reason this amendment exists is that those headings carry backticks, em-dashes, arrows, section signs and quotes that a naive slugify mangles, and `documentations` already did the GitHub-verification work once; re-deriving locally would reintroduce the exact silent-breakage risk the amendment closes. The map stays a committed snapshot, not a live fetch — unchanged reasoning from the original build (D029, no direct hexagon/vault polling outside the state-feed). **Where it landed.** Committed to `feat/decision-code-links` (still-open PR #23, the actual home of the D079 feature — not the unrelated `feat/documentation-screen` branch this session happened to start on) as a follow-up commit, `a7f6599`, extending the existing unreviewed PR rather than forking the fix onto a second branch. **Tests:** updated the one test in `decision-links.spec.ts` that hardcoded the old `#L16` anchor for D002, and the one in `markdown-to-html.spec.ts` that hardcoded `#L162` for D029, to their real anchors; added two new cases to `decision-links.spec.ts` — D081 (proves the map now reaches past the D001..D080 the original snapshot capped at) and D062 (an anchor with heavy punctuation — arrows, section sign, apostrophe-s — resolving correctly rather than via a locally-guessed slug). Full suite: **1400/1400 green**, 167 files, 0 failures. **Not re-raising the open follow-up demand.** `demands/2026-07-24-platform-vault-decision-link- snapshot-and-spec-drift.md` (`to: [platform-vault]`, still `status: open` on `main` as of this session) already names both remaining asks — spec-dashboard.md §9 drift closure, and a ruling on snapshot-vs-served-index staleness now that `documentations` exists — and this session's work is exactly what that demand's second ask was waiting on, not a new gap. Left it as-is for `platform- vault` to action; this session did not touch the vault or that demand file (D035). --- ## Original fulfillment (first session, below, unchanged) ## Current-state check (before working) Checked first per this demand's own instruction: no prior linkifier existed anywhere in the repo (`grep -ri "linkif|decision-link|decisionCode"` found nothing but this session's own in-progress `.brain` session file). Not previously shipped — proceeded with the build. ## Resolution mechanism shipped, and why **Shipped the demand's own named "floor," not the "nicer" popover** — a plain deep link to the vault's hosted `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md`, with a heading-line anchor when resolvable: `decisionUrl(code)` → `https://github.com/elmoul/platform-vault/blob/main/PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md#L` (falls back to the bare file URL, no anchor, when the code isn't in the snapshot — still resolves the reader to the vault file, the acceptance floor, never a broken link). **Line anchor over a GitHub heading-slug anchor.** The demand's own text flagged that heading anchors "need the title text, so a bare number → anchor map requires *some* index." Building that index still requires **some** bundled D-number → location map either way; a GitHub *blob-view* line anchor (`#L678`, on the raw-source view, not the rendered-markdown view) needs only a **line number** per code, not the full heading title text plus GitHub's slug algorithm reimplemented (lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse spaces, dedupe suffixes — a real algorithm to get exactly right or ship subtly-broken anchors). Simpler, same "one bundled snapshot" cost, and it degrades the same way (a stale/missing entry still opens the file). `DECISION_LINES` in `core/decision-links.ts` is a one-time snapshot of every `### D0xx` heading's line number, taken 2026-07-24 against `platform-vault`'s `main` (commit `8c57163`, covers D001..D080 — the vault gained D080 *while this session was reading the file*, confirming live drift is real and current). **Did not build the popover.** D079's own consequences text is explicit that a popover's data path "must be proposed, not invented" here; I judged the deep-link floor sufficient to close this demand and left the popover as a genuinely separate, not-yet-scoped enhancement (see Follow-up below) rather than inventing a title/status data path unasked. **No served index or bundled title/status map was built.** Per the demand's own instruction not to assume `documentation`'s `reference/decisions.md` exists — confirmed live: `../documentation` isn't even `git init`'d yet (`spec-documentation.md` still says "repo not yet bootstrapped"). # Fulfillment — dashboard: Documentations screen (`/documentation`)

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.
Full build-notes trail: `PROGRESS.md`'s Session 18 (2026-07-24) entry, `.brain/sessions/2026-07-24_1952_fulfill-demand-platform-vault-20260724-d.md`.

## Checked current state first

Two prior dispatch attempts for this same demand had already been supervised-launched
(`.brain/sessions/2026-07-24_1925...md` and `2026-07-24_1952...md`, both logged only "Session opened",
`status: partial`, empty `changes`) — but the working tree already held a complete, uncommitted
implementation: the full `src/app/documentation/` feature folder, `scripts/sync-docs-content.mjs`,
and matching edits to `app.routes.ts`, `sidebar.component.ts` (+specs), `app.component.spec.ts`,
`markdown-to-html.ts` (+spec), `decision-links.ts` (+spec), `package.json`, and `.gitignore`. Per the
task brief's own instruction ("if it is [already shipped], write the fulfillment report documenting
that instead of redoing the work"), this session verified the existing implementation against every
acceptance criterion and the real sibling `../documentations` checkout, closed the two orphaned brain
sessions honestly (1925 marked `abandoned`, superseded by 1952; 1952 closed `done` with the real
change list), filled three gaps the self-describing-repo convention flagged (below), and committed —
rather than re-implementing something that was already correct.

The 1925/1952 session files' own empty logs suggest the worker process that actually wrote this code
died before recording anything in `.brain/` (the same failure class the repo's own `2026-07-24_0419`
precedent names) — recorded per D052 rather than silently deleted or silently reused as if this
session had written the code from scratch.

## What shipped

- **`src/app/documentation/`** — `docs-manifest.model.ts` (`DocEntry`/`DocsSection`/`DocsManifest`),
  `docs-manifest.service.ts` (`DocsManifestService`: `manifest()`, `docContent(path)`,
  `assetUrl(sectionKey, relativeSrc)`), `documentation-screen.component.{ts,html}` (the routed
  `/documentation` screen) — 13 tests across the two spec files.
- **`scripts/sync-docs-content.mjs`** — copies `../documentations`' README + section directories
  (`workflows`, `overview`, `runbooks`, `guides`, `reference`, `onboarding` — the fixed taxonomy
  mirroring that repo's own README table) into `public/docs-content/`, generating `manifest.json`.
  Never fails the build if the sibling checkout is absent — writes an honest `available: false`
  manifest and warns instead.
- **`package.json`** — `docs:sync` script, prepended to `start`/`build`/`watch` via `npm run docs:sync
  && ng ...`.
- **`.gitignore`** — `/public/docs-content` (generated, never authored/committed).
- **`src/app/app.routes.ts`** — `/documentation` route (no `:id` split; one screen with in-page
  section/doc selection, per its own doc comment).
- **`src/app/shell/sidebar.component.ts`** (+spec) — `Documentation` nav entry appended straight after
  `Brain`, same placement rule every post-§3.1 addition has used.
- **`src/app/app.component.spec.ts`** — nav-link count assertion `15 -> 16`.
- **`src/app/brain/view/markdown-to-html.ts`** (+spec) — added pipe-table, `[text](url)` link, and
  `![alt](src)` image rendering (shared with the pre-existing brain docs viewer). An absolute
  `http(s)` link becomes a real out-link; a relative one (meaningless once rendered outside its own
  file tree) renders its label only, never a dead `href`. A new `resolveImageSrc` parameter lets a
  caller rewrite relative image paths against wherever it served the copied asset; callers that never
  emit images can omit it.
- **`src/app/core/decision-links.ts`** (+spec) — `linkifyDecisionCodesInHtml`'s existing code-span
  skip extended to also skip already-rendered `<a>` spans, so a D-code that is itself a markdown link
  label (`reference/decisions.md`'s `[D001](vault-url)` rows) never produces a nested `<a><a>...`.
- **Self-describing-repo gaps filled this session** (the code's own comments referenced these but they
  didn't exist yet — precision ethic, D053): `DEPLOYMENT.md` gained a "Documentations content sync"
  section describing the build-time mechanism and its honest-degrade path; `HEXAGON.md` gained
  `documentations` in `deps`, a Dependencies-section entry explaining it's a build-time file
  dependency (not a runtime port — `documentations` "is not deployed"), and D078/D080 in the decisions
  row; `CHANGELOG.md` gained an `[Unreleased]` entry for the whole feature.

## Acceptance criteria — how each is met

1. **Reachable from main nav, consistent with other Era II screens** — `Documentation` sidebar entry,
   same placement/styling pattern as `Brain`/`Design`/`Agents`; `SidebarComponent` spec asserts the
   full label list including it.
2. **Real, non-broken state for any missing section/doc — a missing doc is normal, never a dead link
   or console error** — `exists: false` per section (`runbooks`/`guides` today, confirmed against the
   real `../documentations` checkout, which has no such directories yet) renders an explicit "Not
   created yet" block, never a dead link; `manifest.available === false` (sibling checkout absent at
   build time) renders an explicit unavailable state with a link out; a doc-content fetch failure
   renders the shared error/unreachable state via `StateShellComponent`, never a blank pane or thrown
   error. Ten `DocumentationScreenComponent` tests cover every one of these branches, including the
   AMENDED "7 real docs now exist" state (a section with docs renders them; selecting one fetches and
   renders real formatted markdown).
3. **Content-fetch mechanism is the worker's judgment, reasoning recorded** — **build-time bundle**,
   documented in three places (`DocsManifestService`'s own doc comment, `documentation-screen.
   component.ts`'s own doc comment, `sync-docs-content.mjs`'s own doc comment, and now `DEPLOYMENT.md`
   too): `documentations` itself declares "not deployed... v1 is plain-repo-only" (its own
   `DEPLOYMENT.md`, read this session to confirm still true), and this console never polls a hexagon
   directly outside the state-feed (D029) — there is no live endpoint to bundle-fetch from instead.
   `scripts/sync-docs-content.mjs` reads the sibling checkout the same way any agent session reads
   `../platform-vault`, no auth, no network call. A link out to the hosted repo (`https://github.com/
   elmoul/documentations`) is present as the floor in every degraded state.
4. **AMENDED — README/overview/workflows/reference/onboarding exist and are relied on; runbooks/guides
   don't and aren't assumed; new docs pick up without a hardcoded file list** — verified live against
   the real sibling checkout this session (`sync-docs-content.mjs` run directly: "bundled 6 doc(s)
   across 4 section(s)" — `overview`, `workflows`, `reference`, `onboarding` all present with real
   `.md` files, `runbooks`/`guides` correctly absent). The *docs inside* each section are read off
   `readdirSync` at sync time, never hardcoded — a newly-landed doc needs a rebuild (the build-time
   mechanism's own named cost), never a dashboard code change.
5. **A dependency on another repo serving/exposing something is named as a follow-up demand, not
   assumed or built into a sibling repo** — the chosen mechanism needs no such thing: it reads plain
   files off a checkout, same posture as `conventions`/`platform-vault`. No follow-up demand was
   required or raised. A *live/served index* is named in three places as a real, optional future
   capability, not built here and not assumed of `documentations` — left as a named option, not filed
   as a demand, since nothing here depends on it.
6. **Existing tests stay green; new screen has its own tests covering the pre-content state at
   minimum** — full suite **1423/1423 green** (`npx vitest run`, 169 test files), including all
   pre-existing suites unmodified in behavior. The new feature's own 17 tests (`DocsManifestService`:
   3, `DocumentationScreenComponent`: 10, plus 4 new `markdown-to-html`/`decision-links` groups)
   explicitly cover the pre-content states: loading, unreachable (status 0), error (non-2xx),
   `available: false`, and `exists: false` per section — every one asserted as its own real DOM state,
   never a generic blank.

## Placement / design decisions (as implemented; verified, not re-litigated)

- **One route, no `:id` split** — a doc is lightweight content with no action surface, unlike
  `demands`/`design`/`brain/*`'s list/detail split.
- **Fixed section taxonomy, dynamic doc list within each** — the six sections mirror
  `documentations/README.md`'s own table (a rare-to-change structural fact); the docs inside are never
  hardcoded, satisfying the "grows on demand" requirement without a live-fetch mechanism.
- **`renderMarkdownToHtml` shared, not forked** — the pre-existing brain docs viewer and this screen
  now share one renderer; extended rather than duplicated, keeping the escape-then-emit safety
  property (D036, XSS posture) in exactly one place.
- **No new markdown/table npm dependency** — same reasoning this repo's own prior brain-browser
  fulfillment gave: a small hand-written extension covers exactly what the real corpus needs (mostly
  pipe tables and relative/absolute links) without adding to the `Vitest`-pinned toolchain's dependency
  surface.

## Not done / caveats

- **Bundle-budget WARNING, not error**: `ng build` succeeds; initial bundle is 786.15 kB against a
  686.08 kB *warning* threshold (100.07 kB over — a real build-time WARNING, verified this session,
  not previously present at this magnitude). `maximumError` is 1 MB, well clear. Flagged honestly per
  this repo's own precedent (WU-117/119, theme-c restyle) rather than silently ignored; not bumped in
  `angular.json` this session since it does not block the build and this demand did not ask for a
  budget change.
- **No live browser round-trip against a served `ng serve`** — verified via `HttpTestingController`
  -mocked requests (route paths/response shapes cross-checked against the service's own real
  implementation) and a direct, real run of `sync-docs-content.mjs` against the actual `../documentations`
  checkout (confirmed 6 docs / 4 sections bundled correctly). Starting `ng serve` and clicking through
  the live UI in a browser was not done this session — the standing gap every prior dashboard
  fulfillment report in this repo has named for the same reason (no browser available in this
  environment); the full Vitest suite plus a real production `ng build` are the verification depth
  available here.
- **`documentations` HEXAGON.md already names `dashboard` as its documented consumer** (its own
  `HEXAGON.md`, row: "`dashboard` (Documentations console page, D080)") — read this session to confirm
  alignment, not edited (never patch a sibling repo from here).

## Tests / build

- `npx vitest run` (full suite): **1423/1423 green**, 169 test files, no pre-existing assertion
  changed except the one intentional nav-count bump (`app.component.spec.ts`, 15 -> 16).
- `node scripts/sync-docs-content.mjs` run directly against the real `../documentations` checkout:
  `[sync-docs-content] bundled 6 doc(s) across 4 section(s)`.
- `npm run build`: clean (`docs:sync` + `ng build`), one pre-existing-class bundle-budget WARNING
  (not an error, see above).
- Conventions validator (`java -jar conventions/validator/target/conventions-validator-0.1.0-shaded.jar
  dashboard`, run from the platform root): **PASS, 15 checks, 0 failed, 1 pre-existing UNVERIFIED**
  (`status-coherence` — HEXAGON.md's `status: building` vs. the vault register's `active`-shaped prose;
  pre-existing drift, explicitly noted in the register itself as "not touched here" by a prior session,
  unrelated to this demand).

## For the origin (platform-vault) / the architect

- No follow-up owed from `platform-vault` or `documentations` to close this out — the chosen mechanism
  (build-time bundle off a sibling checkout) needs nothing served or exposed by either repo beyond what
  already exists.
- A live/served index for `documentations` remains a real, named, *optional* future capability (three
  separate doc comments + `DEPLOYMENT.md` name it) — only worth raising as its own demand if
  build-time-only freshness (new doc needs a dashboard rebuild to appear) becomes a real operational
  pain point. Not raised this session since nothing here is blocked on it.
- Per `../DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4: `done` is a claim; the coordinator/owner validates and delivers this
  report. The origin demand lives in `platform-vault`'s own `demands/` — `platform-vault` archives it
  once the coordinator confirms this report.

COPY --from=documentations . /documentations

# Fulfillment — dashboard: D084 executioner model + effort selectors on the brain surface

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary.

## What was asked

Of this repo, two criteria (the `ai-gateway` and `brain-toolkit` legs are other repos'):

- the brain surface offers model and effort selectors pre-filled with the current defaults, which
  **write the stored policy** through `ai-gateway`'s policy surface (owner-ruled 2026-07-28, the
  D084 addendum);
- **no run-trigger route is added on either side** — D070's reads-only `GET /brain/*` invariant
  stands unqualified and `dashboard` holds no policy state of its own;

plus the shared criterion that each repo's spec/build-notes cite D084.

## Current state before the work

Checked first, as instructed. Not shipped. Two earlier supervised sessions on this demand
(`2026-07-28_0536`, status `failed`; `2026-07-28_0700`, still open) had left an uncommitted
working tree: the `model-policy.model.ts` wire-shape edits and a first cut of
`executioner-policy-form.ts`, with no component, no wiring, no tests, and nothing committed. Those
two files were kept and built on; everything else here is new. The `/brain` screen itself carried
only D070 reads plus the D083 dispatch selectors — no policy editing at all.

The `ai-gateway` leg **is** already live (`b78154a`), so this leg was built against its real code,
read directly: `SetPolicyRequest`'s merge semantics and `CLEAR_EFFORT`, `ReasoningEffort`'s four
tiers, `PolicyEntryDto.effort`, `PolicyResolutionResponse`'s `resolvedEffort` +
`providerModelHint` — not against the demand text alone.

## What shipped

A new panel on `/brain`, `ExecutionerPolicyPanelComponent`, under the fleet table. Per `.brain`
repo it shows the three frontier functions — `extraction`, `tier3-classifier`,
`contradiction-screen` — each with its stored row (`policy` + `effort`, with the
explicit/inherited badge), the live resolution rendered as one phrase
(`claude-opus-5 at high effort, routed on claude-code`), and an Edit affordance opening two
selectors seeded from what is stored. Saving goes through the shared class-2 before→after confirm
dialog to `PUT /ai/policy/{repo}/{function}`, then re-reads.

Three decisions worth naming, because each one could have gone the other way:

1. **The model selector is deliberately narrow** — `auto` (labelled with the model it currently
   inherits), the resolved frontier model itself, and whatever the row already pins if that is
   neither. Not the model catalog. `ai-gateway` gives *only* the frontier default the separate
   `providerModelHint: claude-code`; any other `claude-*` id resolves its hint to its own name,
   matches `AnthropicAdapter`'s prefix, and moves the nightly sweep onto `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — the
   API-credit path the owner declined on 2026-07-28. `ai.catalog.models` in `ai-gateway`'s own
   `application.yml` says this in as many words ("The brain surface's model selector should read
   `GET /ai/policy/resolve` for the D084 default instead"), and that is what this does. The
   unrestricted `force:<anything>` text input still exists on the Settings screen for the case
   where an owner really means it.
2. **The form seeds from the stored row, never from the resolution.** Pre-filling a `force:` box
   with the resolved `claude-opus-5` would let one confirming click convert an inherited `auto` row
   into an explicit pin at today's value — precisely the drift D072's standing watch exists for and
   which D084's supersede-on-load had to undo once already. The resolved pair is shown *beside* the
   form instead. For the same reason Save stays disabled until something actually changes: a no-op
   PUT would still flip `explicit` to `true`.
3. **Writes carry only the changed fields**, which is what `ai-gateway`'s per-field merge is built
   for — the model selector cannot clear a pinned effort, and unpinning an effort uses the explicit
   `effort: "default"` sentinel rather than an absent field.

`embeddings` renders no row here at all: it carries no effort by ruling, and a write attempting one
is a 400. It remains fully editable on the Settings screen's own model-policy panel, which is
unchanged apart from the optional-`policy` handling D084's merge semantics required.

## The reads-only criterion, explicitly

No route was added on either side. The panel talks to `ai-gateway` only — its spec asserts this
directly (`httpMock.expectNone(agentRunnerBaseUrl)` after a full load). The one thing it takes from
`agent-runner` is the repo list the screen had already read via `GET /brain/repos`, passed down as
an input rather than fetched again. Nothing here launches a run: a pick lands in the **stored-row
tier** of D084's precedence order (per-run flag > stored row > fleet default, privacy above all),
changing what the *next* executioner run resolves. The panel's own on-screen note says this to the
owner in those terms, so the surface does not read as a run button.

`dashboard` holds no policy state of its own: both the row and the resolution are read live per
repo, and a save is followed by a re-read rather than a local patch.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **1553/1553 green** (21 new cases; no existing test rewritten to accommodate
  the change beyond adding the new DTO fields to fixtures and draining the new ai-gateway reads in
  the brain-screen spec's `afterEach`, which previously drained only the rollup).
- `npm run build` — clean (the pre-existing initial-bundle budget warning is unchanged).
- **Not live-verified against a running gateway.** This session had no owner-granted scope for live
  writes against `runtime`'s `ai-gateway`, and a live check here would mean mutating real policy
  rows for real repos. The wire shapes were instead verified by reading `ai-gateway`'s shipped
  source directly (`PolicyController.mergeWrite`, `SetPolicyRequest`, `ReasoningEffort`,
  `PolicyEntryDto`, `PolicyResolutionResponse`). Stated plainly rather than implied: the console
  leg is source-verified against the server leg, not exercised end-to-end.

## Not done here, and why

- **`spec-dashboard.md` §9 build-note.** The spec lives in the vault, D035's single writer. Raised
  as `dashboard-20260728-platform-vault-spec-d084-build-note`, carrying both scoping judgments
  above so they are reviewable rather than tribal.
- **The `ai-gateway` and `brain-toolkit` legs.** Other repos' criteria; the gateway's is already
  live (`b78154a`) and was read, not touched.
- **D081 doc-sync.** D084's own entry records the doc-sync demand as already raised by the vault
  with the rest of the D084 set; this session raised no duplicate.

Pin moved **from v0.4.0** (confirmed by reading `.brain/toolkit-pin` before editing — not v0.5.1) **to v0.6.2**.

All four acceptance criteria completed in this repo:

1. `.brain/toolkit-pin` reads `v0.6.2`, committed (`43d783a`, `754...` chain) and pushed to `main`.
2. Verified by actual use, not by reading the file: ran `python .brain/bin/brain session open "fleet re-pin to brain-toolkit v0.6.2" --priority 2` and confirmed `.brain/sessions/2026-07-31_2258_fleet-re-pin-to-brain-toolkit-v0-6-2.md` was written to disk.
3. `python .brain/bin/structurer --kind incremental` run once, CPU-only — regenerated `AGENT.md` (8 units created, 0 merged/superseded/staled), committed.
4. `CLAUDE.md`'s `.brain` section hand-edited: the bare `.brain/bin/brain session open ...` / `.brain/bin/brain session close` forms are replaced with the `python`-prefixed forms, with an explanatory note (shims are extensionless `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, PowerShell honours no shebang, bare form exits clean and silently writes nothing). The pin-mechanism paragraph's "(currently `v0.4.0`)" note was also updated to `v0.6.2`.

Session closed cleanly (`brain session close`, status: done), `PROGRESS.md` handoff block regenerated as the projection, all commits pushed to `origin/main`.

# Fulfillment — CORS allow-list for the console origin

## What changed

- `connector_gmail/config.py` — `Settings` gained `cors_allowed_origins:
  tuple[str, ...]`, loaded from env var `CONNECTOR_CORS_ORIGINS`
  (comma-separated), defaulting to `http://localhost:4200` when unset. A new
  `_parse_cors_origins()` helper strips whitespace and **raises `ValueError`
  if a wildcard (`*`) is present** — the service refuses to construct
  `Settings` (and therefore refuses to start) rather than silently accept a
  wildcard origin.
- `connector_gmail/cors.py` (new) — `PathScopedCORSMiddleware`, a thin ASGI
  wrapper around Starlette's stock `CORSMiddleware`.
- `connector_gmail/main.py` — mounts `PathScopedCORSMiddleware` with
  `paths={"/vocabulary", "/health"}` and `allow_origins=settings
  .cors_allowed_origins`, `allow_methods=["GET"]`.
- `DEPLOYMENT.md` — documents the new env var and a "Console CORS grant"
  section explaining the design choice below.
- `tests/test_cors.py` (new) — 7 tests: grant present on `/vocabulary` and
  `/health` for the console origin, absent for an unlisted origin, absent on
  `POST /invoke` (both the actual response and an OPTIONS preflight), plus
  two unit tests on the env-var parser (split/strip, wildcard rejection).

## The app-wide vs. route-scoped decision — **route-scoped, not app-wide**

I did **not** use FastAPI/Starlette's stock `CORSMiddleware` mounted directly
on `app`. I inspected `starlette/middleware/cors.py` (installed version, in
`.venv`) to check its actual behavior before deciding, and confirmed it is
**path-agnostic**: `CORSMiddleware.__call__` keys off the request's `Origin`
header only — it never looks at `scope["path"]`. If mounted app-wide with
`allow_origins=["http://localhost:4200"]`, it would stamp
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:4200` onto **every** matching
response, `POST /invoke` included, the moment a request carried that Origin
header. That directly violates the requirement that `/invoke` stay outside
the browser grant.

Instead, `connector_gmail/cors.py` implements `PathScopedCORSMiddleware`: an
ASGI wrapper holding one real `CORSMiddleware` instance internally. On each
request it checks `scope["path"]`; only `/vocabulary` and `/health` are
delegated into the wrapped `CORSMiddleware` (so they get the standard,
well-tested preflight/simple-response CORS handling). Every other path,
`/invoke` included, is passed straight to the app — the `CORSMiddleware`
instance never runs against it, so no `Origin` value a browser sends can ever
earn `/invoke` a CORS header. This was verified live (below): the preflight
`OPTIONS /invoke` doesn't even succeed (405, no route registered for OPTIONS
there), and a same-Origin `POST /invoke` returns 200 with no
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header — a browser page cannot read that
response's body cross-origin regardless of what verb was requested.

`gmail.readonly` scope and D026 ("flag never act") are untouched; no new
endpoints were added.

## Test result

Full existing suite plus the new file, run via `.venv/Scripts/python -m
pytest -q`:

```
35 passed, 1 warning in 0.95s
```

(warning is the pre-existing, unrelated `httpx`/`starlette.testclient`
deprecation notice — not new.)

## Live verification (container rebuilt)

Rebuilt only this service against the running local stack:

```
docker compose -f C:\Users\pc\Desktop\platform\runtime\docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build --no-deps connector-gmail
```

Build succeeded (`DONE_0`), only `runtime-connector-gmail-1` was recreated —
every other container in the stack stayed `Running` untouched. Confirmed
clean startup via `docker logs runtime-connector-gmail-1`:

```
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8090 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
```

`curl` evidence against the live container on `localhost:8090`:

**`GET /vocabulary` with `Origin: http://localhost:4200`:**
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
vary: Origin
```

**`GET /health` with `Origin: http://localhost:4200`:**
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
vary: Origin
```

**`GET /vocabulary` with an unlisted `Origin: http://evil.example`** — no
`access-control-allow-origin` header in the response at all (grant correctly
withheld).

**`POST /invoke` with `Origin: http://localhost:4200`** (undeclared verb,
still gets a normal `refused` response body):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
— no `access-control-allow-origin` header. Confirmed excluded from the grant.

**`OPTIONS /invoke` preflight with `Origin: http://localhost:4200` +
`Access-Control-Request-Method: POST`:**
```
HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
allow: POST
```
— no CORS headers either; a real browser's preflight would fail here before
the actual POST is ever attempted for the console origin, which is an
additional (if incidental) layer on top of the missing response header.

## For dashboard's next session

- The console can now `fetch()` `http://localhost:8090/vocabulary` and
  `http://localhost:8090/health` directly from `http://localhost:4200` and
  read the response bodies in page script (loopback-only, per D040 — this
  only works from the same machine, same as today).
- `POST /invoke` remains structurally unreachable from browser script on this
  origin (or any other) — if the console needs to dispatch a Gmail verb, that
  must continue to go through a server-side hop (e.g. `orchestrator`), not
  directly from the browser. This was a deliberate exclusion per the demand,
  not an oversight to raise a follow-up about.
- If a second console origin (e.g. a deployed dashboard URL, not just
  `localhost:4200`) ever needs the same grant, set `CONNECTOR_CORS_ORIGINS`
  to a comma-separated list in `connector-gmail`'s `.env` /
  `runtime/secrets` — no code change needed, wildcards remain rejected.

# Fulfillment — ai-gateway: per-hexagon model-policy store + resolution API [R4]

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and delivers this summary to
`agent-runner`. This report is the authoritative API contract for the sibling `to: [dashboard]`
demand (owner-facing settings panel, R4 item 4) to build against.

## What shipped

New `io.platform.aigateway.policy` package (13 main classes) + `PolicyController`
(`io.platform.aigateway.web`), 49 new tests, **187/187 total green** (`mvn test`, JDK 21).

- `ModelFunction` — `extraction | tier3-classifier | embeddings` (§9.0's exact wire tokens).
- `ModelPolicy` — sealed `Auto`/`Force(model)`, parses/emits exactly `auto` / `force:<model>`.
- `PrivacyMode` — `frontier | local | rules-only` (§9.2a's `config.yml` literal values).
- `PolicyStore` — the persisted store (repo × function → override), JSON-file-backed.
- `PolicyResolutionService` — turns a stored/default policy + optional declared privacy mode
  into a concrete model.
- `PolicyController` — `GET /ai/policy`, `GET /ai/policy/{repo}`, `PUT /ai/policy/{repo}/{function}`,
  `GET /ai/policy/resolve`.

## API contract (authoritative — code against this)

All responses are `ApiResponse<T>` (`{"data": ..., "error": null}` on success; `{"data": null,
"error": "<message>"}` on a 4xx). All self-invented shapes — nothing here is `contracts`-defined.

### `GET /ai/policy`

Every explicitly-set override, across every repo. Empty list means no repo has ever had an
override set — every repo/function is on its §9.0 default.

Response `data`: `PolicyEntryDto[]`
```json
[
  {"repo": "agent-runner", "function": "tier3-classifier", "policy": "force:claude-opus-4-8", "explicit": true}
]
```

### `GET /ai/policy/{repo}`

Effective policy for **all 3 functions** for one repo — merges stored overrides with §9.0
defaults. `explicit: false` means "this is the inherited default, no override has ever been set
here"; `explicit: true` means "an owner explicitly set this."

Response `data`: `PolicyEntryDto[]` (always length 3, one per `ModelFunction`)
```json
[
  {"repo": "agent-runner", "function": "extraction", "policy": "auto", "explicit": false},
  {"repo": "agent-runner", "function": "tier3-classifier", "policy": "force:claude-opus-4-8", "explicit": true},
  {"repo": "agent-runner", "function": "embeddings", "policy": "auto", "explicit": false}
]
```

400 (`MissingRepoIdentifierException`) if `repo` is blank.

### `PUT /ai/policy/{repo}/{function}`

Owner sets (or resets) one repo/function's policy. `{function}` is a path segment, one of the
3 literal tokens above (e.g. `PUT /ai/policy/agent-runner/tier3-classifier`).

Request body:
```json
{"policy": "auto"}
```
or
```json
{"policy": "force:claude-opus-4-8"}
```

Response `data`: one `PolicyEntryDto` (`explicit: true` always — a `PUT` is always an explicit
act, even when the value happens to be `"auto"`).

**There is no DELETE endpoint.** `PUT {"policy": "auto"}` is how the dashboard resets a
repo/function back to its §9.0 default — this sidesteps this repo's soft-deletes-only house
convention entirely rather than inventing a tombstone shape for a single config value. The
dashboard's settings panel should render this as a "reset to default" action that issues this
exact `PUT`, not a delete.

Failure modes: 400 `UnknownModelFunctionException` (bad `{function}` segment — must be exactly
`extraction`, `tier3-classifier`, or `embeddings`), 400 `InvalidModelPolicyException` (body
`policy` isn't exactly `auto` or `force:<model>`, or the `<model>` half is blank), 400
`MissingRepoIdentifierException` (blank `{repo}`).

### `GET /ai/policy/resolve?repo={repo}&function={function}&privacy={privacy}`

**The endpoint the structurer calls.** `repo` and `function` are required query parameters;
`privacy` is optional and is only consulted for `function=tier3-classifier` (§9.2a's `config.yml`
switch has no meaning for the other two functions — it is silently ignored there, not rejected).

Response `data`: `PolicyResolutionResponse`
```json
{
  "repo": "agent-runner",
  "function": "tier3-classifier",
  "policy": "force:claude-opus-4-8",
  "resolvedModel": "claude-opus-4-8",
  "privacyEnforced": false,
  "selfDefendingAuditRequired": false
}
```

- `resolvedModel` — pass this straight through as `modelHint` on a subsequent
  `POST /ai/request` (or `/ai/jobs`) call. **`null` only** when `function=tier3-classifier` and
  `privacy=rules-only` — §9.2a: "rules-only treats unresolved as mentioned", no model call
  happens at all; the caller should skip the LLM call entirely in that case, not retry or
  substitute a default.
- `privacyEnforced` — `true` only when a declared `local` or `rules-only` privacy constraint
  determined the outcome (never `true` for `frontier` or an absent `privacy` param — those apply
  no restriction). Signals "the policy store's own answer was overridden by repo-local law."
- `selfDefendingAuditRequired` — `tier3-classifier` only, always `false` for the other two
  functions. `true` whenever the resolved model is not the configured frontier model (whether
  because of an owner `force:<model>` override or a `privacy=local` constraint). This flag only
  signals that §9.2a's weekly audit-agreement floor (0.75) applies to this call — evaluating that
  floor is the structurer's own metric (external to this gateway; `graph.md`-reported), not
  computed here.

400 (`UnknownModelFunctionException` / `InvalidPrivacyModeException` /
`MissingRepoIdentifierException`) on a bad `function`, a bad `privacy` value, or a blank `repo`.

**Two-step flow for the structurer:** (1) `GET /ai/policy/resolve?repo=agent-runner&function=extraction`
→ read `resolvedModel`; (2) `POST /ai/request` with `modelHint: <resolvedModel>`. The resolution
call makes no provider call itself — see Metering below.

## §9.0 default-resolution semantics (what `auto` means per function)

| Function | `auto` resolves to | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `extraction` | `ai.policy.frontier-model` (default `claude-code`) | The multi-run frontier→downshift *progression* itself (§9.0: first ~10 runs, then downshift, spot-check escalation) is stateful run-counting logic left to the structurer (not yet built) — this gateway holds no per-repo run history (spec-ai-gateway.md §5, "deliberately close to stateless"). What's guaranteed here is only the resolved *default* model today; once the structurer decides to downshift by its own bookkeeping, it expresses that via `PUT .../force:<model>`, not by this gateway tracking counts on its behalf. |
| `tier3-classifier` | `ai.policy.frontier-model`, **always** | Never auto-downshifted (§9.0's explicit override of generic `auto` semantics) — this is enforced unconditionally, not by any counting logic. |
| `embeddings` | `ai.ollama.model` (the same local-model config every other Ollama-routed call in this repo already uses — no second source of truth) | Cheap by design, no progression. |

`ai.policy.frontier-model` defaults to `claude-code` (not a generic Anthropic model) because
Appendix A.5 names the `claude-code` provider specifically as the frontier path for tier-3
classification and frontier-mode structurer runs, metered under `claude-credits`.

## Privacy precedence — how it's implemented, and why

**Chosen mechanism: the resolution API takes the caller's declared privacy mode as a request
parameter; the gateway enforces the precedence rule on it server-side.** This is the demand's own
documented fallback, chosen deliberately over having the gateway read a sibling repo's
`.brain/config.yml` directly:

- This gateway's one filesystem-access precedent, `ManifestRegistry` (gap G5), scans a single
  **gateway-owned, explicitly mounted** directory of `ai-model-manifest.yaml` files — it is not an
  open-ended read of an arbitrary sibling repo's arbitrary path. Its own javadoc/DEPLOYMENT.md
  explain why: the built Docker image never contains sibling repos' source at all, so any such
  read needs its own `runtime`-compose volume mount, same as `AI_MANIFEST_DIR` already needs.
- Standing up a second, differently-shaped mount (a scan of every `.brain`-enabled repo's
  `config.yml`) for this one demand, with no compose wiring to back it and no other consumer
  today, would be exactly the kind of speculative infrastructure the platform's conventions warn
  against — and this repo cannot make that `runtime`-repo change itself (never edit a sibling
  repo).
- The demand text explicitly sanctions this fallback: *"if not, the resolution API takes the
  declared privacy mode as a caller-presented constraint and the gateway enforces the precedence
  rule on it."*

**Enforcement is still genuinely gateway-side, not UI-side**, because the *decision* — does a
forced/auto frontier resolution get overridden — happens inside `PolicyResolutionService`, never
left to the caller to self-police. The caller only supplies the one input this gateway has no
other way to observe yet (the repo's own `config.yml` value); it cannot use that input to talk the
gateway into a different outcome than the precedence rule dictates. Concretely: a caller declaring
`privacy=local` while the store says `force:claude-opus-4-8` still gets `resolvedModel:
"gemma3:4b"` (or whatever `ai.ollama.model` is configured to) back — the caller cannot get the
forced remote model by omitting the parameter either, since the *structurer itself* is the one
reading its own `config.yml` and is expected to pass it honestly; a caller lying about its own
privacy mode is a different trust problem than this demand scopes (same trust boundary every other
caller-supplied field on this gateway already has — `appId`, `userId`, etc.).

**Follow-up flagged, not built:** if a stronger mechanism (the gateway independently reading a
mounted `.brain/config.yml` per repo, so a caller cannot even accidentally under-declare privacy)
is wanted later, it needs a `runtime`-repo compose volume mount analogous to `AI_MANIFEST_DIR` —
raise that as its own demand when a second consumer exists to justify the mount, per the same
reasoning `AI_MANIFEST_DIR` itself was scoped this way.

## Metering — confirmed untouched

`PolicyResolutionService`/`PolicyController` call no `ProviderPort`, no `PreflightPort`, no
`UsageEmitterPort` — they only read `PolicyStore` and configuration and return a string. The
actual model invocation still goes through the existing `POST /ai/request` (or `POST /ai/jobs`)
flow, which already runs the unconditional Treasury pre-flight and Kafka usage-emit for every
call — `claude-code` included, still metered under `claude-credits` exactly as before. This
satisfies "no new unmetered path introduced" by construction (nothing in the new code path can
reach a provider), not merely by not having tested for it.

## Persistence — pattern and rationale

This repo owns no database (spec-ai-gateway.md §5: "deliberately close to stateless"); its one
existing persistence-shaped precedent (`ManifestRegistry`) is read-only. Since the store must
additionally be owner-writable, `PolicyStore` extends that same pattern honestly: a single JSON
file this repo owns and writes itself (`ai.policy.store-path`, env `AI_POLICY_STORE_PATH`, default
`./data/model-policy.json`), loaded into an in-memory map at startup (graceful degradation — a
missing/malformed file is never a startup failure, mirroring `ManifestRegistry#loadAll()`'s own
posture) and kept as the read-path source of truth; every write updates the map, then persists the
whole map via a temp-file-plus-atomic-move so a crash mid-write can't corrupt the file. Only
explicit overrides are ever stored — nothing is written for a repo/function on its default.

**Container-volume caveat, inherited, not fixed here:** exactly like `AI_MANIFEST_DIR`, this path
is ephemeral inside a container unless mounted as a volume. That `runtime`-repo compose change is
out of scope for this demand (never edit a sibling repo) and is flagged in DEPLOYMENT.md — the
same open item `AI_MANIFEST_DIR` has carried since gap G5, now shared by this store too. Until
mounted, owner-set overrides survive process restarts on a host-native run but not a container
recreate; every repo/function still safely falls back to its §9.0 default in that case (never a
startup failure, never a wrong-model silent substitution).

## Tests

`mvn test` — **187/187 green** (baseline 138 + 49 new):
- `ModelFunctionTest` (4), `ModelPolicyTest` (12), `PrivacyModeTest` (2) — parsing/round-trip,
  valid + invalid inputs for all three value types.
- `PolicyStoreTest` (8) — get/set, cross-instance reload (write with one `PolicyStore`, construct
  a fresh one against the same path, confirm it loads back), `listAll`/`listForRepo`, missing file
  / unconfigured path / malformed entry all degrade gracefully without failing other entries.
- `PolicyResolutionServiceTest` (12) — every function × auto/force combination; tier-3's
  never-downshifts-on-auto guarantee; `selfDefendingAuditRequired` flagged exactly when the
  resolved model isn't frontier (forced or privacy-driven); `privacy=local` overriding both a
  forced remote model and the auto frontier default; `privacy=rules-only` returning a null model
  even over a forced override; blank-repo rejection.
- `PolicyControllerTest` (11) — endpoint wiring, `ApiResponse` unwrapping, the `GET /ai/policy/{repo}`
  merge-with-defaults/`explicit`-flag behavior, all four new exception types surfacing correctly.

## Redeploy decision: not redeployed — rationale

Checked precedent across this repo's other `demands/fulfilled/` reports before deciding.
`dashboard-20260718-ai-gateway-console-cors` and `-job-submit-201-status` both rebuilt and
redeployed the live container — both were explicitly required to "verify against the live
container, not source alone" because a live browser caller (the dashboard console) was actively
blocked by the bug being fixed. `contracts-20260714-ai-gateway-repin-skip-shape` and
`plantpal-20260709-ai-gateway-full-coverage` did neither — no redeploy, no live-container
verification — because nothing was live-blocked on them.

This demand is the second kind: its own text states *"This is explicitly not a blocker for the
rest of the batch... the store is a prerequisite for forcing, not for running"* (Appendix A.8),
and its one intended consumer — `agent-runner`'s structurer, W15 — is explicitly **not yet
built**. There is no live caller today that this capability unblocks, so there is nothing to
verify against a running container yet, and no precedent in this repo's own history for
redeploying a fulfillment with no live consumer. Not redeployed this session; the next session
that builds the structurer (or the dashboard settings panel) should redeploy once it's ready to
call these endpoints for real.

### Addendum — 2026-07-20 (later same day): redeployed

The condition named above as the trigger has now been met: `dashboard` shipped the model-policy
settings panel (its commit `196c7cf`) and raised
`dashboard-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-console-cors`, finding that this repo's `/ai/policy/**`
had no CORS grant **and** that the live `runtime-ai-gateway-1` container didn't yet serve
`/ai/policy/**` at all (this section, above). Both were closed together in that CORS demand's own
fulfillment (`demands/fulfilled/dashboard-20260720-ai-gateway-model-policy-console-cors-report.md`)
— the live container was rebuilt and redeployed there, with full live-verification evidence
(including confirming `/ai/policy`, `/ai/policy/{repo}`, a real `PUT` round-trip, `/ai/policy/resolve`
with and without a privacy constraint, and no regression on `/ai/request`/`/ai/jobs`) recorded in
that report rather than duplicated here. This paragraph is appended, not a rewrite: the reasoning
above was correct *at the time this report was written* — redeploy was genuinely not warranted
until a real live consumer existed — and that consumer arrived the same day.

## Vault-sync

`none` — no owner ruling made this session, no `contracts` re-pin, no port/service/layout change.
R4 itself is already an owner-ratified ruling as of 2026-07-19 (per the demand's own "Why /
what's blocked" section) with its own vault-adoption path (Appendix A.7 item 1, a separate
`platform-vault` demand not raised by this session) — this session only builds the ai-gateway side
A.7 item 3 already commissions, it does not itself ring the vault's doorbell.
