# Fulfillment report — design-studio + design-studio-postgres registration (runtime)

## What shipped

Read `design-studio/demands/2026-07-19-runtime-compose-registration.md` in
full, including its 2026-07-20 addendum (owner ruling: containerize + KEEP
HISTORY). `design-studio`'s own container-readiness (Dockerfile,
Postgres-ready ledger, `SERVER_HOST`/`SERVER_PORT` env support, the
migration script) had already shipped in that repo at commit `4b0f62c`;
this session does the compose side plus the real cutover (build → bring up
dedicated Postgres → migrate the ledger → stop the host-native process →
bring up the container → verify), per the demand's own framing
("`runtime`'s own agent lands the compose side").

### `docker-compose.local.yml`

Two new services, closest structural analog `media-generation` (same
D038/D039/D040 posture — own dedicated Postgres, no shared instance, no GPU
section since design-studio is a plain FastAPI+SQLAlchemy service):

- **`design-studio-postgres`**: `postgres:16-alpine`, host port
  `127.0.0.1:5438:5432` (re-verified free against the live file before use —
  5433/5434/5435/5436 already taken by sibling dedicated-Postgres services,
  5437 is agent-runner's own standalone Postgres and not part of this
  file), named volume `design-studio-postgres-data`, `pg_isready`
  healthcheck matching the demand's own illustrative shape.
- **`design-studio`**: build context `../design-studio` (no
  `additional_contexts` needed — Python, `platform-contracts` resolves via
  a pip git-URL dependency inside the Dockerfile itself, same idiom
  `media-generation` uses). Port `127.0.0.1:8087:8087` (D040). Environment:
  `DATABASE_URL` to the new Postgres, `SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0`,
  `SERVER_PORT=8087`, `ARTIFACTS_ROOT=/data/artifacts`,
  `PLATFORM_ROOT=/platform`, `EMIT_STATE_EVENTS=true`, `STATE_FEED_URL`,
  `AGENT_RUNNER_URL` (see judgment calls below). `depends_on
  design-studio-postgres`.

**Addendum riders applied:**
1. Artifacts mount is `../design-studio/artifacts_store:/data/artifacts`
   (an **rw bind-mount** of the repo's own host directory), *not* a fresh
   named volume — so mission `8991305d`'s already-produced
   theme-proposition mocks stayed servable through the cutover instead of
   starting the container era with an empty store.
2. `..:/platform:ro` — same whole-tree read-only mount + rationale as
   `control-plane`'s `inventory.root` / `demand-coordinator`'s
   `board.root` above it in the same file (design-studio's own
   `HarvestService` needs to read a target's `HEXAGON.md`/spec/contracts
   schemas at `PLATFORM_ROOT`).

New named volume declared in the top-level `volumes:` block:
`design-studio-postgres-data`. No `design-studio-artifacts` named volume —
superseded by the bind-mount per the addendum, so nothing to declare there.

### `services.json`

```json
{
  "name": "design-studio",
  "composeFile": "docker-compose.local.yml",
  "healthUrl": "http://localhost:8087/health",
  "secretsFile": null,
  "port": 8087
}
```

## Judgment calls (the two the demand explicitly left open)

**`STATE_FEED_URL`**: `http://state-feed:8080` — the exact in-network
hostname:port every other compose service in this file already uses to
reach `state-feed` (`treasury`, `ai-gateway`, `connector-gmail`,
`orchestrator`, `sentinel-hub`, `publishing`, `media-generation`). No
ambiguity here; matched the fleet's own established pattern.

**`AGENT_RUNNER_URL`**: `http://host.docker.internal:8089`. Reasoning: (1)
this repo's own compose file confirmed by grep before writing — no existing
service calls `agent-runner` from inside a container, so there was no
in-file precedent to copy; (2) `agent-runner` runs host-native by design
(needs Windows filesystem write access into allow-listed repos + the host's
own `claude` CLI auth state, per `spec-agent-runner.md` §8 Q1), so this is
a container→**host** route, not container→container; (3)
`host.docker.internal` is Docker Desktop's standard host-gateway DNS name
and resolves bare (no `extra_hosts:` entry needed) on Docker Desktop for
Windows/Mac — the platform runs on Docker Desktop for Windows (this repo's
own `.env.example`/`DEPLOYMENT.md` M2/SOPS conventions, and no other
service in this file carries an `extra_hosts:` mapping, consistent with
never having needed one). An explicit
`extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` mapping is only
required on native Linux Docker Engine, which is not this host's
situation. Not a hard dependency for this cutover to succeed either way:
per spec §6's own failure posture, `InterviewService`/`PropositionService`
degrade to freezing a mission at `interview` rather than crashing if
`agent-runner` is unreachable — not exercised live this session (no new
mission was created), so this route is verified by container-network
reasoning, not yet by a live agent-runner round-trip.

## Cutover sequence — executed in full, in order

1. `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml build design-studio` —
   succeeded (`Image runtime-design-studio Built`), before touching
   anything live.
2. `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d design-studio-postgres`
   — container started; polled `docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}'`
   until `healthy` (first poll already returned `healthy`).
3. **Migration** (host venv, cwd `design-studio`):

# Fulfillment report — media-generation + media-generation-postgres registration (runtime)

## What shipped

`docker-compose.local.yml` gains two new services (commit `084f168`,
pushed) plus three lines in the `volumes:` top-level block; `services.json`
gains a matching entry. Landed now rather than bundled with W3's own
hunyuan3d-worker additions — the demand's own text says either timing
satisfies it.

### `media-generation-postgres`

Own dedicated Postgres per D038 (the same `<service>-postgres` pattern
already live for `control-plane`/`demand-coordinator`/`publishing`), host
port `127.0.0.1:5436:5432` (D039/D040 — the port this repo's own
`HEXAGON.md`/`DEPLOYMENT.md` had self-declared and that was still free,
re-verified against the live file before use), own named volume
`media-generation-postgres-data` (project-prefixed `runtime_...`, **not**
external — a fresh, dedicated volume distinct from the
`media-generation_media-generation-postgres-data` that `media-generation`'s
own dev/gate compose already created for its own separate use; D038's
whole point is that these must never be shared).

### `media-generation`

Build context `../media-generation` (no `additional_contexts` needed —
confirmed by reading this repo's own `Dockerfile`/`requirements.txt`: unlike
the 4 Java services, its `contracts` Python binding installs via a network
`pip install git+https://...@v0.14.0` inside the Dockerfile itself, not a
host-`.m2`-copy workaround). Port `127.0.0.1:8084:8084` (D040 loopback).
Environment: `DATABASE_URL` to the new Postgres, `SERVER_PORT=8084`,
`STATE_FEED_URL=http://state-feed:8080` (the in-network hostname:port every
other service already uses to reach it — the demand flagged this exact gap
since its own bare-process default doesn't resolve inside a container),
`EMIT_STATE_EVENTS="false"`, `MEDIA_INPUTS_DIR`/`ARTIFACTS_DIR` matching the
mount points. `HUNYUAN_WORKER_URL` deliberately left unset ("worker env off
for now") — see the GPU/worker note below.

**GPU device reservation included on `media-generation` itself**
(`deploy.resources.reservations.devices`, `driver: nvidia`,
`capabilities: ["gpu"]`) — required for `PynvmlAdapter`'s in-process NVML
reads (admission fail-closes on every job without it, per this repo's own
`docker-compose.dev.yml` comment and `HEXAGON.md`). This is a
metadata-read-only reservation, unrelated to the hunyuan3d worker's own
(not-yet-added) compute reservation — see next section for why the worker
itself stays out.

### Volumes — attached to what already exists, no duplicates

Verified live via `docker volume ls` before writing anything:
`media-models` and `media-inputs` already exist as plain (unprefixed)
names (media-generation's own `docker-compose.dev.yml` pins them that way
on purpose). Declared both `external: true` in this file — compose attaches
to the real volumes (the weights cache, already ~17.5 GiB downloaded; the
seeded gate-test demo image) instead of minting empty
`runtime_media-models`/`runtime_media-inputs` duplicates. Confirmed
post-`up`: no new prefixed duplicates were created (`docker volume ls`
re-checked after bringing the service up — only the pre-existing plain
names plus the new `runtime_media-generation-postgres-data`).

`media-models` is declared but **not mounted on any service in this file
yet** — nothing here reads it until the hunyuan3d worker joins in W3;
declaring it now just reserves the name.

**Judgment call flagged for owner attention — `media-artifacts`:** the only
artifacts volume that actually exists today is
`media-generation_media-artifacts` (prefixed by media-generation's own
dev-compose project name) — there is no bare `media-artifacts` volume.
media-generation's own `docker-compose.dev.yml` deliberately leaves this one
project-prefixed/disposable rather than pinning a bare name (its own header
comment: "nothing external seeds them"). Per this session's own commissioned
instructions, `media-artifacts` was still to be treated as external/shared
like the other two, so it points `name:` at the volume that actually exists
(`media-generation_media-artifacts`) rather than either failing at `up`
(looking for a nonexistent bare name) or minting a second, empty
`runtime_media-artifacts` duplicate. Practically low-risk — job artifacts
are namespaced by job UUID — but this does mean `runtime`'s stack and
`media-generation`'s own dev/gate stack now share one artifacts directory,
diverging from that dev-compose's documented "stay disposable" intent for
this specific volume. Worth the owner confirming this is the intended
shape rather than, e.g., giving `runtime` its own separate (non-external)
artifacts volume.

### `services.json`

```json
{
  "name": "media-generation",
  "composeFile": "docker-compose.local.yml",
  "healthUrl": "http://localhost:8084/health",
  "secretsFile": null,
  "port": 8084
}
```

## hunyuan3d worker — deliberately NOT included

Per this session's own instructions and re-confirmed directly against
`media-generation`'s own `PROGRESS.md` (2026-07-16 gate session): the
committed cold-GPU VRAM reservation default (`HUNYUAN_VRAM_RESERVATION_MB`
23000) cannot admit against the worker's real warm-resident footprint
(~15.4 GiB parked at boot, discovered live during that gate). Which
reservation semantics should ship — cold-footprint vs warm-marginal — is an
**open owner question, not yet ruled** (`media-generation`'s own
`Vault-sync: pending` line names it explicitly). Not runtime's call to make
unilaterally, so the worker service is out of this compose file entirely
for now. Consequence, stated plainly: `media-generation`'s own
`CapabilityRegistry` still unconditionally registers `image-to-3d`
(`HunyuanWorkerAdapter.from_env()` is unconditional in its `api.py`), so a
submitted job will admit (VRAM-fit is the only check, and the GPU is
otherwise idle in this stack) and then fail cleanly with a
worker-unreachable reason — the adapter's own documented degraded posture,
never a crash. `media-generation`'s queue has no registered *live*
capability in this platform stack until the ruling lands and W3 adds the
worker — which is the honest state, not a regression.

## Apply + verification (real, not just file-read)

```
docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d media-generation-postgres media-generation
```

- Both containers `Running`; `restart: unless-stopped` confirmed via
  `docker inspect` on both.
- `curl http://127.0.0.1:8084/health` → `200`, body
  `{"status":"UP","components":null}` (real `AppHealth` response, not a
  stub).
- GPU passthrough confirmed from inside the container:
  `docker exec runtime-media-generation-1 python -c "import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetCount())"`
  → `NVML OK, device count: 1`.
- `docker volume ls` re-checked post-`up`: `media-models`, `media-inputs`
  (plain names) and `media-generation_media-artifacts` unchanged/reused;
  only new volume created is `runtime_media-generation-postgres-data`. No
  `runtime_media-models`/`runtime_media-inputs`/`runtime_media-artifacts`
  duplicates exist.
- Coordinator/other services unaffected: `demand-coordinator`
  `/actuator/health` → `200`, `publishing` `/actuator/health` → `200`,
  full 18-container stack (16 original + these 2) `Up` at session end.

## Not done / out of scope

- hunyuan3d worker (W3) — see above, gated on the owner's
  GPU-reservation-semantics ruling.
- `EMIT_STATE_EVENTS` stays `false` — unchanged until `state-feed`'s own W7
  re-pin (v0.7.0 → v0.14.0) lands; not this session's call either.
- The `media-artifacts` external-name judgment call above is flagged, not
  silently decided — owner confirmation invited, not required before this
  report counts as shipped.

Two builds were run, in this order, from `runtime/`:

verification finished, so nothing from this session touched dashboard's git history). Rebuilt:

script needed zero changes, confirming the demand's own `/documentations` path prediction. `up -d
dashboard`, then real HTTP + a headless-browser (Playwright, installed to a scratch `/tmp` dir, not
this repo) round-trip against the live container at `127.0.0.1:4200`:

# Fulfillment report — treasury: D074 fleet-brain cost exposure

`status: done` here is a claim, not a verdict, per `DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4 — this report is
treasury's only output for this demand. This report covers **treasury's half only**;
`ai-gateway`'s half (fleet-level model-policy default) is a separate repo/session, not touched
here. Full analysis: `docs/BRAIN_FLEET_COST_EXPOSURE.md` (same content, more detail).

## NEEDS-OWNER — nothing here rules a ceiling

Per the demand's own instruction ("neither repo rules a ceiling, pin, or throttle on its own
authority where the ruling is the owner's"), this session proposes figures and flags them;
it does not apply any of them. **The `V7__dimension_threshold_seed.sql` placeholder
(5,000,000 tokens/day) was left unchanged** — not just as a matter of authority, but because
an already-applied Flyway migration's own value/checksum should not be hand-edited regardless
of who's asking; a ruled change belongs in a new migration or the existing admin CRUD.

## Finding 1 — which ceiling binds first during a nightly fleet sweep (code-verified fact)

**`claude-credits` binds first, and is the *only* ceiling that can ever bind on this
traffic — not merely "binds before" the global $ ceiling, but genuinely exclusive of it.**

Read directly from the enforcement code (`PreflightService`, `AggregationService`):

- `AggregationService.CLAUDE_CREDITS_PROVIDERS` = `{claude-code, claude-code-session}`, which
  is also a subset of `KNOWN_ZERO_COST_PROVIDERS` — every `usage.event` from these providers
  is recorded at `computedCost == 0.0` by design (D049: flat-rate Claude Code subscription,
  metered in tokens, not per-call dollars). `apply(event)` folds their tokens into the
  `claude-credits` `dimension_rollup` **and** feeds `$0` into `ConsumptionCounter`, the global
  $ ledger — one event, two counters, one of them structurally always zero for this traffic.
- `PreflightService.evaluate()` runs `checkDimensionGate(...)` **before** any of the four `$`
  `CapCheck`s (global daily/monthly, app daily/monthly) are even constructed; a dimension block
  returns immediately.
- Per `spec-agent-memory-system.md` line 541 ("Every frontier call ... goes through
  `ai-gateway`'s `claude-code` provider, metered under `claude-credits`"), **100% of the fleet
  `.brain` sweep's frontier traffic** (tier-3 classification + the D072-forced
  `contradiction-screen`) is `claude-code`-routed.

**Consequence:** the owner's existing $5/day / $50/month global ceiling provides **zero**
protection against fleet-brain frontier spend under the current design — its `consumed` side
is always `$0` for this traffic regardless of token volume. `claude-credits` is not a
sub-budget nested inside the $ ceiling; it is an independent limit that happens to be the sole
guard on an entire cost class the $ ceiling cannot see at all.

## Finding 2 — projected cost, one full nightly sweep (estimate, assumptions stated)

No hard per-session token figures exist anywhere in the vault or this repo — this is a stated
-assumption estimate, not a measurement (refusing to estimate was explicitly ruled out by the
demand).

**Assumptions:** worst-case first-sweep (all 23 repos qualify same night, per FP-5's ≥3-session
trigger and the demand's own "before the first large sweep" framing) · 4 new sessions/repo ·
2.5 tier-3 calls/session (500 in/150 out tokens each) · 8 contradiction-screen calls/session
(800 in/200 out tokens each, D072's forced `claude-opus-4-8`).

**Per repo:** 30,600 in + 7,900 out = 38,500 tokens.
**Fleet (23 repos):** 703,800 in + 181,700 out = **885,500 tokens, one night.**

**$-equivalent at claude-opus-4-8 rates ($5/MTok in, $25/MTok out):**
input $3.52 + output $4.54 = **≈ $8.06 economic-equivalent** — not what the $ ledger shows
(that's $0 per Finding 1), but the real economic magnitude the current design hides from it.
**This already exceeds the owner's own $5.00/day figure** — the concrete shape of D074's "real
exposure, not hypothetical."

Against the current 5,000,000-token placeholder: 885,500 tokens is only **~17.7%** of it on
this worst-case night — the placeholder has enough slack that it would not itself have caught
or slowed a full 23-repo sweep.

## Finding 3 — proposed real `claude-credits` figure (needs-owner, not applied)

Two candidates, full derivation in `docs/BRAIN_FLEET_COST_EXPOSURE.md` §3:

- **A, mechanically tied to the already-ruled $5/day figure:** using this session's own
  projected sweep mix (79.5% in / 20.5% out) as the blend weight against claude-opus-4-8 rates
  → blended $9.10/MTok → **≈ 549,000 tokens/day**. Ties back to a ruled number, but still folds
  in this session's own mix assumption — not purely mechanical, flagged accordingly.
- **B, headroom over this session's own projected sweep:** 2× the 885,500-token worst-case
  estimate → **≈ 1,770,000 tokens/day**.

Recommendation offered (not ruled): A as the primary figure since it's legibly anchored to a
number the owner already set; B as the safer operational floor if headroom matters more than
anchoring right now. **The owner rules; this session did not apply either.**

## Finding 4 — observability shipped (no ruling needed)

New read-only endpoint: `GET /treasury/admin/dimension-thresholds/{appId}/{dimensionKey}/usage`
— live `current`/`limit`/`ratio` read off `DimensionCounter` (already updated in real time by
the existing `AggregationService` path) against `DimensionThresholdRegistry`. Directly answers
"make projected nightly spend observable before it's spent" with the cheapest available
mechanism — no new architecture, no forecasting engine, just a live view of accrual as it
happens. `limit`/`ratio` report `null` (not `0`/`Infinity`) when no threshold is configured.

Example once live: `GET /treasury/admin/dimension-thresholds/__platform__/claude-credits/usage`
→ `{"data":{"appId":"__platform__","dimensionKey":"claude-credits","bucket":"<today's
UTC date>","current":<live count>,"limit":5000000,"ratio":<current/limit>}}`.

## Files changed

- `src/main/java/io/platform/treasury/dimension/DimensionUsage.java` — new record.
- `src/main/java/io/platform/treasury/dimension/DimensionThresholdService.java` — new `usage()`
  method; constructor gains `DimensionCounter`, `DimensionPeriodProperties`, `Clock` (all
  existing beans, constructor injection only).
- `src/main/java/io/platform/treasury/dimension/DimensionThresholdController.java` — new
  `GET .../usage` mapping, `ApiResponse<DimensionUsage>`.
- `src/test/java/io/platform/treasury/dimension/DimensionThresholdServiceTest.java` — updated
  `@Import` for the new constructor deps; 2 new tests
  (`usageReportsCurrentConsumptionAgainstTheSeededCeiling`,
  `usageReportsNullLimitAndRatioWhenNoThresholdIsConfigured`).
- `docs/BRAIN_FLEET_COST_EXPOSURE.md` — new, full analysis + proposal (this report's source).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry under `[Unreleased]`.
- **Not changed:** `src/main/resources/db/migration/V7__dimension_threshold_seed.sql` —
  deliberately untouched (see NEEDS-OWNER section above).

## Tests

`mvn -B test`: **55 run, 0 failures, 10 errors.** The 10 errors are the pre-existing,
previously-documented Docker-Desktop/testcontainers-bom 1.20.1 incompatibility on this box
(`IllegalStateException: Could not find a valid Docker environment` / "Previous attempts...
failed") — environment, not code; identical count and identical failing classes to this
repo's last documented baseline (`PROGRESS.md`, prior session). The new
`DimensionThresholdServiceTest` cases are Testcontainers-backed (same class as the pre-existing
ones) and hit the same environment wall — not a new regression, same standing limitation.
Non-Testcontainers slices (`DimensionPeriodPropertiesTest`, `DimensionServiceTest`,
`PreflightServiceTest`, `DimensionGatePropertiesTest`) all pass green, including the ones
exercising the exact code paths this session touched (`PreflightServiceTest`'s dimension-gate
tests confirm Finding 1's "dimension check runs first" behavior unchanged).

## Not in scope / not touched

- `ai-gateway`'s half of this demand (fleet-level model-policy default, `contradiction-screen`
  D072 pin statement) — separate repo/session.
- FP-4/FP-5/FP-6 executioner behavior (staging adoption, etc.) — explicitly named as
  `brain-toolkit`'s question by the demand itself, not this session's to touch.
- No container rebuild/redeploy performed, per this task's explicit instruction.
- No `platform-vault` files read for anything beyond the demand file itself and the linked
  spec/decisions text (read-only, to source Finding 1/2's factual basis); nothing in
  `platform-vault` was written.

# Fulfillment — accept an `app.mission` state-event

## What shipped

Investigation, and one raised demand — **not** the ingest capability. Read the caveats
section before treating this as delivered: the demand's own sequencing precondition is
only half met.

- `demands/2026-08-04-contracts-state-event-app-mission-member.md`
  (id `state-feed-20260804-state-event-app-mission-member`), raised to `contracts`.

Current state of this repo, verified this session:

- `EventIngestService` handles ten `state.event` types (`component.health`, `load`,
  `cost.tick`, `ci.run`, `app.status`, `activity.count`, `job.progress`, `agent.run`,
  `design.mission`, `design.designSystem`). `app.mission` is not among them, and no
  prior session shipped it.
- `contracts` is pinned at `0.17.0` in `pom.xml`.

## What the origin must know

**The precondition landed on the wrong side of the wall.** `contracts` v0.19.0
(`92ca10e`, "feat(app-studio): add app.mission and app.task-plan schemas") added
`schemas/app-studio/app.mission.json` — the app-studio **mission ledger record**. It did
not add an `app.mission` member to the `state.event` oneOf union: neither
`schemas/state-feed/state.event.json` (no `"type": { "const": "app.mission" }`) nor
`schemas/state-feed/state-event-java.yaml` (no `AppMissionEvent` / `AppMissionPayload`)
mentions it. Those are two different artifacts — the ledger record is app-studio's API
shape, the event variant is the observable projection state-feed ingests — and only the
first exists.

state-feed's ingest is strictly typed against generated
`io.platform.contracts.events.*Event` classes, with one `StateService.accept` overload
per variant. There is no generic/untyped path, and adding one would break the standing
rule that all cross-repo interfaces come from `contracts`. Hand-rolling the type here,
or reaching into `contracts` to add it from this session, are both forbidden — hence a
demand rather than a commit.

The raised demand asks for `AppMissionPayload` carrying exactly the four fields this
demand's acceptance criteria name — `missionId`, `appName`, `stage`, `currentWave` —
plus an optional `lastGate` (`gate` / `outcome` / `wave` / `decidedAt`) for the latest
gate outcome, reusing `app.mission.json`'s `missionStage`, `missionGateStage` and
`approved`/`rejected` vocabularies rather than restating them.

**Once contracts releases it,** state-feed re-pins, adds the ingest case and a
`StateService.accept(AppMissionEvent)` keyed `("app.mission", missionId)` — one live
snapshot row per mission, so a console watching the feed sees each mission's current
stage/wave/gate and replaces it in place as the mission moves. That is a small,
well-precedented change; `design.mission` is the same shape end to end.

**Acceptance criterion 3 is already structurally satisfied and needs nothing from
app-studio.** state-feed is a read-only sink that never writes back to any hexagon and
is explicitly not load-bearing (D011, and this repo's standing invariant). Ingest is
`POST` → validate → snapshot → SSE fan-out, with no acknowledgement any producer waits
on. An app-studio mission held open cannot depend on state-feed being up, now or after
the ingest case lands. app-studio should still make its own emission call fire-and-forget
on its side (async, failures swallowed and logged) — that half of the contract lives in
app-studio, not here.

## Not done / caveats

- **The capability itself is not shipped.** state-feed does not yet accept an
  `app.mission` state-event; posting one returns the `unknown state.event type` error
  from `EventIngestService`'s default branch. No code changed in `src/`.
- Blocked on `contracts` demand `state-feed-20260804-state-event-app-mission-member`.
  This demand should be re-dispatched to state-feed, or reopened, once that lands — the
  remaining work is roughly one ingest case, one `accept` overload, a `pom.xml` re-pin
  and two test additions.
- The payload shape in the contracts demand is state-feed's proposal, inferred from this
  demand's acceptance criteria and the existing `design.mission` variant. If app-studio
  wants additional fields on the wire (`class`, `targetRepo`, `stageKind`,
  `designMissionId`), say so on the contracts demand before it is worked — adding them
  later is another version bump.

# Fulfillment — emit `origin` on StateEvents through `GET /feed`

## Root cause

`origin` was never dropped at ingest — `EventIngestService` correctly deserializes
each contracts event POJO (`ComponentHealthEvent`, `LoadEvent`, `CostTickEvent`,
`CiRunEvent`, `AppStatusEvent`, `ActivityCountEvent`), and every one of those six
POJOs (contracts v0.7.0, pinned in `pom.xml`) carries `getOrigin()` returning the
`io.platform.contracts.events.Origin` enum (`HOST`/`HUB`).

The drop happened one hop later, in `StateService`. The internal representation
`io.platform.statefeed.state.StateEvent` — the record the snapshot store, the
ring buffer, and the `/feed` SSE broadcaster all operate on and serialize
directly — was declared as `record StateEvent(String type, OffsetDateTime
timestamp, Object payload)`. It had no `origin` component at all. `StateService.apply(...)`
constructed this record from only `type`, `timestamp`, and `payload`, discarding
`event.getOrigin()` on every one of the six `accept(...)` overloads. Since
`SseFeedBroadcaster` serializes the `StateEvent` record as-is
(`emitter.send(...).data(event))`), whatever fields weren't on the record could
never reach `GET /feed`, regardless of what ingest had correctly parsed.

An existing test (`IngestControllerTest.acceptsAComponentHealthEventWithHubOrigin`
/ `FeedControllerTest.activityCountEventRoundTripsFromIngestToSseWithHubOrigin`)
posted an event with `"origin": "hub"` but never actually asserted that `origin`
(or `hub`) appeared in the delta payload — it only checked the unrelated fields
still round-tripped, so the drop shipped silently.

## What changed

- `src/main/java/io/platform/statefeed/state/StateEvent.java` — added an
  `Origin origin` component to the record (nullable — origin is optional on
  ingest per contracts). This is the internal representation used everywhere
  downstream of ingest (snapshot store, ring buffer, SSE broadcaster), so adding
  it here is the single change that makes it available at every consumer,
  including `/feed`.
- `src/main/java/io/platform/statefeed/state/StateService.java` — every
  `accept(...)` overload now passes `event.getOrigin()` through to `apply(...)`,
  which threads it into the `StateEvent` it stores/broadcasts.
- Two existing tests that constructed `StateEvent` directly with the old
  3-arg shape (`SseFeedBroadcasterOrderingTest`, `SseFeedBroadcasterOverflowTest`)
  were updated to the new 4-arg shape (passing `null` for origin — those tests
  aren't about origin and don't need a real value).
- `src/test/java/io/platform/statefeed/feed/FeedControllerTest.java` — the two
  existing origin-adjacent tests were strengthened to actually assert on the
  wire payload (`"origin":"hub"` / absence of `"hub"`/`"host"` when unset), and
  two new tests were added:
  `componentHealthEventRoundTripsFromIngestToSseWithHostOrigin` (delta path) and
  `subscriberConnectingMidStreamGetsOriginOnTheSnapshot` (snapshot path — a
  subscriber connecting after the event was ingested must also see `origin` on
  the snapshot, not just on live deltas).

No changes were needed in `EventIngestService.java`, `SnapshotKey.java`,
`InMemorySnapshotStore.java`, `RecentEventsBuffer.java`, `FeedController.java`,
or `SseFeedBroadcaster.java` — none of them touch or need to touch `origin`
directly; they all operate generically on `StateEvent`, so fixing the record
was sufficient. `SnapshotKey` was a red herring: it's a dedup/grouping key
(`type` + entity id) and correctly has nothing to do with `origin` — a later
event from a different origin is *supposed* to replace the snapshot slot for
the same entity (that's the "current state" semantics), it's just that neither
the old nor the new snapshot value used to carry origin at all.

## Test results

`mvn test` — **32 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (was 30 before this change; two
new tests added). `FeedControllerTest` alone: 7 tests (was 5), all green,
including the two new origin round-trip tests.

## For theme-kasbah's next session

`GET /feed` now emits `"origin":"hub"` or `"origin":"host"` on every event
(both the initial snapshot and live deltas) for producers that set it, and
omits/`null`s it for producers that don't (origin remains optional on ingest —
this is not a breaking change for existing emitters). No contracts version bump
was needed; the field was already in the pinned v0.7.0 schema, it just wasn't
being threaded through internally. Any code path that special-cased "no origin
field visible in the feed" should be revisited — it can now read `origin`
directly off each event.

# Fulfillment — board allowlist drift is now loud, not silent

## Scope note — criterion 1 was already done

Acceptance criterion 1 (`brain-toolkit` added to `demand-coordinator.board.repos`,
`GET /board` classifying `brain-toolkit-20260723-platform-vault-gitattributes-lf`
into `demands`) was already shipped and pushed by the prior session before this
one started — commits `a576b85` (feat), `b816b93` (test), `0e21e25` (changelog).
This session started from that HEAD and built criteria 2-5 only. Verified live
(before this session's own changes) that `GET /board` already surfaced both the
brain-toolkit demand and its fulfillment report correctly.

## What shipped (criteria 2-5)

**Criterion 2 — drift surfaced, not ignored, both ways the demand asked for:**
- `BoardService.detectUnlistedRepoDrift()` (and a no-arg overload against the
  configured root): scans the board root's immediate subdirectories; a
  directory counts as drift only if it (a) carries a `.git` marker (file or
  directory) and (b) has at least one live, non-README file directly inside
  its `demands/` folder (the same file set `markdownFiles()` already hands the
  real classifier) that isn't in `board.repos`.
- `BoardDriftStartupWarner` (`ApplicationRunner`, runs once after boot): logs
  one `WARN` per drifted repo, naming it and its live-file count.
- `BoardResponse.unlistedRepoDrift` — new field, `List<UnlistedRepoDrift>`,
  `UnlistedRepoDrift(String repo, int demandFileCount)`. Appended as the 5th
  field; a 4-arg `BoardResponse` constructor overload defaulting it to `List.of()`
  was kept so every existing call site (production and test) compiles
  unchanged — purely additive, no existing consumer's shape or values change.

Example `GET /board` fragment (empty today against the real fleet — see
comparison below):
```json
"unlistedRepoDrift": [
  { "repo": "some-new-repo", "demandFileCount": 1 }
]
```

**Criterion 3 — a test that fails against today's (pre-fix) code:**
`BoardServiceTest.unlistedRepoWithALiveDemandIsSurfacedAsDriftInsteadOfSilentlyDropped`
writes an unlisted repo with a `.git` marker and one live demand file, asserts
it's absent from both `demands` and `errors` (the bug itself, still true
post-fix — that's not what changed) AND present in `unlistedRepoDrift`.
Verified this genuinely catches the bug: temporarily reverted
`detectUnlistedRepoDrift(Path)` to `return List.of();` (the pre-fix
behavior — the method existing but never populated), reran
`mvn -Dtest=BoardServiceTest test`, got `Expected size: 1 but was: 0` at the
new test's assertion. Restored the real implementation, reran, all 7

# Fulfillment — surface "satisfied but unarchived" demand state

## What shipped

`GET /loop-open` — every demand approved at this hexagon's gate whose origin
repo hasn't done its own archival bookkeeping yet. One request, no
client-side joining of `/board` against `/satisfied/{repo}`.

**Endpoint:** `GET http://<host>:8082/loop-open` (no path/query params — the
whole approved-but-unarchived set, not scoped per repo; the console already
gets `originRepo` per row to group/filter client-side if it wants to).

**Response shape** (`ApiResponse<List<LoopOpenItem>>`, same envelope every
other endpoint on this service uses):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "demandId": "plantpal-20260709-ai-gateway-full-ai-coverage",
      "originRepo": "plantpal",
      "approvedAt": "2026-07-20T10:15:30.123456Z",
      "file": "2026-07-09-ai-gateway-full-ai-coverage.md"
    }
  ]
}
```

Field-by-field:
- `demandId` — the demand's own stable id, verbatim.
- `originRepo` — the repo that must do the archiving: `envelope.repo`, the
  disk-derived folder this demand's file was actually found in (same field
  `/board`'s own `envelope.repo` already returns) — not necessarily the
  fulfilling worker, and used in preference to the YAML-content `from:`
  field precisely because it's the one guaranteed to match a real,
  dispatchable folder on disk.
- `approvedAt` — `Approval.approvedAt`, the same timestamp value
  `/satisfied/{repo}`'s `AssembledSummary.approvedAt` already returns for
  this demandId.
- `file` — the origin demand file's path relative to that repo's `demands/`
  folder (same value `/board`'s `envelope.file` already returns) — e.g. the
  origin session's next step is
  `git mv demands/<file> demands/archive/<file>` plus flipping its
  frontmatter `status: archived`.

An empty demand today is `{"data": []}` — no `error` key, matching every
other empty-list endpoint on this service (`/pending-approval` when nothing
is claimed, `/satisfied/{repo}` when nothing's approved for that repo).

**Derivation (no new persisted state):** `ApprovalService.loopOpen()` reads
the same `ApprovalRepository` this hexagon already keeps (the one genuinely
stateful piece of this service — an approval has no file anywhere to
re-derive it from) and joins it against the live board `BoardService`
already recomputes from disk on every call. An entry appears only while
**both** of these hold:
1. the demandId has an `ApprovalEntity` row (owner called
   `POST /demands/{id}/approve` and it succeeded — for a multi-hexagon
   demand this already implies every target reported, same join semantics
   `pendingApproval()`/`satisfiedFor()` use, not a second notion), **and**
2. the demand's envelope is still resolvable on the live board (`BoardService`
   only walks `demands/` and `demands/fulfilled/`, never `demands/archive/`
   — a file the origin moved simply stops being parsed into an envelope at
   all, exactly the mechanism `satisfiedFor()` already relies on to know a
   demand closed) **and** that envelope's own `status` field hasn't already
   been flipped to `archived` in place (covers the origin editing the field
   before it gets around to moving the file).

Either half of "the origin did its bookkeeping" — the move, or the status
edit — removes the entry on the very next read. Nothing here is written by
this endpoint or kept in sync by hand; per D012 this hexagon still never
writes into any repo, and never auto-archives anything.

## What the origin (dashboard) must know

The console's Close-loop button can now be built directly against
`GET /loop-open`: one row per entry, `originRepo` names which repo session
to dispatch into, `demandId` + `file` are what that session's brief needs to
name the file it must edit/move. No new coordinator write path exists or was
added — the dispatched session does the actual archive commit itself, same
as every other origin-side demand-file edit today.

CORS: `/loop-open` (GET) was added to the same allow-list
`/board`/`/pending-approval`/`/satisfied/**` already use
(`demand-coordinator.cors.allowed-origins`, default
`http://localhost:4200`) — this is a browser-facing console read.

## Tests

- `ApprovalServiceTest` +4: an approved+unarchived demand appears with the
  right `originRepo`/`approvedAt`/`file`; an unapproved demand (even with a
  reported fulfillment) never appears; the same demand disappears once its
  origin file has moved to `demands/archive/` (mocked board drops the
  envelope entirely, same as a real move would); the same demand disappears
  once its envelope's `status` flips to `archived` in place, file not yet
  moved.
- `ApprovalControllerTest` +2: `/loop-open` routes to
  `ApprovalService.loopOpen()` and returns its shape; empty-list shape when
  nothing's owed.
- `CorsConfigTest` +2: allowed origin gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` on
  `/loop-open`; disallowed origin doesn't.
- `BoardControllerTest`: one pre-existing time-coupled real-fleet fixture
  refreshed (`getBoardAutoRoutesASingleTargetDemand`) — unrelated to this
  change, fleet drift since 2026-07-19 (the prior fixture,
  `design-studio-20260719-control-plane-registration`, was itself
  approved+archived in the time since). Re-pointed at this very session's
  own demand (`dashboard-20260720-demand-coordinator-loop-close-state`,
  currently the one real open demand on the board) — same maintenance
  convention this suite's own javadoc documents ("expect to swap these out
  again as the real fleet keeps moving").
- Full suite: `mvn -o test` — **81/81 passed, 0 failures, 0 errors**,
  `BUILD SUCCESS`.

## Live verification

Rebuilt and redeployed via `runtime`'s own compose — only this service
touched; every other container's `Status`/uptime was unchanged before and
after:

```
docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml build demand-coordinator
docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d demand-coordinator
```

Result: `runtime-demand-coordinator-1` recreated and started clean
(`Started DemandCoordinatorApplication in 3.504 seconds`, no errors in the
boot log, Flyway "up to date", Hikari pool started). All 19 other
`runtime-*` containers stayed at their pre-existing `Up 2-3 hours`/`healthy`
status — none were recreated.

Live probes against the rebuilt, running instance (loopback `:8082`):

```
GET /loop-open         -> 200 {"data":[]}
GET /board             -> 200, 0 parse errors
GET /pending-approval   -> 200 {"data":[]}
```

The empty `/loop-open` result is the **correct positive-confirmed** live
answer today, not an untested default: as of 2026-07-20 every demand
fleet-wide that was ever approved has also already been archived at its
origin (confirmed via `/board`'s live parse — no `status: open`/`satisfied`
envelope anywhere carries an `ApprovalEntity` row), so there is nothing real
left in the "approved but unarchived" set to show. The positive case (an
entry actually appearing, and actually disappearing once archived) is
proven by `ApprovalServiceTest`'s fixture-based unit tests instead — per the
task's own instruction, no repo's demand files were edited to manufacture a
live positive case.

## What we did NOT do

- Did not write into any other repo's `demands/` folder, and did not
  auto-archive anything anywhere — `loopOpen()` is read-only, exactly like
  every other endpoint this hexagon serves (D012's post-office rule,
  unchanged).
- Did not call `POST /demands/{id}/approve` for this demand or any other,
  and did not mark this fulfillment `/satisfied` myself — `done` is a
  claim, not a verdict; the owner validates.
- Did not touch `../dashboard` (the origin repo) in any way — its own
  follow-up (the console's Close-loop button, driven by this listing) is a
  separate session, explicitly out of scope here per the demand's own "What
  we do once closed."

# Fulfillment — register `design-studio` on the coordinator board

## What shipped

`src/main/resources/application.yml`'s `demand-coordinator.board.repos` now

## Tests

# Fulfillment — register `documentations` on the coordinator board

This is the `demand-coordinator` leg only of a five-target demand
(`to: [demand-coordinator, platform-vault, agent-runner, control-plane,
conventions]`). The other four legs are out of scope for this report.

## What shipped

`src/main/resources/application.yml`'s `demand-coordinator.board.repos` now
includes `documentations`, appended after `brain-toolkit` at the end of the
list (matching the existing append-at-the-end convention; no reordering of
the other 27 entries). Commit `0f86e04` (`fix(board): add documentations to
board.repos allowlist`).

## Live verification (container rebuilt and redeployed, not just inspection)

The change is baked into the jar, so inspection alone doesn't prove it. Used
the launcher board at `:5055` → Platform Stack → demand-coordinator →
"Rebuild + restart" (full Maven build inside the container, then a clean
container recreate — confirmed via `docker ps` showing a fresh "Up N
seconds" instance immediately after).

`GET http://localhost:8082/board` immediately after redeploy:

- `documentations`' demand file
  (`2026-07-24-fleet-register-documentations-hexagon.md`, this demand
  itself) now appears under `demands`, correctly parsed with its full
  five-target `to` list.
- `unlistedRepoDrift` — empty (`[]`). Before this change it was
  `[{"repo":"documentations","demandFileCount":1}]`.
- `errors` — empty (`[]`), both before and after.

All three of this leg's acceptance criteria hold against the live,
post-redeploy response, not a build log.

## What the origin must know

None of `documentations`' own demand-authoring behavior needs to change —
its file was already well-formed; it was purely invisible to this service
until the allowlist entry existed.

## Worth noting (raised as a proposal, not built — out of scope for this demand)

The reason this hid for a day: `GET /inbox/documentations` worked the whole
time (the demand dispatched *to* `documentations` lives in `platform-vault`'s
already-allowlisted `demands/`), while `documentations`' own *outbound* raise
silently landed in `unlistedRepoDrift` instead of erroring or paging anyone.
Inbound routing degrades gracefully for an unlisted repo; outbound does not
surface as a blocker to the repo that needs to know. A session doing only
the prescribed session-start inbox check has no way to discover it is unable
to raise.

Proposal for an owner ruling (not implemented here): have `/board` (or a new
lightweight endpoint) flag `unlistedRepoDrift` entries back at the drifting
repo somehow — e.g. a well-known sentinel file or response any repo's own

  `mvn test`, a pre-existing staleness this test class's own javadoc already
  documents as expected ("time-coupled... not a maintenance burden to design
  away"), not something introduced by this change. Swapped in demands
  genuinely open today; one of the two replacements
  (`media-generation-20260716-control-plane-registration`) is itself one of
  the five demands this same board.repos change made visible for the first
  time.

  session, so the Testcontainers-Postgres tests ran for real rather than
  degrading): `mvn -B test` (JDK 21 / Maven 3.9.9 via
  `C:\Users\pc\tools\env.sh`) — **72/72 tests passed, 0 failures, 0 errors**,
  `BUILD SUCCESS`. Includes `ApprovalServiceTest`/`ApprovalControllerTest`
  and `BoardControllerTest`, all real-Postgres-backed, all green.

The live `:8082` instance was stopped when this session started
(`runtime-demand-coordinator-1` / `-postgres-1` both `Exited`). Rebuilt and
brought back up via `runtime`'s own compose:

```
docker compose -f C:\Users\pc\Desktop\platform\runtime\docker-compose.local.yml build demand-coordinator
docker compose -f C:\Users\pc\Desktop\platform\runtime\docker-compose.local.yml up -d demand-coordinator
```

and `control-plane`/`control-plane-postgres` (its own `depends_on` chain, also
stopped) started alongside it, `demand-coordinator` container recreated and
started clean (`Started DemandCoordinatorApplication in 3.596 seconds`, no
errors in the boot log).

Live probes against the rebuilt, running instance:

```
GET http://localhost:8082/inbox/media-generation      -> 200 {"data":[]}
```

None of these were reachable via `/board` before this session's redeploy.

# Fulfillment — register `platform-vault` and `launcher` on the coordinator board

`src/main/resources/application.yml`'s `demand-coordinator.board.repos` now
includes `platform-vault` and `launcher`, appended after `demand-coordinator`

  (`src/main/java/io/platform/demandcoordinator/board/BoardService.java`)
  checks `Files.isDirectory(dir)` first and returns `List.of()` if the
  `demands/` folder (or the repo folder itself) doesn't exist — no

The redeploy/restart of the live `:8082` instance (so the running board

   runtime/docker-compose.local.yml build demand-coordinator` then `up -d

   up to date. No migration necessary", confirming the approval table's 18

   unclean shutdown mid-session; recovered cleanly via normal WAL redo, row

this demand's own acceptance criteria, flagging for visibility since it
surfaced from the same work.

real fleet (its two prior real-demand fixtures had since been
fulfilled/approved/archived; swapped for two currently-open real demands, and

bare count). Live redeploy verified as described above — real container, real

`contracts` v0.11.0 `Demand.Status` enum (`open`/`satisfied`/`archived`; the
fleet convention is `status: open`) — so all three parse as `Error`, not
`Parsed`. This is real, correct D023 behavior (surface malformed input,
never silently drop) surfacing a genuine issue in app-studio's own files; it
is not a demand-coordinator bug and, per the platform's cross-repo rule, not
this repo's to fix — noted here for app-studio's own next session, not acted
on. It has no bearing on this demand's acceptance criteria, none of which
require the fleet to be error-free.

- Extended `BoardPropertiesConfigTest` with

    pre-existing time-coupled drift unrelated to app-studio. Fixed in the
    same pass since they blocked `mvn test` going green: re-pointed the
    single-target fixture at `platform-vault-20260804-app-studio-board-registration`

    `demandId` to membership (`hasItem`) plus an `everyItem` worker check,

# Fulfillment — amend spec-agent-memory-system.md Appendix A.3 for explicit session_id pairing

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4) — never self-approved, the
coordinator's owner gate still applies. The owner had already ruled **yes** on the underlying
question (2026-07-20, relayed by the accompanying-architect session); this report is the vault's
record of the editorial mechanics the demand deliberately left open, not a re-litigation of the
ruling itself.

## What was done

**Appendix A.3 amended.** The `PROGRESS.md` handoff block now names the `session_id` of the session
that generated it, via a new fifth line:

```
- State: <what shipped / what's true now>
- Next step: <next concrete action>
- Standing: <any standing reminder for the next session>
- Vault-sync: none | demand raised <id> | pending — <items>
- Session: <session_id of the file this block projects from>
```

The three editorial questions the demand left open are settled, explicitly, in both the spec and
the decision entry:

1. **Placement — a new fifth line, not an annotation on `Vault-sync:`.** Stated plainly that the
   block grows from four lines to five, since `conventions`' `vault-sync-handoff` check asserts
   today's exact four-line shape and this is itself a format change, not something to leave for
   that check to discover on its own. An annotation on `Vault-sync:` was considered and rejected —
   that line already carries a three-way mini-grammar using `—` as a separator, and overloading it
   with a second, differently-shaped value reintroduces the same parsing ambiguity this amendment
   exists to remove.
2. **Rollout — v0.6-shaped sessions going forward only; the existing corpus is strongly
   grandfathered, never rewritten.** The ~27-session corpus across both `.brain` pilots
   (`agent-runner`, `media-generation`) as of 2026-07-20 is Phase-1 seed material per the spec's own
   Appendix A.2 and stays that way. A cross-reference line was added to A.2 itself so the rule is
   visible from both directions.
3. **D-number — new (D063), not folded into D061.** D061 closed a specific, dated batch (v0.6
   adoption + R1–R6, ratified 2026-07-19, landed 2026-07-20). This is a separate, later owner
   ruling — discovered and made only after `conventions` hit the file-ordering defect live in
   `agent-runner` sessions 13/14, *after* D061 had already landed. D062 (design doctrine v0.4,
   minted fresh rather than folded into D053 the same day) is the vault's own precedent for treating
   a later, independently-timed ruling as its own D-number rather than blurring it into an
   already-closed entry. D061's own entry carries a dated addendum pointing at D063.

**Downstream work named, not executed.** Per the demand's own explicit scoping ("`agent-runner`
does neither of these as part of this demand"), this session did not raise a demand to
`conventions` and did not touch any pilot repo's `brain` CLI. Both pieces of downstream work are
named directly in the governed spec text so implementers build against it:

- A.6 gains two bullets: `brain-projection-equality` re-points from file-ordering inference
  (mtime-with-filename-tiebreaker, `conventions` commit `8d56cfe`) to a direct comparison of the
  handoff block's `Session:` line against the named session file's `session_id`; `vault-sync-handoff`
  relaxes its shape assertion to five lines.
- A.7 gains two checklist items (7, 8): the `conventions` demand, and the `brain` CLI `session close`
  generator update in both pilots (`agent-runner` as reference implementation, `media-generation`
  copying verbatim, per the existing Phase 0 pattern).

**A new Appendix D ("Amendments record")** was added, distinct from Appendix C (a one-time landing
note for the original v0.6 *adoption* event). Appendix D is a running, dated log for post-adoption
amendments — this is its first entry, D.1 (D063).

**PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md.** D063 minted with the full Status/Decision/Why/Consequences record,
including the reasoning for all three editorial calls above. D061's Consequences amended in place
via a dated addendum (2026-07-20) pointing at D063, mirroring the D062→D053 addendum pattern from
earlier the same day. The file's running tail summary sentence updated to include D063.

**PLATFORM_STATE.md.** The §1 governed-docs footnote (the only place STATE tracks this spec's
version) updated to record the A.3/D063 amendment alongside the existing D052→D061 supersession
note.

## Acceptance criteria, checked

1. Appendix A.3 amended to require the handoff projection to carry `session_id`, in a concrete
   shape (a new fifth line) — **done**.
2. The amendment explicitly states the block shape changes from four lines to five — **done**,
   stated in A.3's own text, in D063's Decision, and in Appendix D — not left for `conventions` to
   infer.
3. Rollout scope stated explicitly: v0.6-shaped sessions going forward only, existing ~27-session
   corpus across both pilots grandfathered and never rewritten — **done**, in A.3, cross-referenced
   in A.2, and in D063.
4. Whether this lands as a new D-number or amends D061 in place is recorded — **done**: new
   D-number, **D063**, with the reasoning stated in both the spec (Appendix D) and the decision
   entry.
5. The amendment names, or points at, the two pieces of downstream work it unblocks — **done**: A.6

   Consequences.

# Fulfillment — agent-runner's concurrency cap: default 3, runtime-adjustable to 10

All four acceptance criteria addressed. The first three are spec edits; the fourth asked for a
judgment, which is recorded here.

## What changed in `spec-agent-runner.md`

**§2 "Supervise"** now reads `default 3` with the owner ruling of 2026-08-04 named inline (and the
prior value shown as superseded, so a reader meeting an older quote of "2" can tell what happened
rather than suspecting drift). A sub-bullet beneath it records the half the demand correctly
identified as the more consequential one: the cap is changeable at runtime via `GET`/`PUT /settings`
under a **hard ceiling of 10**, and a runtime change is **not persisted** —
`AGENT_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY_CAP` stays the durable default and the cap reverts on restart. The
two-sided enforcement asymmetry is recorded with its reasoning intact (env path clamps so a bad
variable never blocks boot; API path returns `400` so a caller asking for 25 learns its expectation
is wrong), because the asymmetry is a deliberate design position, not an implementation detail — the
next reader would otherwise be tempted to "fix" one side into consistency with the other.

The consequence a reader most needs is stated explicitly: **the cap in force is no longer derivable
from the environment alone** — ask `GET /settings`.

**§4** gains a driving-port row for `GET /settings` and `PUT /settings {concurrencyCap}`, so the
spec's endpoint surface matches the shipped one.

## The fourth criterion: no new decision, and why

**Judgment: a bare spec amendment is the right instrument here — no new D-number.** Nothing is
minted, and no decision id is named, because none should be.

The vault mints a D-number for a **ruling** — a position that constrains future choices across
repos. What the owner ruled on 2026-08-04 is a **tuning of a parameter inside a capability an
existing decision already governs**: dispatch supervision is D059's and D083's territory, and
neither is contradicted or narrowed by moving a default from 2 to 3 or by making it adjustable. A
decision entry here would assert more permanence than the fact deserves — the whole point of the
runtime `/settings` surface is that this number is *meant* to move, and a D-number that says "the
cap is 3" would be stale the first time the owner turns the dial and would then need its own
superseding addendum for a non-event.

The one part that genuinely is durable — that the cap is bounded at 10 and does not survive a
restart — is a property of `agent-runner`'s contract, which is exactly what its spec is for. It is
recorded there.

If the owner disagrees and wants the ruling carried at fleet level rather than in the spec, that is
theirs to say and a vault session will mint it; this report is the vault declining to invent a
ruling's weight on its own authority, per this repo's standing orders.

## Not done, deliberately

No behavior claim is made about `agent-runner` — the vault did not run its tests and did not read
its source beyond what the demand stated. The spec now records what the demand says shipped; if the
implementation and this text ever disagree, the implementation is the thing that moved.

# Fulfillment — D084's `ai-gateway` leg recorded in `spec-ai-gateway.md`

## What shipped

`spec-ai-gateway.md` carries the amendment, in two places:

1. **Decisions line** — now cites **D084** alongside D022/D023/D025/D010/D047/D049 (D055 stays
   marked adjacent).
2. **§9 build notes** — a dated `D084 ... shipped (2026-07-28, commit b78154a, 283/283)` note with
   four sub-bullets, covering exactly the three points the demand asked to have written down
   because they were reasoned to rather than read off the ruling:
   - the **effort value** on the three frontier functions, `embeddings` carrying none with a
     **400** rather than accepted-and-ignored, the resolved **pair** defaulting to
     `claude-opus-5` / `high`, plus the merge-write and widened-on-disk-shape semantics;
   - the **model-identity-vs-routing-hint split** — `providerModelHint`, why collapsing it would
     match `AnthropicAdapter`'s `claude-` prefix and land the nightly sweeps on
     `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (the API-credit path declined 2026-07-28), and why `claude-opus-5` is
     deliberately absent from `ai.catalog.models`;
   - the **value-targeted supersede-on-load** retirement of `force:claude-opus-4-8` and
     `force:claude-code`, rewritten to `auto` rather than to a fresh pin, and why a fleet-default
     write could never have reached those rows.
3. **Verified-vs-reported is stated explicitly**, per the charter and your fourth criterion. The
   vault independently verified, live against `runtime-ai-gateway-1` `:8085`: the new API shape is
   deployed and serving (`resolvedEffort` + `providerModelHint` present on all three frontier
   functions across `agent-runner`, `media-generation`, `dashboard`), `resolvedEffort` = `high`,
   `providerModelHint` = `claude-code`, and **the supersede-on-load demonstrably fired** — the two
   pilots' `contradiction-screen` rows, explicitly pinned since D072's restoration, now read
   `policy: auto`. Taken from your report and *not* independently checked: the 283-test count, the
   merge/400 write semantics, the on-disk shape, and the adapter forwarding `context.model` /
   `context.effort` onto the CLI flags.

## What the origin must know

1. **Your leg is correct and the ruled model value is still not in force.** The same probe that
   confirmed your API shape found the live resolved model is **`claude-opus-4-8`**, not
   `claude-opus-5`. This is **not** an `ai-gateway` defect: `application.yml` ships
   `${AI_POLICY_FRONTIER_MODEL:claude-opus-5}` correctly. The running container is overridden by
   `runtime/docker-compose.local.yml` — `AI_POLICY_FRONTIER_MODEL: claude-opus-4-8`, a line written
   for D072's now-superseded pin, with a comment still describing D072's world. Raised
   `to: [runtime]` as `platform-vault-20260728-runtime-d084-frontier-model-env-drift`. Nothing is
   asked of this repo.
2. **Your supersede-on-load widened the blast radius of that override, correctly and unluckily.**
   Rewriting the explicit rows to `auto` was the right call (it keeps rows tracking the ruled
   default), but it also pointed all 23 repos at the env-overridden frontier model — so the stale
   value went from pilot-scoped to fleet-wide. Recorded in the build-note as fact, not as a fault:
   the mechanism did what D084 wanted; the environment was wrong underneath it. Worth knowing if
   anyone reads the fleet's resolutions before the runtime fix lands.
3. **Your effort-vocabulary flag is RULED — your implementation stands, no follow-up demand.** Put
   to the owner in this session and ratified: **`low | medium | high | xhigh`** is the platform
   vocabulary, on your own stated rationale (the owner-facing selector should not be narrower than
   the thing it drives). `high` and `low` are defaults *within* it, not the vocabulary. Recorded as
   a D084 addendum and in `spec-agent-memory-system.md` §9.0 / D.6 and this repo's §9 build-note.
   The one-enum change you offered is not needed. Your `providerModelHint` split is sanctioned in
   the same addendum, in the same terms you argued it.
4. **Your point 4 (a pickable frontier-model list for the console) is agreed as a real gap**, and
   agreed as *not* this demand's to solve. If `dashboard`'s D084 selector needs it, it comes from
   `dashboard` as its own demand — the vault has not pre-empted that.

## Not done / caveats

- The build-note records `b78154a` and the 283-test count **as reported by you**; the vault did not
  build or run this repo's test suite.
- The live verification covers three repos × three functions, not all 23 — enough to establish the
  API shape, the effort value, the hint, and that the rewrite fired; not a fleet census.
- `PLATFORM_STATE.md` §4 item 10's drift-watch stays **open**, now pointed at the runtime override
  rather than at the un-versioned store's unknown-origin rows. It closes when the live resolution
  reads `claude-opus-5` / `high`.

  rule exists.
- **227 tests, confirmed.** `pytest --collect-only -q` collects 227. This one matched, and it is

`:8093` was probed again this session and **still does not answer** — the "built but not deployed,

W2 (99), W3 (156), W4 (200) and W5 (206) are marked done 2026-08-04 with their test counts carried
as **worker-reported** — those are per-wave historical counts the vault cannot re-derive after the
fact, and the register says so rather than laundering them into observed fact. Only the final 227 is
marked vault-counted. W6 is 🟨 in progress: D066's gate on it is met, since W5 is what D066 was
waiting for.

The W5 row now carries mission `d34de281-c5c5-4e44-b3c5-6085c225adea`, target `tutor`, kids-class;
concept, architecture and plan gates all owner-approved with recorded notes; **wave 1 staged, not

stage-not-raise posture held under real load rather than only in principle.

`tutor`*, which needs the app actually built. The demand was right to frame this as evidence, and
the register does not upgrade it. A gate the vault marks passed on a worker's summary is exactly the
failure this register was built to prevent.

waves without amendment — every correction the pilot produced went to app-studio's code, never to
the spec. That is a fact about the spec's quality worth keeping.

# Fulfillment — `app-studio` register row refreshed against observed reality

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4). All three acceptance criteria are
met. Per this repo's state-register directive, **nothing below was taken from the demand's own
account** — every fact was checked read-only against the `app-studio` repo, the running fleet, or
the coordinator's config.

## Criterion 1 — the row says building

Verified before writing, not after:

| Claim | How it was checked | Result |
|---|---|---|
| repo exists, `.brain/` adopted | `git log`, `ls .brain/sessions`, `cat .brain/toolkit-pin` | ✅ — pin **v0.6.2**, one closed session file |
| "three commits" | `git log --oneline` | ⚠️ **already stale — 6 commits.** The demand was written mid-session; two later commits (the W1 feature commit and the session close) landed after it. Recorded as 6 |
| `status: building`, contracts `v0.17.0` | read `HEXAGON.md` frontmatter | ✅ — also `kind: runtime`, `side: host`, `spec:` and `decisions:` present, so D085 dispatchability holds by construction |
| ledger + 15-stage/5-gate machine + projections + HTTP surface | read `src/app_studio/` layout | ✅ — `domain/ ports/ adapters/ api.py` as the spec specifies |
| **41 tests** | counted `def test_` across the three test files: 13 + 6 + 22 | ✅ **41 exactly** — counted, not believed |

The row now reads **building**, and says plainly that the "approved — awaiting bootstrap / `git init`
has not happened" text it carried at landing was true for a few hours and is superseded. The top
banner carries the same correction and moves the fleet count **28 → 29**.

## Criterion 2 — §3 keeps 8093/5439 as not-live

Kept, but the *reason* was rewritten, because the old reason had gone false. §3 said "planned, not
yet live: **the repo is not bootstrapped**" — the repo is now bootstrapped. Re-verified the
underlying fact independently: **`curl :8093/health` does not answer**, and `grep` over
`runtime/services.json` and `docker-compose.local.yml` finds no `app-studio`. So the entry now reads
*allocated; the repo exists and is building; nothing binds this port*. Same verdict, honest reason.

## Criterion 3 — fleet registration stated as outstanding

Done in the row, and given its own dated block in **§2**, because the finding is worse than
"outstanding" and the next session should not have to rediscover it:

**`app-studio` is not in `demand-coordinator.board.repos`** — checked read-only against
`demand-coordinator/src/main/resources/application.yml`: **29 repos listed, `app-studio` absent**.
The coordinator scans registered repos' `demands/` off disk, so **everything `app-studio` raises is
invisible to routing — including its own registration demand.** Its inbox answers normally, which is
what makes the failure quiet.

Live confirmation, not inference: `GET /inbox/platform-vault` returned `{"data":[]}` while *this
very demand*, addressed to `platform-vault`, sat unread on disk in `app-studio/demands/`. **It
reached this repo because the owner carried it by hand.**

## What the origin must know

1. **The deadlock has a way out already raised.** Of the three registration demands in flight, the
   two `app-studio` raised (`…-coordinator-board-registration`, control-plane inventory) **cannot be
   ingested** — the demand asking to be listed is unlistable. The third,
   `platform-vault-20260804-app-studio-board-registration`, was raised by **this** repo, which *is*
   a registered board repo, so it is the only copy the routing system can deliver. The duplication
   is deliberate and is being kept; one board entry is the outcome either way.
2. **Your envelope does not validate against `contracts` `demand-coordinator/demand.json`** — two
   defects, and I did not touch your file (cross-repo edits are forbidden, D035/house rule):
   - `status: raised` — not a member of `Demand.Status` (`open | satisfied | archived`). Use `open`.
     **This is the same defect that stopped the vault's own birth demand from parsing hours earlier**;
     a coordinator parse error reports only the *first* failure, so fixing what it names is not the
     same as validating.
   - **`acceptance-criteria` is missing** — a required frontmatter array. Yours are prose under
     `## Acceptance criteria`; they need to be lifted into the envelope too. (`needs-owner: no` is
     fine — YAML reads it as boolean false.)

   Worth fixing before the board registration lands, or the demand will be ingestable and still
   unparseable.
3. **Nothing here is a ruling.** This was a register refresh against observed reality, exactly as
   your demand framed it. D093–D096 are untouched; v1 stage-not-raise and the Lane-1 deferral stand.
4. Wave 8's W1 row in `PLATFORM_GANTT.md` is flipped to done with the observed evidence; **W2
   (conception machinery) is next**.

# Fulfillment — retire D074's exclusion list entirely; `.brain` has no excluded hexagons

**Ruling recorded as D092.** No D-number was reserved by the demand and none was suggested; the vault
assigned the next free one, per the demand's own first criterion.

## Against each acceptance criterion

1. **Fresh dated entry with a fresh D-number** — **D092**, `Status: Accepted (owner-ruled 2026-08-02
   … recorded off demand brain-toolkit-20260802-platform-vault-d074-exclusions-lifted, needs-owner:
   false on the D063 precedent)`. The new-ruling-new-number precedent (D062 on D053, D074 on D052,
   D086 on D074) is cited in the entry's own *"Why a fresh D-number"* paragraph.
2. **D074 part 1 gains a dated addendum; D086 gains a pointer** — both landed, both in the style D086
   itself used. D074's addendum retires the list in place and states the scope rule is now simply
   *every hexagon carries `.brain/`*. D086's addendum names the two superseded passages precisely —
   the *"remain excluded and their exclusions are unamended"* sentence and the *"Not ruled here"*
   paragraph that left the three-repo question open — and states that **everything else in D086
   stands and is relied upon**, in particular its FP-1 correction and its D035 confirmation.
3. **The owner's words verbatim** — recorded in D092's `Status:` line, in D074's addendum, and in
   A.2, exactly as given, including its typos: *"i want all hexagons to have brain, no exclustion, and
   i want it done , not just in the D074, raise demands to make it happen"*.
4. **The shared rationale recorded as retired, not silently dropped** — D092 sub-ruling 1 is dedicated
   to this and says so in terms: D086 found the rationale factually wrong for the vault while leaving
   it *"sound for the other three"*, and **this ruling removes the category rather than refuting it
   three more times**. Being infrastructure is no longer a ground for exclusion from `.brain`,
   whatever else is true of a repo. Repeated in D074's addendum and in spec A.2 so the retirement is
   findable from any of the three places a reader might start.
5. **Spec Appendix A.2 amended** — the three-name clause is struck (never deleted, per the vault's
   supersede convention) and replaced with the no-exclusions posture plus the retired rationale. The
   D075 *"Unaffected"* line is struck and corrected in the same pass, since FP-6 now reaches every
   repo without exception. New **Appendix D.8** carries the full amendment record. **The frozen core
   (§§1–17) is untouched** — every edit is Appendix A / platform-binding territory, exempt exactly as
   D061/D063/D068/D072/D074/D075/D084/D086's own Appendix A changes were. No metric, threshold, or
   kill criterion is altered.
6. **PLATFORM_STATE.md records the posture and the count** — new `AS OF 2026-08-02` entry, and it
   explicitly supersedes the 2026-07-31 banner's *"the three D074 exclusions hold exactly"* line.
7. **FP-4 carried forward honestly, not re-litigated** — recorded in D092's own consequence paragraph,
   in Appendix D.8, and in the register: auto-enrolment by directory presence (D068 / A.5) takes the
   swept fleet from **25 to 28** against D076's `claude-credits` ceiling and Treasury's $5/day /
   $50/month. D074 flagged it at 23 and ruled no throttle; D086 carried it at 24; **D092 records the
   delta and rules nothing new on it.**

## One correction to the demand's own figures, made rather than accepted

The demand states **24 → 27**. That is one behind: the register's **2026-07-31 full scan re-counted
25** — the first time the figure was counted rather than derived — and a read-only sweep this session
confirms **25 committed `.brain/` directories**. The pair of record is therefore **25 → 28**, which is

# Fulfillment — record dashboard Era II completion in the vault (D036 ratified)

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4). The owner
approves; the coordinator assembles the summary. This report records what the
vault session changed and, honestly, one governance wrinkle it found.

## The owner ruling, as relayed
Promote **D036** ("dashboard is the platform's management console; writes stay
forms-over-owning-APIs", drafted in `dashboard-console-design.md` §10.1) from
**Proposed → Accepted**, and record Era II as complete on `spec-dashboard.md`.

## Facts verified before recording (observed, not trusted)
The vault records reality, so every figure below was checked against the
dashboard repo, not taken from the demand text:

- **G1 passed 2026-07-10** — evidence pack §11.2 + `dashboard/PROGRESS.md`
  ("WU-104: Operate screen — G1 PASSED"). Live socket start/stop from the browser.
- **G2 passed 2026-07-13** — evidence pack §11.6, owner-attested ("the owner drove
  the real platform through the console and declared it passed").
- **581/581 specs** — evidence pack §11.5 (`Tests 581 passed (581)`).
- **`v0.2.0` tagged** — the pack itself deferred the tag "to the architect on merge"
  (§11.5), so this was **not** assumed: `git show v0.2.0` in `dashboard` confirms an
  **annotated** tag, "Era II: the management console (WU-100..WU-116, gates G1+G2
  passed)", dated 2026-07-13, on the PR #15 merge commit. Real.
- **Evidence pack** `dashboard/design/era-ii-acceptance-2026-07-13.md` present and
  read (22 KB, WU-115, post-G2). It is candid about its own two soft spots (needs-you
  slot, a live approve never executed) — recorded here so the acceptance isn't
  overstated.

## What was changed in the vault
1. **`PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md` — D036 status.** Replaced the bare `Accepted` with an
   owner-ratified status line (dated 2026-07-13, citing this demand, the gates, the
   tag, the spec count, and the evidence pack) — see the governance note below for
   why the wording is what it is. Closing-summary line for D036 annotated to match.
2. **`spec-dashboard.md` — status header (the demand's primary ask).** "Era II
   (management console) design accepted 2026-07-10" → **"Era II (management console)
   complete 2026-07-13"** with G1/G2 dates, `v0.2.0`, 581/581, and both the design
   pack and the acceptance pack cited. **`Proposes: D036`** removed and **D036 folded
   into the `Decisions:` list** (it is a decision now, not a proposal).
3. **`spec-dashboard.md` §9 build notes.** The Era II bullet was still written as a
   future work order; flipped to "complete 2026-07-13" so §9 doesn't contradict the
   new header.
4. **`dashboard-console-design.md` §10.1 + header.** The governing design pack still
   read `Status: Proposed` on its draft D036 and `Proposes: D036` in its header —

# Fulfillment -- amend dashboard-console-design.md's design-screen section

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4). No approval self-certified, no origin notified.

## Preflight

Checked by evidence, not commit recency, per the dispatch's refined instruction: `git status --porcelain`
empty; `git status -sb` showed `main...origin/main` with no ahead/behind; the most recent commit
(`c4ad640`, 2026-07-28 20:13:21) is `progress: handoff -- D085 closed, both legs verified by direct
read and archived` -- a session-end handoff, the final act of a vault session per this repo's own
CLAUDE.md. Repo was quiescent. Proceeded.

## What changed

`dashboard-console-design.md` §12, last paragraph. The paragraph asserting *"design-studio's own served
review pages remain the mechanism for any other target repo's mission ... WU-120 is the console-as-
mission-subject special case, not a reversal of the general rule"* is corrected in place: that claim is
now false as stated, since mission `e8e4b3e5-ef0c-46b1-8a76-57c4126f219d` targets `plantpal` (not
`dashboard`) and was driven end to end from the console on 2026-07-28 -- design-system build, artifact
review, theme-gate approval, validate-and-pin at `system-gate`, through to `clone` -- with no served
review page involved.

The withdrawal is a **negative** correction only: it removes the false "confined to the mission's own
subject repo" claim. It does **not** assert the opposite general claim ("the console is now the
mechanism for every target repo's mission review") -- one cross-repo mission does not prove a general
rule in either direction. That question is named explicitly as open and unresolved for the owner, per
the demand's own hard limit.

The amendment records, by name, the surfaces that shipped across the twelve 2026-07-28 demands (cited
where a full id is confirmed; full sequencing and reasoning left to the source doc rather than
restated): the design-system build panel and validate-and-pin at `system-gate`
(`design-studio-20260728-dashboard-system-build-console`,
`dashboard-20260728-design-studio-build-dispatch-visibility`), artifact readers
(`design-studio-20260728-dashboard-artifact-readers`), the three-phase stage spine + Now panel, the
theme-gate review workspace, the rewind control, the design-systems browser, the needs-you queue's
design-mission source, and unblock for an attempt-exhausted build. Full id list and the diagnosis/
reasoning behind each: `docs/DESIGN_CONSOLE_REDESIGN_PLAN.md` §4 (platform root, read-only for this
pack, not restated here).

Also recorded: the pack's own accessibility law (§5, *"Status is never color-alone"*) is now satisfied
by the stage rail, which previously encoded current-versus-past by colour alone and now encodes stage
kind by glyph plus accessible text.

## Hard limits honored

No D-number invented; `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md` untouched. No owner ruling recorded or implied as settled
-- the amendment explicitly stops at recorded fact (one cross-repo mission) and names the broader
question ("is the console now the general mechanism for every target repo's mission review, or does
design-studio's served-page path remain load-bearing for some other case not yet exercised?") as open
for the owner. Nothing else in the pack was restructured; only §12's last paragraph was replaced/
extended. `PLATFORM_STATE.md`, `PLATFORM_GANTT.md`, and every `spec-*.md` were left untouched.

## Open question escalated to the owner

Whether the console is the *general* mechanism for every target repo's design-mission review now, not
just for the one cross-repo case (`e8e4b3e5`, `plantpal`) that has actually run end to end. Not decided
here.
