## State before

Not already shipped. `spec-dashboard.md` described `/brain` as a D070 read surface with a dispatch
trigger and carried no mention of D084; its header decisions line stopped at D077. The drift the
demand names was real.

## What shipped

**`spec-dashboard.md` §9 — new dated build-note (2026-07-28, D084)**, covering both acceptance
criteria:

1. **Criterion 1 — what shipped, that it writes the stored policy row and never triggers a run, and
   that D070 is untouched.** The note records the per-repo × three-frontier-function rows, the
   stored-row-plus-live-`resolve`-pair display, `PUT /ai/policy/{repo}/{function}` with merge
   semantics (`effort: "default"` unpins), the class-2 confirm + action-log entry, and the three
   explicit negatives: **no run trigger, no `agent-runner` call** (asserted by a test in the repo),
   **no new read route on either side** — the panel rides the `GET /brain/repos` read the screen
   already makes. **D070's `GET /brain/*` reads-only invariant is stated as untouched and standing
   unqualified**, with the reason spelled out: these are `ai-gateway` policy writes on `ai-gateway`'s
   own routes, not `/brain/*` writes. Also recorded: form state seeds from the **stored** row, never
   from the resolution, so a confirming click on an `auto` row cannot freeze it at today's value.
   1553/1553 tests, files named.
2. **Criterion 2 — the two scoping judgments, recorded as reviewable rather than tribal.** (a) The
   model selector offers only `auto` + the resolved frontier model (+ any value the row itself pins),
   because `ai-gateway` gives only the frontier default the separate `providerModelHint: claude-code`
   and any other `claude-*` id matches `AnthropicAdapter`'s prefix, routing the sweep onto
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — **the API-credit path the owner declined 2026-07-28**. The note states the
   consequence plainly: the narrow selector is a **billing guard**, not a UI simplification.
   (b) `embeddings` renders **no row at all** — effort-free by ruling, a 400 upstream, so the surface
   omits it rather than offering a control that can only fail.
   Plus the effort vocabulary (`low | medium | high | xhigh`, D084 addendum) and why it is
   deliberately not dispatch-options' list, which includes `max` and would 400 here.

# Fulfillment — record the D059 amendment: per-dispatch model + effort, default Opus 5 / low

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4) — never self-approved; the
coordinator assembles the summary and the owner's gate still applies.

## Scope

This demand names five targets' worth of work across three repos. **Only the `platform-vault` leg
is done here** — acceptance criterion 4: *"platform-vault records a decision entry
amending/superseding D059's blanket Sonnet-5-only cap with the new default (Opus 5, effort low) and
the per-dispatch override, citing this demand."*

Criteria 1–3 (`agent-runner`'s `POST /dispatch` fields and default change; the
`AGENT_RUNNER_MODEL`/`DEFAULT_MODEL` fallback semantics; `dashboard`'s `/agents` form selectors) are
`agent-runner`'s and `dashboard`'s own work. This session **wrote no code in either repo and
verified neither** — per the vault's single-writer boundary (D035), the vault never edits a sibling
repo, and it does not certify another repo's shipment.

## What was done

**1. D083 minted.** The entry records the owner's 2026-07-28 ruling as three sub-points: (a) D059's
config mechanism is *kept* and its exclusivity *dropped* — `AGENT_RUNNER_MODEL`/`DEFAULT_MODEL`
becomes the fallback rather than the only permitted value, its empty-string escape hatch intact, and
`effort` joins it as a second orthogonal knob with its own default; (b) `dashboard`'s `/agents` form
is the owner-facing surface, extended with two pre-filled selectors, not a new screen; (c) the
ruling closes `spec-agent-runner.md` §8 open question 2, which had carried an explicit *lean* toward
"form field with a default" since the spec was written. Sonnet 5 remains fully selectable.

**2. D059 amended, not rewritten.** Following this vault's standing supersede convention (D042 over
D031's TS leg; D061/D063; D064/D067), D059 keeps its entry and gains a dated addendum stating
precisely what survives (the mechanism, the reason it is config rather than a process-env hack, the
2026-07-17/18 history) and what does not (the "every dispatch, without exception" exclusivity).
A reader landing on D059 first is pointed at D083 for the current default.

**3. Consistency sweep.** `spec-agent-runner.md` (§8 Q2, §9 build-notes, header Decisions line) and
`PLATFORM_STATE.md` §4 item 5 were each updated — the register's item 5 previously recorded the cap
as a *resolved* ruling and would otherwise have kept asserting Sonnet-5-only as current fact, which
is exactly the drift D083's own Consequences forbid. Two further Sonnet references were checked and
**deliberately left alone** as accurate history, not live claims: `PLATFORM_STATE.md`'s dated
2026-07-20 session banner (line ~588) and `PLATFORM_GANTT.md`'s Wave 7 governing-law line, both of
which describe what was true at their own as-of date. `spec-design-studio.md`'s "batched Sonnet
dispatches" is a separate D051 propositions-authoring choice, untouched by this ruling.

**4. Doc-sync duty discharged (D081).** Dispatching an agent is a documented operational process and
its form now has two new fields, so a demand went `to: [documentations]`
(`platform-vault-20260728-documentations-dispatch-model-effort-choice`) — a one-way heads-up, not a
review gate, carrying the explicit caveat that D083 records a ruling and not a shipment.

## What this entry does NOT claim

- **Not that the feature works.** No `POST /dispatch` call was made, no console form was opened, no
  `agent-runner` or `dashboard` source was read. The vault records decisions ahead of their
  execution by charter; the demand's other four criteria carry their own evidence.
- **Not a new owner ruling.** `needs-owner: false` was correct — the owner ruled directly in the
  `demand-coordinator` session's chat on 2026-07-28. The vault's own judgment calls were narrow and
  are stated in the entry: a fresh D-number rather than folding into D059 (a genuine new owner
  ruling on a real option set — the D062/D063/D068 precedent), and D059 kept-with-addendum rather
  than superseded-and-struck.

## One flagged consequence, recorded not resolved

Defaulting dispatch to the most expensive tier makes `treasury`'s `claude-credits` daily ceiling
(D076, 549,000 tokens/day) bind sooner than its 2026-07-23 sizing assumed — that sizing was done
against fleet-brain traffic, not Opus-default dispatch. Recorded in D083's Consequences and in the
spec build-note as a watch item for `treasury`/`ai-gateway`. **No demand raised for it** and no
figure changed: it is a forecast, not an observed breach, and re-sizing a ruled ceiling is an owner
call, not something to pre-empt on speculation.

# Fulfillment — owner ruling on the shape of `POST /missions/{id}/execute` (D073)

## What shipped

The owner ruled all four questions in this session's chat, put as an explicit option set with the
demand's own leans surfaced as the recommended options. Recorded as **D073**, with governed text in
`spec-design-studio.md` §2's "Plan & execution" bullet — written to be built against without
further interpretation, per your criterion 6.

**1. Raise mechanism → (b), staging.** `execute` writes rendered demand files into
`artifacts_store/<mission-id>/demands-staged/`. It never writes into `demands/`, never commits,
never pushes. **"Raised" keeps exactly the meaning `DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §3 gives it.** Your lean was
right and is now law. (a) and (d) are rejected in D073's own text with reasons.

**2. Granularity → one demand per work unit.** N work units, N staged files, each independently
trackable and closable.

**3. Dispatch → none.** `execute` stops at staging. Dispatch happens through the ordinary
demand-coordinator flow after a human raises.

**4. The invariant, squared explicitly** — this was the question you most wanted ruled, and it is
ruled in your stricter direction: the standing invariant's "agents do the writing, dispatched
through `agent-runner`" clause does **not** sanction this repo pointing a write-capable agent at a
target repo's checkout. `propose`'s self-targeting is the correct reading; **"never writes to any
target repo" stands unweakened**. D073 names D055 as the reason it stays closed — an HTTP call must
never be able to launch a bypass-enabled agent inside another repo.

**5. Repeat calls → idempotent per work unit; pre-`plan-gate` refused mechanically.** Re-calling
regenerates without duplicating, so re-raising after a rejected-and-redone round — including via
D067's `rewind` — stays legitimate. Your reading of the pre-`plan-gate` question ("a firm no") is
confirmed and is now a `PipelineStageMismatchError`-class guard rather than a convention, exactly as
you proposed to build it.

## What the origin must know

- **One dependency you should not break, discovered while working your sibling demand:** the staging
  location works *because* `artifacts_store` is a **host bind-mount**, not a named volume (D060's
  keep-history addendum, live-verified this session). Staged files must be reachable on the host for
  a later session to review and commit them. Had the cutover used a named volume, this ruling would
  stage demands into a place no session could reach. Both D073's Consequences and §2's route text
  record this as load-bearing: **switching `artifacts_store` to a named volume requires revisiting
  D073.**
- **Deliberately not ruled:** what the later session's raising step looks like operationally (a
  script, a checklist, or plain hand-raising). The convention already covers it, and specifying
  ceremony ahead of the first real use would over-specify. Build the route; let the first atlas
  execution show whether anything more is needed.
- **§9's old build-note has been corrected** — its "that route remains unbuilt, pending its own owner
  ruling on shape" now points forward to D073, while still stating the route itself is unbuilt.

## Not done / caveats

- **This is a ruling, not a shipment.** The route is not built; nothing in this repo changed but
  governed text. D073's §9 build-note says so explicitly, and notes that `plan.py`'s TODO had
  already outlived three spec amendments (D064, D067, D069) before being ruled — worth not
  repeating on the build side.
- The vault did not evaluate whether per-unit granularity will flood the coordinator board on a
  large plan (D071's `frontend-atlas` will be the first real test). The owner chose per-unit with
  that trade-off stated; if it proves noisy in practice, that is a follow-on demand with real
  evidence, not a reason to deviate from the ruling now.

# Fulfillment — pause semantics stated in both halves

## State before

Not already shipped, and the demand's diagnosis was exactly right. `spec-design-studio.md` asserted
the batch-boundary-only rule at **three** separate sites — §2's mission-ledger bullet, §7's
`dashboard` consumer row, and §9's D069 build-note. The demand named the spec generally; all three
were corrected, since leaving two of them would have reproduced the drift the demand exists to close.

## Against the acceptance criteria

1. **"no longer states batch boundaries only, full stop; states both halves"** — done at all three
   sites. §2 carries the full statement (mechanism included: the artifact `paused` flag written in
   one place at consolidation vs. the live `mission.pause_requested` re-read per pass); §7 and §9
   carry the short form and point at §2.
2. **`documentations/workflows/design-mission.md`** — **not this repo's leg.** That criterion belongs
   to the demand's other target (`to: [platform-vault, documentations]`); the vault does not write
   `documentations`, and this report claims nothing about it.
3. **"neither document implies a pause is ignored until the current batch consolidates when the
   background advancer is carrying the build"** — the corrected text makes the advancer's behaviour
   the *immediate* case and says so in the same sentence as the batch-boundary case, so the omission
   that produced the wrong reading is gone rather than merely qualified.
4. **"design-studio needs no code change"** — respected; nothing was asked of that repo, and the §9
   build-note records explicitly that the documents moved to the behaviour, not the reverse.

## Judgment recorded rather than left tribal

The spec now also carries the *reason* the two halves differ, not just the fact: a background loop
that keeps dispatching for minutes after the owner pressed pause is not "stop spending on my behalf,"
while an in-flight hand-driven call's guarantee is that nothing is torn in half. Stating both
behaviours without the reason would leave the next reader assuming one of them is a bug.

Also worth the record, and noted in the §9 build-note: this demand was generated because
`platform-vault-20260728-design-studio-build-resilience`'s own acceptance criteria required raising
it **if the documentation turned out to be what was wrong**. Criteria that admit the docs — not the
code — may be the defect are cheap to write and caught this one.

## What is explicitly NOT claimed

This report does not close the loop. `done` is the worker's claim; the coordinator/owner approval
gate closes it, and the demand's `documentations` leg is still outstanding besides. The demand file
in `design-studio/demands/` is untouched — origin-owned.

# Fulfillment report — the third gate action, and reference imagery, are now in the spec

## What changed

One file: `spec-design-studio.md`, commit `00e5410`. Three sections.

**§2** — the divergent sentence is amended in place, and a new block, *"What an owner may do at a
gate"*, sits at the end of the mission-ledger bullet, where the abort (D064) and rewind (D067)
paragraphs already live. It enumerates the three actions with their consequences, states the
own-append-only-list separation against D067's precedent, and gives the never-folded rule its own
paragraph. Reference imagery is recorded on the REJECT action, since that is the only action that
can carry it.

**§4** — `POST /missions/{id}/send-back` joins the inbound table with its refusal shapes; the gates
route's payload gains `referenceImages?`; a new paragraph records the `sendBacks` projection in the
same place §4 already records `activeDispatch` (D064) and `rewinds` (D067), and notes
`referenceImages` on gate records.

**§5** — the ledger sentence now names three separate append-only lists rather than leaving
send-backs unmentioned; the artifact list gains owner-supplied reference imagery.

**Field and endpoint names were taken from the fulfilment reports, not from the demand text**, as
the demand's §2 instructed: `dashboard-20260728-design-studio-gate-send-back-report.md` and
`dashboard-20260729-design-studio-reference-imagery-in-direction-report.md`, both in
`design-studio/demands/fulfilled/`. The second had already closed by the time this was picked up.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
|---|---|
| §2's gated-mission description amended to three actions, two-outcome text retired | §2, opening sentence of the mission-ledger bullet + the new gate-actions block |
| Send-back as its own append-only list, not a gate record, not a third `GateOutcome`; §5 names it | §2 separation paragraph (D067 precedent named); §5's three-list sentence |
| The never-folded consequence stated | §2, its own paragraph, with the `e8e4b3e5` cost and the corrective |
| Rejection may carry reference imagery; own subtree, registry, absolute paths in direction | §2's REJECT bullet; §4's `referenceImages?` and the projection paragraph |
| §5's artifact list gains reference imagery | §5 |
| The vault decides on a decision entry, reserving none | Judged below — **no entry** |
| No behaviour changed, no other repo's spec touched | Documentation only; one file edited |

## Criterion 6 — the judgment: no `PLATFORM_DECISIONS` entry, for either amendment

**Neither amendment gets a D-number, and none is reserved.** Three reasons, in the order they
weighed:

1. **There is no owner ruling to record.** This repo's charter is that a decision entry is written
   *behind an actual owner ruling* — the vault records rulings, it does not mint them to dignify a
   change. Send-back shipped off `dashboard-20260728-design-studio-gate-send-back`, `needs-owner:
   false`; reference imagery off `dashboard-20260729-design-studio-reference-imagery-in-direction`.
   Both are repo-to-repo capability demands the owner approved at the coordinator's gate, which is
   approval of *work*, not a ruling on platform law. Writing D086 here would put a decision in the
   log that no one made.
2. **Both sit inside an already-ruled surface.** D064 (abort, `activeDispatch`, propose rounds) and
   D067 (rewind, and specifically the *separate-list* principle these amendments reuse verbatim)
   already rule the gate machinery. The send-back's governing rule — a non-decision event is kept
   off `gate_records` and out of the dispatch fold-in — is D067's rule applied to a new event, not a
   new rule. Reference imagery is an additive artifact kind inside `design-studio`'s own artifact
   store, which §5 has always owned.
3. **A spec amendment is the right instrument, and it is what the demand actually asked for.** Five
   of the six criteria are §2/§5 text. A reader who wants to know what a gate decision records now
   finds it in the spec, which is where the demand says they would look.

**If the owner disagrees**, the correction is cheap and this report is the place it would be
noticed: the entry would take the next free number (D086 at the time of writing) and the spec text
above would gain the citation. Nothing in the amendment presumes its absence.

## One thing raised, deliberately

`documentations` describes the gate as two-outcome — `send back` appears nowhere in that repo. That
is the same staleness this demand fixed in the vault, one repo over. Per the D081 doc-sync duty
(one-way heads-up, not a review gate) a demand goes `to: [documentations]`:
`platform-vault-20260729-documentations-gate-third-action`. It touches no other repo's spec and
changes no behaviour, so it stays inside this demand's scope note.

# Fulfillment — spec-sync the dispatch-retry semantics

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4).

## What was done

All seven acceptance criteria are addressed in `spec-design-studio.md`:

1. **Self-heal on four stages (§2)** — `theme-interview`, `clone`, `content-interview` and
   `theme-gate` all self-heal on a dead dispatch: the stage stays, the next call re-dispatches, no
   owner ceremony. `theme-gate` is explicitly recorded as **no longer requiring `abandon-round`**.
2. **The attempt cap (§2)** — three dead dispatches → terminal `blocked`, dispatching nothing until
   an owner clears it. Stated **once as a shared rule** with `system-gate`'s per-unit
   `MAX_UNIT_ATTEMPTS = 3`, including why the two implementations stay separate while agreeing on
   the number, the record shape and the field names, and the derived-not-stored counting rule.
3. **`POST /missions/{id}/dispatch/unblock` (§4)** — listed with the one-route-not-four rationale,
   the fresh-budget watermark, "dispatches nothing itself", and the 409 cases (nothing blocked, or a
   stage with no dispatch-tracking artifact — which is how it refuses at `system-gate`).
4. **The second background advancer (§2)** — `DispatchAdvancer` as `BuildAdvancer`'s twin, including
   death *discovery* via a direct agent-runner probe (the "died with nobody watching" case), and all
   four negatives: never consolidates → never advances a stage, never starts one, never re-enters a
   blocked one, honors `pauseRequested` on the live flag per the 2026-07-28 pause correction.
   `system-gate` named as out of its business, with the one-artifact-two-loops race as the reason.
5. **`abandon-round`** — retained, no longer mandatory, and the only route for a run agent-runner
   still reports `launched`.
6. **The standing invariant** — restated and shown to survive: neither advancer advances a stage,
   and the retry advancer cannot even consolidate.
7. **The flagged open question — ruled by the vault, in the §9 build-note.** No
   `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md` entry, and it rides no existing one. The demand's premise that D081 is
   the build-resilience decision is wrong on the record: **D081 is `documentations` adopting
   `.brain`**, and the 2026-07-28 build-resilience work has **no D-number at all** — it shipped off
   a vault-raised demand and was recorded in `PLATFORM_STATE.md`. Recording the generalization as a
   decision while the thing it generalizes is not one would invert their standing, so both live in
   this spec plus the state register. Escalation to a D-number is reserved for the case where the cap
   becomes a *fleet* rule — that would be an owner ruling, and is not what shipped.

## What we found while fulfilling, and fixed unasked

The demand's §4 criterion says `dispatch/unblock` should sit "alongside the already-listed
`POST /missions/{id}/build-system/unblock`". **It was not listed** — the whole 2026-07-28
build-resilience shipment (per-unit cap, blocked build, `build-system/unblock`) had never reached
this spec; the only trace was a §9 build-note about the *pause* correction that mentioned "capped
retries" in passing. §2 could not honestly state the new cap "once as a shared rule" while the rule
it shares with was undocumented, so both are now recorded. Flagged rather than silently absorbed
because it means the vault's own 2026-07-28 demand closed without a spec-sync of its own.

Also noted, not acted on: the §2 sentence the demand quotes as current spec text
(`retry = re-dispatch (idempotent, like interview polling)`) is not in this spec — it lives in
`design-studio`'s `CHANGELOG.md`. §2 previously said nothing at all about dispatch failure, so the
new bullet is additive rather than a correction of a wrong line.

`domain/dispatch_advancer.py`, `domain/dispatch_recovery.py`, `domain/clone.py`, `api.py`) — the

`dispatch/unblock` 409 semantics are recorded as the code states them, not as the demand paraphrased
them. **Not vault-verified:** no test run, no live probe of a running instance; the shipment claim
(`84411c0`) is the origin repo's.

# Fulfillment — the stage machine records `refresh-inputs`

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4).

## Criterion by criterion

1. **Recorded in the stage-machine section** — §2 gains a dedicated bullet: `POST
   /missions/{id}/refresh-inputs` re-derives `harvest.json` + `brief.json` against the target repo as
   it stands today, owner-initiated with a required reason, **moving no stage and reversing no gate
   decision**.
2. **The changed implication is stated** — the bullet says outright that *being past `brief` no
   longer means the brief is fixed*, with the concrete shape of it (a mission at `coverage-gate` may
   be sitting on a brief composed minutes ago from a target that changed a week earlier). §9's
   build-note names *"past `brief`"* as the sentence whose meaning changed, so a future reader
   auditing for drift knows what to look for. No surviving sentence reasons from the old implication:
   §5's "three separate append-only lists" was the one place the old model was load-bearing, and it
   is now four.
3. **The owner ruling and its reason are recorded** — in D087 (item 2) and, where a reader would
   actually trip over it, inside §2's **rewind** bullet: D067's exclusion of the mechanical stages
   rests on "no decision to revisit, only work to redo, which is what the forward machinery is for",
   the forward machinery could not reach `harvest` either, and the gap is closed by a new action
   rather than by stretching `rewind`. **`REWIND_TARGET_STAGES` is unchanged**, stated in both
   places.
4. **D069's open question is left open** — said explicitly in three places (§2's rewind bullet,
   D087's Consequences, §9's build-note), each stating that this ruling is *adjacent to* that
   question and settles nothing there. The §2 line that flags it (*"Not ruled by D069, flagged per
   §8's ask-don't-invent"*) is untouched.
5. **The decision-entry question — the vault's call — ruled YES.** D087 is minted, and per the
   demand's request it records the append-only `RefreshRecord` shape and the nothing-erased rule
   explicitly, both as governance surface rather than as implementation detail. The reasoning for
   minting rather than staying spec-only: the question underneath this is *what happens to approvals
   already earned when the inputs beneath them change*, which is about §3's core invariant. The
   contrast is deliberate and same-day — `design-studio-20260730-platform-vault-dispatch-retry-semantics`
   was ruled **no D-number** hours earlier, because a retry cap is operational tuning. This one is
   law.

## What D087 says that the demand did not ask for, and why

The entry states the **counter-argument it is rejecting**: that re-deriving the premise beneath an
approval could be held to retroactively invalidate it, which would force the mission backward. The
ruling says no — the owner approved *a theme*, and a theme does not become un-approved because the
target repo grew a route; what changes is what remains to be *covered*, and the coverage gate already
exists to answer exactly that. A decision entry that records only the chosen branch is worth much
less later, when someone asks why the obvious alternative was wrong.

## Verification

Read-only against `design-studio`'s working tree (`domain/refresh_inputs.py`, `domain/mission.py`'s
`RefreshRecord`, and the origin's own fulfilment report for
`dashboard-20260730-design-studio-refresh-mission-inputs`). The invariants recorded here are the ones
the code states. **Not vault-verified:** the 624-green suite and the live PlantPal re-derivation
(inbound rows 5 → 14, `stage.companion.turn` absent) are the origin repo's claims, recorded as such
in §9 and in D087's Consequences — no tests were run and no instance was probed from this session.

# Fulfillment — the brief has a third input: the owner

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4). Owner approval for both of this
session's demands was given directly in chat, 2026-08-01.

## Criterion by criterion

1. **D087 amended by redefining the brief's INPUT SET, not `refresh-inputs`** — done, and done in
   D087's own entry as an amendment note rather than by editing its Decision line. The line *"against
   the target repo as it stands today"* is untouched and stays literally true: a refresh still derives
   harvest mechanically from the target, and now reads a third persisted input alongside the other two.
2. **None of the four sub-rulings contradicted, stated explicitly** — done, one clause each in the
   amendment note: no approval disturbed (1); rewind-target set not widened (2); nothing erased,
   append-only (3); and sub-ruling 4's *"an item the refresh adds is genuinely uncovered and appears in
   the matrix gaps"* named as anticipating the mechanic verbatim.
3. **The separation preserved and named** — D090 sub-ruling 2: a refresh means *the world changed*, an
   owner addition means *the owner changed their mind*; separate routes, separate append-only records,
   never one endpoint whose reason field means both. Recorded in the spec's owner-additions bullet too,
   because that is where a future implementer reads it.
4. **The never-invents invariant confirmed NOT widened** — D090 sub-ruling 4: the note alone is always
   accepted, only structured items create rows, owner items carry an `ownerAdded` provenance tag rather
   than an `owner:` category, and **prose-alone item creation is written down as a hard prerequisite
   ruling** if ever wanted. Recorded as a boundary, not merely observed.
5. **Stale matrix = server-computed banner, not a refusal** — D090 sub-ruling 5, including the part
   that matters later: turning it into a refusal changes what an approval means and needs its own
   ruling. The corresponding refusals that *do* stay service-side are listed in D091 ruling 4 so the
   three verifiable facts sit in one place.
6. **An item added after a scope round was approved is a blocker in the CURRENT round** — D090
   sub-ruling 6, worded as the demand asked: never a silent widening of an approval already earned.
7. **spec-design-studio.md gains the action, the third input, the fifth list, the artifact classes and
   a §9 build note** — all four, plus the §4 route row. §5's "four separate append-only lists" is now
   five, with the reason sentence updated to match ("five different kinds of event, and only the first
   is a decision").
8. **Whether it warrants its own decision entry** — the vault's call, made: **yes, D090**, on the same
   test D087 passed. The question underneath is what an Interface Brief *is*, which is governed subject
   matter rather than an endpoint. No number was pre-reserved by the demand, correctly (D088 precedent).

## What this repo did NOT do

- **No implementation was verified.** Standing charter: the vault records decisions without waiting on
  or re-running their execution. Nothing here confirms the route, the record, the artifact or the
  `matrixStale` projection exists.
- **The adjacent `openQuestions` freeze is recorded, not fixed** — carried into D090's Consequences and
  into `PLATFORM_STATE.md` §5 item 10(a), since `design-studio` said it will raise it separately.
- **No agent-grounding layer is ruled.** The demand deliberately did not ask; D090 records it as
  strictly additive and unruled.

(*"the brief already contains everything I want built"*) has no available remedy without it.

# Fulfillment — git-based staleness detection + one-click rebuild/restart ruled and routed

## What shipped

- **D077** recorded in `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md`: staleness is defined by **git** (running container's
  build commit/timestamp vs. the owning repo's `main` HEAD) — not by the demand-coordinator's board
  state. Text mirrors the D034 precedent (own `Status`/`Decision`/`Why`/`Consequences` block, plus a
  `spec-launcher.md §8.7` promoted-text subsection).
- **`spec-launcher.md` amended in place**: §2 gains the responsibility bullet; §3's "never becomes
  automated deploy/restart" and "never becomes a second registry" bullets each gain a 2026-07-23
  restatement confirming the preserved invariants named in the acceptance criteria (host-native
  `:5055` only, `:5056` stays 503 with no `docker.sock`, human-triggered always, no-second-registry
  under D014); §4's outbound table gains the new local-git read and the `rebuild` action, and a new
  inbound row records `dashboard` reading the new `stale` field off the socket-board API it already
  polls; §8 gains a resolved open-question item (7) plus the full §8.7 decision-text block; §9 gains
  a dated build note listing the two demands raised and explaining why no `runtime` demand was
  needed.
- **Two follow-on demands raised**, both committed this session:
  - `platform-vault-20260723-launcher-stale-rebuild-restart-build` → `launcher` — builds the actual
    detection + badge + `POST /api/sockets/{id}/rebuild` action.
  - `platform-vault-20260723-dashboard-launcher-staleness-badge` → `dashboard` — the console-visibility
    half named explicitly in this demand's own acceptance criteria ("the stale SIGNAL must be visible
    wherever the owner actually looks").

## What the origin must know

- **No `runtime` demand was raised.** The rebuild sequence (`git pull` / `docker compose build` /
  `docker compose up -d`) targets `runtime/`'s already-existing compose files through the same
  spawn-and-log mechanism launcher already uses for start/stop — no new compose service, no registry
  change. If `launcher`'s own build session finds this assumption wrong (e.g. a compose file needs a
  new target, or `runtime/services.json` needs a new field), flag it back rather than silently
  reaching into `runtime` — same rule as always.
- The `stale` object's field names in both raised demands (`isStale`/`runningCommit`/`mainHead`/
  `checkedAt`) are **illustrative, not prescriptive** — `launcher`'s build session owns the exact
  shape; `dashboard`'s demand says to confirm against whatever actually ships.
- Nothing is built yet. This vault session is spec-and-decision-only, by design (D035 — the vault
  records rulings, workers build). The two raised demands carry all implementation.

## Not done / caveats

- Non-Compose (local-process) socket coverage for staleness/rebuild is left to the `launcher` build
  demand's own acceptance criteria to either cover or name as an explicit gap — not resolved here,
  since it's an implementation-shape question, not a ruling.
- This report closes the `platform-vault` leg of a demand whose real build work is still open on two
  freshly-raised demands — "done" here means "ruled and routed," not "shipped and running."

# Fulfillment — D077's fifth definition gap recorded

All four acceptance criteria are met. `needs-owner: false` was correct: this is register lag on a
governed mechanism, the same class as the fourth addendum it corrects, and no ruling was needed or
invented.

## The four criteria

1. **Build-note under the D077 series** — added to `spec-launcher.md` §9, dated 2026-08-01, naming
   `launcher` commit `cb0fb56` on `main`. It records the root cause as the demand states it: `isStale`
   decides from `mainHeadTime` (the component's Dockerfile-declared build paths, which D077's *first*
   bugfix narrowed it to) while the override keyed on `mainHead` (the repo's overall HEAD), so the two
   halves disagreed about what counts as a change and "a real new commit" meant any commit at all.
2. **The 2026-07-24 sentence corrected in place** — bracketed, not rewritten. The original wording
   stays visible because it was an *accurate* description of what shipped; what shipped was the
   defect. Deleting it would hide that the gap was introduced by the fix one bugfix earlier, which is
   the single most useful fact in this entry.
3. **Not the content-hash option, and why** — recorded in both the spec note and the decision
   addendum, and marked load-bearing rather than a technicality. The rejected option required
   promoting `gitCommitBefore` — a display-only nearest-commit approximation by its own code's
   documentation — into a deciding input. `mainHeadTime` is the exact value `isStale` already computes
   from, so the fix narrows the override to the verdict's **own input** rather than adding a new one.
   The 2026-07-24 rejection therefore stands rather than being quietly reversed.
4. **D077 addendum** — fifth in the series, same form as the second/third/fourth.

## Two things carried in beyond the criteria

**The failure was permanent, not merely noisy, and the record says so.** `gateway`'s badge could not
be cleared by *either* available action: unrelated commits kept voiding the acknowledgement, and a
byte-identical `Caddyfile` makes a rebuild a legitimate Docker cache hit that never advances the
image's `Created` stamp. A reader who takes it for a re-acknowledgement nuisance would not understand
why the owner directed a durable fix instead of clicking the button again — the button was the move
that had already failed.

**The pre-2026-08-01 migration is recorded as narrow-by-default**: old overrides carry no
`buildRelevantTime`, stay keyed on `mainHead`, and are honoured as written rather than silently
widened into the new, more permissive meaning.

## What was deliberately NOT done

**The series' closing line is left standing, not marked discharged.** `spec-launcher.md` says that if
a fifth definition gap appeared, the timestamp/tag-proxy model itself should be rethought toward
content-addressed comparison — a fleet-wide Dockerfile change. This fix closes the fifth gap *without*
that change, so the question is still open. `launcher` asked for exactly this and was right to: a
fifth gap arriving on schedule is evidence for the concern, not against it, and closing it locally is
not the same as answering it. Whether to act on it is an owner call and is not made here.

**Nothing was ruled.** The demand asked to record a shipped fix, and only that was recorded. The
implementation is unverified by this repo per the standing record-ahead-of-execution charter —
`launcher`'s own live verification is cited as its claim, including the sha256 byte-comparison.

## Doc-sync (D081)

Raised: `platform-vault-20260802-documentations-d077-fifth-gap-doc-sync`. This one is not optional
bookkeeping — a grep of `documentations` found the now-false self-expiry claim in **two** places
(`runbooks/rebuild-stale-service.md` §"acknowledge", `runbooks/troubleshooting.md`), both telling an
owner the override self-expires "the moment either one moves". That is the sentence this addendum
corrected.

# Fulfillment — tenant-app ↔ platform-service networking convention under D040

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4).

## The ruling (owner, 2026-07-15)

The demand was `needs-owner: true`; the owner ruled **option 1**:
**`host.docker.internal:<port>` is THE sanctioned tenant-app →
platform-service address** for local-first dev. Tenant apps stay in their
own compose networks; the shared-external-`platform-net` alternative
(option 2) was considered and rejected — inside a shared docker network
there is no loopback control, so a tenant container would bypass the
published-port layer where D040's compensating control lives and gain
direct reach to the unauthenticated admin surfaces D040 exists to fence
off. Option 1 costs zero `runtime` changes and PlantPal already proved it
live (`POST http://host.docker.internal:8085/ai/request` → 200).

The owner additionally ruled the **clone-model consequences** into the same
entry (PlantPal's stated future: the owner's instance stays local; a
*separate* clone gets hosted publicly): the hosted clone is a separate
trust domain with a one-way boundary — it **never calls back home** (its
own ai-gateway, keys, and ceilings; real auth is *its* gate item per
D040's exposure trigger), and "local monitors hosted" means **outbound
pull-only** from the local box (scrape/poll a public endpoint; no inbound
path into the local stack).

## What shipped

- **`PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md` — D045** (Status/Decision/Why/Known
  limitation/Clone-model consequences/Consequences). The known limitation
  is recorded, not hidden: `host.docker.internal` reaching loopback-bound
  ports is Docker Desktop behavior; on native Linux it maps to the bridge
  gateway IP and this convention needs rework — acceptable because D040
  already names any VPS/go-commercial move as the trigger that forces real
  auth, so the two rework points are the same event.
- **`PLATFORM_ARCHITECTURE.md` §11** ("Runtime — local-first") — the
  short, findable convention the demand asked for: one paragraph + the
  example line `PLATFORM_GATEWAY_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8085`.
- **D040's entry** — addendum cross-referencing D045 as the documented
  cross-network access path (posture not widened).

## What the origin should know

- PlantPal's own fix (defaulting platform-profile URLs to
  `host.docker.internal`) is now the platform convention — nothing further
  owed by plantpal; archive the demand file on approval per the usual flow.
- No `runtime` change was needed; no follow-up demand was dispatched.
- `pregnancy`, `tutor`, and future tenant apps inherit the convention at
  scaffold time (it's in the architecture doc, cited by D-number).

# Fulfillment — `app-studio` birth: spec, decisions, port, Gantt, register

`status: done` is a claim, not a verdict (`DEMAND_SYSTEM.md` §4). All five acceptance criteria are
addressed below, plus the envelope repair that had to happen before the demand could be ingested
at all.

## 0. The envelope repair (why the coordinator could not parse it)

The demand arrived as a draft staged in the root meta-repo and failed schema validation against
`contracts` `demand-coordinator/demand.json`. Four fields corrected, none substantive — the full
record is in a "Raise note" block at the top of the demand file itself, kept there rather than in
this report so it travels with the demand:

| Field | Draft | Corrected | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `raise-ready (draft — …)` | `open` | **The reported parse error.** Not a member of `Demand.Status` (`open \| satisfied \| archived`) |
| `from` | `owner (root meta-repo architect session)` | `platform-vault` | Must be a repo's functional name (D002, `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$`). The root meta-repo is not a fleet hexagon and has no outbox; the file lives in this repo's `demands/`. **Authorship is unchanged and is the owner's** |
| `id` | `root-20260804-app-studio-birth` | `platform-vault-20260804-app-studio-birth` | The `<from-repo>-<YYYYMMDD>-<slug>` rule, once `from` changed |
| `acceptance-criteria` | absent (prose only) | present | Required array; lifted from the demand's own prose section, which stays as the human-readable form |

Only `status` was reported by the coordinator because Jackson stops at the first failure; the other
three would have failed on the next parse.

## 1. Spec (criterion 1)

`spec-app-studio.md` landed, adopting the root meta-repo's W0 draft. **Amendments are consistency
only:** the draft's placeholder "next-free D-numbers" resolved to D093–D096 in the header and at
the two in-body citations (§2 regime critique, §2 ship-clean), and §8's open question *"exact
hub-boundary redraw text"* struck through as closed by D096. Sections 1–9 are otherwise the draft's
own text. **No substantive change was made, so nothing is flagged back to the owner** under the
demand's own "amend for consistency, not substance" clause.

## 2. Decisions (criterion 2)

Next free numbers, never pre-reserved — the log stood at D092, so **D093, D094, D095, D096**,
mapping 1:1 onto the criterion's (a)/(b)/(c)/(d). Each entry carries Status/Decision/Why/
Consequences and cites the specific owner ruling behind it. Worth naming for the origin:

- **D093** records the Lane-1 deferral as a deferral — it states in its own text that it does not
  pre-approve Lane 1, so a later session cannot read the hexagon's existence as authorization.
- **D096** does the wording the owner delegated (R9). The redraw keeps D039's scheme and moves one
  boundary: host extends over 8093; hub's three **live** members are grandfathered on D039's own
  cheapness reasoning applied in reverse; a future hub service takes the next free 809x above 8092.
  Its honest cost is recorded rather than hidden — the boundary is now a lookup, not arithmetic.

## 3. Gantt (criterion 3)

`PLATFORM_GANTT.md` §2 gains **Wave 8 — "The Application Factory"**, a W0–W6 table in the Wave-7
row format: W0 ✅ done at this landing, W1–W6 ⬜ not started, pilot = `tutor`, gate **G-APP-1**.
W1 is marked **blocked on the owner's own go**, and W6 marked gated on W5 by D066.

## 4. Register (criterion 4)

§1 Host wing gains the `app-studio` row (**approved — awaiting bootstrap**), §3's scheme sentence
is rewritten per D096 with a boundary-redraw note, and **8093** + **5439** are registered as
**planned, not yet live**. A new as-of banner dates the register 2026-08-04 and states its scope
plainly: one hexagon's birth, **no fleet scan** — every other row is as of its own prior date.

## 5. Doc-sync (criterion 5)

It names all four decisions, calls out **D096 as the one that changes an operational fact people
may already have written down** ("host is 808x, hub is 809x" is no longer literally true), and
explicitly does **not** ask for an app-mission workflow page yet — that waits for the pilot.

# Fulfillment — launcher CORS allow-list for the dashboard console

## What we did

Added an explicit CORS allow-list to `server.js`'s `/api/*` routes, on
branch `demand/dashboard-cors` (commit `3a07df1`), pushed to
`origin/demand/dashboard-cors` (not merged to `main` — that's the owner's
call via PR review, per this repo's normal branch flow):

- `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` defaults to `http://localhost:4200`; overridable via
  the `LAUNCHER_CORS_ORIGINS` env var (comma-separated), never `*`.
- `OPTIONS` preflight is answered (204 + `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`/
  `-Headers`) on `/api/*` only.
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (+ `Vary: Origin`) is set only when the
  request's `Origin` header matches the allow-list; a non-matching origin
  gets no CORS headers at all (the request still completes for
  non-browser callers, it's just not readable cross-origin by a browser).
- `server.listen` still binds `127.0.0.1` only — untouched, zero new
  dependencies (Node built-ins only, unchanged).
- Documented in `README.md` (new "CORS" section), `HEXAGON.md` (inbound
  ports table gains the dashboard-console row), and `DEPLOYMENT.md`
  (security-posture note distinguishing CORS from the loopback bind).

## How it was verified

**Not against the live `:5055` instance** (owner's, must not be
touched/restarted). Copied `server.js` + `apps.json` + `public/` to a
scratch directory, changed only the copy's `PORT` constant to `5056`, ran
it in the background (output to a log file, under a timeout). Confirmed
with curl against `127.0.0.1:5056`:

1. `OPTIONS /api/sockets/theme-howl/start` with `Origin:
   http://localhost:4200` + `Access-Control-Request-Method: POST` → `204`
   with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:4200`,
   `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS`,
   `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type`, `Vary: Origin`.
2. `GET /api/sockets` with `Origin: http://localhost:4200` → `200` + the
   same allow headers, full socket list in the body.
3. `GET /api/sockets` with `Origin: http://localhost:9999` → `200`, body
   unchanged, but **no** `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers at all (criterion
   2 — no grant for a non-allow-listed origin).
4. The test instance itself was still bound `127.0.0.1:5056` only
   (`netstat`) — the loopback fix from an earlier session is unaffected.

Then killed the test process (`taskkill /PID ... /T /F`) and re-confirmed
via `netstat` that port `5056` had no `LISTENING` state left. The real
`:5055` instance (PID unrelated, owner's) was checked before and after and
was never started, stopped, or restarted by this session — it will pick
up this fix on its **next manual restart by the owner**.

## What the origin should know

- The running `:5055` instance predates this fix. WU-104's `/operate`
  screen will keep seeing CORS failures until the owner restarts launcher
  from this branch (or `main`, once merged).
- `LAUNCHER_CORS_ORIGINS` is the escape hatch if the console ever serves
  from a different origin than `http://localhost:4200` (e.g. the nginx
  container on a different port) — no code change needed, just set the
  env var before starting `server.js`.
- Not merged to `main` yet — branch `demand/dashboard-cors` is pushed and
  ready for review/merge at the owner's discretion.

# Fulfillment — launcher: fix D077 rebuild not applying + shared log ring

Checked current state before starting: the D077 feature (commit `81241f8`)
was live and its own fulfillment report said the `git pull` → `compose
build` → `compose up -d` success path had only been **code-reviewed, not
live-tested**, to avoid disrupting the shared running stack — so this
demand's symptom (rebuild "succeeds" but the image never changes) was
plausible and unverified, not something to assume already fixed. Confirmed
it live before touching any code (see "Root cause" below); this was a real,
reproducible bug on the owner's own running fleet, not a report artifact.

## Root cause (three distinct bugs, not one)

**1. Staleness false positives on unrelated commits (the demand's primary
symptom — state-feed/design-studio/publishing).** `isStale` compared a
component's Docker image build time against the owning repo's raw `main`
HEAD commit time. Every platform repo picked up a `.brain`-toolkit adoption
commit today (plus ongoing `PROGRESS.md`/demand-file churn each session) —
none of which touches anything a Java/Python service's Dockerfile actually
`COPY`s (`pom.xml`+`src`, `requirements.txt`+`src`). Confirmed directly:
`git diff --stat <runningCommit> <mainHead>` for `state-feed`, `publishing`,
and `design-studio` showed **only** `.brain/`, `.gitattributes`,
`.githooks/`, `AGENT.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `PROGRESS.md`, `demands/*.md` — zero
overlap with any COPY'd path. So `docker compose build` was doing exactly
the right thing: a 100%-cache-hit no-op, because there was truly nothing to
rebuild. Docker Desktop also reuses the original image ID (and its
`Created` timestamp) when a build's output is byte-identical to what's
already tagged — confirmed live: `state-feed`'s `imageBuiltAt` was still
`2026-07-23T04:22:05Z` a full 8 minutes after a `[rebuild state-feed exited
with code 0]` at `22:42:17`, past the 60s staleness-recheck interval. The
rebuild was never a no-op that got mistreated as success — it **was**
legitimately a no-op; the bug was that `isStale` had no way to know that and
kept the badge on forever, making a working rebuild look broken.

**2. `plantpal-backend` rebuild/start always failed outright (a separate,
concrete bug — not a staleness read).** Confirmed live: every rebuild
attempt exited **code 1**, log showing `failed to solve: pull access
denied ... contracts-m2` — Docker trying to *pull* an image named
`contracts-m2` from Docker Hub. Cause: `plantpal/docker-compose.yml`'s
`additional_contexts: contracts-m2: ${CONTRACTS_M2_0_15_0}` needs that env
var set in whatever process runs `docker compose`; `node server.js` had no
such var (confirmed: neither User nor Machine-scoped, and the logon
autostart path — `startup/launcher-startup.cmd` — never sets it), so it
resolved blank and Docker read the resulting bare string as a registry
image name. Compounding find: `apps.json`'s own `start`/`stop` commands for
`plantpal` were *also* exporting the wrong variable —
`CONTRACTS_M2_0_7_0` — stale since plantpal's contracts pin moved to
`0.15.0` (`DEPLOYMENT.md` documents `CONTRACTS_M2_0_15_0` as the current
name). So even a manual "flip the switch" `up -d --build` from the board
was silently building against a blank build-context, not just `rebuild`.

**3. Shared per-socket log ring (as the demand described).** Confirmed
live: `[rebuild state-feed exited with code 0]` was evicted from
`platform-stack`'s 200-line ring within minutes by the very next
component's rebuild (`hunyuan3d-worker`'s ML dependency install alone
produced hundreds of lines). A socket with several components rebuilding
around the same time had no way to read back what happened to any one of
them.

## What shipped (commit `af6ab9e` on `main`)

- **`server.js`** — `buildRelevantPaths()` parses a component's own
  Dockerfile `COPY`/`ADD` lines (skipping `--from=<stage>` copies) into a
  git pathspec; `gitMainBuildRelevantTime()` uses `git log -1 --format=%cI
  main -- <paths>` instead of raw `main` HEAD to decide `isStale`. A bare
  `COPY . .` (dashboard, plantpal-frontend) falls back to "everything under
  this component's own build-context directory" (not the whole repo, when
  `contextDir` names a subdirectory) — dashboard's context *is* the repo
  root, so it correctly keeps comparing against full `main` HEAD, and
  stayed `isStale: true` throughout (it has a real, unrelated, pending
  frontend diff — see "Not done" below). `rebuildSocket()` now merges a new
  socket-level `apps.json` field, `buildEnv`, into the spawned build's
  environment. Per-component build output now goes to its own ring
  (`appendComponentLog`/`rt.buildRings`, `GET
  /api/sockets/{id}/logs?component=<id>`); the shared ring keeps only the
  coarse `[rebuild issued]`/`[rebuild ... exited]` markers.
- **`apps.json`** — `platform-stack.buildEnv.M2_CONTRACTS_ROOT` and
  `plantpal.buildEnv.CONTRACTS_M2_0_15_0`, both pointed at the real local
  `.m2` paths (confirmed present on disk: `.../contracts/0.17.0`,
  `.../contracts/0.15.0`). Fixed `plantpal`'s `start`/`stop` commands'
  stale `CONTRACTS_M2_0_7_0` → `CONTRACTS_M2_0_15_0`. Added `contextDir` to
  the three components whose compose `build.context` isn't their repo root:
  `hunyuan3d-worker` (`workers/hunyuan3d`), `plantpal-backend` (`backend`),
  `plantpal-frontend` (`frontend`).
- **`public/index.html`** — a "Build log" button next to each stale
  component's "Rebuild + restart" button, opening the logs modal scoped to
  `?component=<id>`.
- **`README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`** updated to describe the corrected
  staleness comparison, the new `contextDir`/`buildEnv` fields, and the
  per-component log ring.

## Live verification (this session, against the real running fleet)

Restarted `:5055` (killed the specific PID on the port, started fresh via
`node server.js`, same as every prior session's convention) to pick up
`apps.json`/`server.js`. Immediately after restart, with **no rebuild
issued yet**:

| component | before (raw-HEAD compare) | after (build-relevant compare) |
|---|---|---|
| state-feed | stale | **not stale** |
| connector-gmail | stale | **not stale** |
| orchestrator | stale | **not stale** |
| sentinel-hub | stale | **not stale** |
| publishing | stale | **not stale** |
| design-studio | stale | **not stale** |
| plantpal-frontend | stale | **not stale** |
| dashboard | stale | still stale (real pending frontend diff) |
| gateway | stale | still stale (see "Not done") |

Then live-triggered a real rebuild end-to-end: **`plantpal-backend`** was
chosen because it had both a genuine pending Java diff (confirmed via `git
diff --stat` before touching anything: `backend/Dockerfile` +
`CompanionController`/`CompanionService`/tests changed) *and* was the exact
component bug #2 broke, so one rebuild verifies both fixes at once.
`POST /api/sockets/plantpal/rebuild {"component":"plantpal-backend"}` →
exited code **0** (previously: code 1, "pull access denied"); the
`contracts-m2` context step in the build log now shows `load from client`
succeeding, not an auth error. `docker inspect --format={{.Created}}
plantpal-backend` before: `2026-07-22T00:54:21Z`; after: **advanced** to
`2026-07-23T23:12:45Z`. Polled `GET /api/sockets` (no manual nudge) — on
the very next read, `plantpal-backend.isStale` flipped to **`false`**,
`runningCommit === mainHead`. Full end-to-end pass, exactly as the
acceptance criteria asked, just against `plantpal-backend` rather than a
platform-stack component — see "Not done" for why no platform-stack
component could stand in for this at the moment of testing.

Also exercised the per-component log ring live: `hunyuan3d-worker` (a real,
independently-pending Dockerfile change) and `gateway` were each rebuilt
through the new code; both produced full, uninterrupted build logs at their
own `?component=` URL while `platform-stack`'s shared ring kept only the
two components' coarse issue/exit markers, legible side by side — the
eviction problem observed pre-fix did not recur.

## plantpal — which bug, exactly (acceptance criterion #4)

**Not** the same root cause as platform-stack's non-applying rebuild, and
**not** a narrower staleness-recompute-timing issue either — a third,
distinct bug: `plantpal-backend`'s build was **hard-failing** (exit 1) on
every attempt, this whole time, on the missing/wrong `additional_contexts`
env var (bug #2 above). The owner's "seemed to work" read is explained by
what the log actually shows: a *failing* `build` step doesn't stop
`docker compose up -d <frontend>` from still recreating `plantpal-backend`
as a *dependency* container using whatever image already existed locally —
new container, fresh logs, restart-looking activity, but running the same
old image the whole time. `plantpal-frontend` was a different, narrower
case: its Dockerfile is `COPY . .` from the `frontend/` subdirectory, but
`apps.json` had no `contextDir` for it, so staleness fell back to comparing
against the **whole repo's** `main` HEAD (picking up unrelated `backend/`
and `.brain/` changes) instead of just `frontend/` — a real false positive,
fixed by adding `contextDir: "frontend"`; confirmed `plantpal-frontend`
flipped to `isStale: false` immediately after restart (zero real diff
under `frontend/` since the image was built).

## Not done / caveats

- **No platform-stack component could serve as the "real rebuild" example
  from the acceptance criteria's own suggestion (design-studio) at the
  moment of testing** — after the false-positive fix landed, `design-studio`
  (and every other previously-"stale" platform-stack component except
  `dashboard`/`gateway`) correctly reports `isStale: false`, because none
  of them has a real pending diff right now; forcing a rebuild there would
  only re-demonstrate the legitimate no-op case, not prove the fix.
  `dashboard` *does* have a real pending diff (this session confirmed
  `src/app/launcher/socket-summary.ts` etc., the dashboard-side D077
  consumption work) but its build fails on a pre-existing, unrelated
  esbuild/TypeScript resolution error in `src/app/treasury/
  cost-history.service.ts` (`import type { CostTickEvent } from
  '@platform/contracts'` unresolved) — a bug in `dashboard`'s own repo, out
  of scope here per this repo's standing rule against fixing sibling-repo
  bugs from the wrong session. `gateway` was rebuilt live (exit 0,
  container recreated) but turned out to be a **third** false-positive
  flavor this fix doesn't cover: its only commit touching `Dockerfile`/
  `Caddyfile` (`e02ffca`) is dated ~65 minutes *after* the image's build
  time, but the committed content is byte-identical to what's already
  built (the image was evidently built from the working tree just before
  that commit landed) — Docker correctly cache-hit it and preserved the
  original `2026-07-09` timestamp. Used `plantpal-backend` instead, which
  gave a strictly stronger proof (real content diff **and** the exact
  component bug #2 broke) — see "Live verification" above.
- **`gateway`'s pre-commit-build-timing false positive is not fixed by this
  session.** Narrower and rarer than bug #1 (needs a same-minute
  build-then-commit sequence) — noted, not chased further; would need
  comparing image *content* rather than commit timestamps to fully close,
  a bigger change than this demand's scope.
- **`dashboard`'s build failure is a real, separate bug in `dashboard`'s own
  repo** (unresolved `@platform/contracts` type-only import in
  `cost-history.service.ts`, `npm run build` exit 1) — not touched here,
  per the standing rule against cross-repo fixes; write-up left in this
  report for whoever owns `dashboard` next, not filed as a formal demand
  (out of this fulfillment's scope to raise).
- `:5056`'s observe-only container was not rebuilt this session (its
  `server.js` is baked in at image-build time) — same known gap the
  original D077 report already named; the container's own `stale`
  reporting was already inert before this fix (no git/Docker access there)
  and remains so, unaffected by anything shipped here.

# Fulfillment — launcher: git-based staleness detection + one-click rebuild (D077)

Checked current state before starting: the feature was **not yet built** —
`spec-launcher.md`'s own §9 build-note said so explicitly ("Implementation is
not yet built as of this spec amendment"), and a grep of `server.js`/
`apps.json`/`public/index.html` confirmed no `stale`/`rebuild` surface
existed. Built in full this session, commit `81241f8` on `main`.

## What shipped

- **`apps.json`**: `platform-stack` and `plantpal` (the two `type: compose`
  sockets with sibling repos launcher can actually read locally) gain a
  `components` array — one entry per buildable compose service (`id`,
  `label`, `repo`, `service`, `image`) — plus a socket-level `composeFile`.
  `platform-stack` carries 14 components (the 12 hexagons named in its
  description + `hunyuan3d-worker` + `design-studio`, matching
  `runtime/docker-compose.local.yml`'s actual service list, re-derived
  directly against that file rather than the socket's own slightly-stale
  description text). `plantpal` carries 2 (`plantpal-backend`,
  `plantpal-frontend`).
- **`server.js`** — staleness (git-based, per D077, not coordinator-based):
  - Per component, on its own 60s interval (separate from the 3s HTTP-probe
    poll — heavier, spawns `git`/`docker` per component): reads the owning
    repo's local `main` HEAD commit and its commit time
    (`git rev-parse main` / `git log -1 --format=%cI`, **no `git fetch`** —
    deliberately network-free so a staleness check can never block or fail
    launcher's own boot/poll loop on remote reachability, matching spec §6's
    zero-required-dependency property), and the running image's build time
    (`docker inspect --format={{.Created}} <image>`). `isStale` = image
    built strictly before `main`'s current HEAD commit. A best-effort
    `runningCommit` (nearest `main` commit not younger than the image's
    build time) is included for display, not used to decide `isStale`
    itself.
  - `GET /api/sockets` gains a per-socket `stale` object — **`null`** for
    every socket without tracked components (`heartbeat`, `theme-howl`,
    `theme-kasbah`, `agent-runner`, `observability`, `portfolio` — today's
    UI/any consumer sees these exactly as before), else
    `{ isStale, checkedAt, components: [{ id, label, isStale, runningCommit,
    mainHead, imageBuiltAt, checkedAt }] }`. Confirmed additive by direct
    test: `sockets.every(s => 'stale' in s)` true, no other field changed
    shape.
  - `POST /api/sockets/{id}/rebuild` (body `{"component": "<id>"}`, omissible
    only when the socket has exactly one component): runs
    `git pull` in the component's own repo, then
    `docker compose -f <composeFile> build <service>` and
    `... up -d <service>` in the socket's compose cwd, output captured in
    that socket's existing log ring (same `spawn`+`attachLogging` path
    `start`/`stop` already use). Guards, all live-tested against the running
    host instance: unknown socket → 404; socket with no components
    (`observability`) → 400; multi-component socket with no `component`
    given → 400 + the list of valid ids; unknown component id → 404.
  - `LAUNCHER_OBSERVE_ONLY=1` (the `:5056` container) returns 503 for
    `rebuild` — verified live after rebuilding that container's image (its
    `server.js` is baked in at build time, not volume-mounted, so it needed
    `docker compose up -d --build` to pick up this session's code; only
    `apps.json` is live-mounted). No `docker.sock` was added to it, same as
    before.
- **`public/index.html`**: a "stale — newer build on main" badge plus one
  "Rebuild + restart" button per stale component (disabled while a rebuild
  for that component is in flight or on the observe-only board). Verified
  served correctly from `:5055` (`grep` for the new markers in the served
  HTML).
- **`README.md`/`HEXAGON.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`** updated alongside the existing
  start/stop documentation.

## What the origin must know

- Live-tested against the real running platform stack (not a fixture): as
  of this session, `platform-stack`'s `state-feed` component genuinely *is*
  stale (image built 2026-07-23T04:22Z, `main` HEAD commit at
  2026-07-23T16:29Z) — this is a real, currently-true signal on the owner's
  own machine, not a synthetic test result. Both `plantpal` components also
  show stale (images from 2026-07-21/22, `main` has since moved). I did
  **not** click "rebuild" against these live components — the guard/error
  paths were verified directly, but the actual `git pull` → `compose build`
  → `compose up -d` success path was verified by code review only, to avoid
  disrupting the shared running stack mid-session. Recommend the owner
  trigger one rebuild by hand once ready, to confirm the full path
  end-to-end.
- The routing demand's own acceptance criteria also named a `dashboard`-side
  demand for consuming this `stale` object — that is `dashboard`'s own
  fulfillment, not this one; nothing in `dashboard`'s repo was touched here.
  Per README's existing CORS section, `dashboard` (`http://localhost:4200`)
  is already an allow-listed origin against the **host-native `:5055`**
  instance — that's the intended integration point (see next bullet for why
  the `:5056` container is a weaker source for this specific signal).

## Not done / caveats (named gaps, not silent ones)

- **Non-Compose (process-type) sockets excluded**: `heartbeat`,
  `theme-howl`, `theme-kasbah`, `agent-runner` get no staleness read in this
  pass. A Docker image gives a clean build-timestamp to compare against
  `main`; a plain `node`/`npm` process has no equivalent artifact — the
  closest analogue (comparing the process's start time against `main`'s
  HEAD commit time) is a real option but a shakier one (a process not
  started by launcher this session has no recorded start time; it was left
  out rather than shipping a heuristic that would misfire silently). A
  future session could add it as a process-restart action gated on that
  weaker signal.
- **`observability`'s only buildable service** (`headline-bridge`, compose
  context `../bridge`) **has no git repo at that path** (confirmed:
  `../bridge/.git` does not exist) — excluded from `components`, not
  silently. `observability`'s other four services are unmodified vendor
  images (Prometheus/Loki/Promtail/Grafana), correctly out of scope (no
  owning platform repo to compare against).
- **The `:5056` observe-only container's own `stale` reporting is inert**:
  it has neither the sibling repos' git checkouts nor Docker socket access
  (by the same design boundary that already blocks its `start`/`stop`), so
  every component there resolves through the "image not found locally"
  fallback and reports `isStale: false` — not "unknown," just always false.
  This is a real, minor UX gap for anyone looking at the `:5056` board
  directly (it will never show a stale badge, even when one is true) but
  does not affect the intended integration path, since the host instance
  (`:5055`) — which does have real git/Docker access — is the one
  `dashboard` is set up to poll (see above). Worth a follow-up if the owner
  ever wants the container board itself to show accurate badges (would need
  either the sibling repos bind-mounted read-only, matching `control-plane`/
  `demand-coordinator`'s existing `..:/platform:ro` pattern, or a
  read-only Docker socket mount — both are bigger boundary questions than
  this demand asked for, and out of scope here).
- **`runningCommit` is a best-effort approximation**, not an exact "which
  commit built this image" — no image label carries the true build commit
  today (this retrofit does not add one, to avoid touching 13+ sibling
  repos' own Dockerfiles, which is out of this repo's write scope
  regardless). It is the nearest `main` commit not younger than the image's
  build timestamp; `isStale` itself is decided on the timestamp comparison,
  not on this approximation, so a wrong `runningCommit` guess cannot flip a
  correct `isStale` verdict.

# Fulfillment — launcher: staleness off the running container, not the image tag

Checked current state before starting: `af6ab9e` (2026-07-23) had already
fixed the false-positive-on-unrelated-commits and rebuild-not-applying bugs,
and its own report explicitly named `gateway`'s timestamp-vs-content false
positive as **not fixed, out of scope**. Read `server.js`'s
`computeComponentStaleness` directly — confirmed it still called
`dockerImageCreatedAt(component.image)`, i.e. `docker inspect
<image-tag>`, never touching the running container at all. Neither half of
this demand had shipped; nothing to no-op on.

## Root cause

`isStale` compared `main` HEAD against `docker inspect <image-name>`'s
`Created` time — the image **tag**, not whatever container is actually
running. `docker compose build` retags `:latest` the moment a build
finishes, well before anyone runs `up -d` against it, so a built-but-never-
deployed image cleared the badge while the old container kept serving
traffic underneath it. Confirmed the shape of this live against the real
fleet (see the table below) before writing any fix.

## What shipped

**`server.js`**
- `composeContainerId(socket, component)` — resolves the actual running
  container via `docker compose -f <composeFile> ps -q <service>` (run from
  the socket's `cwd`, with `--env-file` when the socket declares one). Chosen
  over guessing a `<project>-<service>-1` container name because naming
  isn't uniform across the two composes here: `platform-stack` uses that
  default pattern, `plantpal` overrides `container_name` to the bare image
  name with **no** numeric suffix at all (confirmed live: `plantpal-backend`
  container, not `plantpal-backend-1`) — `compose ps` sidesteps the guess
  entirely.
- `dockerContainerImageId(containerId)` — `docker inspect
  --format={{.Image}}` on that container, giving its actual image **ID**
  (`sha256:...`), not a tag. That ID is what `dockerImageCreatedAt` (kept,
  unchanged) now inspects for `Created`.
- `computeComponentStaleness` rewritten to source `imageBuiltAt` off the
  container path above. No running container → `isStale: null` with an
  explicit `note`, not a silent fall-through to a tag comparison that no
  longer reflects anything running.
- `markComponentCurrent` / `staleOverrides` (new `stale-overrides.json`,
  gitignored) — the "mark current" resolution for the `gateway`-shaped
  false positive (see below). `POST /api/sockets/{id}/mark-current`, body
  `{"component": "<id>"}`; refuses (400) unless the component is currently,
  actually `isStale: true`.

**`apps.json`** — new `envFile` field on `platform-stack` (mirrors what its
existing `start`/`stop` commands already pass as `--env-file`), consumed by
the new `compose ps` call.

**`public/index.html`** — "Mark current" button next to a stale component's
"Rebuild + restart", with a confirm-dialog guard (the note it carries
explains it's for manually-verified-identical content only, not a shortcut
around a real rebuild).

**`README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`** — updated to describe the container-based
comparison, the `null`/no-container case, `envFile`, and `mark-current`.

## `gateway`'s standing false positive — which resolution, and why

Confirmed live it's exactly the scenario the demand describes: `gateway`'s
only commit ever touching `Dockerfile`/`Caddyfile` (`e02ffca`) is timestamped
`2026-07-09T04:59:08+01:00` (`03:59:08Z`), five minutes *after* the running
image's build time (`03:54:24Z`) — and since it's the *only* commit in
`gateway`'s history touching either file, the content is necessarily
identical to what's built (there's nothing else it could have been built
from). The timestamp compare has no way to distinguish "re-committed,
unchanged" from "genuinely rebuilt," so it lights forever with no rebuild
able to clear it — a no-op rebuild is a legitimate Docker cache-hit that
never advances `Created` either.

Considered the content-hash resolution the demand offers as the preferred
option: diff the tracked build paths' git blob hashes between `mainHead` and
the commit `gitCommitBefore` estimates was checked out at build time. Chose
**not** to ship that one — `gitCommitBefore` is explicitly documented in its
own comment as a display-only approximation ("nearest `main` commit not
younger than the image's build time," not what `isStale` is decided on).
Promoting that guess into the input for an actual staleness verdict risks a
confidently-wrong "not stale" on a component that guessed the wrong commit,
which is worse than a badge the owner already knows to double-check by hand.
Shipped the demand's other acceptable option instead: a one-click,
human-only "mark current" that records the exact `(mainHead, imageBuiltAt)`
pair verified, self-expiring the instant either value moves — a real new
commit or a real rebuild both invalidate it with no separate cleanup path.

## Live verification (this session, against the real running fleet, `:5055`)

Restarted the real daemon (killed the specific PID on `:5055`, started fresh
via `node server.js`, same convention as the prior two sessions) so the fix
is live, not just tested on a side port.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `plantpal` container naming isn't uniform | confirmed: `runtime-dashboard-1`/`runtime-gateway-1` (default pattern) vs. `plantpal-backend` (bare `container_name`, no suffix) — `compose ps -q` resolves both correctly, no name-guessing needed |
| `gateway` tag vs. running-container image | confirmed identical (`sha256:0811e451...`, built `2026-07-09T03:54:24Z`) both ways at time of testing — no tag/container drift live right now, so this component instead proved the *second* half of the fix (`mark-current`), not the tag-drift half |
| in-sync components read correctly off the container path | `dashboard`, `treasury`, `control-plane`, `demand-coordinator`, `media-generation`, `hunyuan3d-worker` all show `runningCommit === mainHead` (or a sensible non-match) with `imageBuiltAt` matching their container's actual image — confirms the container-read mechanism agrees with the tag in the normal case, no regression |
| no-running-container case | `plantpal-frontend` (socket off) → `isStale: null`, explicit note, correctly excluded from the UI's stale list; `plantpal-backend` (a container that genuinely is running) → compared normally, `isStale: true` (real, unrelated pending backend diff, unaffected by this fix) |
| `mark-current` end-to-end | `POST .../mark-current {"component":"dashboard"}` (not stale) → `400`, correct rejection. `POST .../mark-current {"component":"gateway"}` (stale) → `200`; immediate re-fetch: `isStale: false`, `note` naming the override; `stale-overrides.json` persisted the `(mainHead, imageBuiltAt, ackedAt)` triple; socket-level `isStale` flipped `true → false` |

**Not done:** did not trigger a real `docker compose build`+`up -d` this
session (mid-fix, avoided a multi-minute build against the owner's live
stack beyond what verifying this fix needed). The rebuild-then-recheck path
itself is unchanged — it already calls the same container-read function
proven above — and the prior session's `plantpal-backend` live rebuild
(`af6ab9e`'s own report) already exercised that exact call path end-to-end,
including the `imageBuiltAt` advance and automatic `isStale` flip. Left
`gateway`'s "mark current" override in place afterward (real, correctly
verified state — this repo's Dockerfile/Caddyfile content genuinely hasn't
drifted since `e02ffca`) rather than reverting it as test cleanup.
