# CORS allow-list for the console's Studio screen

## What changed

`media_generation/api.py` registered no middleware at all before this
change, so no browser origin — including the dashboard console at
`http://localhost:4200` — could read a response from this service: every
cross-origin `fetch()` from the console failed with `TypeError: Failed to
fetch` regardless of what the endpoint itself returned. Reproduced live
against the running (pre-fix) `runtime-media-generation-1` container before
touching any code (`GET /jobs` with `Origin: http://localhost:4200` returned
`200` with no `access-control-allow-origin` header), confirming the demand's
own finding rather than assuming it from source alone.

- **`src/media_generation/api.py`**: added `DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS =
  ("http://localhost:4200",)` and `parse_cors_origins(raw: str) -> list[str]`
  (comma-split, trim, drop-blank entries, de-dupe — blank/unset input yields
  an **empty** list, never a wildcard). `create_app()` gained a
  `cors_origins` parameter (default `DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS`) and now
  registers `fastapi.middleware.cors.CORSMiddleware` with
  `allow_origins=list(cors_origins)` (explicit allow-list, never `"*"`),
  `allow_methods=["GET", "POST"]` (`OPTIONS` preflight is handled by the
  middleware itself), `allow_headers=["*"]`. The real `__main__` block reads
  the origin list from `MEDIA_GENERATION_CORS_ORIGINS` (comma-separated,
  same default) through `parse_cors_origins()`, the same pattern every other
  env-sourced setting in that block already uses.
- This repo has no `config.py` (unlike sentinel-hub/orchestrator) — every
  other env-sourced setting here is assembled inline in `api.py`, so the new
  CORS constants/helper follow that existing local convention rather than
  introducing a new file shape this repo doesn't otherwise use. Function
  name and parsing semantics are otherwise identical to sentinel-hub's own
  `parse_cors_origins`, deliberately, for cross-repo grep-consistency.
- **Shape chosen: app-wide `CORSMiddleware`** (sentinel-hub's/orchestrator's
  precedent), not connector-gmail's route-scoped variant — this demand's own
  endpoint list carves out no route that must be walled off from the browser
  grant (unlike connector-gmail's `POST /invoke`). `GET
  /jobs/{id}/artifacts/{filename}` (the file download, deliberately absent
  from this demand's list because the console reaches it via `<a href
  download>`, a top-level navigation, not `fetch()`) ends up carrying the
  header too as a harmless side effect of app-wide middleware — inert for a
  navigation, since browsers only consult CORS headers for fetch/XHR-style
  requests. Stated explicitly per the demand's own ask to name the choice
  either way.
- Covers every route the demand lists: `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}`, `POST
  /jobs/{id}/cancel`, `POST /jobs/{id}/force-run`, `POST /queue/pause`,
  `POST /queue/resume`, `GET /jobs/{id}/artifacts`, `GET /health`. No new
  endpoint, no new action — D040 (loopback-bound service) is untouched, this
  only widens which browser origins may read a response from the same
  loopback-reachable service.
- **Minor heads-up on the demand text itself:** its "What we need" section
  says "Preflight (OPTIONS) must succeed for the two POST routes", but the
  endpoint list directly above it names *four* POST routes (cancel,
  force-run, pause, resume) — likely a copy-edit slip. Resolved by following
  the acceptance-criteria bullet instead, which is unambiguous ("the
  equivalent for every route listed above"): all four POST routes' preflights
  are tested and verified live below, not just two. Not a blocker, just
  worth a fix if this phrasing gets reused in a future demand.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_api.py`:
- `TestParseCorsOrigins` (4) — `parse_cors_origins` unit coverage: default
  value, comma-split + trim, blank-entry drop + dedupe, and the "blank input
  never becomes a wildcard" guarantee (empty list, not `["*"]`).
- `TestCorsGrant` (7) — `TestClient`-level, using the existing `client`
  fixture (which already builds its app with the real default
  `cors_origins`): `GET /jobs` and `GET /health` carry the grant for the
  console origin; a parametrized `OPTIONS` preflight check across all four
  console-reachable `POST` routes (`cancel`, `force-run`, `queue/pause`,
  `queue/resume`) asserting `200` + the allow-origin header; and a negative
  check proving a non-listed origin (`http://evil.example`) gets **no**
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header on the same route — confirms this is
  an allow-list, not a filter-out.

**Full suite result: 216 passed, 1 warning in 1.14s** (was 205 before this
change; the 1 warning is the pre-existing, unrelated
`StarletteDeprecationWarning` re: `httpx`/`starlette.testclient`, present
before this change too). `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q`.

## Live verification (container rebuilt)

The running container was rebuilt and recreated from this change — not just
approved on paper. Baseline captured first, against the still-running
pre-fix container:

```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8084/jobs -H "Origin: http://localhost:4200"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
(no access-control-allow-origin header present)
```

Rebuild + redeploy:
```
docker compose -f C:\Users\pc\Desktop\platform\runtime\docker-compose.local.yml build media-generation
docker compose -f C:\Users\pc\Desktop\platform\runtime\docker-compose.local.yml up -d --no-deps media-generation
```
Result: `Image runtime-media-generation Built` (cache hit on every layer
except the `src/` copy) → `Container runtime-media-generation-1 Recreated` →
`Started`. `--no-deps` left every other stack container (including its own
`media-generation-postgres` dependency, already running) untouched. Health
status `healthy` within ~2 seconds; `/health` `200` in the container's own
logs.

Live evidence captured against the rebuilt container on `http://127.0.0.1:8084`,
`Origin: http://localhost:4200`:

**`GET /jobs`** (actual request):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
vary: Origin
```

**`GET /jobs/{id}`** (actual request, unknown id — 404 still carries the grant):
```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
vary: Origin
```

**`OPTIONS /jobs/{id}/cancel`** (POST preflight):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
vary: Origin
access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST
access-control-max-age: 600
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
```

**`OPTIONS /jobs/{id}/force-run`** (POST preflight):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
vary: Origin
access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST
access-control-max-age: 600
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
```

**`OPTIONS /queue/pause`** (POST preflight):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
vary: Origin
access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST
access-control-max-age: 600
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
```

**`OPTIONS /queue/resume`** (POST preflight):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
vary: Origin
access-control-allow-methods: GET, POST
access-control-max-age: 600
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
```

**`GET /jobs/{id}/artifacts`** (actual request, unknown id — 404 still carries the grant):
```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
vary: Origin
```

**`GET /health`** (actual request):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200
vary: Origin
```

**Sanity check — disallowed origin** (`GET /jobs` with `Origin: http://evil.example`):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
(no access-control-allow-origin header present)
```
Confirms this is an explicit allow-list, not a wildcard/filter-out — an
unlisted origin still gets the response (loopback reachability is
unaffected, D040 is about network binding, not this) but no CORS grant, so a
browser will block script access to it.

## For dashboard's next session

- The console origin `http://localhost:4200` is now allow-listed on every
  endpoint the Studio screen needs: `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}`, `POST
  /jobs/{id}/cancel`, `POST /jobs/{id}/force-run`, `POST /queue/pause`,
  `POST /queue/resume`, `GET /jobs/{id}/artifacts`, `GET /health`. All
  preflights and actual requests verified live above, against the rebuilt
  container, not just tests.
- `GET /jobs/{id}/artifacts/{filename}` (the file download) was intentionally
  left out of this demand's list and out of live-verification above, exactly
  as the demand specified (top-level navigation, not subject to CORS) — it
  still incidentally carries the header as a side effect of app-wide
  middleware, but nothing depends on that.
- If the console is ever served from a different origin (different port,
  `https`, a different host), set `MEDIA_GENERATION_CORS_ORIGINS` on the
  media-generation container to a comma-separated list including that
  origin — no code change needed. There is no wildcard fallback by design.
- Service remains loopback-bound (`127.0.0.1:8084`, D040) — this change only
  affects which browser origins may read responses via CORS, not network
  reachability.
- Minor doc slip noticed in the demand text itself (see "What changed"
  above) — worth a fix at the source if this exact phrasing is reused for a
  future console-CORS demand to another repo.

# CORS allow-list for the console's Agents screen

## What changed

`src/api/app.ts` registered only `express.json()` before this session — no browser
origin, including the dashboard console at `http://localhost:4200` (the Agents
screen, WU-119: dispatchable panel, dispatch form, runs list + transcript tail,
stop), could read a response from this service: every cross-origin `fetch()` from
the console would fail with `TypeError: Failed to fetch` regardless of what the
endpoint itself returned. The demand's own finding was **source-only** (agent-runner
wasn't running that session, and the file was short/complete enough to be
conclusive on its own) — this session re-confirmed it live, against a real
ephemeral boot of this exact server, before touching any code (see "Live
verification" below), then fixed it and verified the fix the same way.

- **`src/config/env.ts`**: added `DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS: readonly string[] =
  ['http://localhost:4200']` and `parseCorsOrigins(raw: string): string[]`
  (comma-split, trim, drop-blank, dedupe — blank/unset input yields an **empty**
  list, never `['*']`). New `corsOrigins: string[]` field on `Config`, sourced from
  `AGENT_RUNNER_CORS_ORIGINS` through `parseCorsOrigins`, assembled in `loadConfig()`
  the same way every other env-sourced setting in this repo already is.
- **`src/api/app.ts`**: `createApp()` gained an optional third parameter
  `corsOrigins` (default `DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS`) and now registers the `cors` npm
  package app-wide, before every route: `cors({ origin: [...corsOrigins], methods:
  ['GET', 'POST'] })`. `allowedHeaders` is deliberately left unset so the package's
  own default (reflect back whatever the browser's preflight
  `Access-Control-Request-Headers` asked for) applies, rather than a hand-maintained
  or blanket header allow-list.
- **`src/index.ts`**: the real composition root now threads `config.corsOrigins`
  into `createApp`, exactly like every other config value.
- **This mirrors `media-generation`'s own `DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS`/
  `parse_cors_origins()`/`CORSMiddleware` shape conceptually** — same allow-list
  posture, same parse/dedupe semantics — ported to this repo's Express/TypeScript
  idiom. One deliberate divergence from where the helper lives: media-generation
  colocates its equivalent in `api.py` because it has no `config.py` of its own;
  this repo already has `env.ts`/`loadConfig` as the one place every other
  env-sourced setting is assembled, so `parseCorsOrigins`/`DEFAULT_CORS_ORIGINS`
  follow that existing local convention instead of introducing a new one.
- **Shape chosen: app-wide middleware**, not route-scoped — this demand's own
  endpoint list (`GET /dispatchable`, `POST /dispatch`, `GET /runs`, `GET
  /runs/{id}`, `POST /runs/{id}/stop`, `GET /health`) is already this entire API's
  full route surface, so there is no route left over that needs excluding from the
  browser grant.
- New dependency: `cors` (`^2.8.6`). Dev-only: `@types/cors`, `supertest`,
  `@types/supertest` (the last two per this task's own instruction to test the
  grant with `supertest` and a real `Origin` header, distinct from `app.test.ts`'s
  existing raw-`fetch` requests, which never set one).
- Covers every route the demand lists. No new endpoint, no new action — D040
  (loopback-bound service) is untouched; this only widens which browser origins may
  read a response from the same loopback-reachable service.

## Tests

Added `src/api/cors.test.ts`:
- **`agent-runner CORS grant`** (8, `supertest`-driven against the real `createApp`,
  not a hand-mocked req/res) — `GET /health`, `GET /runs`, `GET /dispatchable` carry
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:4200` for the allowed origin;
  `OPTIONS` preflight succeeds (204 + the grant + `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`
  containing `POST`) for both `POST /dispatch` and `POST /runs/:id/stop`; a
  disallowed origin (`http://evil.example`) gets **no** grant header on either a
  plain request or a preflight; a second configured origin can be added via the
  `corsOrigins` parameter without displacing the console default.
- **`parseCorsOrigins`** (4) — comma-split + trim, blank-entry drop + dedupe (first
  occurrence kept, order preserved), and the "blank/whitespace-only input never
  becomes a wildcard" guarantee (`[]`, not `['*']`).

**Full suite result: 119 total, 111 passed, 8 skipped (pending `DATABASE_URL`/
live-state-feed opt-in), 0 failures — up from the 107 baseline (99 passed + 8
skipped) confirmed at this session's own orientation.** `npx jest`, no warnings, no
leaked-handle notices. `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Live verification (real ephemeral boot — no standing redeploy exists)

Unlike `media-generation` (a long-running `runtime`-compose container that could be
rebuilt/recreated in place), agent-runner is host-native and was **not running**
this session, per the demand's own note. Rather than stop at the test suite, this
session booted a real instance of this exact server on a scratch port, verified the
genuine pre-fix baseline, applied the fix, verified again, then tore everything
down.

**Setup:** a throwaway `postgres:16-alpine` container was needed only because
`main()`'s `PostgresLedger.init()` requires a reachable database at startup — no
other config in this task's path (coordinator/state-feed/Kafka URLs) is ever
dialed for a plain CORS check. Before starting one, a `docker ps -a` check
surfaced a container already running under the exact name/port DEPLOYMENT.md's own
prerequisites section documents as an example (`agent-runner-postgres`, port
5437) — genuinely started by something other than this session partway through it
(absent from this session's own first `docker ps -a` at orientation; confirmed
recent via `docker inspect`'s `StartedAt` cross-checked against the verification
server's own real `Date` response header). Left it completely untouched and used
an isolated, differently-named/ported throwaway container instead
(`agent-runner-cors-verify-pg`, port 5555) so this verification could not interfere

**Before (genuine pre-fix baseline):** `git stash` reverted the working tree to

  reachability.

# Fulfillment — reconcile orphaned `launched` runs on startup

## Current-state check (before writing anything)

Checked whether this capability already existed before doing any work, per this
task's own instruction. It did not: `RunManager` had no `reconcile`/`orphan`
method, `src/index.ts`'s `main()` never revisited ledger state after
`ledger.init()`, and a grep for `reconcil|orphan` across `src/` only turned up
unrelated Windows-process-tree-orphan comments in `processSupervisor.ts` /
`windowsProcessRunner.ts` (a different concern — child-process trees, not
ledger rows). `RunManager.activeRuns` is a plain in-memory `Map`, populated
only by `dispatch()` calls made *within the current process* — so a run left
`state: 'launched'` by a process instance that crashed or was killed had no
path back out of `launched`; nothing else in the codebase ever revisited that
state. This was a real gap, not already-shipped work.

## What shipped

- **`src/domain/runManager.ts`**: new `RunManager.reconcileOrphans()`. Lists
  the ledger; any row still `state: 'launched'` that is not tracked in this
  instance's `activeRuns` is finalized to `failed` (sets `endedAt`, `exitCode:
  null`, an explanatory `error` string) via the same `emitTerminal()` path a
  normal failure uses — so it emits both the terminal `agent.run` state-event
  and a `usage.event`, keeping downstream consumers (state-feed, Kafka usage
  sink) consistent with every other terminal transition.
- **`src/index.ts`**: calls `runManager.reconcileOrphans()` once at startup,
  immediately after `RunManager` construction and before `app.listen()` — so
  reconciliation completes before the process accepts new dispatches. Logs
  the reconciled count when non-zero.
- **`src/domain/runManager.test.ts`**: four new tests under a
  `RunManager -- orphaned-run reconciliation` block:
  1. a `launched` row seeded directly into the ledger (simulating a prior
     process instance that died mid-run) is reconciled to `failed`, with the
     ledger update, the returned record, the state-feed emission, and the
     usage-event emission all asserted.
  2. a run dispatched *within the same manager instance* — still
     `state: 'launched'` but tracked in `activeRuns` — is left untouched
     (proves the check is "not in this process's active set", not merely
     "state is launched").
  3. an already-terminal (`finished`) row is left alone.
  4. `reconcileOrphans()` on a clean ledger returns `[]`.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: `[Unreleased]` entry.

## What the origin (dashboard) must know

- No new HTTP surface — reconciliation is a startup-only internal step, not a
  route. Existing `GET /runs` / `GET /runs/{id}` will simply show any
  previously-`launched`, now-restart-orphaned row as `failed` with
  `error: "orphaned: no supervising process for this run in the current
  service instance (reconciled at startup)"` the next time agent-runner boots
  after such a row exists.
- This only fires **on startup**, not on every `stop()` call (the demand's
  capability line said "on startup (or on stop)" — startup was the natural
  fit here: `activeRuns` is only ever empty at boot, and `stop()` already has
  its own defined behavior for unknown/already-terminal ids). If a future
  need surfaces for reconciling mid-run (e.g. a periodic sweep), that would
  be new scope, not implied by this report.
- `tokensUsed`/`tokensIn`/`tokensOut`/`model` are left as whatever the
  orphaned row already had (typically `undefined`, since the process died
  before the CLI's terminal `result` line was ever parsed) — the `usage.event`
  emitted for a reconciled run will carry no token counts. Worth knowing if
  the dashboard's usage aggregation expects every terminal event to carry
  them.

## Tests

`npx jest src/domain/runManager.test.ts`: 33/33 passed (29 pre-existing + 4
new). `npm run typecheck`: clean. Full suite (`npx jest`): 201 passed, 8
skipped (pre-existing `DATABASE_URL`-gated Postgres-ledger/`httpStateFeedSink`
integration tests, expected to self-skip), 0 failures — no regressions against
the pre-existing baseline.

## Not done / caveats

- Not exercised against the real `PostgresLedger` (only `InMemoryLedger`, per
  this repo's existing test convention) — `reconcileOrphans()` uses only
  `LedgerPort.list()`/`.update()`, the same interface every other `RunManager`
  path already relies on and which `postgresLedger.integration.test.ts`
  already covers generically; no `PostgresLedger`-specific behavior was added.
- No live-process kill-and-restart demonstration was performed (would require
  standing up a real Postgres + a real `claude` dispatch + killing the Node
  process mid-run) — verified via unit tests seeding the ledger directly,
  which exercises the exact same code path (`ledger.list()` returning a
  `launched` row not in a fresh `activeRuns`) a real restart would produce.

# Fulfillment — `GET /brain/:repo/pending-audit` read-time enrichment

## Current-state check (before writing anything)

Checked whether this capability already existed before doing any work, per
this task's own instruction. It did not: `GET /:repo/pending-audit`
(`src/api/brainRoutes.ts`) already served the real, parsed sample via
`parsePendingAudit` (`src/domain/brain.ts`), but every item's `context` field
was the raw (present-but-blank) value from the file itself — no unit title,
no unit body, no session task/date, no cited excerpt. This was a real gap,
not already-shipped work; there was also a session file already opened for
this exact demand by agent-runner's own dispatch supervisor (`launch:
supervised`), status `partial`, with no actual work logged yet — this session
picked that dispatch up and did the work.

## What shipped

- **`src/domain/brain.ts`**: new `enrichPendingAudit(parsed, repoPath)`.
  For each parsed item, reads and frontmatter/body-splits the cited session
  file (`.brain/sessions/<sessionId>.md`) and knowledge unit file
  (`.brain/knowledge/<unitId>.md`) under `repoPath`, and adds:
  - `unitTitle` — the unit's `title:` frontmatter value, verbatim.
  - `unitBody` — the unit's full body (everything after its frontmatter), trimmed.
  - `sessionTask` — the session's `task:` frontmatter value, verbatim.
  - `sessionDate` — the `YYYY-MM-DD` date portion of the session's `started:` frontmatter value.
  - `citedText` — for `line_ref: log:N`, the cited log line plus up to 2 lines
    of surrounding log text either side, joined with `\n`; for
    `line_ref: decision:D-id`, that decision's full `text:` from the
    session's `decisions:` frontmatter list, unquoted.

  Every failure mode (missing session id/unit id, missing session/unit file,
  unparseable `lineRef`, out-of-range log index, unknown decision id) returns
  explicit `null` on the affected field(s) — the item is always still
  returned, never dropped, never a thrown exception.

  **`log:N` mapping — how it was derived.** `.brain/bin/structurer` in this
  checkout is a thin pinned shim onto the `brain-toolkit` repo (not present
  in this environment), so the real line_ref-generation source wasn't
  readable locally. The mapping was reverse-derived empirically instead:
  grepped each of the 5 real `log:N` citations in the live `pending-audit.md`
  against the exact line their cited K-id actually appears on, across the 2
  real session files those citations point at. All 5 data points agree
  exactly on one rule: `log:N` indexes directly (0-indexed) into the same
  `bodyLines` array `brainSupervisor.ts`'s own `parseFrontmatter` already
  produces (`bodyLines[0]` = the first line immediately after the closing
  `---`) — i.e. `bodyLines[N]` is the cited line, not a conventional
  1-indexed line count. This was verified exact (not off-by-one) against raw
  file content before any code was written against it, and is pinned by a
  live-verification test (below) that will fail loudly if this convention
  ever turns out to differ from what a future structurer run actually
  produces.

- **`src/api/brainRoutes.ts`**: `GET /:repo/pending-audit` now calls
  `enrichPendingAudit(parsePendingAudit(text), repoPath)` before responding.
  No change to `withBrainRepo`'s existing `{repo}` path-traversal / `.brain`-
  enablement guard. The handler still only ever reads
  `.brain/derived/pending-audit.md`, `.brain/sessions/*`, and
  `.brain/knowledge/*` — `pending-audit.md` itself is never rewritten (a
  route-level test asserts the file is byte-identical before/after a
  request).

- **`src/domain/brain.test.ts`**: unit tests against synthetic temp-dir
  fixtures — happy path, context-window clamping near the start of a body,
  out-of-range log index, unrecognized/null `lineRef`, unknown decision id,
  missing session file (unit fields still resolve), missing unit file
  (session fields still resolve), null session/unit ids (never throws) — plus
  a **live-verification suite** that reads this repo's own real, committed
  `.brain/derived/pending-audit.md` (the actual 9-item queue named in the
  demand) and asserts every item resolves with no unexpected nulls, with a
  direct raw-file cross-check on item 1's `log:46` -> real file line 87
  resolution.

- **`src/api/brainRoutes.test.ts`**: one route-level enrichment test (fixture
  session + unit under the temp platform root) and one not-found-citation
  test asserting explicit nulls and a `200`, never a `500`.

- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Response shape (for dashboard to consume without reading source)

`GET /brain/{repo}/pending-audit` — unchanged envelope, each item in `items[]`
gains 5 new fields alongside the existing ones:

```jsonc
{
  "exists": true,
  "generatedAt": "2026-07-21T16:28:51+01:00",
  "filledCount": 0,
  "totalCount": 9,
  "items": [
    {
      // -- unchanged, from the raw pending-audit.md sample --
      "sessionId": "2026-07-21_1505_wave-7-c-3-structurer-appid-bug-fix-ai-g",
      "unitId": "K-0096",
      "lineRef": "log:46",
      "tier": "3",
      "classifierClass": "applied",
      "context": "",       // present-but-blank in the real, unfilled sample
      "humanClass": "",    // present-but-blank in the real, unfilled sample

      // -- NEW: read-time enrichment --
      "unitTitle": "The v0.6 session schema (§6.1) actually dropped context_used/context_loaded",
      "unitBody": "\"The v0.6 session schema (§6.1) actually dropped context_used/context_loaded",
      "sessionTask": "Wave 7 C-3: structurer appId bug fix, ai-gateway 502 demand, W8 supervised-path build (v0.6 section 8.1)",
      "sessionDate": "2026-07-21",
      "citedText": "`FrontmatterDoc` algorithm byte-for-byte (same top-level-key regex, same\n`_yaml_quote`/`_unquote` escaping) so a file this module writes and a file\n`bin/brain` writes obey the identical rule in two languages -- **K-0096**\n(v0.6 schema dropped `context_used`/`context_loaded`) informed the exact\nfield set emitted (no dead fields reintroduced), and the platform's own"
    }
  ]
}
```

Field notes for the dashboard:

- All 5 new fields are **item-level, `string | null`** — never omitted, never
  an empty-string stand-in for "unavailable" (that convention is reserved for
  `context`/`humanClass`, which mean something different: "present but not
  yet filled in"). `null` on any of the 5 new fields means: session/unit id
  was null, the referenced file doesn't exist, or (for `citedText` only) the
  `lineRef` didn't parse / the index was out of range / the decision id
  wasn't found in that session's `decisions:` list. Render an explicit
  "context unavailable" state for `null`, per this demand's own companion
  acceptance criteria on the dashboard side — never a blank cell.
- `citedText` for a `log:N` ref can be shorter than 5 lines if `N` is near
  the very start of the session's `## Log` section (context clamps, it never
  goes negative or wraps).
- `unitBody`/`citedText` can be arbitrarily long (some knowledge-unit bodies
  and log excerpts run to several hundred characters) — this demand's
  companion dashboard acceptance criteria already calls for
  expandable/collapsible rendering, not truncation on this side; nothing here
  truncates.
- Ground truth for this exact shape is `agent-runner`'s own real, live
  `.brain/derived/pending-audit.md` (9 items, `generatedAt
  2026-07-21T16:28:51+01:00`) — `GET :8089/brain/agent-runner/pending-audit`
  against a running instance of this service returns it directly; no fixture
  file needed to see the real shape.

## Tests

`npx jest src/domain/brain.test.ts src/api/brainRoutes.test.ts`: 51/51
passed. Full suite (`npm test`): 220 passed, 8 pre-existing skips (Postgres-
ledger / `httpStateFeedSink` integration tests, self-skip without
`DATABASE_URL`), 0 failures — no regressions. `npm run typecheck`: clean.

## Not done / caveats

- The `log:N` -> line mapping is an empirical reverse-derivation (5 real data
  points, 2 real files, all in exact agreement), not a read of
  `brain-toolkit`'s own generation source, which isn't checked out in this
  environment. If `brain-toolkit`'s structurer's numbering convention is ever
  changed there, this repo's enrichment would silently start mis-resolving
  `log:N` refs until this repo's own live-verification test is re-run and
  caught it (it reads the real, live `pending-audit.md` and its real cited
  session files every test run, so it would fail the next time this repo's
  CI/tests run against updated real data, not silently).
- No new HTTP surface, no schema/route change beyond the 5 additive fields —
  a dashboard client that ignores unknown JSON fields today needs no changes
  to keep working; it only needs to change to actually *use* the new fields.

# Fulfillment — prompt delivered on stdin, not argv (ENAMETOOLONG at ~32 KB)

## Checked first

**Not previously shipped.** At session start `buildArgv` still emitted the
prompt as `argv[2]` (`claude -p <prompt> …`), and `windowsProcessRunner.ts:89`
still carried the unconditional `child.stdin?.end()` under the comment *"Never
used — the claude invocation passes its prompt as an argument."* Both were
exactly as the demand describes. Built this session.

(The supervisor-opened `.brain` session file for this session's own launch
existed with `changes: []`, `status: partial` — no code had landed.)

## Baseline (pre-work), as required

`npm test` before any edit:

```
Test Suites: 1 failed, 2 skipped, 19 passed, 20 of 22 total
Tests:       2 failed, 8 skipped, 294 passed, 304 total
```

The 2 failures are both in `src/domain/brain.test.ts`
(`enrichPendingAudit`, live-corpus drift — the test pins a specific
`sessionId`/excerpt from this repo's own growing `.brain` corpus, which has moved
on). **Pre-existing and unrelated to this demand**; untouched by this work.

## Root cause

Windows' `CreateProcess` caps an *entire* command line at 32767 characters. The
argv this repo built was perfectly well-formed — the OS is what refused it — so
the failure surfaced as `spawn ENAMETOOLONG` in ~58 ms, before `claude` ever
started. **No `buildArgv` unit test could have caught it**, which is precisely
why the demand's acceptance bar rules out a `buildArgv`-only fix.

## What shipped

### 1. The prompt goes on stdin

`claude -p` with **no positional prompt** reads the prompt from stdin. This was
not assumed — it was verified against the real binary before writing any code:

```
$ echo 'Reply with exactly: STDIN_OK' | claude.exe -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --model claude-sonnet-5
…{"type":"result",…,"result":"STDIN_OK"…}
```

So `buildArgv(executable, permissionArgs, model, effort)` — the `prompt`
parameter is **gone** — emits `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose
<permissionArgs> [--model …] [--effort …]`, a command line under 200 characters
at any prompt size. `runWindowsProcess` gained an optional `RunOptions.stdin`,
and `ProcessSupervisor.spawn` passes `args.prompt` through it. stdin has no size
cap and needs no escaping, quoting or encoding of any kind.

### 2. The stale comment and the code were corrected together

The comment asserting "never used / passed as an argument" is gone, replaced by
one describing what the code now actually does and *why* (the ENAMETOOLONG
history, so the next reader doesn't "simplify" it back). The demand is right that
a comment asserting the opposite of its code is its own defect — it is what made
the argv path look deliberate.

### 3. The fast-fail property that comment protected is preserved

stdin is still closed the instant the prompt has been written (`stdin.end(input)`
— a single write-and-close), and still closed *immediately* when there is no
`stdin` option at all. A CLI that unexpectedly wants **more** input therefore
still hits EOF rather than hanging to the wall-clock timeout. Both halves are
tested — with stdin and without — against a child process that exits *only* on
stdin EOF, asserting it finishes well inside its 30 s budget.

### 4. Delivery failure names the size and the limit

New `ProcessInputError`:

```
Failed to deliver 61440 bytes of input to the process's stdin (input is passed on
stdin rather than as a command-line argument precisely because Windows caps an
entire command line at 32767 characters): <cause>
```

One deliberate non-escalation: a child that **ignores** stdin and exits (write
fails with `EPIPE`, or `EOF` on Windows named pipes — observed, not assumed, from
`cmd.exe /c echo` with a 200 KB write — or a destroyed stream) is *not* reported
as an input failure. That is the child's story to tell through its own exit code
and stderr; surfacing it as a delivery error would mask the real cause.

### 5. The live gate — the criterion that actually matters

`src/adapters/promptDelivery.live.test.ts` drives the **real** `claude.exe`
2.1.220 through the **real** `ProcessSupervisor`. Not a fake, not a stand-in, not
a unit test over `buildArgv` (K-0049's lesson from the chunk-3 gate: a live gate
claiming a real capability must assert a real effect).

- **60 KB prompt.** 1200 filler paragraphs with the actual instruction placed at
  the **very end** — the session can only produce the expected marker if the
  *whole* prompt arrived, not a truncated prefix. Asserts `exitCode 0`,
  `timedOut false`, a normal parseable stream-json transcript, and the marker in
  the transcript's own `result`.
- **Byte fidelity.** A second real run whose prompt carries newlines, single and
  double quotes, backslashes (including a literal `\n` two-character sequence),
  non-ASCII (`é ü 日本語 → ✓`) and a trailing newline, echoed back by the session
  and compared against what was sent.

Both passed against the real CLI:

```
$ AGENT_RUNNER_LIVE_CLAUDE=1 npx jest promptDelivery.live
Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total
Tests:       2 passed, 2 total
```

It **self-skips** unless `AGENT_RUNNER_LIVE_CLAUDE` is set — same posture as
`postgresLedger.integration.test.ts` — so `npm test` stays green and free on a
machine with no `claude` install, credentials or network. It spends real tokens;
`DEPLOYMENT.md` documents how and when to run it.

### 6. Scope held

`ProcessPort` / `SpawnArgs`, `RunManager`, the HTTP surface and the contracts pin
are **unchanged** — verified, not just intended: no file under `src/domain/ports/`,
`src/api/`, `src/domain/runManager.ts` or `package.json`'s contracts dependency was
touched. This is an adapter-level fix. `buildArgv`'s signature changed, but it is
internal to `processSupervisor.ts` and its own test file.

## Suite status

```
Test Suites: 1 failed, 3 skipped, 19 passed, 20 of 23 total
```

# Fulfillment — per-dispatch model + reasoning-effort selector on `agent-runner`

## What shipped

**Checked first:** confirmed via `git log`/source read that no prior session had
started this (an untracked, unfinished `.brain` session file existed from a
supervisor launch earlier the same day, `changes: []`, `status: partial` — no code
had actually landed). Built from scratch this session.

`POST /dispatch` now accepts optional `model` and `effort` string fields. When
either is omitted, the dispatched Claude Code session falls back to the configured
default — **now Opus 5 / effort `low`**, replacing the prior hardcoded Sonnet-5-only
cap (D059).

- `src/config/env.ts` — `DEFAULT_MODEL` changed `'sonnet'` → `'opus'`; new
  `DEFAULT_EFFORT = 'low'`, `VALID_EFFORT_LEVELS = ['low','medium','high','xhigh',
  'max']` (verified against the real installed `claude.exe` v2.1.210's own
  `--effort <level>` enum, not assumed), `parseEffortArg`, `Config.effort` — same
  `??`-fires-only-on-unset / explicit-empty-string-escape-hatch shape
  `AGENT_RUNNER_MODEL` already established.
- `src/domain/ports/processPort.ts` — `SpawnArgs` gains optional `model?`/`effort?`:
  `undefined` = "use the supervisor's configured default", any explicit value
  (including `''`) overrides it for that one dispatch.
- `src/adapters/processSupervisor.ts` — constructor now takes `defaultModel` +
  `defaultEffort` (was `model` only); new exported `resolveOverride(perCall,
  configDefault)` performs the unset-vs-explicit-value resolution, unit-tested
  directly; `buildArgv` now also appends `--effort <level>` after `--model`, same
  empty-string-means-no-flag-at-all rule.
- `src/domain/run.ts` / `runManager.ts` — `DispatchInput.model?`/`.effort?`, threaded
  straight through to `ProcessPort.spawn`, no domain logic in between.
- `src/api/app.ts` — `POST /dispatch` accepts `model`/`effort`; `effort` is
  validated against `VALID_EFFORT_LEVELS` (or `''`) and rejected with 400 **before**
  a ledger row or process exists for anything else — a typo'd effort level fails
  fast, not after a run has already launched and burned the concurrency-cap slot.
- `src/index.ts` — composition root threads `config.effort` into `ProcessSupervisor`
  alongside `config.model`.
- `DEPLOYMENT.md` — `AGENT_RUNNER_MODEL`/`AGENT_RUNNER_EFFORT` documented in the
  environment-variable table (the former was, on inspection, never documented at
  all prior to this session — added now alongside its new sibling).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` entry recording the full shape of this change.
- Tests: +19 across `processSupervisor.test.ts` (pure `buildArgv`/`resolveOverride`/
  config-threading), `runManager.test.ts` (domain-level override threading, both the
  explicit-value and explicit-empty-string paths), `app.test.ts` (HTTP-level
  acceptance + the 400 validation path). Full suite: 290 tests, 288 passing — the 2
  failures are pre-existing, unrelated `.brain` corpus-drift assertions in
  `src/domain/brain.test.ts` (a live pending-audit item count/session-id the test
  hardcodes, which the corpus has since moved past; untouched by this session's
  diff, confirmed via `git diff --stat`). `npm run typecheck` clean.

## What the origin must know

This demand's other two acceptance criteria are **outside `agent-runner`'s write
boundary** (D048 standing invariant: this repo never writes to another repo) and
were raised as sibling demands instead of attempted here:

- **Dashboard Agents-screen (WU-119) model/effort form fields** — raised to
  `dashboard`: `agent-runner-20260728-dashboard-model-effort-dispatch-form`. The API
  contract it needs to build against (field names, defaults, the enum, the
  escape-hatch semantics) is shipped and documented above.
- **platform-vault decision entry amending D059** — raised to `platform-vault`:
  `agent-runner-20260728-platform-vault-d059-model-effort-amendment`. Cites this
  demand and this report per the coordinator's own envelope convention.

The origin's join across all three targets (`agent-runner`, `dashboard`,
`platform-vault`) won't reach `pending-approval` until those two sibling demands
also report back — this repo's own leg is complete and is not what's still open.

## Not done / caveats

- No ledger/`RunRecord` persistence of the *requested* `model`/`effort` was added —
  only the *actually-reported* `model` (parsed from the CLI's own JSON output,
  pre-existing field) is persisted. The acceptance criteria didn't ask for
  request-side persistence, and adding it would touch the Postgres schema
  (`postgresLedger.ts`) for a field nothing downstream currently reads; flagged
  rather than silently added as unscoped surface, not because it's a gap in the
  stated criteria.
- `effort` validation happens only at the `POST /dispatch` HTTP layer, not inside
  `RunManager`/`ProcessSupervisor` — an internal caller that bypasses the HTTP layer
  (none exist today) could still pass an invalid effort straight to `buildArgv`,
  which would pass it to the CLI unvalidated. Matches the existing precedent: `model`
  itself has never been validated at any layer (arbitrary alias/full name, no fixed
  enum), so this isn't a new inconsistency, just an explicit note that `effort`'s
  validation is HTTP-boundary-only by design (spec's own "validate at system
  boundaries" convention).

# Fulfillment — dispatched agent's answer content reachable from `GET /runs/{id}`

## What shipped

Two of the demand's four candidates, combined — **(a)** `transcriptTail` now
always populates (no longer gated behind `?tail=`), and **(b)** a new
dedicated `result` field carries the agent's own final answer text. Neither
candidate (c) (an alternate path form) nor (d) (a dedicated endpoint) was
built: (a)+(b) already satisfy every acceptance criterion without a
consumer ever touching agent-runner's filesystem, which is the cleaner
hexagonal boundary (D007) the demand itself recommended leaning toward.

### The API contract design-studio should build against

`GET /runs/{id}` (unchanged path, unchanged for 404/other existing fields)
now **always** includes, regardless of whether `?tail=` is present:

```json
{
  "...(all pre-existing fields, unchanged)...": "...",
  "transcriptTail": ["<line>", "..."],
  "result": "All four contracts schemas are confirmed... (the agent's own answer text)" ,
  "resultTruncated": false
}
```

- **`transcriptTail: string[]`** — the trailing `N` non-empty lines of the
  transcript file, **line-based** (never byte-based). Default `N = 100`
  (unchanged constant, `DEFAULT_TAIL_LINES`); `?tail=N` still overrides it,
  same as before this fix. The only behavior change: this field used to be
  **absent entirely** unless `?tail=` was present in the query string — it is
  now present on every `GET /runs/{id}` response, `[]` if the transcript
  file doesn't exist (yet, or ever).
- **`result: string | null`** — new field. The `result` field of the
  transcript's terminal `{"type":"result",...}` JSONL record (the `claude`
  CLI's `--output-format stream-json` emits exactly one such record, always
  last, once a run reaches a terminal state). `null` while the run is still
  `launched` (no such record written yet) or if the transcript file is
  missing/unreadable — this never 500s, never throws.
- **`resultTruncated: boolean`** — new field, `true` iff `result` was cut at
  a 20,000-character cap (`... [truncated]` appended in that case). Guards
  against a pathological answer ever ballooning a status response the way
  returning the whole transcript file would (the W16 transcript itself is
  593,494 bytes; its answer text is 5,972 characters — comfortably under the
  cap in the one real case inspected).

design-studio's own `AgentRunnerPort.transcript_tail`/`HttpAgentRunner`
mapping (`data.get("transcriptTail")`) is satisfied as-is by this change —
no port/adapter rename needed on your side for that field. **A new field
this repo's dataclass does not yet have: add `result: str | None` (mapped
from `data.get("result")`) to `RunRecord` and `_record_from_json` if you
want the clean answer text — `InterviewService` should prefer `result` over
parsing `transcript_tail` for the answer**, since `transcript_tail` is raw
JSONL lines (each one still a full JSON object, `result`'s own line
included, mixed with system/assistant/user event lines), not extracted
answer text.

### The tail-vs-byte question the demand asked us to answer explicitly

**Line-based tail, verified safe against the real transcript, not assumed.**
Loaded `transcripts/0623ba6e-6414-4187-b5da-f0f847a0e01d.ndjson` directly
(303 lines, 593,494 bytes) and inspected the terminal record: `result` (the
answer, 5,972 characters) starts at byte offset 202 of that record's 7,522
total bytes; the trailing `usage`/`total_cost_usd`/`modelUsage` block starts
only at byte offset 6,385 — **after** `result`, not before. A byte-limited
tail with a small budget (e.g. "last 2,000 bytes") would land inside that
trailing metadata block and miss the answer text entirely — exactly the
failure mode the demand flagged as a live risk.

`readTranscriptTail`/`readTranscriptSnapshot` (`src/api/transcript.ts`) are
and always were **line-based**: `content.split('\n')`, never a byte slice.
Because `--output-format stream-json` never splits one JSON object across
multiple lines, a line-based tail of `N >= 1` is guaranteed to include the
complete terminal record — answer text and all — whenever a run has reached
a terminal state and produced a result event. This guarantee is stated here
explicitly and covered by a dedicated test
(`src/api/transcript.test.ts`, "extracts the terminal result field even
with a large usage/cost block after it on the same line") that reconstructs
the real record shape (result before a deliberately bulky trailing `usage`
block) and asserts the full, untruncated answer is returned.

We did not stop at "tail happens to be safe" — we also added the dedicated
`result` field (candidate b) precisely so a consumer never has to reason
about JSONL structure, line ordering, or field position within a line at
all to get the answer. `result` is extracted server-side by scanning
backward from the end of the transcript for the terminal
`{"type":"result",...}` record and returning its own `result` field
directly (`extractResult()` in `src/api/transcript.ts`) — no client-side
JSON-parsing-a-JSONL-line-then-JSON-parsing-again required.

### Files changed

- `src/api/transcript.ts` — `readTranscriptTail` kept (line-based, unchanged
  behavior); added `readTranscriptSnapshot()` (one file read, returns both
  `tail` and the extracted `result`/`resultTruncated`) and its internal
  `extractResult()` helper.
- `src/api/app.ts` — `GET /runs/:id` now always computes and returns
  `transcriptTail`, `result`, `resultTruncated`, not only when `?tail=` is
  present.
- `src/api/transcript.test.ts` — new unit suite: finished-run extraction
  (with the byte-order adversarial case above), still-launched run (`result:
  null`), missing transcript file, unreadable transcript file (simulated
  `fs.readFileSync` throw), oversized-result truncation, malformed
  `result`-field-not-a-string.
- `src/api/app.test.ts` — three new HTTP-level tests: plain `GET /runs/:id`
  (no `?tail=`) on a finished run returns both fields populated; a
  still-`launched` run returns `result: null` without throwing; a run whose
  transcript file was deleted degrades to `result: null`,
  `transcriptTail: []`, still `200`.

## Live verification (not just green tests)

1. `npm run build` — clean. `npm test` — 133 passed, 8 skipped (the
   Postgres-backed ledger test, self-skips without `DATABASE_URL`, unrelated
   to this change), 0 failed.
2. Found the live `:8089` listener (`netstat -ano | findstr :8089`, PID
   12760), confirmed it was a `node.exe` process before touching it, killed
   *only* that PID, started the freshly built `dist/index.js` in the
   background with output redirected to the repo's existing
   `agent-runner.out.log`/`.err.log`. New listener confirmed on a fresh PID.
3. `GET http://127.0.0.1:8089/health` → `{"status":"ok","service":"agent-runner"}`.
4. `GET http://127.0.0.1:8089/runs/0623ba6e-6414-4187-b5da-f0f847a0e01d`
   (no `?tail=` query — exactly what `HttpAgentRunner.get_run()` sends by
   default) → `state: "finished"`, `transcriptTail` present (100 lines),
   `result` present (5,972 characters), `resultTruncated: false`. The
   `result` text opens:

   > "All four contracts schemas are confirmed, and the DTO/UI/doc sweep is
   > complete... | `app.health` | `contracts/schemas/app/health.yaml` |
   > ... | `ai.request` | `contracts/schemas/ai-gateway/request.yaml`,
   > component `AiRequest` | ... Full DTO inventory (18 request-bearing
   > endpoints across auth/user, plant, identification, reminder,
   > treatment, chat...)"

   — the same contracts-schema mapping and endpoint inventory the demand
   named as what W16's brief was missing. This is the real agent answer,
   returned from agent-runner's own API, with no filesystem access into
   this repo required.

## What the origin must know

- Field names are `transcriptTail` (existing, now always populated),
  `result` (new), `resultTruncated` (new) — all camelCase, on the plain
  `GET /runs/{id}` response, no dedicated endpoint added.
- `result` is `null`, not an empty string, for a non-terminal run or a
  missing/unreadable transcript — check for `null`, not falsy-string.
- `transcript_tail`'s existing snake_case Python field maps 1:1 already
  (`data.get("transcriptTail")` — no adapter change needed); `result` is a
  field your `RunRecord`/`_record_from_json` don't read yet — this repo
  recommends adding it there and preferring it over parsing
  `transcript_tail` for answer extraction, but that change is yours to make
  in your own repo, not made here.
- The Windows-host-path issue (`transcriptPath`, Layer 2 in the demand) is
  **not addressed by this fulfillment** — `transcriptPath` is unchanged, still
  a host path. It's now moot for the specific need this demand names (getting
  the answer content), since `result`/`transcriptTail` make that reachable
  without ever opening `transcriptPath` — but if design-studio has some other
  reason to want a container-resolvable transcript path, that would need a
  separate demand naming that specific need.

## Not done / caveats

- No dedicated `/runs/{id}/transcript` or `/runs/{id}/result` endpoint
  (candidate d) — not needed once (a)+(b) closed every acceptance criterion;
  can be raised as a separate demand later if a consumer needs raw-file
  streaming rather than a bounded JSON field.
- `result` extraction assumes the CLI's `stream-json` terminal record always
  carries the answer in a `result`-named string field — the same assumption
  `processSupervisor.ts`'s own `tryParseUsage`/`tryParseModel` already make
  about this CLI's output shape (not this repo's to change; upstream CLI
  behavior).
- `GET /runs` (the list endpoint) was deliberately **not** changed to
  include `result`/`transcriptTail` per-run — that would mean reading every
  run's transcript file on every list call, unbounded by how many runs
  exist; the demand's acceptance criteria only named `GET /runs/{id}`.

# Fulfillment — fleet-level rollup for the `/brain/*` read surface

## Current-state check (before writing anything)

Confirmed the capability did not already exist. `GET /brain/fleet`
(`src/api/brainRoutes.ts`) served the executioner's `--dry-run --json`
verbatim, and `GET /brain/{repo}/pending-audit` / `GET /brain/{repo}/overrides`
served correct per-repo data — but there was no composed surface, so the
console's only path to per-repo counts was 2N requests. Verified live against
the running instance on `:8089` before starting.

## What shipped

**`GET /brain/rollup`** — a **sibling** endpoint, not a change to
`/brain/fleet`. The demand left the shape open ("extra fields on
`/brain/fleet`, or a `/brain/rollup` sibling"); a sibling was chosen because
`/brain/fleet`'s documented contract is literally "the executioner's JSON,
verbatim" (D070, spec brief 2026-07-22) and folding composed fields into it
would break that contract for its existing caller. The rollup instead embeds
each fleet entry unreshaped under `eligibility`, so nothing is lost.

Response shape (real output, live probe 2026-07-25 23:32, abridged to one repo
of 24):

```json
{
  "generatedAt": "2026-07-25T23:32:00+01:00",
  "nightWindow": { "spec": "01:00-08:00", "start": "01:00", "end": "08:00",
                   "crossesMidnight": false, "open": false,
                   "nextOpenAt": "2026-07-26T01:00:00+01:00", "invalidReason": null },
  "eligibilitySource": { "ok": true, "reason": null },
  "repos": [{
    "name": "agent-runner",
    "pendingAudit": { "totalCount": 10, "filledCount": 0, "generatedAt": "2026-07-24T04:56:25+01:00" },
    "pendingAuditExists": true, "pendingAuditReason": null,
    "overrides": { "pins": 0, "ratifiedConventions": 0, "clearedStaleFlags": 0, "total": 0 },
    "overridesExists": true, "overridesReason": null,
    "lastFullRunAt": "2026-07-24T15:26:00+01:00", "lastFullRunReason": null,
    "lastFullRunSessionId": "2026-07-24_0451_close-the-loop-on-demand-agent-runner-20",
    "eligibility": { "name": "agent-runner", "sessionsSinceLastFull": 3, "threshold": 3,
                     "eligible": true, "lastFullRunAt": "2026-07-24T15:26:00+01:00",
                     "windowOpen": false, "blockedReason": "outside night window" },
    "eligibilityReason": null
  }]
}
```

Full field contract is in `DEPLOYMENT.md` (§ "`GET /brain/*` — the read-only
brain-data surface"), documented as a read-only contract alongside the whole
surface — criterion 6.

## Acceptance criteria — each, and how it was verified

1. **Per-repo `totalCount`/`filledCount` and overrides counts in one request.**
   ✅ `repos[].pendingAudit.{totalCount,filledCount}` and
   `repos[].overrides.*`, from the same files the per-repo routes serve
   (`parsePendingAudit`/`parseOverrides` reused, not reimplemented). Live: 24
   repos, one request, `agent-runner` reporting the real `10/0` queue.

2. **D047 night-window bounds + next open instant, alongside `windowOpen`.**
   ✅ Top-level `nightWindow` (the window is a platform constant, not a
   per-repo fact, so it is returned once). `nextOpenAt` is computed against
   `generatedAt`: equal to `generatedAt` when the window is already open,
   otherwise the next occurrence of `start`. The per-repo
   `eligibility.windowOpen` boolean is untouched and still present, as asked.
   Live at 23:32: `open: false`, `nextOpenAt: 2026-07-26T01:00:00+01:00` — the
   "closed · opens 02:00" story the demand described.

3. **Never-run distinguishable from unreadable marker.** ✅ This is why
   `readLastFullRunMarker()` reads `.brain/derived/last-full-run.json`
   *directly* rather than trusting the executioner's `lastFullRunAt`: the
   executioner's `eligibility_to_json_dict` collapses every cause into one
   `null`. Four distinct `reason` strings now: `null` (real timestamp), `"no
   full run recorded (marker file absent)"`, `"marker file unreadable
   (<code>: …)"`, `"marker file malformed (…)"`, `"marker file present but
   carries no \`ts\` field"`. **Live-verified on the demand's own example**:
   `documentations` → `lastFullRunAt: null` + `"no full run recorded (marker
   file absent)"`, while `agent-runner` → a real
   `2026-07-24T15:26:00+01:00`.

4. **Per-repo read failure degrades to null + reason, whole rollup survives.**
   ✅ Each of the three reads per repo degrades independently. Tested with a
   real non-ENOENT read failure (a directory where the file should be), not a
   mock. Also covered above the per-repo level: an **executioner** failure
   returns 200 with `eligibilitySource.ok: false` and every repo's
   locally-read counts intact — `/brain/fleet`'s honest-503 posture is
   deliberately *not* copied here, because a rollup that blanks 24 repos'
   counts over one unavailable subprocess would be less honest, not more.
   An unparseable `NIGHT_WINDOW` likewise yields `open: null` +
   `invalidReason` rather than a fabricated boolean.

5. **Read-only and traversal-guarded, no new write path.** ✅ `brainRollup.ts`
   contains no `fs` mutation call (all reads route through `brain.ts`'s
   `readBrainFile` → `fs.readFileSync`). It also introduces **no new
   caller-supplied path input**: repo names come from `discoverBrainRepos`
   (directory presence under the platform root), never from a request
   parameter, so there is no new traversal surface — the existing
   `isSafeRepoName` guard still governs every caller-named path on the
   per-repo routes, unchanged. A route-level test asserts the fixture files
   are byte-identical and the `.brain/` directory listing unchanged after
   repeated calls (in particular: reading for a marker never creates one).

6. **Documented in DEPLOYMENT.md as a read-only contract.** ✅ New
   "`GET /brain/*`" section: a table of the whole surface plus the rollup's
   full field contract, timestamp-format rule, degradation semantics, and the
   `NIGHT_WINDOW` env row in the environment-variable table.

## One deviation from the demand's wording, and why

The demand asks for "the overrides **proposed/ratified** counts". There is no
`proposed` section in the real `overrides.md` schema — the fleet-wide file
carries exactly three sections: `## pins`, `## ratified conventions`,
`## cleared stale flags` (a *proposal* lives in a session log's `decisions:`
list; `overrides.md` records only what the owner already ratified). So the
rollup returns the three real section counts plus their `total`, rather than
inventing a `proposed` field that would always be zero.

**Mapping for the dashboard demand's "Ratify · N" affordance:**
`overrides.ratifiedConventions` is the count of ratified conventions on file;
`overrides.total` is the "this repo has overrides at all" number. If the
console's "Ratify" affordance was meant to count *pending* ratifications
rather than completed ones, that is a different data source entirely (session
`decisions`) and is not in this rollup — flagging it explicitly rather than
silently mapping one to the other. `design-studio` may want to reconcile this
against `design-studio-20260725-dashboard-brain-screen-legibility`'s own
criterion before that demand is built.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- New tests: 18 in `src/domain/brainRollup.test.ts` + 4 route-level in
  `src/api/brainRoutes.test.ts`. All 34 tests in those two suites pass.
- Full suite: **237 passed, 8 skipped, 2 failed**. The 2 failures are
  **pre-existing and unrelated** — `src/domain/brain.test.ts`'s
  live-verification cases assert against this repo's own real, regenerated
  `pending-audit.md`, whose contents have since changed. Confirmed pre-existing
  by stashing this session's changes and re-running on clean `HEAD`: same 2
  failures. Not introduced here, and not fixed here (out of scope; noted below
  for whoever owns that suite).
- **Live-verified end to end**: rebuilt, restarted the running `:8089`
  instance, and probed the real endpoint against the real 24-repo fleet — the
  probe output quoted above is genuine, not a fixture.

## Notes for the origin

- The pre-existing `brain.test.ts` failures are a real, separate problem: two
  tests assert against a generated file that the structurer legitimately
  rewrites, so they will keep breaking on every full run. Worth a follow-up in
  `agent-runner`'s own backlog (not raised as a demand — it is this repo's own
  code).
- Nothing here changes `/brain/fleet`, so the dashboard's existing calls are
  unaffected; the rollup is purely additive.

shipped: src/domain/brainRollup.ts — readPendingRatification() + parseRatifiedUnitIds(); pendingRatification/pendingRatificationExists/pendingRatificationReason on every rollup entry

# Fulfillment — `pendingRatification` on `GET /brain/rollup`

This is a two-repo demand (`to: [dashboard, agent-runner]`). **Only
`agent-runner`'s leg was done here** — criteria 4, 6, 7 and 8. Criteria 1, 2,
3 and 5 are the `/brain` screen's wiring, which is `dashboard`'s work; not one
line of it was written from this session, per the platform's own rule.

## Current-state check (before writing anything)

Confirmed the field did not exist. `GET /brain/rollup` shipped this morning
with `overrides.{pins,ratifiedConventions,clearedStaleFlags,total}` and no
pending count of any kind — the exact gap the previous report flagged and this
demand reconciles.

## The source, and one correction to the demand's own wording

Criterion 4 names the source as "session decisions", echoing this repo's
earlier report. **That parenthetical is one step upstream of the real queue,
and following it literally would have produced a wrong number** — so it was
not followed literally. The criterion's primary clause ("a per-repo count of
convention units awaiting ratification") is what shipped.

Per spec §7 / §9.2 step 5 / §9.5: `status: proposed` is the **only** state a
structurer-created `convention` unit may hold, and it leaves that state
**only** by human ratification recorded in `overrides.md`. So the pending
queue is exactly the `.brain/knowledge/*.md` units with `type: convention` +
`status: proposed` — literally the units an `overrides.md` entry flips. A
session's `decisions:` list is the *input* the extractor turns into those
units; counting it would tally proposals long since extracted, ratified,
superseded or archived as though they were still waiting.

Verified against real fleet data before committing to it: in `agent-runner`,
`type: convention` and `status: proposed` coincide **exactly** — 44 units, no
unit holds one without the other.

## A defect the live probe caught, and the fix

The first working version counted `status: proposed` naively. Probing the real
fleet immediately surfaced a case the fixtures had not:

```
dashboard          -> count 3   (overrides.md `## ratified conventions` lists K-0005, K-0008, K-0010)
demand-coordinator -> count 2   (same shape)
```

All five of those units are listed as **ratified by the owner** in
`overrides.md`, but their unit files still read `status: proposed` — the
structurer applies the flip on its next full run. So a naive count would have
shown the owner **"Ratify · 3"** for work they had already done: precisely the
confidently-wrong-number failure mode this demand exists to prevent, arriving
by a different route than the one it anticipated.

Fixed: `parseRatifiedUnitIds()` reads the ids listed under `##  ratified
conventions` and those units are excluded from `count`, reported instead as
`ratifiedNotYetApplied`. After the fix, live:

```
agent-runner       -> {"count":44,"ratifiedNotYetApplied":0,"unreadableUnits":0}  (overrides.ratified=0)
media-generation   -> {"count":63,"ratifiedNotYetApplied":0,"unreadableUnits":0}  (overrides.ratified=0)
dashboard          -> {"count":0, "ratifiedNotYetApplied":3,"unreadableUnits":0}  (overrides.ratified=3)
demand-coordinator -> {"count":0, "ratifiedNotYetApplied":2,"unreadableUnits":0}  (overrides.ratified=2)
```

**Fleet-wide: 107 units genuinely pending** (112 before the exclusion), across
24 repos, in one request.

`ratifiedNotYetApplied` is exposed rather than silently absorbed because a
persistently non-zero value means full runs aren't landing — that is worth the
owner seeing, just not in the "Ratify" number.

## Acceptance criteria — agent-runner's leg

4. **Per-repo count of convention units awaiting ratification, distinct from
   the overrides.md ratified counts.** ✅ `repos[].pendingRatification.count`,
   from `.brain/knowledge/` (see above for why that source, not session
   decisions). Genuinely a different quantity from
   `overrides.ratifiedConventions`, and a test asserts the two differ rather
   than coincidentally matching.

6. **Unreadable source reports null with a reason, not zero.** ✅ Same contract
   as every field shipped in the first rollup. An **absent**
   `.brain/knowledge/` (no structurer run yet) → `count: 0` with `exists:
   false`, which is a real answer. An **unreadable** directory → the whole
   `pendingRatification` object `null` plus
   `pendingRatificationReason`. Tested with a real `ENOTDIR` failure, not a
   mock. A single unparseable unit file inside a readable directory is neither
   — it makes `count` a floor, which `unreadableUnits` says out loud.
   Additionally: if `overrides.md` is unreadable, the exclusion list is empty,
   so `count` errs toward showing **more** pending work than there is, never
   less — a silently under-reported `Ratify · 0` would hide work.

7. **Documented in DEPLOYMENT.md.** ✅ In the existing "`GET /brain/*` — the
   read-only brain-data surface" section, alongside the rest of the contract,
   including the sub-field semantics and the degradation rules above.

8. **Read-only, owner-gate unchanged.** ✅ The addition is `readdirSync` +
   `readFileSync` only; no `fs` mutation call exists anywhere in
   `brainRollup.ts`. No new caller-supplied path input (repo names still come
   from directory discovery, never a request parameter). Nothing about
   dispatch or the owner gate was touched.

## For `dashboard`'s leg (criterion 5)

Feed the Ratify affordance from **`repos[].pendingRatification.count`**.

Handle the null case as absent/unlabelled, not `0` — `pendingRatification:
null` means unknown, and `pendingRatificationReason` carries the why. Note
that `count: 0` with `ratifiedNotYetApplied > 0` is a real, correct state
(`dashboard`'s own repo is in it right now): nothing pending, some
ratifications awaiting the next structurer run. Rendering "Ratify · 0" there
is correct; rendering "Ratify · 3" is not.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- 7 new tests; **43 passing** across `brainRollup.test.ts` and
  `brainRoutes.test.ts`.
- Full suite: **246 passed, 8 skipped, 2 failed**. The 2 failures are the
  same **pre-existing, unrelated** `src/domain/brain.test.ts` cases reported
  against the previous demand (they assert against this repo's own real,
  structurer-regenerated `pending-audit.md`). Re-confirmed pre-existing, not
  introduced here, and still out of scope to fix.
- **Live-verified** against the real 24-repo fleet on `:8089`, before and
  after the already-ratified fix — the figures quoted above are genuine
  output, not fixtures.

# Fulfillment — one source of truth for ratification candidates

Two-repo demand (`to: [dashboard, agent-runner]`). **Only `agent-runner`'s leg
was done here** — criteria 2, 3, 5, 7 and the read-only/owner-gate half of 8.
Criteria 1 and 6, and the rendering half of criterion 4, are the `/brain`
screen's work in `dashboard`'s repo; not one line of it from this session.

## Current-state check (before writing anything)

Confirmed the gap. `/brain/rollup` served `pendingRatification` **counts** and
nothing else — there was no candidate endpoint at all, which is exactly why the
screen had to reconstruct candidates from `graph.md`. The demand's diagnosis is
correct and I reproduced it on disk before writing anything.

## The defect, measured

`agent-runner`'s `.brain/graph.md` `## Proposed conventions` section today
lists **2** units. Its actual gated set is **46**. The projection is a snapshot
of the last structurer full run's output; the unit files are the primary
record, and they move every time a session closes. That is the whole mechanism
— not a parsing bug on either side, a freshness gap between a generated
projection and its source.

(The demand's figures were 44 and 0; both numbers have moved since — 46 gated
now, and `graph.md` picked up 2 entries from the intervening runs. The shape of
the divergence is unchanged and, if anything, the live figures make the point
better: the projection is not merely empty, it is *confidently wrong by 44*.)

## What shipped

**`scanRatification()` — one function, both answers.** The candidate list and
the rollup's count now come from the same call: `readPendingRatification()`
returns `list.length` rather than tallying in a second pass. The demand asks
that badge and queue "be derived from the same source"; this makes them the
same *data structure*, so they cannot drift even if someone later changes the
predicate.

**`GET /brain/{repo}/ratification-candidates`** serves it:

```json
{
  "exists": true, "reason": null,
  "count": 46,
  "candidates": [{
    "unitId": "K-0010",
    "title": "RunManager must claim the per-repo lock and concurrency-cap slot BEFORE calling processPort.spawn()...",
    "body": "…the full unit body, so the owner can judge without opening the file…",
    "created": "2026-07-18", "bornFrom": "lesson", "sources": ["2026-07-18_001"]
  }],
  "ratifiedNotYetApplied": [], "ratifiedNotYetAppliedCount": 0,
  "unreadableUnits": 0
}
```

`unitId` comes from the filename — the structurer's own addressing scheme, and
the same id `overrides.md` lists and a ratification dispatch submits, so the
existing prompt shape needs no change.

## Acceptance criteria — agent-runner's leg

2. **agent-runner serves the candidate list from the same scan that produces
   the rollup count.** ✅ Structurally, per above. A test asserts
   `rollup.pendingRatification.count === candidates.length` for the same repo
   through two real HTTP calls, and the live check below asserts it across the
   whole fleet.

3. **Units already ratified in overrides.md excluded from the list and the
   count.** ✅ Both, from the one exclusion set (`readRatifiedUnitIds`, shared
   by rollup and route). Previously the exclusion existed only for the count,
   because there was no list. Also hardened: the rollup's `overrides.md` parse
   moved outside its summarize-`try`, so a failure to *count* the file's
   sections can never silently change *which units are excluded*.

5. **Both owner-reported cases reproduce correctly; badge and queue agree.**
   ✅ Live, across **all 24 repos, zero mismatches** (`count` and
   `ratifiedNotYetApplied` compared per repo between `/brain/rollup` and the
   new endpoint):

   ```
   agent-runner        badge=46 listed=46 ratifiedNotYetApplied=0  AGREE
   dashboard           badge=0  listed=0  ratifiedNotYetApplied=3  AGREE
   demand-coordinator  badge=0  listed=0  ratifiedNotYetApplied=2  AGREE
   media-generation    badge=63 listed=63 ratifiedNotYetApplied=0  AGREE
   repos checked: 24 | mismatches: 0
   ```

   The staleness *cause* is not fixed by this — `graph.md` will keep lagging,
   because that is what a projection does. What is fixed is that nothing the
   console renders reads it any more.

7. **Documented in DEPLOYMENT.md.** ✅ In the existing read-only `/brain/*`
   section: full field contract, degradation rules, and an explicit "do not
   rebuild this list from `graph.md`" note carrying the measured 2-vs-46
   divergence, so the reason survives longer than this demand.

8. **Read-only; owner gate unchanged (agent-runner's half).** ✅ The endpoint
   lists what awaits ratification and ratifies nothing — `readdirSync` +
   `readFileSync` only, no `fs` mutation call anywhere in `brainRollup.ts`, and
   no new caller-supplied path input beyond `{repo}`, which passes the same
   `isSafeRepoName` guard as every other per-repo route (tested: 400 on an
   encoded traversal, 404 on a non-`.brain` repo). A test asserts unit files are
   byte-identical after repeated calls. Nothing about dispatch was touched.

## For `dashboard`'s leg

- **Criterion 1/6:** bind `/brain/ratify/:repo` to
  `GET /brain/{repo}/ratification-candidates`. `count` is authoritative and
  equals `candidates.length`; retiring `parse-proposed-conventions.ts` outright
  is cleaner than keeping it as a fallback, since any fallback reading
  `graph.md` *can* disagree with the badge — that is the defect, not a
  mitigation of it.
- **Criterion 4:** `ratifiedNotYetApplied` now arrives as full entries, not
  just a count, so the screen can render those three `dashboard` units as their
  own state with their titles. `count: 0` with
  `ratifiedNotYetAppliedCount: 3` is a real, correct state — `dashboard`'s own
  repo is in it right now.
- **Degradation:** `candidates: null` (with `count: null` and a `reason`) means
  unknown — render unlabelled, never as an empty queue. `unreadableUnits > 0`
  means the list is a floor.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- 14 new tests; **57 passing** across `brainRollup.test.ts` and
  `brainRoutes.test.ts`.
- Full suite: **260 passed, 8 skipped, 2 failed**. The 2 failures are the same
  **pre-existing, unrelated** `src/domain/brain.test.ts` cases reported against
  the two previous demands (they assert against this repo's own real,
  structurer-regenerated `pending-audit.md`). Still not introduced here, still
  out of scope.
- **Live-verified** on the real 24-repo fleet on `:8089` — the agreement table
  above is genuine output, not fixtures.

## Note for the origin

The demand's framing that the omission "is `design-studio`'s" is noted and not
contested, but it is also not the whole picture: this repo shipped a count in
the previous demand without asking what the screen behind it was reading. Worth
recording on both sides that a number is only as good as the queue it links to.

# Fulfillment — register `documentations` in agent-runner's dispatch allowlist

## Current-state check (before writing anything)

Checked `config/repo-allowlist.json` first, per this demand's own instruction
to check before redoing work. `documentations` was absent from the `repos`
array — this leg was not already shipped.

## What shipped

- **`config/repo-allowlist.json`**: added a `documentations` entry (alongside

  demand id, consistent with this file's existing convention of dated notes

- The allow-list is the **sole gate** `RunManager.dispatch()` checks
  (`src/domain/runManager.ts:88`, synchronously, before any process is
  spawned or lock/cap slot is claimed) — no other code path needed touching.
  `RepoAllowList.isAllowed()` (`src/domain/allowList.ts:38`) does a plain

# Report — the agent-runner-postgres named volume is now documented

**Checked current state first, as asked.** Not previously shipped. At
`51ec087`, DEPLOYMENT.md's `docker run` block had no `-v` flag at all, while
the container actually in service was mounted on a named volume:

```
$ docker inspect agent-runner-postgres --format '{{json .Mounts}}'
[{"Type":"volume","Name":"agent-runner-postgres-data",
  "Destination":"/var/lib/postgresql/data", ...}]
```

So the docs and the running reality genuinely disagreed, exactly as the demand
described. Anyone recreating the container from DEPLOYMENT.md would have got a
fresh anonymous volume and an empty `runs` table — and would not have noticed,
because `PostgresLedger.init()`'s `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` succeeds
identically against an empty database.

## Canonical name: `agent-runner-postgres-data` — unchanged, no migration

Kept the name already in service rather than inventing a new one. That is the
whole point of the third acceptance criterion, and choosing any other name
would have created the migration problem it warns about for no gain. So:
**no migration section is needed and none is written** — the ledger in service
today stays exactly where it is, and the documented `docker run` line now
re-attaches to it.

## The durability question — answered: **durable**

The demand is right that launcher's socket restarts this container but never
removes it, and that this was an assumption. It happens to be the correct
behaviour, and it now has a stated basis rather than luck:

`spec-agent-runner.md` lists the run ledger under this hexagon's state
alongside the transcripts as **the audit trail** — the record of every
owner-gated dispatch (demand id, repo, prompt, start/end, exit state, token
usage). Transcripts carry a stated 90-day retention (§5); **the ledger carries
no expiry at all**. Read together, that is durable, keep-forever data, and
DEPLOYMENT.md now says so in those words.

Practical consequence for launcher, now written into DEPLOYMENT.md: restarting
and even recreating the container is fine; `docker rm -v`, `docker volume rm
agent-runner-postgres-data`, and `docker compose down -v` are data loss. The
current socket behaviour needs no change.

One honest scope note: this is agent-runner stating the durability of its own
hexagon's state from its own spec — it is not an owner ruling and not a vault
edit, and it does not bind how `runtime`'s eventual compose stack declares the
volume when this container is finally registered there (still a later-chunk
demand, per the same DEPLOYMENT.md paragraph). If that registration wants a
different name, the migration question reopens there, not here.

## Not touched

No code changed; this was a documentation-truth defect only. The volume, the
container, and the running ledger were all left exactly as found — no
recreate, no restart, nothing removed.
