# Fulfillment — HEXAGON.md-driven dispatch discovery + `platform-vault` behind a manual-session guard (D085)

## Checked first

Not previously shipped. `config/repo-allowlist.json` was still the
hand-maintained roster, still carrying the `_note` that named itself the gate,
denied auto-discovery, and excluded `platform-vault` pending an owner ruling;
`src/domain/allowList.ts` was still a `Set` built from that file's `repos`
array. Built from scratch this session. (An untracked, supervisor-opened
`.brain` session file from this session's own launch existed — `changes: []`,
`status: partial` — no code had landed.)

## What shipped

### 1. The gate is auto-discovery (`src/domain/allowList.ts`)

`RepoAllowList` no longer holds a name set. `isAllowed(repo)` is now
"`<PLATFORM_ROOT>/<repo>/HEXAGON.md` exists", and `list()` is a `readdir` of
`PLATFORM_ROOT` filtered by that same marker, sorted. **The scan runs on every
call**, so discovery is live at request time, not a boot-time snapshot — a
newly-bootstrapped hexagon is dispatchable with no restart and no edit to any
file here.

Two things worth flagging:

- **Traversal is closed before the filesystem is touched.** A repo name that
  isn't a bare directory name (`..`, `.`, `''`, `a/b`, `./x`, `C:\Windows`) is
  rejected outright — otherwise a marker file reachable via such a path would
  have passed the existence check and resolved a `cwd` outside `PLATFORM_ROOT`.
- **The roster had already drifted.** `media-generation` — a live `.brain` pilot
  repo — was missing from the hand-maintained list and was therefore
  undispatchable. Discovery includes it. This is the concrete cost of the
  hand-maintained gate, not a hypothetical one.

`config/repo-allowlist.json` survives as a **notes overlay only**:
`loadFromFile` reads it for per-repo owner-facing `note` strings (`noteFor()`)
and treats a missing, unreadable or malformed file as "no notes" rather than an
error — it can no longer cost access, because it no longer decides access. Its
`_note` is rewritten; all three superseded claims (file-is-the-gate, no
auto-discovery, `platform-vault` excluded) are gone, replaced by a description
of the D085 gate and the preflight guard. A test asserts the shipped `_note`
mentions D085 and contains neither "does not auto-discover" nor "deliberately
excluded", so the prose can't quietly drift back.

### 2. `platform-vault` is dispatchable, guarded by a preflight (`src/domain/preflight.ts`)

D035 still makes the vault a single-writer governed hexagon. What D085 changes
is *where* that property is enforced: not by excluding the repo from the gate,
but inside the dispatched session. `MANUAL_SESSION_GUARD_REPOS = ['platform-vault']`;
`applyPreflight(repo, prompt)` prefixes a guarded repo's prompt with a mandatory
preflight — run `git log -1 --format=%H%n%cI%n%s` and `git status --porcelain`
**before the first write**, and if the last commit is recent (~15 min) or the
tree is dirty, **stop, write nothing, and report what was observed**. The
preamble states explicitly that a stopped session is the correct outcome, not a
failure, so the guard isn't read as something to work around.

The reasoning for putting it in-session: agent-runner's one-live-session-per-repo
lock only knows about runs *it* launched. The owner's own interactive vault
sessions are invisible to it. The only observer that can see both is the
dispatched session itself, against the repo's own git state.

Two placement decisions:

- **Applied in `RunManager.dispatch`, not at the API layer** — so every dispatch
  path (console form, demand-driven, brain executioner, any future caller) is
  covered rather than each one having to remember it.
- **The ledger records the effective prompt**, not the owner's bare prompt.
  The transcript is this repo's audit surface (D048); ledger and transcript must
  not disagree about what the session was told.

### 3. Nothing weakened for `platform-vault`

The per-repo lock, the concurrency cap, and `computeDispatchable`'s active-run
filter are entirely repo-agnostic and were left that way — there is no
`platform-vault` branch in any of them. Both are asserted directly by new tests
(a second vault dispatch while one is live rejects with `RepoLockedError`; a
vault entry with an active run is filtered out of `/dispatchable`).

## Acceptance criteria — how each was demonstrated

Live gate: the built service run on spare ports (`8189` real `PLATFORM_ROOT`,
`8190` a throwaway root), both stopped afterwards.

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `/repos` = every sibling with a `HEXAGON.md`, discovered at request time | Live `GET :8189/repos` returned all 28 marker-carrying siblings |
| Marker-less dirs absent and rejected | `tmp`, `docs`, `contracts-worktrees`, `brain-toolkit-worktrees` all absent from that response; live `POST /dispatch {repo:"tmp"}` → **HTTP 400** |

# Report — the dispatch supervisor now commits the two files it writes (D089)

Not previously shipped; checked first. `brainSupervisor.ts` at `c1a2b63` still
carried the never-commit boundary in both code and docstring, and
`deriveChangesFromGit`'s docstring still asserted "this module never runs `git
add`/`git commit`".

## What changed

`onSupervisedExit` now ends with `commitSupervisorFiles(repoPath, sessionId,
status)` — **last**, after both files are already on disk, so a git failure can
never cost the session record itself. It runs:

```
git add    --                 .brain/sessions/<session_id>.md PROGRESS.md
git commit -m "brain: supervisor close for <id> (status: <status>)" -- <same two>
```

The pathspec on **`commit`**, not just on `add`, is the load-bearing part: it is
what makes any content the worker left staged in the index irrelevant to the
supervisor's commit. There is a test for exactly that case
(`does not sweep in content the worker left STAGED in the index`), alongside one
proving a worker's unstaged edits to a source file and to `.brain/conventions.md`
are still dirty afterwards.

Between `add` and `commit` it runs `git diff --cached --quiet -- <paths>` to
distinguish "nothing of *ours* to commit" from "the index has unrelated worker
content" — an empty-commit attempt would otherwise fail noisily for the wrong
reason.

It never throws. `skipped-not-a-git-repo`, `skipped-nothing-to-commit` and
`failed` (with the git stderr, truncated) come back on the new
`SupervisedExitResult.commit` field, and `processSupervisor.ts` logs a
`… was not committed` warning on anything but `committed` — a best-effort commit
that fails silently would have reproduced the original bug in a quieter form.

The docstring: the old never-commit argument is kept and labelled as the
considered position it was ("a supervisor that commits is a supervisor that can
pick up work it did not write"), then amended with what it was wrong about —
that the files land after the worker is gone, so nobody is left who could commit
them. Per D089 limit 3, it reads as an amendment, not as if the position had
never existed.

One honest edge recorded in the docstring, DEPLOYMENT.md and here: **`PROGRESS.md`
is committed as a whole file.** If a worker left its own uncommitted `PROGRESS.md`
edits behind, they ride along. That is the same file, not a different one, so no
by-name rule can exclude them.

## The question asked: can an already-dispatched run ever leave a clean tree today?

**Confirmed — no.** This repo's belief is correct, for a stronger reason than
timing luck:

1. The supervisor's two writes happen in `onSupervisedExit`, which by
   construction runs after the worker process has exited. There is no ordering a
   worker can choose that puts its own final commit after them.
2. It is not avoidable by prompting. A worker instructed "do not open a brain
   session" still gets a supervisor-created session file — `onSupervisedLaunch`
   creates it from the dispatch, not from anything the worker does — and still
   gets an auto-drafted close on exit. The `observability` re-dispatch cited in
   D089 is the live proof.
3. It is not avoidable by dispatching again. A corrective dispatch's own
   supervisor writes a fresh pair as it exits: one in, one out. The demand's
   "provably infinite" framing is right, and the proof is just (1) applied to the
   corrective run.

The single exception, and it is narrow: if the worker runs `brain session close`
itself, the file it closes is the supervisor's own session file, and
`onSupervisedExit` sees `close: confirmed` and returns `skipped-already-closed`
without writing anything. A run that does that — and commits — *can* end clean.
That is exactly what happened on demand `platform-vault-20260731-commit-the-sweep-handoffs`
(commit `ac17fcb`), which is why that sweep looked cleanable by hand. It depends
entirely on the worker choosing to close the supervisor's session, which nothing
requires and most dispatched briefs never mention.

Two corrections to how the answer should be read going forward:

- **After this change, the "no" becomes "yes, by the supervisor" — forward-only.**
  A dispatched run into a `.brain` repo now ends with those two files committed
  rather than dirty. It does not clean residue already on disk (`observability`
  and every repo swept 2026-07-31 that has not since had an ordinary session);
  D089 says the same, and each repo's next session commits what is already there.
- **Clean tree ≠ pushed.** The supervisor commits; it does not push, and nothing
  in this change makes it push. A dispatched run now ends with `git status`
  honest and `origin` behind by one commit. That was true of the worker's own
  commits already, so it is not a regression, but it means "clean tree" is the
  claim being made here, not "synced".

## This session's own residue

Stated plainly because it is the same bug: this session runs under the
supervisor process that launched it, which is executing the *pre-change* build.
Its own auto-drafted close will still be left uncommitted when it exits. The fix
takes effect for runs launched after `agent-runner` is rebuilt and restarted.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npx jest src/adapters/brainSupervisor.test.ts` — 25/25 pass.
- `npm test` — 305 pass, 10 skipped, **2 pre-existing failures in
  `src/domain/brain.test.ts`** (citation-enrichment assertions over the live
  `.brain` corpus). Confirmed pre-existing by stashing this change and
  re-running that suite alone: the same 2 fail at `c1a2b63`. Untouched by this
  work and not fixed by it.

## Vault-side leg

`spec-agent-runner.md` is vault-owned (D035) and agent-runner must not edit it,
so the third acceptance criterion is raised as demand
`agent-runner-20260801-spec-agent-runner-d089-narrowed-git-boundary`
(`to: [platform-vault]`) rather than done here. It carries the exact shipped
shape for the spec text to describe. D089's other two vault-side follow-ups (the
`spec-agent-memory-system.md` A.3/D063 supervised-close note and the D081
doc-sync to `documentations`) are named there but left for the vault to route.

# Fulfilment report — judge `guided-turn-class`, and author its doctrine if it holds

## The judgment

**Accepted.** The demand explicitly permitted rejection in favour of an existing regime, and that
was the live alternative — bending a doctrine beats multiplying doctrines, and a near-miss regime is
usually the right answer. It is not the right answer here, on three grounds (full text in the
doctrine's §0bis):

1. **The `inhabited-class` argument is structural, not stylistic.** The inhabited doctrine's
   retention mechanism (a place that accumulates), its Companion rung ladder (R5, power earned
   across visits), its state→material mapping (§4) and its cold-start §6 are all continuity
   machinery. Amputating continuity does not leave a smaller inhabited surface; it leaves the
   checklist **unrunnable** — a reviewer would tick "does day zero feel inhabited?" on a surface
   that is day zero every day. That is the exact D053 harm (a wrong checklist applied confidently)
   the regime machinery exists to prevent, so the named fallback in the demand is worse than it
   looked.
2. **The other two rejections are correct and cheaply verified.** D036's seven laws are written for
   an operator. The atlas doctrine's C1–C26 are written for orientation in a persistent world whose
   R4/R5 stable geography is itself a retention mechanism built on a user returning to a world they
   remember — and, as app-studio noted, a traversal record is a profile.
3. **The proposal names failures no existing checklist asks about.** This is the D071 test, and it
   is the one that decides. Refusal-as-a-designed-screen, a declared reading floor,
   warmth-without-memory, and the prohibition on progress surfaces have no item in D036's seven
   laws, the inhabited §8, or the atlas §8.

**The critique was fair** (its own `isFair: true` is borne out): each regime got a real `for` case,
and the `inhabited-class` `for` was argued honestly enough that rejecting the proposal on that basis
was a live option rather than a formality. app-studio proposed and did not author — exactly the
D071/D095 boundary.

## The one amendment, and why it needs the owner's eye

app-studio proposed a **child-facing** regime. The draft deliberately does **not** name children in
any rule. §4's discriminator is *a user working alone, with low reading fluency, on one thing at a
time, whose relationship with the app cannot be accumulated* — which also covers a first-time user
in distress, a user operating in a second language, and any surface a data-minimisation duty forbids
from remembering its user. **Children are the exemplar, not the definition.**

Reasoning: a doctrine keyed to an age would have been re-litigated the first time a non-child
surface needed it, and the regime's actual load-bearing constraint (R3, warmth without memory) has
nothing to do with age. This is flagged for the owner at adoption — reverting to the narrower,
child-only class is a legitimate ruling and should be made there rather than discovered later.

## What the doctrine adds beyond the proposal

The proposal supplied five bullets; the draft is twelve rules. The additions, each recorded in §14
with its reasoning:

- **R3 (warmth without memory)** promoted to the load-bearing rule, and faked continuity made a
  **regime violation** rather than a copy defect. The predicted failure is not coldness — it is a
  designer who correctly senses the surface should feel warm and reaches for the only warmth
  mechanism they have seen (remembered history) and invents it.
- **R7 (patience is unbounded and uncounted)** — new. The concept named unlimited re-explanation as
  a product behaviour; it is promoted to a rule with its own choreography (§5's "asking again") and
  two checklist items, because the real failure is an interface that stays patient for two attempts
  and then sounds tired, which teaches an already-unsure user that they are slow.
- **R9 (input is forgiving; the user is never wrong)** — new. A user who cannot read a validation
  message cannot recover from one.
- **R10 (the adult surface is a different surface)** — the concept noted the parent half was
  console-shaped; the draft makes the separation a rule and, importantly, requires the adult half to
  be **gated under `console-class`'s own checklist** rather than waved through as "the other half"
  of a guided-turn mission.
- **R8 (no progress surface, no engagement mechanics)** — implicit in the concept's non-goals,
  stated as design law on the grounds that the components are *visual*: the moment a designer draws
  a progress ring, the data to fill it must be collected, and the regime has been left before anyone
  wrote a line of storage code.
- **R5** is a **stricter** degradation obligation than any other doctrine's — five required states
  rather than four — with §9 recording why it was re-derived rather than imported.

§10's worked example predicts the five defects a competent designer will produce from `tutor`'s own
core loop with no regime law in hand (a home screen, a hint counter, a progress ring, a stock error
string, a disabled "show me the answer"), each mapped to the checklist item that catches it.

## Sequencing — where this leaves `tutor`

D071's sequence is preserved exactly and is now the whole remaining critical path:

1. ✅ **Drafted** (this session).
2. ⏳ **Vault adoption** — `design-studio-20260804-platform-vault-guided-turn-doctrine-adoption`,
   `needs-owner: true`. Asks for the numbered decision, four-regime custodianship, and a ruling on
   §12's four open questions.
3. ⏳ **`contracts` `Regime` enum** — `design-studio-20260804-contracts-guided-turn-class-regime-enum`,
   raised now for critical-path reasons but **explicitly gated** on step 2 and marked to be closed
   unactioned if the vault rejects or renames the regime.
4. ⏳ **`design-studio` local adoption** — re-pin, fourth enum member, `GUIDED_TURN_CLASS_CHECKLIST`
   keyed to G1–G23, fourth arm at all six regime-dispatching sites, four-way theme-interview
   question. Not started, deliberately: nothing is stubbed, shimmed or faked ahead of the rulings,
   and the fail-closed branches mean a premature `guided-turn-class` mission raises
   `UnhandledRegimeError` rather than being silently gated against D036.

`app-studio`'s staged mission demand (`app-studio-20260804-design-tutor`) should stay staged behind
step 4, not step 1.

## The question with the earliest deadline

§12 question 4, surfaced to the owner in the adoption demand: R10 requires a guarded product's adult
half to be a separate surface under `console-class`'s own checklist. Is that a **second design
mission**, or **one mission with two gated surfaces**? This shapes `design-studio`'s mission model
rather than only the doctrine, and `tutor` hits it the moment a mission is created.

## Note on status

`done` is a claim, not a verdict. The coordinator validates; `design-studio` has not marked this
satisfied and has not notified `app-studio` directly.

## Pre-check finding

Both of this repo's own blocking demands had already closed independently
before this session: `contracts` shipped `Regime.atlas_class` at `v0.17.0`
(`f8c8e19`, `release: v0.17.0 (Regime enum gains atlas-class)`, with its own
fulfillment/re-pin-demand commits `713006b`/`7f61ad4`), and `platform-vault`
adopted `design-doctrine-atlas-interface.md` v0.1 verbatim (archived demand
`2026-07-23-platform-vault-atlas-doctrine-adoption.md`, no renumbering, §12's
four questions carried forward as open). Neither blocker's closure had yet
been acted on in `design-studio` — `requirements.txt` still pinned `v0.16.0`,
`domain/regime.py`'s `Regime` enum still had only two members, and all six
regime-dispatching sites still raised `UnhandledRegimeError` for any
`atlas-class` mission. This session did the actual re-pin and local adoption
work; nothing was a no-op.

## What was done

1. **Re-pinned** `requirements.txt`: `platform-contracts` `v0.16.0` → `v0.17.0`.
   Reinstalled into the repo's `.venv` and verified live:
   `ContractRegime('atlas-class')` constructs, and
   `design_studio.adapters.event_sink_state_feed._build_event`/
   `_build_design_system_event` round-trip a real `Mission`/`DesignSystem`
   carrying `Regime.ATLAS_CLASS` through to a validated
   `DesignMissionEvent`/`DesignSystemEvent` with no schema-validation error.
2. **Added `Regime.ATLAS_CLASS = "atlas-class"`** to the local domain enum
   (`domain/regime.py`), plus `ATLAS_CLASS_CHECKLIST` — 26 `ChecklistItem`s,
   one per doctrine Sec.8 C-number (C1–C26), grouped exactly as the doctrine
   groups them (Core / Geography / Motion / Interaction /
   Choreography-and-resilience).
3. **Filled in all six previously-raising `match` arms**, per the demand's own
   "what we do once closed" list:
   - `regime.checklist_for` → returns `ATLAS_CLASS_CHECKLIST`.

# Fulfillment report — `contracts`: re-pin to `v0.18.0`, adopt the fourth `guided-turn-class` `Regime` member

## Pre-check finding

Nothing here had been shipped by a prior session. `requirements.txt` still
pinned `v0.17.0`, `platform_contracts` was not installed in the working
interpreter at all, and no test or comment in this repo referenced the fourth
enum member. `contracts` had genuinely shipped it: `v0.18.0` is tagged, and
`gen/python/platform_contracts/state_feed/state_event.py` carries
`guided_turn_class = 'guided-turn-class'` on the `Regime` enum, with both the
`design.mission` and `design.designSystem` field descriptions updated. This
session did the real re-pin and adaptation work.

## Acceptance criteria, one by one

1. **Pin reads `0.18.0`.** ✅ `requirements.txt`:
   `platform-contracts @ git+…/contracts.git@v0.18.0#subdirectory=gen/python`.
   Installed into `.venv` (`platform-contracts-0.18.0`) so every claim below is
   made against the real package.

2. **The adapter can construct the member without a schema-validation error.**
   ✅ Verified live, not by inspection:
   `ContractRegime('guided-turn-class') is ContractRegime.guided_turn_class`,
   and both of `event_sink_state_feed`'s builders
   (`_build_event`, `_build_design_system_event`) construct and serialise a
   full `DesignMissionEvent` / `DesignSystemEvent` carrying the regime —
   `DesignMissionPayload` / `DesignSystemPayload` are pydantic models, so
   construction *is* the validation.

3. **Value-projection emits it verbatim, no mapping table.** ✅ Confirmed and
   left alone. The sink already projects
   `ContractRegime(<aggregate>.regime.value)` at both sites
   (`event_sink_state_feed.py:188`, `:210`); because `contracts` spells the
   member `guided-turn-class` exactly as this repo's slugs are spelled, the
   correct change was **no change**. The serialised payloads read
   `"regime": "guided-turn-class"` on both event types. A new test
   (`test_contracts_regime_enum_carries_guided_turn_class`) asserts this so a
   future mapping table cannot be introduced silently.

4. **Workarounds/stopgap comments predating support are removed.** ✅ There was
   no code workaround to remove — the projection was already spelling-agnostic
   and no branch anywhere special-cased the missing member. What existed was
   **stale prose**, which was corrected rather than deleted:
   - `domain/errors.py` — `UnhandledRegimeError`'s docstring said the
     fail-closed default is reached "only by a FOURTH regime this repo has not
     yet been taught", written when no such regime existed anywhere. It now
     names `guided-turn-class`, records that `contracts` `v0.18.0` carries it
     and this repo is pinned to it, and states why the local enum still does
     not — D071's sequence is contract, then law, then local adoption.
   - `tests/test_regime_fail_closed.py` — its module docstring called the
     fourth regime "STILL-unknown" and "hypothetical", flat out. It now
     distinguishes *downstream* (real, in `contracts`) from *here* (still
     hypothetical, by design), and records why the test's sentinel stays a
     nonsense string rather than becoming `"guided-turn-class"`: these tests
     assert behaviour for **any** untaught regime, and hard-coding the next one
     would turn them into a countdown that stops testing the thing it exists
     to test.

## What was deliberately left undone, and why

**No `Regime.GUIDED_TURN_CLASS` in `domain/regime.py`, no
`GUIDED_TURN_CLASS_CHECKLIST`, no fourth arm at any of the six
regime-dispatching sites.** This is not an omission — it is the demand's own
gating condition still holding.

The atlas-class precedent
(`contracts-20260723-design-studio-repin-atlas-class-regime-enum`) *did* do
full local adoption in one session, but only because **both** of its blockers
had closed: `contracts` shipped the enum **and** `platform-vault` adopted
`design-doctrine-atlas-interface.md` the same day. Here only the first has
closed. The vault carries no `design-doctrine-guided-turn-interface.md` and no
decision creating the regime; the adoption demand
(`design-studio-20260804-platform-vault-guided-turn-doctrine-adoption`) is
open. The doctrine currently lives as a v0.1 draft at this repo's root.

Adopting the local enum member now would create a regime a mission can be
opened against with **no adopted law to judge it by** — `checklist_for` would
have nothing to return, and a `guided-turn-class` gate would either be
unapprovable or, far worse, approvable against another regime's checklist.
That is the exact D053 harm this repo's whole regime module exists to prevent.
The fail-closed default is the correct behaviour today: a premature
`guided-turn-class` mission raises `UnhandledRegimeError` loudly instead of
being quietly judged as console-class.

**What closes the rest.** When the vault adopts the doctrine and records the
decision, a follow-up session in this repo adds the enum member, transcribes
the doctrine's G1–G23 checklist as `GUIDED_TURN_CLASS_CHECKLIST` (positively
stated per the R13 authoring law), fills the six `match` arms, widens
`theme_interview.py`'s regime question from three-way to four-way, and adds
the fourth entry to `GET /regimes`. The emission half is already done and will
need no further work — that is what this demand bought.

## Verification

- `PYTHONPATH=src pytest` — **703 passed**, run against the reinstalled
  `v0.18.0` package. Previous count 702; the one addition is the new
  emission-path test.
- No behaviour change to any existing path: the only `src/` edit in this
  session is a docstring.

# Fulfillment — design-studio: serve mission artifacts inline, not as forced download

## What was done

Exactly the fix the demand proposed, the "simplest fix" option it named as preferred
absent a reason to special-case: `get_artifact`
(`src/design_studio/api.py`, `GET /missions/{mission_id}/artifacts/{file_path:path}`)
now passes `content_disposition_type="inline"` explicitly into `FileResponse`,
alongside the `filename=` it already passed:

```python
return FileResponse(
    path, media_type=media_type, filename=path.name, content_disposition_type="inline"
)
```

Starlette's `FileResponse` defaults `content_disposition_type` to `"attachment"`
whenever `filename=` is set, regardless of `media_type` — so every artifact this
route ever served (not just `.html`) was carrying a forced-download header. `filename=`
is kept (not dropped) so a user's own Save As still names the file correctly; only the
disposition changed.

**Checked whether any other route shares the pattern** (the demand's own ask): grepped
the full `src/` tree for `FileResponse` — this is the only call site in the repo. No
sibling route needed the same fix.

## Tests

Two existing tests gained a `Content-Disposition` assertion each (no new test functions
— the suite count is unchanged at 81):

- `test_artifacts_list_and_download` — a flat-file artifact (`theme-a.html`):
  `assert r.headers["content-disposition"] == 'inline; filename="theme-a.html"'`
- `test_artifacts_serve_nested_mock_tree` — a nested theme-mock artifact
  (`theme-a/index.html`), the exact shape of the reported bug (a real theme
  proposition's mock page):
  `assert r.headers["content-disposition"] == 'inline; filename="index.html"'`
  (confirms the preserved filename is the artifact's own basename via `path.name`,
  not the full relative path under the mission subtree).

Both values were derived from reading Starlette's own `FileResponse.__init__`
(`.venv/Lib/site-packages/starlette/responses.py`) rather than guessed, so the
assertions match the real header-assembly logic exactly (ASCII filenames here never
hit the `filename*=utf-8''...` branch).

**Full suite: 81 passed, 0 failed** (`PYTHONPATH=src pytest`, run twice — once before
the docs commit, once as a final check) — unchanged from the 81 baseline this session
started at, since no new test functions were added.

## Acceptance criteria vs. what was verified

1. *A real `GET` (not HEAD) against a theme mock no longer returns
   `content-disposition: attachment`* — **verified at the TestClient level**
   (FastAPI's `TestClient`/`httpx` drives the real ASGI app end-to-end, exercising the
   exact same `Starlette.FileResponse.__init__` header-assembly code the demand's own
   curl evidence was reading from — there is no separate code path for a real uvicorn
   transport vs. TestClient here; the header is computed identically either way).
   **Not independently re-curled against the live `:8087` process** — see "Live
   verification" below for why.
2. *A theme proposition's "Open in new tab" link opens instead of downloading* — not
   re-driven from a real browser this session (no browser round-trip was attempted);
   follows directly from (1), since Chromium's disposition-driven download-vs-render
   choice on a top-level navigation is governed by exactly this header.
3. *Existing suite green* — **yes, 81/81**, per above.

## Live verification — deliberately not attempted this session, and why

This was a micro-session dispatched with an explicit constraint: **the live service on
`:8087` is orchestrator-managed; this session must not kill or restart it.** That
process is still running the pre-fix code — it predates this session's commits and
was left completely untouched throughout, per that instruction and this repo's own
standing order never to block on or interfere with a process it doesn't own.

Consequently the demand's own stated bar ("live curl evidence against the rebuilt
container/process... same bar this fleet's other live-verified demands have used") is
**not met by this report** — that bar requires the orchestrator to restart/redeploy
`:8087` onto this session's commits first, which is outside this session's authority.
Rather than fabricate or approximate that evidence (e.g. booting an unrelated scratch
instance on a throwaway port), this report states the gap plainly: **source-fixed and
test-verified, not live-verified.**

## For dashboard / the coordinator's next session

- **An orchestrator restart of the `:8087` process is required** before the fix is

  `content-disposition: attachment` exactly as the demand's own curl evidence showed —

  should no longer show `content-disposition: attachment` (expect

# Fulfillment — design-studio: build dispatch visibility + a build that carries itself

## State before this session

Not previously shipped. `dispatch_status.find_pending_dispatch` listed
`system-gate` explicitly among the stages with "no dispatch-shaped tracking file
… `None`, unconditionally" — written before S-E gave `system-gate` a dispatching
service at all, and never revisited when it did. So a running build was the one
dispatched step in the pipeline the console could not see working, and
`POST /missions/{id}/build-system` did exactly one unit of work per call, which
made a browser tab the thing actually driving a ~45-unit build.

## What was done

### 1. `activeDispatch` covers the build (criteria 1 + 2)

`find_pending_dispatch` gained a fifth branch for `Stage.SYSTEM_GATE`, reading
`design-system-build.json` and reporting the build's current in-flight unit as
`{"runId": ..., "kind": "build", "state": ...}` — byte-for-byte the shape the
other four kinds already produce, resolved through the same single
`agent_runner.get_run` probe with the same honest `"unknown"` degradation on an
outage. `ActiveDispatchTagComponent` needs no new branch; only the `kind` string
is new, and that is data.

The "which unit is current" predicate itself (`pending_build_dispatch`) lives in
`design_system_build.py`, not in `dispatch_status.py`. The other four tracking
files are flat dispatch records that `dispatch_status` can read directly; this
one is a batch/page tree whose notion of "current" is `run_build`'s own
next-undispatched-page walk. Duplicating that walk in the dispatch-status module
would have created two places obliged to agree on it forever.

The module's cost-control rule is preserved exactly: the local JSON read answers
"could anything still be running?" and only a genuinely live build ever causes an
agent-runner call, so `GET /missions` over the whole ledger stays as cheap as it
was.

### 2. Null in every non-live state (criterion 3)

`None` — no probe, nothing reported — for: a build never started, a unit not yet
dispatched, a unit already consolidated, a build paused, a build done
(`currentBatch` past the last batch), and batch 3 (assembly QA is mechanical and
never dispatched at all).

### 3. Failed ≠ running (criterion 4)

A dead run is deliberately *not* an active dispatch — reporting it would say "an
agent is working" when the truth is "retry needed". So the distinction is carried
by a new `designSystemBuild.failure` field:
`{"batch": N, "unit": "...", "runId": ..., "failedAt": "<iso>"}`, naming the exact
batch or page that died. It clears itself the moment the retry dispatches
(`run_build`'s existing retry path already resets `failedAt`). The console can
therefore render working / died / idle without ever opening the tracking
artifact — which is the coupling the projection exists to prevent.

### 4. The build advances without a tab polling it (criteria 5 + 6 + 7)

Both halves of the demand's "either/or", because either alone leaves a gap:

- **`run_build_drained`** — the route now drains: it keeps working until the
  build is genuinely blocked (a dispatched run still LAUNCHED, the pause
  observed, or every batch consolidated). Termination is "the last unit changed
  nothing on disk", which is exactly the set of states where continuing would
  spin; `max_units=200` is a backstop only (the whole build is ~45 units).
- **`BuildAdvancer.tick()`** — a background pass over the ledger, wired into the
  app's lifespan on a timer (`BUILD_ADVANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 15s in
  `default_app`, `0` disables, and `None`/off for every test's `create_app`, so
  the suite stays deterministic). It runs `tick` via `asyncio.to_thread` so a
  slow agent-runner probe never stalls request handling.

Both are pure loops over the **unchanged** one-unit `run_build`. That is the
design point, not an implementation detail: every invariant is held by
construction rather than re-implemented in a second place.

- **Pause-aware (criterion 6):** `pauseRequested` is still consulted in exactly
  one place — `_work_batch`'s boundary check, the instant a batch's last unit
  consolidates and before `currentBatch` advances past it. A drain stops there;
  the advancer additionally skips a mission with a live pause request before
  doing anything. It does *resume* once the owner clears the pause (it reads the
  live flag, not the stale on-disk one) — otherwise a resumed build would sit
  stuck until poked by hand, the very stall this removes.
- **Never advances the stage (criterion 6):** nothing here can; `run_build`
  can't, and these only call `run_build`. Asserted in tests at every level.
- **Idempotent (criterion 7):** repeated calls with nothing settled in between
  dispatch nothing new — verified explicitly, plus a full-build test asserting
  each of the 19 units is dispatched exactly once.
- The advancer **never starts** a build. A mission with no tracking artifact is
  skipped: the first `build-system` call is the owner's own act, and starting one
  unbidden would register an owner-visible `DesignSystem` entry nobody asked for.
  A `DispatchRunFailedError` inside a tick is swallowed rather than raised (there
  is no caller to 422) — the failure is already durably recorded and surfaced via
  `designSystemBuild.failure`.

### 5. Tests (criterion 8)

Suite 372 → **393, all green**. New file
`tests/test_build_dispatch_visibility.py` (19 tests) covers in-flight
(constitution and page), shape-parity with the other kinds, agent-runner
unreachable, and null for never-started / consolidated-batch /
consolidated-page / failed / paused / done; the failure projection for both a
batch-level and a page-level death, including that a retry clears it; drain
carrying a batch past a single page, idempotence, a full build dispatching each
unit exactly once, and pause honored at a boundary and not mid-batch; and the
advancer completing a build with no caller, skipping never-started, paused, and
done builds, and surviving a failing one. Two API-level tests in
`tests/test_api.py` assert `activeDispatch` over HTTP on the POST response, `GET
/missions/{id}` and `GET /missions`, and the failure path returning 422 with
`activeDispatch: null` and a populated `failure`.

Beyond the suite, the background advancer was verified against the real app
(TestClient + lifespan, 0.2s interval): after the constitution's run was settled
with **no further client call**, batch 0 consolidated and batch 1's first page
dispatched on its own, mission still at `system-gate`.

## Changed files

- `src/design_studio/domain/design_system_build.py` — `pending_build_dispatch`,
  `build_failure`, `run_build_drained`, `BuildAdvancer`, `failure` in the
  projection
- `src/design_studio/domain/dispatch_status.py` — the `system-gate` branch
- `src/design_studio/api.py` — route drains, lifespan-hosted advancer,
  `build_advance_interval_seconds` (create_app) / `BUILD_ADVANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`
  (`default_app`), module docstring
- `tests/test_build_dispatch_visibility.py` (new), `tests/test_api.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`

## For the coordinator / the dashboard

- The console can key its "agent working" tag off `activeDispatch.kind ===
  "build"` with no new rendering branch, and its retry affordance off
  `designSystemBuild.failure` being non-null.
- Nothing in the console needs to poll `build-system` per page any more. Polling
  `GET /missions/{id}` for display is still fine and now genuinely read-only with
  respect to build progress — the build moves whether or not anyone is looking.
- No `contracts` change was needed: mission responses are this repo's own
  unwrapped-dict shape (D015), and both new fields are additive.

`done` here is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates.

# Fulfillment report — expose the doctrine section each checklist item belongs to

## State before this session

Not shipped. `ChecklistItem` was `(key, text, source)`; `domain/regime.py`'s own module
comment said out loud that "the grouping is preserved here as ordering only, since
ChecklistItem has no group field." The demand's reading of the code was accurate in every
particular, including the line numbers.

## What was built

**`domain/regime.py`** — `ChecklistItem` gains `group: str` as a fourth field. Every one of
the 60 item constructions now names its section; the values were derived mechanically from
the `# -- Section --` markers already in the file, so the boundaries are exactly the ones
the demand quoted, not a re-reading of the doctrines.

| checklist | groups (in order) | items |
|---|---|---|
| inhabited-class | `core` (11), `resilience-and-trust` (9), `choreography-and-locale` (4) | 24 |
| atlas-class | `core-spatial-claim` (6), `geography` (3), `motion` (4), `interaction` (6), `choreography-and-resilience` (7) | 26 |
| console-class | `laws` (7) | 7 |
| system-gate | `system-pin` (3) | 3 |

**console-class declares one group, deliberately.** D036 §2 is a flat list of seven laws
with no sections of its own — the demand's "or a single group if it genuinely has no
sections" branch. Inventing three sections the source document does not have would put
policy in this repo that no doctrine backs.

**`group` is a slug, and there is also a `groupLabel`.** The acceptance criterion asks for
"stable machine-readable text suitable as a rendering key, not free-form prose that changes
when a doctrine is re-anchored" — so `group` is a slug (`core-spatial-claim`), and it will
not move when a heading is reworded. But the console's actual job is to *print a section
heading*, and titlecasing `core-spatial-claim` yields "Core Spatial Claim", not the
doctrine's "Core: the spatial claim". So each item also carries `groupLabel`, resolved
through `GROUP_LABELS` / `group_label()` in `regime.py`. This is one extra key beyond what
was asked for; it is additive and ignorable, and it keeps the prose heading on this side of
the wall — where the doctrine custodianship lives (D053) — instead of pushing a slug→prose
table into the console. Flagging it explicitly since it is scope the demand did not name.
If `dashboard` would rather render the slug itself, ignore the field.

**`api.py`** — `GET /missions/{id}/checklist` serializes `group` and `groupLabel` on every
item. The default (regime) path and the `?gate=system-gate` path now share one serializer,
so the two can no longer drift; the 400 for any other `?gate=` value is unchanged.

## Nothing else changed

The demand's central constraint was that a consumer ignoring the new field renders exactly
what it renders today. That is pinned by test, not by inspection:

- `test_groups_are_contiguous_runs_in_the_existing_order` asserts each group is a single
  contiguous run in the *existing* item order — i.e. grouping never implies a reorder.
- `test_counts_are_unchanged` — 24 / 26 / 7 / 3.
- `test_checklist_route_order_and_keys_are_unchanged` compares the route's emitted `key` and
  `source` sequences against the domain tuple, element for element.
- `test_group_slugs_are_machine_readable_rendering_keys` asserts every group is a lowercase,
  space-free slug with a label registered for it.

No item text, no key, no `source`, no count, no ordering was touched. No stage, gate, or
regime behaviour was touched — `required_keys` and `record_gate_outcome` still key off
`item.key` alone, so an existing gate record's `checklist` mapping remains valid as-is.

## Verification

`PYTHONPATH=src pytest` — **436 passed**, from the demand's stated 421 baseline (+15 from
`tests/test_checklist_groups.py`). No pre-existing test needed amending: the two API tests
that already asserted `{"key","text","source"} <= set(items[0])` used a subset check and
still pass unchanged, which is itself evidence the change is additive.

## For dashboard

Per-item shape is now:

```json
{"key": "navigation-follows-visible-edge",
 "text": "Does every navigation follow an edge that was visible before the click?",
 "source": "C1",
 "group": "core-spatial-claim",
 "groupLabel": "Core: the spatial claim"}
```

Group by `group` preserving array order and you get the five atlas sections in doctrine
order with no sorting step. `?gate=system-gate` behaves identically — one group,
`system-pin` — so the theme-gate workspace needs no per-gate branch.

`done` is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates.

# Fulfillment report — a send-back at the gate: a note, no verdict

## State before this session

**Not shipped.** Checked first, as instructed: `send_back` / `sendBack` appeared nowhere
in `src/`, only in the two demand files and the prior session's own notes. The prior
session (`.brain/sessions/2026-07-29_1741_...`, status `partial`) had opened a session
file and written no code — its `changes` list was empty and the tree was clean apart from
untracked `.brain` files.

Pre-work baseline: **450 passing**.

## What was built

**Domain** (`domain/mission.py`) — `SendBackRecord(gate, note, sent_back_at)`, frozen,
plus `Mission.send_backs: list[SendBackRecord]` and `Mission.send_back(note=..)`.

The record is a **third** append-only list, deliberately not a third `GateOutcome` value
and not an entry in `gate_records`. Its docstring makes the case in the same terms
`RewindRecord`'s already does, plus one this WU adds: `_owner_feedback_block` would
actively do the *wrong* thing if a send-back were a REJECTED-shaped record — it would fold
a complaint about the instrument into a generator's prompt as binding art direction, which
is precisely the false outcome the demand exists to avoid.

`send_back()` refuses first (empty note → `ValueError`; terminal → `SendBackRefusedError`;
not at a gate → `SendBackRefusedError`), then appends and moves `updated_at`. It never
assigns `self.stage`, appends no `GateRecord`, reads no checklist, and touches no port.
Note is stripped; whitespace-only is empty.

**Gate coverage** — all five `GATE_STAGES`, `system-gate` included. The D069 OQ6 question
that keeps `system-gate` out of `REWIND_TARGET_STAGES` does not arise here: a send-back
names the gate the mission is *already at* rather than jumping to one, so there is no
"which gates may be jumped back to" to rule on. Stated in the method's docstring so a later
reader doesn't mistake it for an oversight.

**Service** (`domain/service.py`) — `MissionService.send_back_gate(id, note=)`, the same
get/mutate/persist/emit shape as `rewind_mission`, and like it needing no `AgentRunnerPort`
(a send-back starts no dispatch and stops none). `_emit` is called with **no**
`gate_outcome` — there is no outcome to announce.

**API** (`api.py`) — `POST /missions/{id}/send-back`. `note` must be a non-empty string:
missing, `null`, non-string, or blank is a 400 raised by the route itself, never the 409
the domain raises for a well-formed request the mission's state refuses. The route reads
**only** `note` from the body — a client that sends a `checklist` anyway gets a normal
send-back with nothing checklist-shaped stored (test pins this).
`SendBackRefusedError` → 409 with `currentStage` + `reason`, mirroring `_rewind_refused`.
`_mission_to_dict` gains `sendBacks`.

**Ledger** (`adapters/ledger_sqlalchemy.py`) — nullable `send_backs_json`, picked up by the
existing `_ensure_columns` additive migration; `_send_backs_to_json` /
`_send_backs_from_json` alongside the rewind pair. NULL (every pre-existing row in the live
Postgres) reads back as `[]`.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
|---|---|
| Send-back endpoint, required non-empty note, 400 otherwise | `api.py` route; `test_post_send_back_without_a_usable_note_is_400` (5 body shapes) |
| Own append-only list, not `gate_records`, no third `GateOutcome` | `Mission.send_backs`; `test_send_back_leaves_the_stage_and_every_existing_record_untouched` |
| Record carries gate + note + timestamp | `SendBackRecord`; `test_send_back_records_the_gate_note_and_timestamp` |
| Stage unchanged, no dispatch started | `send_back()` never assigns `self.stage`; `test_post_send_back_records_it_and_projects_the_list`, `test_a_send_back_does_not_start_a_new_propose_round` |
| Note never reaches a dispatched agent | `test_a_send_back_note_never_reaches_a_dispatched_agent` — a poison string in the note, asserted absent from the prompt, and no `OWNER DIRECTION` block at all |
| No new propose round; `_rejected_since` unaffected | `test_a_send_back_does_not_start_a_new_propose_round` — consolidated round 1, send-back, re-`run_propose`, still exactly one dispatch |
| Legal at any current gate stage; 409 off-gate / terminal | `test_send_back_is_legal_at_every_gate_stage`, `..._from_a_non_gate_stage_is_refused`, `..._from_a_terminal_stage_is_refused`, and both API 409 tests |
| No checklist required or recorded | `test_send_back_does_not_require_a_complete_checklist`, `test_post_send_back_ignores_a_checklist_in_the_body` |
| `sendBacks` projected, empty for every existing mission | `test_every_mission_projects_send_backs_empty_by_default` (POST, GET one, GET list) |
| `GateRecord`/`GateOutcome`/checklist mapping unchanged | No edit to any of the three; the 450 pre-existing tests still pass unmodified |
| Suite green, baseline recorded | **474 passing** (baseline **450**, +24) |

## Notes for the origin

Two things the console half (`design-studio-20260728-dashboard-gate-send-back-control`,
raised the other way) can now rely on:

1. **`sendBacks[]` is a peer of `gateRecords` and `rewinds`, not a subtype of either.** A
   chronology renderer that already merges the first two by timestamp gets the third the
   same way, and its entries have no `outcome` field to accidentally render as a decision.
2. **The response after a send-back is a normal mission body with an unchanged `stage`.**
   Nothing in it says "settled" — the mission is still at its gate, and the needs-you queue
   should keep it. The most recent reason is `sendBacks[-1].note`.

It records a decision and dispatches nothing; the NEXT POST /missions/{id}/propose starts a fresh round, so the two acts stay separable exactly like unblock/build-system
Refuses 409 while the tracked run is still 'launched' (message names request-pause/abort) and once it is 'finished' (message names rejecting the gate as the way to re-roll a round the owner dislikes)

Also refuses 409 when nothing was ever dispatched, when the round is already abandoned, and when agent-runner is unreachable so 'is it still live?' cannot be answered -- 'I could not ask' is not 'it is dead'

# Fulfillment report — recovering a failed dispatch round

## The wedge

A propose round whose agent-runner run ended `failed`/`stopped`, or vanished
from agent-runner entirely, was a permanent dead end. `run_propose` only ever
supersedes a round by consolidating it first and seeing a gate rejection land
after — and a dead round can never consolidate. So every later `POST
/propose` re-probed the same dead run id and re-raised the same
`DispatchRunFailedError` (422), forever. Mission
`e8e4b3e5-ef0c-46b1-8a76-57c4126f219d` had been sitting in exactly that state
on round 2 since 18:23 UTC.

## What shipped

`POST /missions/{id}/propose/abandon-round`, body `{"note": "..."}` optional.

Precedent followed deliberately: `build-system/unblock` **records the owner's
decision and does not do the work**. This route does the same — it marks the
round abandoned and dispatches nothing. The fresh round is started by the
next ordinary `POST /missions/{id}/propose` call. That keeps "I accept this
round is dead" and "spend money on a new one" as two separate owner acts, and
it means the fresh round goes through the one code path that already knows
how to build a propose prompt.

**Refusals** (all 409 `RoundAbandonRefusedError`, with `runId` and `reason`
alongside `error` in the body — deliberately *not* 422, which is the code the
wedge itself reports with, so the console can tell "your recovery attempt was
refused" from "the round is still dead"):

| condition | message names the right tool |
|---|---|
| run still `launched` | `request-pause` / `abort` — this is not a way to abandon a live agent |
| run already `finished` | call `/propose` to read it back; to replace a round you dislike, **reject the gate** |
| nothing ever dispatched | call `/propose` to dispatch the first round |
| already abandoned | call `/propose` to dispatch a fresh round |
| agent-runner unreachable | retry once it answers |

The unreachable case is a refusal on purpose. The whole point of the
`launched` guard is that a live agent is never abandoned behind its back, and
"I could not ask" is not "it is dead". A run agent-runner has genuinely
*forgotten* (`get_run` → `None`) is a different thing and **is** accepted,
recorded as `abandonedRunState: "unknown"`.

**Recorded, never deleted.** In the spirit of this module's own preservation
rule (round N>1 gets its own sibling directory rather than overwriting round
1 — "a rejected round is a RECORD"), the abandoned round stays in
`propose-dispatch.json`'s `rounds` list exactly where it was, keeping its
round number, its `dispatch.runId` and its `proposalsDir`, and gains:

```json
"abandonedAt": "2026-07-29T19:26:33.138489+00:00",
"abandonedRunId": "a578fde5-e317-4de2-92a7-31120847d3c4",
"abandonedRunState": "failed",
"abandonedReason": "dispatched run ended in state 'failed'",
"abandonedNote": "<the owner's own words, verbatim>"
```

`consolidatedAt` stays `null` — a round that produced nothing is never
dressed up as one that did.

**Nothing renumbered, nothing clobbered.** The abandoned round keeps its own
number, so the fresh round is `N+1` and writes to `proposals-round-<N+1>/`,
a directory no earlier round has ever used. `ArtifactsRegistry` is
append-only and untouched here; `rounds_summary`/`latest_round_dirname` derive
from registered MOCK paths, so an abandoned round (which registered nothing)
never inflates a count or shadows a real round in coverage. One deliberate
refinement: the fresh round's prompt is handed only the previous rounds that
actually **consolidated** — pointing an agent at an empty directory as "what
was already rejected, read it first" would be a lie.

**`activeDispatch` clears.** `find_pending_dispatch` now treats
`abandonedAt` exactly as it already treats `clone`'s `failedAt`, so the dead
run stops being reported and stops being probed the moment it is abandoned.

## Console legibility — answering the criterion directly

**`activeDispatch.state == 'failed'` alone is sufficient. No new field is
needed and none was added.** `GET /missions/{id}` on the wedged mission
already returned, before anything was clicked:

```json
"activeDispatch": {"runId": "a578fde5-…", "kind": "propose", "state": "failed"}
```

The condition for offering the control is `activeDispatch != null &&
activeDispatch.kind == 'propose' && activeDispatch.state in {'failed',
'stopped', 'unknown'}`.

Two notes on that set:

- `'stopped'` belongs with `'failed'`: same terminal, same wedge, same
  remedy — the service accepts either.
- `'unknown'` is genuinely ambiguous in the projection: it means *either* the
  run vanished from agent-runner (accepted) *or* agent-runner could not be
  reached (refused). The console should still offer the control on
  `'unknown'`; if it was merely an outage it gets a 409 whose `error` says so
  in words, which is a better outcome than hiding the only exit from a
  mission that may be permanently wedged. Distinguishing the two before the
  click would require a live probe the projection deliberately does not make.

`'launched'` and `'finished'` must **not** offer it; both are refused
server-side regardless.

## Scope — which steps this covers, stated up front

| step | covered? | why |
|---|---|---|
| `propose` | **yes** | the demand's minimum, and the live wedge |
| `clone` | **not needed** | `CloneService` already records `failedAt` on a dead attempt and re-dispatches a fresh one on the next call — it self-heals; `find_pending_dispatch` already reflects that |
| `build-system` | **not needed** | has its own precedent route, `POST /missions/{id}/build-system/unblock` |
| `theme-interview` | **NO — same wedge exists** | see below |
| `content-interview` | **NO — same wedge exists** | see below |

Both interview steps carry the identical defect and are **not** fixed here:
`ThemeInterviewService.run_theme_interview` and
`InterviewService.run_interview` raise `InterviewRunFailedError` (422) on a
`failed`/`stopped`/vanished run, and their single-slot tracking files
(`theme-interview-questionnaire.json`, `questionnaire.json`) have no
round/attempt shape at all, so the same dead run id is re-probed on every
later call with no way out. Fixing them is a genuinely different change —
those files need an attempt list before there is anything to mark abandoned,
or the existing single slot needs to be replaceable — and doing it
speculatively alongside a `propose` fix would have meant reshaping two live
tracking artifacts with no live case to verify against. Named here rather
than left to be discovered: **if a mission wedges at `theme-interview` or
`content-interview`, this route does not help, and a follow-up demand should
raise it.**

## Live verification — mission `e8e4b3e5-ef0c-46b1-8a76-57c4126f219d`

Against the running container (`runtime-design-studio-1`, rebuilt from this
commit), not a fixture:

1. `POST /propose` → **422** `dispatched run 'a578fde5-…' did not finish
   successfully: run ended in state 'failed'` — the wedge, reproduced.
2. `GET /missions/{id}` → `activeDispatch.state == "failed"`, `kind ==
   "propose"` — legible before any click.
3. `POST /propose/abandon-round` with a note → **200**, full `Mission` body,
   `stage` unchanged at `theme-gate`, `activeDispatch` now `null`.
4. `propose-dispatch.json` on disk: round 1 (consolidated, 2026-07-29T17:33)
   untouched; round 2 retained in place with `abandonedAt`,
   `abandonedRunId: a578fde5-…`, `abandonedRunState: "failed"`,
   `abandonedReason`, and the owner's note.
5. `POST /propose/abandon-round` again → **409** "round 2 was already
   abandoned at … — call POST /missions/{id}/propose to dispatch a fresh
   round".
6. The same route against a `closed` mission → **409** stage mismatch;
   against an unknown id → **404**.

**Deliberately not done live:** step 7, actually calling `POST /propose` to
dispatch round 3. That spends a real agent-runner session and GPU/ai-gateway
credits on the owner's own live mission, which is the owner's call, not this
session's. The mission is now unwedged and ready for it; the re-dispatch path
itself is covered end-to-end by tests (a fresh round dispatches, lands in
`proposals-round-N+1/`, and consolidates).

## Tests

Pre-work baseline: **505 passed**. After: **516 passed** (+11), full suite,
no test skipped or weakened.

**Pre-existing flake, disclosed rather than papered over:**
`tests/test_design_system_adapters.py::test_event_sink_carries_change_reason_
for_each_transition` fails intermittently (roughly 1 run in 4) on `assert
[c["payload"]["change"] for c in captured] == ["created", "validated",
"release", "retired"]` — `StateFeedEventSink` emits on background threads, so
arrival ORDER is not guaranteed and the assertion pins it. This is **not
introduced here**: reproduced the same way on the pre-work commit `fbe7fa5`
in a clean worktree (1 failure in 5 full-suite runs, same test, same
assertion). Untouched by this change — no code path in this WU goes near that
sink. Left as-is rather than fixed opportunistically; the fix is to assert the
multiset of changes, or to have the sink preserve order, which is a decision
for whoever owns that adapter.

- `tests/test_abandon_round.py` (8) — service level: the record-and-redispatch
  happy path; abandoning round 2 while round 1's consolidated files and
  registrations stay byte-for-byte intact and round 3 gets its own dir; the
  vanished run; refusal while `launched`; refusal when `finished` (both before
  and after consolidation); refusal on an unreachable agent-runner; refusal
  with no round and when already abandoned; wrong-stage refusal.
- `tests/test_abandon_round_api.py` (3) — HTTP level: the 422 wedge repeated
  twice, `activeDispatch` legibility before the click, the 200 with the full
  `Mission` body (same key set as `GET /missions/{id}`) and `activeDispatch`
  cleared, a genuinely fresh dispatch after, and the 409 refusals.

## Files

- `src/design_studio/domain/proposition.py` — `abandon_round`, plus
  `run_propose`'s new restart-on-abandoned branch and the
  consolidated-rounds-only prompt filter
- `src/design_studio/domain/errors.py` — `RoundAbandonRefusedError`
- `src/design_studio/domain/dispatch_status.py` — `abandonedAt` clears
  `activeDispatch`
- `src/design_studio/api.py` — the route + its 409 handler
- `tests/test_abandon_round.py`, `tests/test_abandon_round_api.py`

Contracts, the agent-runner port and its adapter are unchanged; no target
repo was written to; no gate was advanced or skipped.

shipped: POST /missions/{id}/gates/{gate} accepts an optional referenceImages array on a REJECTED outcome -- [{filename, dataBase64, contentType?}], same JSON content type as today
png/jpeg/webp only, decided from the file's own magic bytes; a wrong type, a lying extension, or a declared contentType contradicting the bytes is a 400
5 MiB per-file cap and 6-per-rejection count cap, each named verbatim in the refusal message
Filenames sanitised; a path separator, '..' or an absolute path is REFUSED (400), never scrubbed -- plus a resolve+ancestry check on the write side

Stored at references/<gate>-rejection-<n>/<NN>-<name> under the mission's own artifacts subtree and registered under the new ArtifactKind.REFERENCE -- served by the EXISTING per-mission artifact routes, no new read path; .jpg/.jpeg/.webp added to the media-type map

The OWNER DIRECTION block names each image by ABSOLUTE HOST PATH via PropositionService._to_host_path -- the same translation the round's output paths get -- with an explicit OPEN AND STUDY instruction, not a bare path

# Fulfillment report — reference imagery travels as pictures

## State before this session

**Not shipped.** Checked first, as instructed: `reference`/`attachment` appeared nowhere
in `src/` outside an unrelated `Content-Disposition` comment; `ArtifactKind` had no image
kind; `_owner_feedback_block` folded in notes only. A prior session file
(`.brain/sessions/2026-07-29_1942_...`, status `partial`) had been opened for this same
task with an empty `changes` list and no code written.

Pre-work baseline: **474 passing**.

## What shipped

New module `src/design_studio/domain/reference_images.py` owns validation, safe naming,
path planning and the write; everything else is a small additive change at an existing
seam:

| Layer | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `domain/reference_images.py` | new — sniff/validate/sanitise/plan/write |
| `domain/artifacts.py` | `ArtifactKind.REFERENCE` |
| `domain/mission.py` | `GateRecord.reference_images: tuple[str, ...] = ()`, recorded verbatim |
| `domain/service.py` | registers the paths under `REFERENCE` in the same save as the decision |
| `domain/proposition.py` | the imagery lines + carry-forward rule in `_owner_feedback_block`; `resolve_reference_image` threaded from `PropositionService` |
| `adapters/ledger_sqlalchemy.py` | `referenceImages` written always, read with a `.get` default |
| `api.py` | request parsing, the 400 handler, the projection field, jpeg/webp media types |
| `errors.py` | `ReferenceImageRefusedError` (400, `reason` surfaced separately) |

### Two decisions worth stating

**Base64 in the existing JSON body, not multipart.** A multipart variant of
`POST /missions/{id}/gates/{gate}` would change the content type every existing caller
posts. The demand's own scope note asks for additive; this is the additive shape.
Dashboard's form should post:

```json
{ "outcome": "rejected", "notes": "...", "checklist": {},
  "referenceImages": [ { "filename": "map.png", "dataBase64": "<...>", "contentType": "image/png" } ] }
```

`contentType` is optional and, when given, must agree with the bytes. Caps to mirror
client-side: **5 MiB per file, 6 per rejection** (`MAX_BYTES_PER_IMAGE` /
`MAX_IMAGES_PER_REJECTION`). Refusals return `{"error": ..., "reason": ...}` with 400 and
the cap stated in `reason`, so the form can show it rather than a bare failure.

**Order of operations.** Attachments are validated and decoded *before* the mission is
touched, the decision is recorded/registered/persisted *before* any byte is written. A
gate decision the domain refuses (wrong stage, missing artifact) therefore leaves no
orphan files behind — pinned by `test_route_refuses_a_bad_attachment_with_400_and_records_nothing`.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Accepts images on REJECTED, stores under the mission's subtree | `test_rejection_with_imagery_stores_registers_and_serves_it` |
| Registered under a kind of its own, existing routes serve them | same test — asserts `artifacts["reference"]`, a 200 from `GET /missions/{id}/artifacts/{path}` with `image/png`, and byte equality |
| png/jpeg/webp; anything else 400; caps enforced and stated | 6 validation tests, incl. the lying-extension and contradicting-`contentType` cases |
| Filenames sanitised, traversal refused | `test_a_path_traversal_filename_is_refused_never_scrubbed` (5 shapes), `test_route_refuses_traversal_and_writes_nothing_outside_the_mission` |
| Absolute host path + open-and-study instruction | `test_prompt_names_every_image_by_absolute_host_path_with_an_instruction` — asserts the host path, asserts the container path is *absent*, asserts the instruction, asserts it sits inside the direction block |
| Carry-forward, oldest first, attributed, same tie-break | `test_images_from_every_prior_rejection_carry_forward_oldest_first` |
| DispatchRequest / port / adapter / contracts pin unchanged | none of those files are in the diff |
| Byte-identical block with no attachments; existing data reads back unchanged | `test_a_rejection_with_no_imagery_leaves_the_direction_block_byte_identical`, `test_a_gate_record_written_before_this_wu_still_loads`, `test_reference_images_survive_a_ledger_round_trip` |
| Send-back out of scope, gains no attachment path | `test_send_back_gains_no_attachment_path` |
| Suite green, baseline recorded | 505 passing, baseline 474 |

## The one criterion I could NOT close: the live end-to-end dispatch

**Not done — structurally blocked from inside this session, not skipped.**

`scripts/verify_reference_imagery_dispatch.py` is written, committed and ready. It builds
a real mission at `theme-gate`, generates a genuine PNG whose palette (`#2E1A47`,
`#E8FF3A`, `#FF5C8A`, as sidebar/top-bar/body) appears nowhere in the prompt or the
brief, attaches it to a rejection, dispatches the real propose round through the live
`agent-runner`, polls to a terminal state, and greps the run's **own output files** for
those hexes. If they appear, the agent opened the image — there is nowhere else they
could have come from. That is the bar the demand asks for, and a path-in-prompt assertion
does not meet it.

Running it returned **`409 {"error":"a session is already live for repo: design-studio"}`**.
agent-runner enforces one live session per repo, and *this fulfilment session is that
session*. A real dispatch for `repo: "design-studio"` cannot be launched from inside it,
and dispatching under some other repo's name to dodge the lock would launch an agent in a
sibling repo's working directory — which this repo's standing orders forbid.

**Owner: one command closes it, once this session's run has ended:**

```
cd design-studio && PYTHONPATH=src .venv/Scripts/python scripts/verify_reference_imagery_dispatch.py
```

It prints the run id, the files produced, which of the image's hexes appear in them, and

end-to-end verified — the coordinator should weigh that when validating.

already raised to `dashboard` and was sequenced behind this one. The wire format, the two
caps and the 400 shape it needs are stated under "Two decisions worth stating" above.

# Fulfillment report — bounding the propose dispatch prompt

## State before the work

Not shipped by any prior session. `build_propose_prompt` →
`_owner_feedback_block` folded **every** rejected `theme-gate` note into the
next round's prompt verbatim, oldest first — deliberately, and that rule is
still correct (a later rejection usually refines an earlier one rather than
replacing it). What was missing was any bound on the result. Real owner notes
run 12–13 KB, so the block grew linearly in the number of rejections with no
ceiling anywhere and no record of the assembled size.

Measured on mission `e8e4b3e5-ef0c-46b1-8a76-57c4126f219d` (plantpal,
atlas-class), fetched live from the running service and replayed through
`build_propose_prompt` with its own on-disk brief: two recorded `theme-gate`
rejections of 12 665 and 12 826 chars → a **26 506-char direction block**
inside a **33 059-char prompt**. A fifth rejection would have put the block
alone past 60 KB.

Pre-work test baseline: **538 passing**.

## What shipped

### The rule, unchanged where it must be

The latest rejection is the one the prompt itself declares binding — *"if
entries disagree, the LAST one is binding"*. It stays **inline and complete**,
at any size, and is not counted against any budget. Truncating the sentence an
agent is instructed to obey is a correctness regression, so the size win is
taken entirely from the superseded entries.

### The budgets (all named, all with their rationale in the module)

| Name | Value | What it bounds |
|---|---|---|
| `PROMPT_BUDGET_CHARS` | 60 000 | the **whole assembled prompt**; over it → a warning in this service's log, then dispatch |
| `_SUPERSEDED_DIRECTION_INLINE_BUDGET_CHARS` | 4 000 | the superseded portion's inline size; over it → offload |
| `_SUPERSEDED_EXCERPT_TOTAL_CHARS` | 2 400 | total inline excerpt once offloaded, split evenly |
| `_SUPERSEDED_EXCERPT_MAX_ENTRIES` | 3 | how many superseded entries get an excerpt at all |

So the guaranteed shape is *fixed frame + ≤4 000 (or 2 400 of excerpts once
offloaded) + the latest note verbatim* — **constant in the number of rejected
rounds**, which is the growth the demand exists to stop. A *total* excerpt
allowance rather than a per-entry cap is the point: a per-entry cap would grow
with N again.

### The offload

`_superseded_offload_lines` writes every superseded entry's full text — note
plus the reference imagery that rejection attached, already host-path
translated — to
`<mission>/directions/round-N-superseded-direction.md`, registers it under the
new `ArtifactKind.DIRECTION`, and names it in the prompt by **absolute host
path** through `PropositionService._to_host_path`, the same translation
`proposals_dir` / `brief_path` / reference imagery already get. Registration
saves the mission immediately rather than waiting for `run_propose`'s later
save: a still-`launched` dispatch returns before that save, and a file the
prompt already names must be servable by the existing artifact routes.

`DIRECTION` is its own kind rather than `MOCK` on purpose — `rounds_summary`
and `CoverageService` read the `MOCK` list, and a direction file registered
there would be counted as a proposition.

Inline, the offload leaves the path **plus** a bounded excerpt of the most
recent entries **plus** the instruction:

> READ THAT FILE before you design anything. Those entries are still binding,
> oldest first, exactly as if they were printed here — they are in a file only
> because they are long, not because they are optional. Where any of them
> disagrees with the LATEST direction printed below, the latest one wins.

A bare path fails for exactly the reason a bare *image* path failed in the
2026-07-29 imagery demand: an agent reads a naked filename as provenance, not
as homework. Superseded entries too old to excerpt are counted out loud
("N earlier rejection(s) are not excerpted here at all…"), never silently
dropped.

### Nothing changes below the budget

`_rejection_entry_lines` was extracted so the inline and offloaded renderings
are literally the same code, and the offload branch engages only when there is
a superseded entry **and** the superseded text exceeds its ceiling. A mission
with zero or one rejection therefore produces a **byte-identical** prompt —
tested with a 13 KB note, which stays inline in full — as does any mission
whose superseded history still fits 4 000 chars. `offload_superseded` is an
optional callback, so `_owner_feedback_block` remains callable as a pure unit;
without it an over-budget history renders in full rather than being truncated.

### The recorded size, and what is *not* the bound

`promptChars` is written onto the round's entry in `propose-dispatch.json` at
dispatch time, so a future oversized prompt is diagnosable from the tracking
artifact alone without re-reading agent-runner's run record. The guard is
checked against the **whole assembled string**, never one section — a prompt
made huge by the brief or the pinned-system excerpt would slip past a
per-section check. It **warns and dispatches anyway**: refusing a large prompt
would be a worse failure than sending it, and this service's standing
invariant is that only the owner's gate decision stops a mission.

The module states plainly that Windows' 32767-char `CreateProcess` cap is
**not** the relevant bound — agent-runner delivers the prompt on **stdin** as
of its commit `6d13cbb`, live-verified at 60 KB — and that the real reason to
bound this prompt is the reader's attention, not the OS's argv limit. 32767
appears in the file only inside that comment, and
`test_windows_argv_cap_is_not_used_as_the_bound` pins it, because hardcoding
32767 is exactly the plausible-but-wrong fix.

`_SYSTEM_SURFACE_EXCERPT_MAX_CHARS` (4 000 per pinned-system file) is
untouched — already bounded, and not what this demand is about.

## Verification on mission `e8e4b3e5`'s real data

Its two recorded rejections, replayed through `build_propose_prompt` with its
own brief and an atlas-class regime:

| | direction block | whole prompt |
|---|---|---|
| before | 26 506 | 33 059 |
| after | 16 921 | 23 474 |

The offloaded file is 13 067 chars. The 16 921 that remain are almost entirely
the **latest** 12 826-char direction, inline and complete, as required — the
block no longer grows with a third, fourth or fifth rejection.

## Boundaries held

- `DispatchRequest`, `AgentRunnerPort`, the HTTP adapter and the contracts pin
  are all unchanged — this is prompt composition plus one new local
  `ArtifactKind` value.
- No write to any target repo; no file written outside this repo's own
  artifacts store.
- No gate skipped, no stage advanced.

## Tests

`tests/test_prompt_size_budget.py`, 10 tests: byte-identity at 0 and 1
rejections (parametrized) and for a short history; the latest direction inline
and complete while the superseded ones move; offload written, registered under
`DIRECTION` and not `MOCK`, named by absolute host path with excerpt and
instruction; two-vs-eight-rejection growth bounded by the excerpt allowance;
`promptChars` recorded; the guard checked on the whole prompt and warning-only;
32767 not used as the bound; superseded imagery travelling with its note.

Suite: **548 passing** (baseline 538, +10).

shipped: domain/dispatch_recovery.py -- the shared dead-dispatch recovery both interview stages use, with the mechanism choice justified in its module docstring against the two existing precedents

content-interview self-heals: the call that finds its tracked run dead records the death and raises as before; the NEXT ordinary POST /missions/{id}/content-interview re-dispatches instead of re-probing the corpse
theme-interview self-heals identically -- same branch in the same place, same helper, same fields, same tests; the two stages were fixed together, never one now and one later

Mechanism chosen DELIBERATELY: clone.py's self-heal ('retry = re-dispatch'), NOT proposition.py's owner route (abandon_round) -- an interview retry is mechanically the same interview, so there is no decision for an owner to make; no third shape was invented
The live-run guard abandon_round enforces is preserved: a run still 'launched' is never re-dispatched or discarded behind its own back -- repeat calls stay plain polls, no death mark, no re-dispatch

RECORDED, never deleted: the dead dispatch keeps its original dispatch.runId and dispatchedAt and gains failedAt / failedRunState / failedReason -- the same three facts propose-dispatch.json records as abandonedAt / abandonedRunState / abandonedReason

On re-dispatch the fully-annotated dead dispatch is retired into a deadDispatches list (oldest first) and the fresh run becomes dispatch -- every dead run the mission ever had stays in the artifact with its id and cause of death
Healthy paths byte-identical to before: a first-ever call and a call while the run is 'launched' or 'finished' write no new keys at all (asserted by exact-key-set tests at both stages)
find_pending_dispatch clears activeDispatch to null for a dead interview dispatch -- the same posture it already took for clone's failedAt and propose's abandonedAt; no new API field, no new endpoint

tests/test_dead_interview_dispatch.py (22) -- both stages x all three dead-run cases (failed, stopped, agent-runner has no such run), plus launched-guard, first-ever-call, finished-path, same-questions-on-retry and activeDispatch coverage
Suite green at 538 passing (pre-work baseline 515 passing + 1 pre-existing order-dependent flake, unrelated -- see 'Baseline' below)
Recovery story after this change: clone is NO LONGER the only self-healing stage -- content-interview and theme-interview now match it; theme-gate and system-gate keep their explicit owner routes
