# Fulfillment report — the dead interview dispatch wedge

## State before this session

Not shipped. The `dashboard-20260729-design-studio-recover-a-failed-dispatch-round`
report and CHANGELOG entry both said so explicitly: "`theme-interview`/
`content-interview` have the same wedge and are **not** covered". Verified in
code before touching anything — both `InterviewService.run_interview` and
`ThemeInterviewService.run_theme_interview` read the questionnaire, took its
`dispatch.runId`, and raised `InterviewRunFailedError` on every dead-run poll
with no branch that could ever supersede that run id. The only routes forward
were hand-editing `questionnaire.json` / `theme-interview-questionnaire.json`
or `POST /missions/{id}/abort`.

## Mechanism: `clone.py`'s self-heal, chosen over `abandon_round`

The demand required picking one of the two precedents already in the repo and
justifying it. The choice is **clone's self-heal**.

- `clone.py` (spec §2: "Failure → the stage stays, retry = re-dispatch
  (idempotent, like interview polling)"): the poll that finds a dead run marks
  it `failedAt` and raises; the next call sees the mark and dispatches a fresh
  attempt.
- `proposition.py`'s `abandon_round`: an explicit owner-invoked endpoint that
  records a decision and dispatches nothing.

An interview re-dispatch is *mechanically identical* to the dispatch that
died: the same fixed question set at `theme-interview`, the same stored
questions at `content-interview`, the same read-only prompt into the same
repo, no numbered output directory that could collide, and no side effect in
the target repo at all. There is nothing an owner could usefully decide
differently, so routing them through a second endpoint would be ceremony with
no decision behind it.

`abandon_round` earns its owner route for the opposite reasons: a propose
round is a *creative deliverable the owner gates*, its rounds are numbered and
carried forward into later prompts as "what was already rejected", and "roll
another round" is a judgement call. Re-asking a repo the same read-only
questions is not. Spec §2's own wording — "retry = re-dispatch (idempotent,
**like interview polling**)" — already named the interview stages as the model
clone was copying; this fix just gives them the retry half of it.

No third shape was invented. The recovery is 4 small functions in
`domain/dispatch_recovery.py`, called from the same position in both services.

## What the artifact records

The demand's rule was: record, never delete, matching `propose-dispatch.json`.

On the call that discovers the death, the questionnaire's `dispatch` is
annotated **in place** — it keeps `runId` and `dispatchedAt` and gains:

| field | mirrors |
|---|---|
| `failedAt` | `abandonedAt` |
| `failedRunState` (`"unknown"` for the vanished case) | `abandonedRunState` |
| `failedReason` | `abandonedReason` |

`failedAt` rather than `abandonedAt` for the name because this is clone's
mechanism and the field is not only a record — it is the flag the next call's
self-heal branch reads, exactly as in `clone-dispatch.json`.

On the next call, that fully-annotated dead dispatch is appended to a
`deadDispatches` list (oldest first) and the fresh run becomes `dispatch`.
Nothing is removed, nothing overwritten: a mission that lost three runs at
`content-interview` ends up with three dated death records and one live
dispatch. There is no `abandonedNote` counterpart because nobody is asked for
one — that is the whole point of choosing self-heal.

## Guards preserved

- **Live run:** `is_dead` is only ever consulted for a dispatch already
  *marked*, and a mark is only ever written by the poll's terminal-state
  branch, which a `launched` run never reaches. A `launched` run is therefore
  structurally un-re-dispatchable, the same invariant `abandon_round` enforces
  with a 409. Asserted at both stages.
- **First-ever call and healthy polls:** unchanged, and asserted by exact
  key-set equality (`{targetRepo, generatedAt, questions, dispatch}` with
  `dispatch == {runId, dispatchedAt}`), so a future accidental key leak into
  the healthy path fails a test.
- **The 422 still happens once.** The call that discovers the death raises
  `InterviewRunFailedError` with the identical reason string as before, so any
  console already showing that error keeps showing it; what changed is that
  the *following* call moves forward instead of repeating it.
- **`activeDispatch`:** `find_pending_dispatch` now returns `None` for a
  `failedAt` interview dispatch, matching what it already did for clone's
  failed attempt and propose's abandoned round. A dead run is no longer
  reported as if something were live behind it.

## The repo's recovery story, in one place

Stated plainly, as the demand asked:

| stage | dead-dispatch recovery |
|---|---|
| `clone` | self-heal (`failedAt` → next `run_clone` re-dispatches) |
| `content-interview` | **self-heal (new, 2026-07-30)** |
| `theme-interview` | **self-heal (new, 2026-07-30)** |
| `theme-gate` (propose) | explicit owner route: `POST .../propose/abandon-round` |
| `system-gate` (build) | explicit owner route: `POST .../build-system/unblock` |

So: **`clone` is no longer the only self-healing stage — the two interview
stages now match it.** The split is principled rather than historical: stages
whose retry is mechanically identical self-heal; stages whose retry is a
judgement call about a gated deliverable ask the owner.

## Tests

`tests/test_dead_interview_dispatch.py`, 22 tests. Both stages are driven
through one small `StageUnderTest` description and the **same parametrized
bodies**, deliberately — a future change that heals only one stage breaks half
this file.

Per stage × all three dead-run cases (`failed`, `stopped`, vanished from
agent-runner):
- the discovering call raises, and the death is recorded with the original run
  id intact plus all three fields;
- the next call re-dispatches (one new dispatch, mission still at the stage);
- the dead dispatch is retired into `deadDispatches`, never deleted, and the
  live dispatch is the fresh run with no `failedAt`;
- the re-dispatched run then consolidates and advances the mission normally —
  the recovery is a real route forward, not just a nicer error.

Per stage, once: the `launched` guard (three repeat polls, zero dispatches,
zero recovery fields), first-ever-call key sets, the `finished` path untouched,
the retry's prompt byte-equal to the original, and `activeDispatch` clearing
and re-arming across the recovery.

## Baseline

Pre-work: **515 passed, 1 failed** —
`tests/test_design_system_adapters.py::test_event_sink_carries_change_reason_for_each_transition`,
which passes in isolation and fails under the full run: a pre-existing
ordering race in `StateFeedEventSink`'s background emitter (asserted event
order `created, validated, release, retired` came back with `release` at index
1). Unrelated to this demand, untouched by it, and it passed in the post-work
runs. Flagged here rather than fixed, since fixing an async event-sink
ordering race is its own piece of work with its own scope.

Post-work: **538 passed** (`PYTHONPATH=src pytest`), +23 (22 new tests, and
the flake passing).

## Not done

- **No new endpoint, deliberately.** The recovery rides the two existing
  stage-advance calls. If the dashboard would rather have an explicit
  "retry interview" button, that is a one-line alias over the existing call
  and worth its own demand — but nothing is blocked without it, since the
  console's existing "advance this stage" control already performs it.
- **The `StateFeedEventSink` ordering flake** described above.

_GATE_REJECTION_SEMANTICS (domain/mission.py, beside _GATE_ARTIFACT_REQUIREMENTS) declares for ALL FIVE gates whether rejecting starts a new round, what it actually does, and the remedy where it starts nothing: theme-gate/system-gate iterate; coverage-gate/plan-gate/feel-gate are advisory with rewind named

POST /missions/{id}/gates/{gate} with outcome=rejected at an advisory gate returns an additive `notice` block (kind, gate, effect, remedy) in the response to the very call that recorded the decision -- absent on every approval and on both gates that do iterate

OWNER RULING 2 (review surface): design-studio emits the rendered view, NOT the console. POST /coverage also writes matrix.html, POST /plan also writes plan.html -- domain/review_view.py, one mechanism and one page skeleton for both gates

The views are rendered from the dict just built, never re-read from disk, so the JSON artifact and its view can never describe different runs; they are served by the EXISTING GET /missions/{id}/artifacts/{path} route, so no new read path exists anywhere

No second gate->step table: gate_decision_context() reads the existing _GATE_ARTIFACT_REQUIREMENTS, and GateArtifactMissingError's refusal message still reads the same map, unchanged
feel-gate untouched: still deliberately outside _GATE_ARTIFACT_REQUIREMENTS, no artifact invented for it (pinned by test); only its rejection semantics are now stated

Verified against live on-disk artifacts: matrix.json/plan.json from missions 8991305d, bd3f8e95 and e8e4b3e5 (the mission this demand was found on) all render as views with no modification to the JSON

# Fulfilment report — `dashboard-20260730-design-studio-gate-iteration-and-reviewable-artifacts`

- **Demand:** `demands/2026-07-30-design-studio-gate-iteration-and-reviewable-artifacts.md`
- **Repo:** design-studio · **Date:** 2026-07-30 · **Claim:** done (the coordinator validates; this is not a self-certification)

## The two owner decisions this demand asked for

Both were put to the owner before any code was written, and both were ruled on 2026-07-30.

### 1. Rejection at `coverage-gate` / `plan-gate` — **advisory, with the remedy named**

**Chosen deliberately, as the demand's third criterion requires.** `CoverageService` and
`PlanService` stay pure deterministic derivations: the cost `coverage.py`'s own docstring
declined — a second, round-versioned history to reconcile against the append-only proposals
history — is still declined. What changes is that the rejection is no longer recorded in
silence.

- `_GATE_REJECTION_SEMANTICS` (`domain/mission.py`, beside `_GATE_ARTIFACT_REQUIREMENTS`)
  declares for **all five** gates whether rejecting starts a new round, what it actually does,
  and the remedy where it starts nothing. `theme-gate`/`system-gate`: new round.
  `coverage-gate`/`plan-gate`/`feel-gate`: advisory, remedy = rewind to the gate that owns the
  inputs.
- `POST /missions/{id}/gates/{gate}` with `outcome: rejected` at an advisory gate returns an
  additive `notice` block (`kind`, `gate`, `effect`, `remedy`) **in the response to the very
  call that recorded the decision**. Absent on every approval and on both gates that do
  iterate, so a console that ignores it behaves exactly as before.

### 2. The reviewable artifact — **design-studio emits it** (not the console)

`POST /coverage` now also writes `matrix.html`; `POST /plan` also writes `plan.html`. Rendered
by the new `domain/review_view.py` from the dict just built (never re-read from disk, so the
JSON and the view can never describe different runs), and served by the **existing**
`GET /missions/{id}/artifacts/{path}` route — no new read path anywhere. One mechanism, both
gates, as the demand's fifth criterion asked.

## Criterion-by-criterion

| # | Criterion | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Each gate declares in one place whether rejecting starts a round | `_GATE_REJECTION_SEMANTICS`, all five gates |
| 2 | A non-iterating gate states that plainly in its own response | `notice` on the gate route's rejection response, naming the rewind remedy |
| 3 | A rejection there is never silently discarded — choose one and state it | Chosen: **advisory-only, remedy named** (above). The record is still appended to the mission's history for the owner |
| 4 | The matrix is reviewable without reading raw JSON | `matrix.html` — rows, covered flags, mapped screen/component, gap list, coverage basis |
| 5 | Same for `plan.json`, one mechanism not two | `plan.html`, same module, same page skeleton, same table helper |
| 6 | If the console renders it instead, say so | It does **not** — design-studio emits the view. Stated as an explicit decision |
| 7 | Read the existing gate→step map; no second table | `gate_decision_context()` reads `_GATE_ARTIFACT_REQUIREMENTS` and `_GATE_REJECTION_SEMANTICS`; `GateArtifactMissingError`'s refusal still reads the same map, unchanged |
| 8 | Required-step info reachable BEFORE a decision is attempted | `gateContext` on every `GET /missions[/{id}]` and every mission response: `requiredArtifact`, `producedBy`, `artifactPresent`, `canDecide`, `reviewViews`, `rejection`. `null` at a non-gate stage |
| 9 | `feel-gate` untouched, no invented artifact | Still absent from `_GATE_ARTIFACT_REQUIREMENTS`; only its rejection semantics are stated. `gate_decision_context(feel-gate)` returns `requiredArtifact: null` — asserted by a test |
| 10 | Existing missions read back unchanged; JSON filenames/shapes/registration kept | `matrix.json`/`plan.json` untouched. Views register under a **new** `ArtifactKind.REVIEW`, never under `MATRIX`/`PLAN`, so the gate's artifact-presence check and `PlanService`'s matrix read see exactly the path they saw before. Every mission in the local ledger projects cleanly; `matrix.json`/`plan.json` from **live** missions `8991305d`, `bd3f8e95` and `e8e4b3e5` (the mission this demand was found on) all render as views without modification |
| 11 | Suite green, pre-work baseline recorded | Below |

## Test baseline and result

- **Pre-work baseline:** 577 passed, 1 failed.
- **After:** 597 passed (20 new tests, `tests/test_gate_review_and_semantics.py`).

The one baseline failure —
`tests/test_design_system_adapters.py::test_event_sink_carries_change_reason_for_each_transition`
— **pre-dates this work** and is unrelated to it: it asserts a fixed ORDER on events captured
from `StateFeedEventSink`'s background emit threads, so it fails intermittently on any run,
before and after these changes. It passes in isolation and on most full runs; it failed once
during this session's verification and once at baseline. Not fixed here (out of this demand's
scope) — flagged as its own item.

## What `dashboard` can now build against

# Fulfillment report — recording WHICH theme the owner approved

## State before the work

Not shipped by any prior session; checked first per the demand's own
instruction. `GateRecord` carried `gate`, `outcome`, `notes`, `checklist`,
`decided_at` and `reference_images` — nothing naming a theme. The owner's
choice between the round's two or three competing propositions existed only as
prose inside `notes`, and two downstream steps paid for that:

- `CoverageService._active_html_paths` filtered a mission's registered `MOCK`
  `.html` paths to the latest propose round and stopped there, so `_covered_tags`
  unioned the tags of **every** theme in that round.
- `PlanService._theme_work_unit` emitted `"Land the approved theme's tokens +
  markup scaffold into <repo>"` with `targetFiles` holding two proposed
  DESTINATION paths and no source of any kind.

The demand's framing is exactly right about the consequence, and live mission
`e8e4b3e5` shows it: its recorded `matrix.json` reports `gaps: []` — perfect
coverage — computed from `proposals-round-10/theme-{a,b,c}/index.html`, all
three at once. Whichever one the owner approved, that zero is not a statement
about it.

Baseline before any edit: **563 passing**.

## What was built

### The field, and where it is read

`approvedTheme` is accepted on `POST /missions/{id}/gates/theme-gate` and read
only when the gate is `theme-gate` **and** the outcome is `APPROVED`. That is
the shape `designSystemId` already has in the same handler for
`system-gate` + `APPROVED`, and it is enforced twice on purpose: `api.py`
only *parses* the key under those conditions, and
`Mission.record_gate_outcome` independently stores `None` unless the same two
conditions hold — so no future caller of the domain method can smuggle a slug
onto a rejection.

Validation is against `themes_in_active_round(mock_paths)`, a new
`proposition.py` helper that derives the theme directories from the mission's
own registered mock paths in the latest round. Deliberately not `THEME_SLUGS`:
that tuple says what the dispatch prompt *asks* for, not what the agent
actually wrote — `run_propose`'s read-back already globs `theme-*` for whatever
landed, and a round that produced two themes must reject the third's slug. The
helper also ignores superseded rounds and round-level deliverables such as
`state-material-mapping.json`, which belong to the round as a whole and to no
single proposition.

Storage follows `reference_images` precisely: a new optional field with a
`None` default on the frozen `GateRecord`, written unconditionally by the
ledger's JSON projection and read back with a `.get` default, so records
persisted before this WU load byte-identically.

`Mission.approved_theme()` scans backwards for the latest **APPROVED**
`theme-gate` record rather than using `latest_gate_record(THEME_GATE)` — that
gate accumulates REJECTED records from three separate mechanisms (owner
rejections, the direction-carry record `rewind()` appends, the dispatch
self-heal), and after a rewind it is the last *approval* that names the live
theme.

### Coverage

`_active_html_paths` now scopes by round (via the extracted
`active_round_paths`, shared with the plan step so one rule has one
implementation) and then, when the mission records an approved theme, to that
theme's own directory. `matrix.json` gains `approvedTheme` and `coverageBasis`.

### Plan

WU-0 names the theme and carries `sourceFiles` — the theme's real registered
`index.html` and `tokens.css` in the latest round, as mission-relative artifact
paths the build agent reads through the existing artifact route. `targetFiles`
is untouched; the WU gained an origin, it did not move.

## The legacy path, and how it was checked

Every behaviour above is conditional on the field being present. Absent, the
union is kept exactly as it was — the demand is explicit that legacy missions
must read back identically, and a "helpful" guess (first theme, or
`theme-a`) would silently fabricate a decision the owner never recorded.

The degrade is stated rather than hidden. `coverageBasis` on a legacy matrix
reads:

> computed across EVERY theme in the latest propose round (union), because this
> mission's theme-gate approval records no approved theme -- it predates that
> field. An item counts as covered when any theme in the round tagged it, which
> may credit the theme the owner actually approved with another theme's work.

Checked against the real thing, not only a fixture: mission `e8e4b3e5`'s actual
on-disk artifact tree was replayed through `CoverageService` with no approved
theme, and its regenerated matrix's `rows`, `gaps`, `sources`, `targetRepo` and
`regime` came back identical to the recorded one — the only difference being
`approvedTheme: null` and the new `coverageBasis` sentence. The original
`matrix.json` was written back afterwards.

Note for the origin, since it is the point of the demand: `e8e4b3e5` is a
console mission that will keep reporting union coverage until it is re-approved
through a round that records a theme. The field cannot be backfilled from here —
nothing in this repo knows which of `theme-a/b/c` the owner picked. If the
console wants that mission's numbers to mean one proposition, the owner has to
say which one.

## Tests

`tests/test_approved_theme.py`, 15 tests. The four the demand names:

- **valid slug** — 200, advances to `coverage-gate`, projected top-level and on
  the record, and re-read from a fresh service over the same ledger.
- **slug absent from the round** — 400 naming the offending slug; the mission is
  still at `theme-gate` with no theme-gate record at all.
- **legacy record, no slug** — today's union: both brief items covered,
  `gaps: []`, both themes in `sources.mocks`, `approvedTheme: null`; plus WU-0's
  original title, and a direct `_gate_records_from_json` test on a payload with
  no `approvedTheme` key.
- **two themes in one round tagging DIFFERENT items** — the case that makes the
  union wrong and that nothing exercised before. `theme-a` tags only the GET,
  `theme-b` only the POST; approving `theme-a` reports the POST as a genuine
  gap. The mirror-image test approves `theme-b` on the same round and gets the
  opposite gap, which is what proves the narrowing follows the recorded field
  rather than a fixed first directory.

Plus: gate-and-outcome scoping on a rejection and at another gate, round + theme
scoping composed (a superseded round's `theme-a` must not leak in just because
the slug matches its dirname too), ledger round-trip, latest-approval-wins after
a rewind, and two unit tests on `themes_in_active_round`.

One pre-existing test changed: `test_rewind_route_backward_to_theme_gate_succeeds`
asserts a gate-record projection by exact dict equality, so the new
`"approvedTheme": None` key was added to its expectation. Behaviour unchanged —
a direction-carry record is a rejection and carries no theme.

**578 passing** (baseline 563, +15). No changes to `contracts`, the
agent-runner port, or any sibling repo.

shipped: OWNER RULING 1 (mechanism, criterion 2): REFRESH IN PLACE, recorded append-only -- NOT a widening of REWIND_TARGET_STAGES. rewind's own docstring stays true as written ('a mechanical stage has no decision to revisit'), because refreshing an input is not revisiting a decision; the gap it pointed at (the forward machinery cannot reach `harvest` either on a mission past it) is closed by a new action rather than by making rewind mean something else

POST /missions/{id}/refresh-inputs (owner-initiated, `reason` required, never automatic): re-runs the harvest read + the brief composition against the target repo as it stands TODAY, in one action, without aborting the mission

NO STAGE MOVES and NO GATE RECORD IS TOUCHED -- the approved theme-gate record, the system-gate pin and every rejection survive verbatim (pinned by a test that compares the whole gateRecords projection before and after)

NOTHING IS ERASED: the superseded harvest.json/brief.json are copied to superseded/<name>-before-refresh-<n>.json BEFORE the new ones are written, and registered under their existing HARVEST/BRIEF kinds -- ArtifactsRegistry stays append-only, and the old files are served by the existing artifact route

The refresh is RECORDED append-only: RefreshRecord (a FOURTH list beside gateRecords/rewinds/sendBacks, folded into none of them) carries the owner's reason, when it ran, what it re-derived, what it preserved, and the brief items ADDED and REMOVED -- so the consequence is readable without diffing two artifacts by hand. New nullable `refreshes_json` column via the ledger's existing additive-migration idiom

NO NEW RECOMPUTATION MACHINERY was needed: coverage and plan are already pure functions of their inputs with no cache, so the next POST /coverage recomputes against the refreshed brief on its own -- proven by tests, not asserted
An item a refresh ADDS is genuinely uncovered and appears in gaps[] -- never suppressed, never auto-healed; an item it REMOVES disappears from the matrix and therefore from the plan

OWNER RULING 2 (criterion 9, the collapsed port): the harvest now EXPANDS a brace family (`/api/v1/{plants,species,...,users}/**`) into one row per family, each keeping `portExpandedFrom` so nothing is lost, and records an explicit GAP wherever a row is STILL a bare wildcard -- expansion makes the families visible, the gap says honestly that none of them is described

brief.compose_actions names those surfaces: the contract cell is read exactly as before wherever there is a real contract id, but where every contract part on a row is an explicit ABSENCE the row's paths are used instead. Before this, PlantPal's whole botanical domain reached the designer as the single item `action:none (app-internal REST API, JWT-authenticated)`, which PlanService then correctly PRUNED -- so the mission's actual subject appeared in no artifact at all

Verified against PlantPal's LIVE HEXAGON.md (read-only): 5 inbound rows -> 14; brief actions 5 -> 14, with `none (...)` gone and eleven named families present; and the stale `stage.companion.turn` row that started this demand is absent from the re-derived harvest, exactly as the demand predicted
harvestGeneratedAt on every mission response, so a stale snapshot is visible where the owner decides rather than discovered after a plan has been generated from it

Refusals: 409 on a terminal mission and on one not yet past `brief` (RefreshRefusedError, same posture rewind/send-back/abort take); 400 on an empty reason. Missions that never refresh project `refreshes: []` and are otherwise byte-identical
Suite green: 624 passing (pre-work baseline 597, +27 in tests/test_refresh_inputs.py)

# Fulfilment report — `dashboard-20260730-design-studio-refresh-mission-inputs`

- **Demand:** `dashboard/demands/2026-07-30-design-studio-refresh-mission-inputs.md`
- **Repo:** design-studio · **Date:** 2026-07-30 · **Claim:** done (the coordinator validates)

## The two owner decisions

Both were put to the owner before any code was written.

### 1. Mechanism (criterion 2) — refresh in place, recorded

`REWIND_TARGET_STAGES` is **unchanged**. `Mission.rewind`'s docstring is **unchanged**, and still
true: a mechanical stage has no decision to revisit. The demand's real finding was that the forward
machinery rewind defers to *cannot reach `harvest` either* on a mission already past it — the
refusal pointed somewhere empty. That emptiness is now filled by an action of its own rather than by
stretching rewind to mean something it does not.

The reasoning, written down where it will be read: `mission.RefreshRecord`'s docstring and
`domain/refresh_inputs.py`'s module docstring.

What follows from the ruling, and is enforced:

| | |
|---|---|
| stage | never moves (`Mission.refresh_inputs` cannot move one) |
| gate records | untouched — approved theme, system-gate pin, every rejection |
| old inputs | copied to `superseded/…-before-refresh-<n>.json` first, and registered |
| the act itself | recorded append-only with the owner's own reason |
| recomputation | none here — `coverage`/`plan` are already pure functions of their inputs |

### 2. The collapsed port (criterion 9) — expanded, and the residue stated

`expand_port_cell`/`expand_inbound_rows` split a brace family into one row per family; each keeps
`portExpandedFrom`, so the harvest still shows that these were written as one line. Expansion makes
eleven families *visible*; it does not make any one of them *described*, so `_coarse_port_gaps`
records a GAP per row that is still a bare wildcard — the question the interview exists to ask.

The second half was in the brief, not the harvest: the brief read only the **contract** column, so
all eleven families collapsed back into `none (app-internal REST API, JWT-authenticated)` — an
explicit absence, which `PlanService` then correctly pruned. `compose_actions` now falls back to the
row's **paths** when every contract part on that row is an absence. An app-internal REST API with no
contract id is not "nothing here"; it is a real surface whose identity is its path.

## Verified against the live target (read-only)

Re-deriving `plantpal`'s harvest against its HEXAGON.md as it stands today:

- inbound rows **5 → 14**; brief actions **5 → 14**
- `none (app-internal REST API, JWT-authenticated)` — **gone**, replaced by eleven named families
  (`/api/v1/plants/**` … `/api/v1/users/**`), each with its own "still a wildcard" GAP
- `stage.companion.turn` — **absent** from the re-derived harvest, which is the stale surface that
  started this demand (criterion 8, confirmed against the real repo rather than a fixture)

Nothing was written to `plantpal`, and no live mission artifact was modified: this was a pure
in-memory re-derivation for verification.

## Criterion-by-criterion

| # | Criterion | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Re-derive harvest+brief in one owner action, no abort, no loss | `POST /missions/{id}/refresh-inputs` |
| 2 | Mechanism chosen deliberately and reasoned in writing | Refresh-in-place; `RefreshRecord` + `refresh_inputs.py` docstrings state the argument and why rewind is not widened |
| 3 | Gate decisions survive | Test compares the full `gateRecords` projection and `approvedTheme` before/after |
| 4 | Recorded append-only, with the owner's reason | `RefreshRecord`, `mission.refreshes`, `refreshes` in the projection, ledger round-trip test |
| 5 | Nothing erased; previous inputs reachable | `superseded/…-before-refresh-<n>.json`, registered and served; registry still append-only |
| 6 | Coverage/plan recompute with no new machinery | None added — test drives `POST /coverage` after a refresh |
| 7 | Previously-covered → gap must be visible, never suppressed | Test: an item the refresh ADDS lands in `gaps[]` |
| 8 | Removed surfaces disappear from brief/matrix/plan | Test with a reverted route; confirmed live against PlantPal |
| 9 | The collapsed-port problem not reproduced | Brace expansion + coarse-row GAPs + the brief's path fallback (above) |
| 10 | Harvest `generatedAt` visible where decisions are made | `harvestGeneratedAt` on every mission response |
| 11 | Never-refreshed missions behave identically; additive; never automatic | `refreshes: []`, no other field changes; the route is the only caller |
| 12 | Tests: item removed, covered→gap, gates survive, terminal refused | All four, plus the ledger round-trip and the parse-level units — 27 tests |

## Test baseline and result

- **Pre-work baseline:** 597 passed.
- **After:** 624 passed (+27, `tests/test_refresh_inputs.py`).

## Follow-ons raised in this same session

- `platform-vault`: `spec-design-studio.md`'s stage-machine section no longer describes this repo —
  "past `brief` implies the brief is fixed" is no longer true, and a new owner action exists.
- `dashboard`: surface `harvestGeneratedAt` and offer the refresh action at the gates where a stale
  brief costs something (its own demand, as the demand's own closing note anticipated).

## Files

- new: `src/design_studio/domain/refresh_inputs.py`, `tests/test_refresh_inputs.py`
- changed: `domain/mission.py` (`RefreshRecord`, `refresh_inputs`), `domain/harvest.py` (port
  expansion + coarse gaps), `domain/brief.py` (`compose_actions`, `compose_brief`,
  `is_explicit_absence_item`), `domain/plan.py` (imports the moved predicate),
  `domain/errors.py` (`RefreshRefusedError`), `domain/artifact_io.py` (nested-path writes),
  `adapters/ledger_sqlalchemy.py` (`refreshes_json`), `api.py`, `CHANGELOG.md`

# Fulfillment — the batched design-system builder can finish Checked first: none of this was already shipped. The live failure was still reproducible against mission `e8e4b3e5`'s snapshot on disk at session start. ## What shipped **1. `link-integrity` stops reading documentation as navigation.** `components/plate.html` of the `Herbarium` system (`100524c3-…`) contains zero live `` tags and one escaped `<img … src="scans/fern-2025-06-12.jpg">` inside a `
` block. The check scanned raw page text with no notion of
code regions, found that attribute, and reported a broken link for a file that
was never meant to exist. Link-shaped strings inside a code region are now
skipped.

**2. One definition of "a code block", shared.** `escaped-code-blocks` and
`link-integrity` previously scanned independently — that disagreement *was* the
bug. Both now resolve regions from a single `code_regions(text)` helper
(`_CodeRegion(start, end, body)`), one scan per page: `escaped-code-blocks`
reads `body`, `link-integrity` skips matches inside `[start, end)`.

**3. The live system passes, as built.** Re-running `run_qa_checks` against
`artifacts_store/design-systems/plantpal-e8e4b3e5/v1.0.0` with that build's own
19-page manifest (`_page_specs_from_tracking`) now returns `passed: true`, all
six checks green — **no page regenerated, no placeholder asset file created,
nothing under `artifacts_store/` written by this session**. Its tracking still
reads `currentBatch: 3`, batch 3 `pending` with a stale `failedAt` and no
`blocked` record, so the owner's next `POST /missions/{id}/build-system` re-runs
QA once and consolidates it.

**4. Retries are bounded, and exhaustion is terminal.**
- `MAX_UNIT_ATTEMPTS = 3` for dispatched units (batch 0's constitution, each
  batch-1/2 page). Counted at dispatch, since a dispatch is what costs.
- `MAX_QA_ATTEMPTS = 1` for the mechanical batch-3 QA — a pure function of an
  unchanged snapshot cannot produce a different report, so a second run is the
  same computation, not a retry. The first fatal failure blocks.
- Exhausting the budget writes `tracking["blocked"] = {batch, unit, attempts,
  reason, at}`. `run_build` does no work at all while it is set, and
  `_is_carryable` skips the mission entirely, so `BuildAdvancer` never
  re-enters it. Surfaced as `designSystemBuild.blocked` on the mission
  projection — the signal `failure` alone could not give (a `failure` still
  means "the next tick retries this").

**5. A fatal QA check now has an owner-visible way forward that needs no code
change here** — `POST /missions/{id}/build-system/unblock`:
- empty body = "I fixed the cause / it was transient": the blocked unit's
  `failedAt`, `attempts` and dead `dispatch` are cleared, so it is dispatched
  fresh with a full budget;
- `{"acceptQaFindings": true, "note": "…"}` = "I read the report and accept
  these findings": a durable `qaOverride` is recorded and batch 3 may
  consolidate. The report is still written in full, the failing check still
  reports `passed: false` with every issue named, and the report gains an
  `ownerOverride` block — nothing is silently re-judged as green. A §8bis
  re-entry clears both the block and the override, since regenerated pages are
  not the artifact the owner looked at.
Documented in `README.md` ("When a system build gets stuck", with the two-row
body table) and `CHANGELOG.md`.

**6. Pause semantics — the documentation moves, not the behaviour.** Both
halves are real and deliberate: a hand-driven `run_build`/`run_build_drained`
call honors `pauseRequested` at batch boundaries only (it reads
`tracking["paused"]`, written solely when a batch consolidates), while
`BuildAdvancer` checks the live flag and starts no further work immediately.
Neither ever kills an in-flight run. "Pause" meaning "stop spending on my
behalf" is worth keeping, so the code is unchanged and the docs are asked to
state both halves: `BuildAdvancer`'s docstring and `api.py`'s route index were
corrected here, and demand `design-studio-20260728-pause-semantics-doc-sync`
was raised to `platform-vault` + `documentations` under D081.

**7. Existing behaviour preserved** — verified by the pre-existing suite, all of
which still passes untouched except the one test noted below: the
constitution-declared name and page manifest (R9), the drain and
`BuildAdvancer` (R2), pause honored at batch boundaries for in-progress
batches, the five advisory QA checks, and the rule that a build never advances
the mission past `system-gate` on its own (asserted again in the new
accept-findings test).

**Tests: 421 passing, from a 411 baseline.** Ten new: the exact live shape
(zero live `img`, one escaped `img` in a `pre/code` whose `src` does not
resolve → link-integrity passes); a real broken link on that same page still
caught; the two checks resolving identical regions; the per-unit cap bounding
dispatches instead of retrying forever; the advancer skipping a blocked build
until `unblock`; the QA batch not re-running against an unchanged failure; the
accept-findings path; re-entry clearing block and override; and two API tests
for the new route.

## What the origin must know

- **New API surface**: `POST /missions/{id}/build-system/unblock`, body
  optional `{acceptQaFindings?: bool, note?: string}`. 409 if the mission never
  started a build. Returns the standard mission dict.
- **New projection fields**: `designSystemBuild.blocked` (null, or `{batch,
  unit, attempts, reason, at}`) and `designSystemBuild.qaOverride`. The console
  will want `blocked` — it is the only signal that distinguishes "this build
  has stopped trying and is waiting for you" from "an agent died, retrying". No
  dashboard demand was raised for it in this session; flagging it here so the
  owner can decide whether to route one.
- **New tracking-artifact keys**: `blocked`, `qaOverride`, and `attempts` on
  each unit. All read with `.get()` defaults, so builds started before this
  change (including `e8e4b3e5`'s) keep working with no migration.
- **The doc-sync demand is open** — nothing in this repo waits on it.

## Not done / caveats

- **One pre-existing test changed shape.**
  `test_link_integrity_failure_recovers_once_the_link_is_fixed` used to fix the
  page on disk and re-run `run_build` to consolidate. Under
  `MAX_QA_ATTEMPTS = 1` that re-run no longer happens on its own, so the test
  now calls `service.unblock(...)` between the fix and the re-run. Its
  substance is unchanged (fixing the link makes QA pass); it gained one owner
  step, which is the documented path. Called out rather than buried: this is
  the one behaviour in the build that a caller could notice changing.
- **A blocked build is not auto-unblocked when the snapshot changes.** Editing
  files under the snapshot dir does not clear the block; the owner's `unblock`
  call does. This was a deliberate choice over fingerprinting the snapshot —
  the demand asked for a terminal state "that the advancer does not re-enter
  until an owner acts", and content-change detection would have re-entered on a
  non-owner event.
- **The live `e8e4b3e5` build was not driven to completion by this session.**
  Its QA now passes as a pure function against the real files (verified), but
  advancing that mission's own tracking is an owner-initiated call against the
  running service, not something a build session should do to live state.
- **`only-existing-classes` still scans inside code regions** and so sees class
  names in escaped sample markup. It is advisory, it did not misfire on the
  live system, and narrowing it was outside the demand's scope — noted as a
  known, bounded inconsistency rather than fixed silently.

# Fulfillment — `bin/structurer`'s pending-audit parser newline-swallow bug

## State check first

No prior session had touched this. `_AUDIT_FIELD_RE` in
`bin/structurer` still read `field:\s*(.*)$` at session start; confirmed
the swallow reproduces exactly as described before changing anything (see
below). Proceeded with the fix rather than a no-op report.

## Root cause, confirmed by direct repro

`_AUDIT_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^(session_id|...|context|human_class):\s*(.*)$")`,
run via `finditer` over each `## N` entry's full body text (not per-line).
`\s*` matches `\n` too. For a `context:` line with nothing after the colon
(exactly what `render_pending_audit_md` writes for an empty context —
`f"context: {context_oneline}\n"` with `context_oneline == ""`, i.e. the
literal line `"context: \n"`), `\s*` consumes the trailing space **and**
the newline, then keeps consuming whitespace into the next line until it
hits the first non-whitespace character — the `h` of `human_class:`. From
there `(.*)$` greedily captures the rest of that line, so `context` ends up
holding the string `"human_class: applied"` and the `human_class:` line's
own `^human_class:` anchor is never revisited by `finditer` (its match
position already moved past it). Direct repro before the fix:

```python
>>> entry
{'session_id': 's1', ..., 'context': 'human_class: applied'}
# no 'human_class' key at all -> parse_pending_audit_md defaults it to ""
```

This is precisely "filled owner verdicts are read as unfilled" — every
entry in agent-runner's real `2026-07-21` `pending-audit.md` sample has
this exact shape (blank `context:` line, verdict on the very next line), so
none of the 9 filled-in entries were ever scored into
`derived/audit.jsonl`.

## Fix

`\s*` → `[ \t]*` (same-line whitespace only) in `_AUDIT_FIELD_RE`. An empty
value now correctly yields `""` and `human_class` is matched as its own,
independent field on the next `finditer` step. Verified against the same
repro:

```python
>>> entry
{'session_id': 's1', ..., 'context': '', 'human_class': 'applied'}
```

## Regression test

`test_empty_context_does_not_swallow_following_human_class_line` (added to
`TestWeeklyAudit` in `bin/test_structurer.py`) builds a `pending-audit.md`
via `render_pending_audit_md` with an empty `context`, replaces the blank
`human_class:` line with `human_class: applied` (the exact shape every real
sample entry has), parses it back, and asserts `context == ""`,
`human_class == "applied"`, that it scores (not left in `remaining`), and
that `agree` is computed correctly (`False` here, since the classifier said
`mentioned`).

## Sweep for the same `\s*`-crosses-newline shape

Checked every `re.compile`/`re.search`/`re.match` call in `bin/structurer`,
`bin/brain`, `bin/adopt`, `bin/executioner` (`test_*` files excluded — the
demand's brief). Two ways this pattern shows up, and each occurrence's
disposition:

**Fixed (real bugs, same shape, same fix — all in `bin/brain`):**

- `_PROGRESS_RETIRED_RE` (`^progress_retired:\s*(.*)$`, `re.M`, searched
  over the whole `.brain/config.yml` text) — an empty `progress_retired:`
  line followed by any other config content would have been misread as a
  non-empty retirement date, since the only guard is `if m and
  m.group(1).strip():`. No whitelist catches a bogus swallowed value here
  (unlike `read_classifier_mode`, below).
- `_read_progress_standing`'s inline `^progress_standing:\s*(.*)$` — same
  shape, same missing guard.
- `_last_progress_block_fields`'s per-key `^-\s*{key}:\s*(.*)$` — the
  State/Next step/Standing/Vault-sync/Session handoff block this session's
  own CLAUDE.md documents as the standard session-close footer. An empty
  handoff line (e.g. `- State: ` with nothing after it) would have
  swallowed the *next* handoff line whole as its own value, corrupting
  `_projection_currently_passes()`'s mechanical comparison. (Each field
  here runs its own fresh `re.search` over the full block, so unlike the
  audit case the *next* field's own match still succeeds independently —
  the corruption is confined to the empty field reading back non-empty.)

All three fixed the same way: `\s*` → `[ \t]*` right after the field's
colon.

**Checked, left as-is, and why each is actually safe:**

- `_DECISION_ITEM_RE`, `_TEXT_KEY_RE`, `_SUPERSEDES_KEY_RE` (`bin/
  structurer`), `_TOP_LEVEL_RE` (`bin/brain`), and `bin/adopt`'s frontmatter
  key/value scanner (`re.match(r"^([A-Za-z0-9_]+):\s*(.*)$", line)`) — all
  matched via `.match()` against a single already-split line string (from
  a `lines[]` list or a `for line in text.splitlines()` loop). There is no
  `\n` character present in the string being matched, so `\s*` has nothing
  to cross.
- `_MANIFEST_LINE_RE` (`<!--\s*structurer run:\s*(\S+)\s*--\s*manifest:\s*
  (.*?)\s*-->`) and the `generated:`/`low_volume:` HTML-comment regexes in
  `parse_pending_audit_md` — self-terminated by a required literal (`-->`),
  not by `$`/end-of-line, and not sequentially scanning adjacent fields via
  `finditer`. Nothing adjacent to bleed into.
- `read_classifier_mode`'s `^classifier:\s*(\S+)` and `_THRESHOLD_CONFIG_RE`
  (`^full_run_session_threshold:\s*(\S+)`) — `\S+` *can* swallow the next
  line's first token on an empty value, but both call sites validate the
  captured value afterward (whitelist membership / `int()` with
  `try/except`) and fall back to the documented default on anything
  unrecognized — a swallowed bogus token just degrades safely, by design
  (both docstrings already state this intent).
- `_check_structurer_freshness`'s `last full run:\s*(\S+)` — same shape,
  same safety: `datetime.fromisoformat()` in a `try/except` that returns a
  "did not parse" message on failure.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest bin.test_structurer` — 121/121 pass (includes the new
  regression test).
- `python -m unittest bin.test_brain` — 32/32 pass (covers the three
  `bin/brain` fixes; no existing test exercised the empty-value crossing
  case, none needed changing).
- `python -m unittest bin.test_adopt bin.test_executioner` — 95/95 pass,
  unaffected by this change (confirms the sweep's "left as-is" calls didn't
  need code changes there either).
- 248/248 across all four suites.

## What agent-runner needs to know

Fix is on `main`, tagged **`v0.5.1`**, pushed to `origin/main` and
`origin/v0.5.1`. Once agent-runner's toolkit pin moves to `v0.5.1` (or
later) and it runs a full `structurer` pass, the 9 already-filled entries
committed at `7c2c079` should parse correctly and score into
`derived/audit.jsonl` — this session did not run `structurer` inside
agent-runner's own repo (out of scope for a brain-toolkit session per this
repo's CLAUDE.md: never edit outside your own repo). The acceptance
criterion's "6/9 agreement on the owner's 2026-07-24 verdicts" expectation
is therefore unverified from this side; it depends on agent-runner
re-running structurer against its own real data after the repin, not on
anything this fix can confirm in isolation.

# Fulfillment — `brain-toolkit`'s half of make-FP-6-retirement-executable

**Scope note, stated up front:** this report covers **only** `brain-toolkit`'s
half of the demand. The `conventions` half — retirement-aware
`vault-sync-handoff` / `brain-projection-equality` (the demand's
`conventions`-prefixed acceptance criteria) — is separate, parallel work in
that repo, not touched or claimed here.

## What shipped

`brain progress retire`, a new command in `bin/brain`, built against
`spec-agent-memory-system.md` Appendix A.3's actual wording (quoted, not
paraphrased, throughout below and in the code's own comments) — the five
normative points landed under **D075**.

### 1. Command name/shape, and why it fits the existing CLI

`brain progress retire [--no-git]` — a new top-level `progress` subparser
with one nested subcommand, `retire`, wired exactly like the existing
`session` subparser's `open`/`session close` pair
(`session_sub = session_p.add_subparsers(...)`,
mirrored as `progress_sub = progress_p.add_subparsers(...)`). Studied
`build_parser()` before writing anything, per the brief's own instruction —
`progress` (noun) / `retire` (verb) reads the same way `session` (noun) /
`open`\|`close` (verb) already does, so a caller who knows the existing CLI
needs no new mental model. Functional name, no theme word (D002). `--no-git`
mirrors `session close`'s own flag of the same name and meaning (skip the
`git add`/`commit` step).

### 2. Counting "closed sessions" and checking the projection passes

**"Closed session," precisely:** a `.brain/sessions/*.md` file whose
frontmatter carries **both** `close: confirmed` **and** a non-empty
`ended:`. This is the exact pair `cmd_session_close` — and only
`cmd_session_close` — writes together, atomically, on a real close; `status`
alone was rejected as the signal because it's free text, settable at open
time and hand-editable afterward, so it's a weaker close-happened proof than
a pair no other code path produces. Implemented as `_count_closed_sessions()`
/ `_newest_closed_session()`, both tolerant of malformed session files
(skipped, not counted or crashed on — the same tolerance `brain rebuild`
already uses). Threshold: `RETIREMENT_THRESHOLD = 5`, matching A.3 point 1's
"≥ 5 closed sessions" verbatim.

**"Projection currently passes," precisely:** mirrors `conventions`'
`brain-projection-equality` (the check A.3 point 5 / A.6 names as one of the
two that must become retirement-aware): the newest `PROGRESS.md`
`## Session N (...)` block's `State`/`Standing`/`Vault-sync`/`Session` lines
must equal what `brain session close` would generate from the newest closed
session file. All four are mechanically re-derivable from data already on
disk — `State` from the frontmatter `task`+`status` scalars, `Standing` from
`.brain/config.yml`'s `progress_standing`, `Vault-sync` from the frontmatter
`vault_sync` scalar, `Session` from the closed session file's own filename
stem (D063's explicit pairing). `Next step` is **deliberately excluded** from
this mechanical check — it is free text supplied at close time via
`--next-step` (or a generic fallback) and is never persisted anywhere in the
session file itself, so there is no stored value to re-derive it from and no
byte-exact check to make honestly. This is a documented, narrower scope than
a hypothetical full five-line diff, not a silent gap — see
`_projection_currently_passes()`'s own docstring in `bin/brain` and the
"What the origin must know" item below. Implemented as
`_last_progress_block_fields()` (parses the last block) +
`_projection_currently_passes()` (compares).

Both checks run in exactly one place — `cmd_progress_retire`, before the
marker is written — and nowhere else in this file re-runs them, per A.3
point 4 / the demand's "critical design constraint" (below).

### 3. Header text + proof PROGRESS.md content survives

Header (rendered by `_progress_retirement_header_text`), inserted once,
right after the `# <repo> -- Progress` title line via
`_insert_retirement_header`:

```
> **Retired 2026-07-23.** PROGRESS.md is retired as an authoring surface
> (spec-agent-memory-system.md Appendix A.3 point 3, D075: >= 5 closed
> sessions, generated projection passing). This file freezes in place --
> never moved, renamed, or deleted -- and everything below is preserved
> exactly as written. For anything after 2026-07-23, see
> `.brain/sessions/`.
```

**Content-preservation proof:** `_insert_retirement_header` never rewrites
the file wholesale — it slices `text[:nl + 1] + header + text[nl + 1:]`
(`nl` = the index of the title line's own newline), so everything from the
end of the title line onward is copied through byte-for-byte, header
inserted, nothing overlaid or truncated. The file is never moved, renamed,
or truncated by any other path either — no `git mv`, no `unlink`, no
`write_text` call anywhere in `cmd_progress_retire` that isn't this
insertion. Verified directly against real bytes (not just presence) in
`test_retire_success_writes_marker_and_header_once_and_preserves_content`:
captures `before`, splits off the title line, retires, then asserts
`after.startswith(title_and_nl)` **and** `after.endswith(rest_before)` —
the entire pre-existing body (five real `## Session N` blocks in the test
fixture) reconstructed as an exact trailing substring of the post-retirement
file.

### 4. Idempotency proof

`test_retire_is_idempotent_on_rerun`: runs `progress retire` twice.
First run succeeds and prints `retired`; second run prints
`already retired` and exits 0. Asserts `config.yml` text is **byte-identical**
between the two post-states, `PROGRESS.md` text is **byte-identical** between
the two post-states, the header marker appears exactly once, and the
`progress_retired:` key appears exactly once — a second call is a true
no-op, not merely idempotent in effect. Mechanism: `cmd_progress_retire`
checks `_read_progress_retired_marker()` **first**, before either
eligibility check runs — so a retired repo's eligibility is never
re-evaluated on a later call either, matching A.3 point 4's "never
recompute" rule at the read path, not just the write path.

### 5. All four suite counts, before/after

Ran all four suites before starting (confirming the demand's own stated
baseline) and again after every change:

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_brain.py` | 26 | **32** (+6, `TestProgressRetirement`) |
| `test_structurer.py` | 120 | 120 (untouched) |
| `test_executioner.py` | 63 | 63 (untouched) |
| `test_adopt.py` | 32 | 32 (untouched) |
| **Total** | **241** | **247** |

All green both times; nothing regressed.

### 6. Commits, tag, push ref, board verification

Commits on `master` (this repo's default branch):
1. `feat: brain progress retire -- PROGRESS.md retirement per D075/A.3`
   (`bin/brain`, `bin/test_brain.py`)
2. `docs: v0.5.0 -- CHANGELOG/DEPLOYMENT/README for brain progress retire`
   (`CHANGELOG.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `README.md`, `PROGRESS.md`)
3. `demand: brain-toolkit half of progress-retirement-validator-delta
   fulfilled` (this report)

Tagged `v0.5.0`. **Pushed to `origin/main`**: `0a32876..7990912 main -> main`
(the docs+code commits), plus `v0.5.0 -> v0.5.0` (new tag). Repo:
`https://github.com/elmoul/brain-toolkit.git`.

**Board verification: NOT ON THE BOARD, confirmed explicitly, not
assumed.** `GET http://localhost:8082/board` (checked after the push above)
returns `data.errors: []` (0 parse errors platform-wide) and 138
fulfillments total, but `data.fulfillments` — enumerated and filtered by
`repo` field — contains **zero** entries with `repo == "brain-toolkit"`,
and the distinct repo set present is: `agent-runner`, `ai-gateway`,
`ci-runner`, `connector-gmail`, `contracts`, `control-plane`, `conventions`,
`dashboard`, `demand-coordinator`, `design-studio`, `launcher`,
`media-generation`, `observability`, `orchestrator`, `platform-vault`,
`portfolio`, `pregnancy`, `publishing`, `runtime`, `sentinel-hub`,
`state-feed`, `treasury` — **`brain-toolkit` is absent from that list
entirely**, not merely from this one report. This is a coordinator
`board.repos`-allowlist gap (this repo was never added to it), not a defect
in this report, this push, or its content — flagged here, per the task
brief's own instruction, for the architect/owner to add `brain-toolkit` to
the allowlist if fulfillment reports from this repo should ever become
board-visible.

### 7. Pin/worktree note for the architect

This release is tagged `v0.5.0`, but **no consumer's `.brain/toolkit-pin`
has been repinned**, and **no `brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.5.0/` entry
exists**. Per this task's own instruction, neither was done here. Both
pilots (`agent-runner`, `media-generation`) still resolve their `brain`
shim against whatever tag their own `.brain/toolkit-pin` currently names
(observed `v0.3.0` for `agent-runner` as of the last session that inspected
it — not re-verified this session, since this session never touched either
pilot). A `brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.5.0/` worktree checkout would need to
exist, per this repo's own `DEPLOYMENT.md` "Intended pin mechanism" section,
before any repo could actually pin to `v0.5.0` and get `progress retire` —
that is fleet-wide follow-up work, not part of this fulfillment.

### 8. Anything in A.3 contradicting this brief

Nothing contradicts it. One point worth surfacing rather than silently
resolving: A.3 point 5 (and A.6) state the **`conventions`-side** blocking
dependency in terms of `brain-projection-equality` **comparing** the
handoff block to the projection — the same check this repo's own
`_projection_currently_passes()` reimplements independently for the
**refusal gate**. A.3/A.6's text never specifies the exact field-by-field
shape of that comparison (only that it exists and that it must gain a
retired-repo skip branch) — this repo's own reading (State/Standing/
Vault-sync/Session mechanically re-derivable, Next-step excluded as
unpersisted free text) is this repo's own engineering judgment on an
underspecified point, not a quote from A.3, and is called out as such in
both `bin/brain`'s own docstring and this report's item 2 above, per the
brief's "quote it, don't paraphrase" instruction — nothing here is
presented as governed text it isn't.

## What the origin (and `conventions`' parallel session) must know

- **The threshold and the marker mechanism now exist on the `brain-toolkit`
  side and are exercised only by `brain progress retire`.** No other
  command in `bin/brain` reads or writes `progress_retired` except
  `cmd_session_close` (read-only, to decide whether to skip block
  generation) and `cmd_progress_retire` itself (the sole writer).
- **`conventions`' own `brain-projection-equality` should not assume this
  repo's four-of-five-line comparison is the governing definition of
  "passes."** This repo's check exists solely to gate its own
  `progress retire` refusal — `conventions`' validator is free to (and per
  A.6 must) implement its own retirement-aware branch independently; the
  two do not need to agree field-for-field, only agree that a retired
  marker means "stop asserting a growing PROGRESS.md."
- **Sequencing, restated as the demand itself states it:** retiring a real
  repo (either pilot) before `conventions`' half lands turns that repo red
  the same night, by construction — this fulfillment does not retire
  anything, and nothing should call `progress retire` against a real repo
  until the `conventions` half is confirmed merged.

## Not done / caveats

- Neither `media-generation` nor `agent-runner` was retired — both are
  threshold-eligible (21 and 33 closed sessions, per the demand's own
  observed figures) but the demand states plainly that's each repo's own
  later session.
- No worktree/repin work (item 7 above) — explicitly out of this
  fulfillment's scope per the task brief.
- `brain-toolkit` itself carries no `.brain/` of its own (one of the four
  D074 exclusions) — nothing here was exercised against this repo's own
  session corpus, only against isolated `tempfile.mkdtemp()` fixtures in
  `test_brain.py`, consistent with every other test in this suite.

# Fulfillment — D084: the executioner's model + reasoning effort become per-run choices

## State check first

Not already shipped. Before writing anything:

- `git log` in `brain-toolkit` showed the newest work as `54d8baa` (the
  v0.5.1 worktree demand) — nothing D084-shaped.
- `grep -i effort bin/` returned **zero** hits across the whole toolkit:
  no effort concept existed anywhere, matching the demand's own "The ruling
  is recorded; none of it is built."
- `bin/structurer` resolved a **model only** (`gateway_resolve_model`,
  returning `resolvedModel`), for three functions on three different
  regimes.

The **`ai-gateway` leg, by contrast, was already shipped** (`ReasoningEffort`,
`PolicyEntry.effort`, `PolicyResolutionResponse.resolvedEffort`,
`ClaudeCodeAdapter`'s `--model`/`--effort` forwarding). That mattered: its
`PolicyResolutionResponse` javadoc specifies exactly what a `brain-toolkit`
caller must do with the answer, and this leg was built against that contract
literally rather than against a guess.

## What was built (the `brain-toolkit` leg only)

`dashboard`'s and `ai-gateway`'s legs are their own repos' work and were not
touched from here.

### 1. `--model` / `--effort`, omitting either falls back to the resolved default

Both flags on `bin/executioner` (fleet sweep) and on `bin/structurer` (single
repo). Each executioner→structurer invocation carries them as **flags and**
as `BRAIN_RUN_MODEL`/`BRAIN_RUN_EFFORT` in the child's environment, the same
belt-and-braces treatment `BRAIN_REPO_ROOT` already gets. `--effort` accepts
`low | medium | high | xhigh` — the Claude Code CLI's tiers, mirrored from
`ai-gateway`'s `ReasoningEffort` enum, not a vocabulary invented here.
Omitting a flag sends nothing, so the gateway-resolved value stands.

### 2. Precedence, in exactly one place

`resolve_run_policy()` = `gateway_resolve_policy()` (stored row → fleet
default, ai-gateway's two tiers) + `apply_run_overrides()` (the per-run
tier). Every model-consuming step calls it; nothing re-derives the order.

- **per-run flag > stored policy row > fleet default** — asserted directly by
  `test_per_run_flags_beat_the_stored_row` and
  `test_omitting_a_flag_falls_back_to_the_resolved_default`.
- **The `config.yml` privacy switch still beats all three.** `ai-gateway`
  enforces the privacy tier itself and says so with `privacyEnforced`; the
  toolkit refuses **both** overrides on top of such an answer and records the
  refusal in `overrides_refused_by_privacy`, which `graph.md` prints. A
  swallowed refusal would look identical to a run that honoured the flag.
- **Nothing is persisted.** A per-run choice never reaches the policy store
  or the `last-full-run.json` marker (asserted:
  `test_the_choice_is_never_written_to_the_marker_file`) — a leaked choice
  would silently re-run itself on the next unflagged sweep.
- **`embeddings` is untouched** by ruling: not in `FRONTIER_FUNCTIONS`, so no
  override reaches it; local Ollama, no effort tier, night-window batch class
  unchanged.

### 3. The resolved effort actually reaches the gateway call

This was the criterion most worth being literal about — a resolved-then-
dropped value is the defect class D072 was minted to fix. Both
`POST /ai/request` payloads (tier-3 classification, contradiction screen) now
follow `PolicyResolutionResponse`'s stated contract:

- `modelHint` := `providerModelHint` (`claude-code`) — **routing and
  metering**;
- `context.model` := the resolved model, `context.effort` := the resolved
  effort — forwarded by `ClaudeCodeAdapter` onto the CLI's own flags.

Proven at the payload level for both calls, and end-to-end through `run()`
(`test_a_full_run_carries_the_pair_all_the_way_into_the_gateway_call`: flag →
HTTP body). A resolution carrying no effort (a local model) sends no `effort`
key at all rather than an explicit null.

### 4. Billing and routing unchanged, by construction

The flags choose a **model, never a provider**: the `modelHint` always stays
whatever the gateway resolved, so a per-run choice cannot re-route a call
onto a different adapter — including the inverse mistake of sending a local
model choice down a paid subscription path. Calls stay on `claude-code`,
metered under `claude-credits`, against D076's 549,000 tokens/day ceiling.
**No API-key provider path was introduced** (offered to the owner
2026-07-28 and declined).

### 5. `--dry-run --json` surfaces what a run *would* use

`structurer --print-policy` resolves the three frontier functions through the
same `resolve_run_policy` and prints JSON — **no lock, no consolidation, no
write, no inference call**. `executioner --dry-run --json` embeds it per repo
as `resolvedPolicy`, which is what `agent-runner`'s reads-only `GET /brain/*`
surface (D070) already consumes. This is a **read**, not a run trigger: the
existing "a dry-run must run nothing" test was sharpened rather than relaxed
— it now asserts every child invocation a dry-run makes is `--print-policy`.
A failed preview degrades to `{"error": ...}` and never changes an
eligibility verdict or the sweep's exit code; `--no-resolve-policy` restores
the exact pre-D084 key set.

### 6. Spec / build-notes citing D084

`spec-agent-memory-system.md` (this toolkit's governing spec, vault-owned)
already carries D084 in §9.0, Appendix A.5 and the new Appendix D.6 —
written by the vault at ruling time, so **no vault demand is needed from
here**. This repo's own build notes now cite D084: `README.md` (executioner
entry), `DEPLOYMENT.md` (a precedence table, the flags, the env vars, the
`resolvedPolicy` contract, the `--print-policy` invocation) and
`CHANGELOG.md` **v0.6.0**.

## Verification

- **Suite: 273 tests passing** (`python -m unittest discover -s bin -p
  "test_*.py"`), up from 248 — 25 new, no pre-existing test deleted.
- Two pre-existing tests were **updated, deliberately, and each with its
  reason recorded in the test itself**: the contradiction-payload dialect
  test (context now also carries the model) and the `--dry-run --json` key-set
  test (the additive `resolvedPolicy` key, plus a new test proving
  `--no-resolve-policy` keeps the original key set exactly).
- **Live-verified against the running `ai-gateway`** (`localhost:8085`), a
  read-only check:
  ```
  BRAIN_REPO_ROOT=.../agent-runner python bin/structurer --print-policy
  ```
  returned all three frontier functions with a model + effort pair,
  `model_hint: claude-code`, and sourced from the gateway; adding
  `--model claude-opus-5 --effort xhigh` flipped both values and both
  `*_source` strings to the per-run tier, with `model_hint` correctly
  unchanged.

## One finding, reported not fixed — for `ai-gateway` / the vault's drift-watch

The **live** gateway currently resolves the frontier default as
**`claude-opus-4-8`**, not D084's `claude-opus-5`:

```
GET /ai/policy/resolve?repo=agent-runner&function=contradiction-screen
-> {"policy":"auto","resolvedModel":"claude-opus-4-8","resolvedEffort":"high",
    "providerModelHint":"claude-code","privacyEnforced":false}
```

`ai-gateway`'s committed `application.yml` says
`frontier-model: ${AI_POLICY_FRONTIER_MODEL:claude-opus-5}` and the effort
half resolves correctly, so the *code* is D084-aware — the **running process**
is serving a stale value (started before the config change, or with
`AI_POLICY_FRONTIER_MODEL` set to the old model in its environment). The
fleet-default rows themselves are `policy: auto`, `effort: null`, so nothing
in the store is pinning it.

This is exactly the re-pointed **D072 drift-watch** the demand's own text
warns about ("the live store must now be checked against Opus 5 / `high`").
It is `ai-gateway`'s leg and its deployment's concern — **not fixed from
here**, per the standing order against cross-repo fixes. A restart (or
clearing the env override) is the likely resolution, and the vault's closing
re-verification should confirm it before recording D084 as in force.

## Known gap, flagged not worked around

`contracts`' `AiRequest` carries no first-class `effort` field, so the pair
travels in `context` — which that contract documents as a provider-agnostic
passthrough and which `ai-gateway`'s `ClaudeCodeAdapter` already reads for
precisely this purpose. That is the shape `ai-gateway` specified, not a
workaround invented here. A first-class field would be a `contracts` change,
which is not this repo's to make.

## Not done here, on purpose

- `ai-gateway`'s four criteria — already shipped in that repo before this
  session; only consumed, never edited from here.
- `dashboard`'s two criteria — that repo's own leg.
- No run-trigger route was added anywhere (D084 addendum): D070's reads-only
  `GET /brain/*` invariant stands unqualified.

Commit: `922a856`.

# Fulfillment — seeded `.brain` lifecycle invocations now run under PowerShell

## State check first

Not already shipped. Before writing anything:

- `git log` showed the newest work as `e1ce565` (v0.6.1, the `--dry-run
  --json` policy-preview fix) — nothing shell-portability shaped, and no
  `demands/fulfilled/` report for this demand id.
- `bin/adopt:414-419` still rendered the defective text verbatim:
  `` `.brain/bin/brain session open "<task>" --priority <1-3>` `` and
  `` `.brain/bin/brain session close` ``, both bare.
- A repo-wide grep for `.brain/bin/(brain|structurer)` found **one further
  live invocation** the demand's "same check elsewhere" clause was right to
  ask about: `bin/structurer:3183`'s generated-`AGENT.md` query hint,
  `` `.brain/bin/brain query "<terms>"` ``, also bare.

So: the reported defect was real and present, plus one instance the demand
did not name.

## The defect, precisely

`.brain/bin/brain` is an **extensionless Python script**. Under a POSIX shell
its shebang makes the bare path executable, which is why the text reads
plausibly. PowerShell has no shebang mechanism: it resolves the path, finds
no recognized executable extension (`$env:PATHEXT`), and the invocation does
not run the script. Whether the operator sees a clear error or nothing useful
depends on how it was invoked — and either way **no session file is
written**, which is the harm the demand identified: an agent following its
own repo's standing orders believes it opened a session when it did not, then
proceeds to change code with no session open and nothing to close.

## What was changed

### 1. The `CLAUDE.md` template (`bin/adopt`, the reported defect)

The section now opens with the rule rather than burying it in a bullet:

> **Always invoke the shims through `python`.** `.brain/bin/brain` is an
> extensionless Python script: PowerShell (this platform's primary shell)
> will not execute it, and depending on how it is invoked you may get no
> output and no session file rather than a clear error … Always prefix
> `python`, and check that a new file appeared under `.brain/sessions/`.

The Open/Close bullets then carry **both** forms with the shell named for
each — `python .brain\bin\brain session open "<task>" --priority <1-3>` for
PowerShell/cmd (the platform's primary shell, so it leads), and the
forward-slash form labelled "under bash/sh". The added
"check `.brain/sessions/`" instruction is the part that makes the failure
loud even if some future variant of this goes quiet again.

### 2. The structurer's generated query hint

`python`-prefixed with the PowerShell form beside it. This is the one surface
that **self-heals**: `AGENT.md` is regenerated on every structurer run, so
each repo picks up the corrected hint on its next nightly with no action.

### 3. `DEPLOYMENT.md`

A "Shell note — always invoke through `python`" subsection now states the
rule once, explains why the failure can be quiet, and shows the
PowerShell/cmd forms. It also notes that `python .brain/bin/brain …` works
fine in PowerShell too (the slashes are just an argument to `python`) — the
backslash form is what the seeded template shows because it is unambiguous on
Windows. The pre-existing `python .brain/bin/brain progress retire` examples
were already correct and were left alone.

### 4. The sweep the demand asked for

Checked every other operator-facing carrier, not just the CLAUDE.md template:

| Surface | Finding |
|---|---|
| adopt console output / `operatorSteps` | Clean. The only command it ever prints for a human to run is `git -C "<target>" config core.hooksPath .githooks` — `git` is a real executable, shell-agnostic. |
| seeded `.brain/conventions.md` | Clean — it deliberately carries no invocations, only pointers to the vault spec (that's its whole design). |
| seeded `.brain/overrides.md`, `.brain/config.yml` | Clean. |
| `DEPLOYMENT.md` (rest of file) | Every executable example already `python`-prefixed. Remaining `.brain/bin/brain` mentions are prose about *where the shim file lives* under the pin mechanism. |
| `README.md`, `HEXAGON.md`, `bin/adopt_templates/brain_shim` | Same — file-location prose, not commands. |
| `bin/brain`'s own `--help` usage | Shows `brain session open …` (the tool's canonical command name, no path). Left as-is: argparse prints the `prog` name, and rewriting it to a path would be wrong for every invocation route. The seeded `CLAUDE.md` is where an agent learns how to reach it. |

### 5. Regression test

`TestSeededInvocationsRunUnderPowerShell` in `bin/test_adopt.py`, 4 cases.
The core one asserts that no text adopt seeds may match
`.brain/bin/<tool>` followed by a subcommand **without** a `python ` prefix —
run against the rendered `CLAUDE.md` section, `conventions.md` and
`overrides.md`, and separately against the `CLAUDE.md` file a real adopt run
actually writes to disk (so a future refactor that bypasses the template
function is still caught). Two more assert the PowerShell forms and the word
"PowerShell" are present by name, so the "documents which shell" half of the
acceptance criteria can't silently regress either.

This test caught something while being written: my first draft of the
explanatory prose quoted the bad invocation as an example of what not to do,
and the regex flagged it. Reworded to "an unprefixed shim call" — a template
that ships the broken string even as a counter-example is a string an agent
can copy.

Full suite: **282 passing** (was 278).

## The migration decision — explicit, as asked: forward-only

**The ~24 already-adopted repos are not rewritten.** Recorded in
`DEPLOYMENT.md` ("Already-adopted repos: the fix is forward-only") and in
`CHANGELOG.md` v0.6.2, so it is discoverable from the deployment doc rather
than only from a demand report.

Reasoning:

- `plan_claude_md` skips `CLAUDE.md` whenever the
  `<!-- brain-adopt:section -->` marker is present — **including under
  `--force`**. That is not an accident of implementation; it exists so adopt
  never edits a repo's standing orders, which its own sessions evolve. So
  a `--force` re-run would not even fix this today; making it do so would
  mean teaching adopt to rewrite hand-maintained files, then applying 24
  unreviewed edits to standing-order documents to correct a documentation
  line. That trade is bad in the direction that matters: the blast radius of
  a bad fleet-wide rewrite of `CLAUDE.md` is much worse than the residual
  cost of the stale text.
- The residual cost is genuinely small and shrinking. The generated surface
  (`AGENT.md`'s hint) self-heals on the next structurer run everywhere. What
  remains stale is one bullet pair in each repo's `CLAUDE.md`.
- Because the bad text is byte-identical fleet-wide (the demand's own
  observation), correcting a given repo is the *same* one-line edit
  everywhere, done by that repo's own session, in its own commit, reviewed
  the way any `CLAUDE.md` change is. `DEPLOYMENT.md` states the exact
  replacement so no session has to work it out.
- Repos are not required to. The platform `CLAUDE.md` standing orders and
  `DEPLOYMENT.md` are operative either way.

If the owner would rather have the fleet corrected mechanically, the shape is
a separate, deliberate change — a `bin/adopt --rewrite-claude-md-section`
that re-renders only the marked block and refuses if anything outside the
marker differs from what adopt wrote. Not built, and not built speculatively;
it needs the owner's call on whether adopt may ever touch `CLAUDE.md` after
the first append. Raised here rather than assumed.

## Not done / out of scope

- No new adopt flag or fleet migration (decision above).
- `bin/brain`'s argparse usage strings untouched (reasoning in the table).
- No vault edit. This report is the write-back; if `PLATFORM_STATE.md` or the
  spec should record "seeded invocations are `python`-prefixed as of v0.6.2",
  that is a `platform-vault` change and would need its own demand — flagged,
  not performed.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s bin -p "test_*.py"` → **282 tests, OK**
  (run on Windows/PowerShell, the shell the bug was about).
- `python -m unittest discover -s bin -p "test_adopt.py"` → 35 tests, OK.
- Repo-wide grep for `` `.brain/bin/(brain|structurer|executioner)` ``
  re-run after the change: every remaining hit is file-location prose.

# Git tags for the v0.6.x releases

All three versions are now annotated git tags on their own release commits,
pushed to `origin` (https://github.com/elmoul/brain-toolkit.git). Nothing was
withheld — all three are adoptable.

## What each tag points at

| Tag | Release commit | Commit subject |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.6.0` | `922a856` | `feat: executioner --model/--effort -- per-run model + reasoning effort (D084)` |
| `v0.6.1` | `e1ce565` | `fix: parallelize + bound the --dry-run --json policy preview (v0.6.1)` |
| `v0.6.2` | `550a681` | `fix: seeded .brain lifecycle invocations now run under PowerShell (v0.6.2)` |

A consuming repo sets `.brain/toolkit-pin` to `v0.6.2` for the current head of
the line; `git rev-parse v0.6.2^{}` resolves to `550a681`.

## How the release commit was chosen per version

The release commit is the commit that introduced that version's `## vX.Y.Z`
heading into `CHANGELOG.md` (`git log -- CHANGELOG.md`):

- `v0.6.1` and `v0.6.2` each ship as a single commit carrying code + CHANGELOG,
  so the choice is unambiguous.
- `v0.6.0` has no separate `docs: v0.6.0` commit — the D084 feature commit
  `922a856` carries the `## v0.6.0 — 2026-07-28` section itself (verified with
  `git show 922a856:CHANGELOG.md`). The later `1692ed7` is only the demand
  fulfilment report and is not the release.

## Note on tag style

The pre-existing `v0.1.0`–`v0.5.1` tags are lightweight. The three new tags are
**annotated**, as the demand asked. Both forms resolve identically for
`git checkout <tag>` and for pinning, so no consumer tooling change is needed;
future releases will be annotated.

## Verification

`git ls-remote --tags origin` on the remote:

```
a33a183…  refs/tags/v0.6.0        922a856…  refs/tags/v0.6.0^{}
847302a…  refs/tags/v0.6.1        e1ce565…  refs/tags/v0.6.1^{}
748bd60…  refs/tags/v0.6.2        550a681…  refs/tags/v0.6.2^{}
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] v0.6.0, v0.6.1, v0.6.2 exist as annotated tags on their own release
      commits, pushed to origin. None deliberately withheld.
- [x] The tag→commit mapping is stated above so a consuming repo can move its
      `.brain/toolkit-pin` without guessing.
