# Fulfillment — `brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.6.2/` git worktree entry

## State check first

`git worktree list` from `brain-toolkit` showed only `v0.2.0`, `v0.3.0`,
`v0.4.0`, `v0.5.1` — no `v0.6.x` entry existed, even though all three
`v0.6.0`/`v0.6.1`/`v0.6.2` tags were already present and pushed (shipped by
`demands/fulfilled/platform-vault-20260731-brain-toolkit-tag-the-v06-releases-report.md`).
The capability was **not** already shipped; the work was done rather than a
no-op report.

## What was done

```
git worktree add "../brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.6.2" v0.6.2
```

Run from the `brain-toolkit` checkout itself — same command shape and same
sibling-directory layout (`brain-toolkit-worktrees/<tag>/`) as the four
pre-existing entries, per DEPLOYMENT.md's D042-mirroring pin mechanism
("only a `brain-toolkit` session may create one", because worktree tracking
lives in `brain-toolkit/.git`). Nothing in `platform-vault` or in any
consumer repo was touched.

## Layout confirmation — this worktree layout is the one, not superseded

The seeded shim (`bin/adopt_templates/brain_shim`) still resolves exactly
this path:

```
<platform-root>/brain-toolkit-worktrees/<pin>/bin/<tool-name>
        TOOLKIT_WORKTREE = PLATFORM_ROOT / "brain-toolkit-worktrees" / PIN
```

So a repo whose `.brain/toolkit-pin` reads `v0.6.2` now resolves. No
alternative layout supersedes this one.

## Verification

- `git worktree list` (from `brain-toolkit`) now shows:
  ```
  C:/Users/pc/Desktop/platform/brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.6.2 550a681 (detached HEAD)
  ```
  HEAD at `550a681` (`fix: seeded .brain lifecycle invocations now run under
  PowerShell (v0.6.2)`) — exactly what tag `v0.6.2` points at.
- `python bin/brain --help` inside `brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.6.2/` exits 0.
- `python bin/structurer --help` inside the same worktree exits 0.
- `bin/` in the worktree carries the full tool set: `adopt`,
  `adopt_templates/`, `brain`, `executioner`, `structurer`.

## Re-pin guidance for the ~25 `.brain` consuming repos

**Pin target is `v0.6.2` — not `v0.6.0` and not `v0.6.1`.** Only the
`v0.6.2` worktree was created. `v0.6.0` and `v0.6.1` are tagged but have no
worktree and therefore will not resolve through the shim; they are strictly
superseded by `v0.6.2` on the same line (v0.6.1 is the fleet-preview timeout
fix, v0.6.2 the PowerShell-invocation fix). If a repo needs one of those two
specifically, raise a demand and this repo will add the worktree — do not
create it yourself.

**Recommendation: wait for a coordinated fleet re-pin, sequenced by
`platform-vault`, rather than 25 independent decisions.** Reasons:

- The move is *safe* either way — `v0.5.1 → v0.6.2` is additive plus fixes,
  no removals or renames per CHANGELOG's own versioning rule, so nothing in
  a consumer breaks by re-pinning early.
- But `v0.6.1` changed how `--dry-run --json` resolves the *whole fleet* for
  `GET /brain/fleet`, and the useful comparison there is a fleet on one pin,
  not a fleet half on `v0.5.1` and half on `v0.6.2`. A staggered re-pin makes
  any regression in that surface hard to attribute.
- The one carve-out: a repo actively blocked today by the v0.6.1 timeout bug
  (`agent-runner`, `dashboard`) may re-pin to `v0.6.2` immediately without
  waiting — pin value is the same, so it does not diverge from where the
  fleet is heading.

Two things a re-pinning repo does in its own session (this repo does not do
them for you, and must not — never edit outside your own repo):

1. Set `.brain/toolkit-pin` to `v0.6.2`.
2. Re-run `python .brain/bin/structurer` once, which regenerates `AGENT.md`'s
   query hint with the `python`-prefixed form from v0.6.2.

Note that the v0.6.2 `CLAUDE.md` `.brain` section fix is **forward-only** —
`adopt` deliberately never rewrites an existing marked block, even under
`--force`. An already-adopted repo that wants its stale `.brain/bin/brain …`
lines corrected does that as a one-line edit in its own session; the stale
text is byte-identical fleet-wide, so it is the same edit everywhere. See
DEPLOYMENT.md, "Already-adopted repos: the fix is forward-only".

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `brain-toolkit-worktrees/v0.6.2/` exists as a git worktree of tag
      `v0.6.2`, with `bin/brain` and `bin/structurer` runnable from it
      (verified above). The existing `brain-toolkit-worktrees/<tag>/` layout
      is current — nothing supersedes it.
- [x] The report states the re-pin position: coordinated fleet re-pin

# Fulfillment report — a runbook for driving a design mission from the console

## State before this session

Checked first, per the demand's own instruction. The capability did not exist:

- `runbooks/` carried four docs — `start-local-stack.md`, `rebuild-stale-service.md`,
  `bootstrap-new-hexagon.md`, `troubleshooting.md`. None of them mentions design missions.
- `workflows/design-mission.md` exists and is correct, but is the **state machine's semantics** — the
  gap the demand names.
- `README.md`'s master index listed no such page.

This was written from scratch here.

## Sources used

No platform facts were invented. The procedure and its traps were synthesised from:

- `../docs/DESIGN_CONSOLE_REDESIGN_PLAN.md` (R1–R12, and §9/§10's record of what the first two real
  builds taught) — the day's raw account.
- `dashboard`'s own fulfillment reports for R11
  (`design-studio-20260728-dashboard-validate-and-pin-at-system-gate`) and R12
  (`design-studio-20260728-dashboard-unblock-a-blocked-build`) — read-only, for the shipped console
  behaviour: the built-system panel, the typed `VALIDATE` / `ACCEPT` confirmations, the disabled-Approve
  reason, the blocked chip and the two unblock buttons, and the needs-you row precedence.
- `dashboard`'s source, read-only, to confirm two details rather than assume them: `clone` is the one
  route with a required `{targetPath}` body (`mission-stage.ts`, `now-panel.component.html`), and
  `harvest` / `theme-interview` are the run-steps preceding the gate (`mission-stage.ts`).
- `workflows/design-mission.md` in this repo — linked, not quoted.

## Against each acceptance criterion

1. **A runbook under `runbooks/`, listed in `README.md`.** `runbooks/run-a-design-mission.md`, added to
   the master index's `runbooks/` table.
2. **The create-new path end to end.** §1 is the sequence, with the four steps that live *inside*
   `system-gate` (build → read docs → validate → approve) called out as such, since that is the part
   the state machine does not make obvious. Clone closes it.
3. **Self-carrying build, and pause linked not restated.** §1.3 states the background advancer carries
   the build with no browser tab open, notes that a hand-driven call and the advancer honour pause at
   different granularities and that neither kills in-flight work — then points at
   `workflows/design-mission.md` §2/§5 and says explicitly: *do not reason about pause from this page*.
   It also flags that older notes saying "keep the tab open" describe the pre-R2b world.
4. **The four traps.** §2's table: class-3 typed `APPROVE`/`REJECT` (an approval that appears not to
   work has usually not been sent), the recorded-outcome card's *Record another decision* button,
   clone's never-defaulted target path, and validate-before-approve with the disabled-Approve reason.
   Two extras that also cost time are recorded: the cached `index.html` false alarm, and the
   rejection-direction wording that decides §8bis re-entry batch.
5. **When a build stops.** §3 draws the line: `failure` still retries on the next pass; `blocked` is
   terminal — budget exhausted, advancer skips the mission, nothing moves. Unblock is the only exit, in
   its two shapes: plain retry with a fresh attempt budget, or accept-QA-findings, which records a
   durable override into `qa-report.json`, still pins and clones, and fixes nothing.
6. **The needs-you queue.** §4, with mission `e8e4b3e5`'s five silent days at `system-gate` as the
   reason the advice is "watch the queue, not the mission page", and the row-precedence detail (blocked
   suppresses failure; a gate row is suppressed while a build runs under it).
7. **Links, never restatements.** No D-number is explained, no spec prose is copied, and no state or
   gate semantics are re-derived — every one of them is a link to `workflows/design-mission.md` or a
   bare `D0xx` citation in the header.
8. **The standard header.** Status `current`, as-of 2026-07-28, owning D-numbers (D064, D067, D069,
   D071, D073, D036/D050, D081), and the repos it touches.

## Judgement calls

- **Scoped to the create-new path through `clone`**, stated in the doc's own Scope line, with a
  sentence saying the choose-existing path is identical from "approve system-gate" onward and that the
  downstream propositions/build phases are not covered. That is exactly the ground the demand
  describes; extending to the theme gate and beyond would be documenting a path nobody has driven yet.
- **No live verification.** This repo doesn't run the console, and the terminal `blocked` state has
  never occurred in reality — R12's own report says as much. Everything here is sourced from shipped
  behaviour as its builders documented it, not observed.

## Nothing was raised to another repo

No sibling repo was edited and nothing needed one. The console behaviour described already ships.
`../docs/DESIGN_CONSOLE_REDESIGN_PLAN.md` row R8a can be marked done by whoever owns that plan — that
is the root session's edit, not this repo's.

# Coverage-gate doc-sync — the gate that stopped being a rubber stamp

## What the demand asked

The design-mission workflow and runbook were to describe `coverage-gate` **as it becomes**: a
round-based scope negotiation the owner iterates with an agent, plus the owner procedure for "the
brief is missing something I want built" — a documented operational procedure that did not exist in
these docs at all.

The demand carried an explicit governance clause: **the doc changes wait on the vault rulings
landing**, and if the rulings came back different from the demand's description, the docs follow the
rulings.

## State check first

Not shipped. Two `.brain` session files existed for this demand
(`2026-08-01_0042_…` and `2026-08-01_0529_…`) but both were opened by the dispatch supervisor and
closed — one auto-drafted, one left `partial` — with **empty `changes`** and no commits behind them.
`git log` confirmed the newest content commit was `d2a8634` (D089 doc-sync). Grepping
`workflows/`, `runbooks/`, `guides/` and `reference/` for `coverage-scope`, `brief-additions`,
`scope round` and `sample` returned nothing. `reference/decisions.md` stopped at D089.

So this was real work, not a re-run.

## The governance precondition: both rulings had landed

Checked before touching a doc, per the demand's own clause. `PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md` carries both:

- **D090** — an Interface Brief has a third input, the owner's own recorded additions;
  `POST /missions/{id}/brief-additions`; a stale coverage matrix is a **banner, not a refusal**.
- **D091** — `coverage-gate` iterates: its rejection is binding and starts a fresh scope round
  (reversing the un-landed 2026-07-30 advisory ruling); theme mocks are a **sample**; a gate whose
  subject is not the design carries its own checklist.

Both owner-ruled 2026-08-01, D090 landed first because D091's scope-checklist item 1 has no remedy
without it. Every page below was written from the vault entries themselves, not from the demand's
summary of them. **Two places where the ruling is narrower than a fast reading of the demand, and the
docs follow the ruling:**

- **The rewind direction-carry is still `theme-gate`'s alone.** D091 retires the *reason* D067 gave
  for the asymmetry (a dated D067 addendum records this), but explicitly does **not** extend the
  carry. §1 of the workflow doc now says exactly that, rather than implying a rewind into
  `coverage-gate` now carries direction.
- **D087 is not amended.** D090 sub-ruling 1 states that none of D087's four sub-rulings is
  contradicted — it widens the brief's *input set*. The demand said "annotate D087 as amended **if**
  the vault amends it"; the vault did not, so `reference/decisions.md` records the non-amendment
  instead of inventing one.

## Acceptance criteria, one by one

| Criterion | Where it landed |
|---|---|
| Coverage-gate as an **ITERATING** gate — agent proposes, owner reviews, rejection carries binding direction into a fresh numbered round, approval is what advances | `workflows/design-mission.md` §3quater ("The loop" verdict table), plus §1's "two gates iterate in numbered rounds" |
| The **SAMPLE** rule, and that an undemonstrated brief item is a normal in-scope item | §3quater, "The SAMPLE rule — what the theme mocks were ever claiming"; also `covered` now means *sampled*, and the 13-of-19 live failure it caused |
| Runbook gains **`POST /missions/{id}/brief-additions`** — note + optional items, at coverage-gate, moving no stage and reversing no gate decision; and plainly **not** what a rejection does | `runbooks/run-a-design-mission.md` §3ter.2, with the reject-vs-addition table: a rejection re-scopes *the round*, an addition grows *the brief* |
| Both docs state the **re-run `/coverage`** consequence and the **stale-matrix banner that does not block Approve** | workflow §3quater "After growing the brief"; runbook §3ter.3 — both say the banner is information, not a veto, and both cite that the gate has never refused on freshness |
| The **two owner controls described as two**, so an addition isn't written into a rejection note | workflow §3quater "The two owner controls at this gate are two, not one"; runbook §3ter's two-subsection structure + a traps row |
| The **rewind-to-theme-gate remedy corrected** wherever the docs give it | Workflow §3quater's superseded block names it and says why it's wrong now (it re-rolls an approved theme); runbook §3ter.1 repeats it at the point of use; a traps row catches anyone arriving from older notes |
| `reference/decisions.md` **indexes the two D-numbers**, annotates D087 as amended if the vault amends it | D090 and D091 in both the numeric table and the `design & design-studio` topic list (counts 89→91, topic 12→14); D067 annotated with its dated D091 addendum; D087 annotated **not amended**, with the reason |
| **Doc changes wait on the rulings** | Both vault entries read in full before the first edit; two ruling-vs-demand divergences resolved in the ruling's favour (above) |

## What else changed, and why it had to

Three pages outside the demand's named set carried statements the rulings make false. Leaving them
would have put the repo in direct contradiction with itself:

- `guides/mission-workspace.md` §3's action table said a `coverage-gate` rejection is **advisory and
  no pipeline step reads it**. Corrected, with a dated note. The note is careful about the seam: this
  page documents what the **console renders**, and `design-studio`'s implementation is not verified
  by D091 — so it points operators at the gate's own `rejection` field, which the workspace has
  always read rather than inferring from the stage. That field is exactly why this reversal does not
  silently mislead someone on a console that hasn't caught up.
- `guides/mission-workspace-states.md`'s `coverage-gate` row said the gate's subject is "matrix
  approved". Now "scope round approved", with the round loop, the checklist replacement and the
  banner named.
- `reference/glossary.md`'s **Regime** entry said the regime "gates the checklist that mission's
  coverage-gate runs" — precisely the sentence D091 ruling 4 replaces. Rewritten to the general rule:
  the regime checklist runs at the gates whose subject *is* the design (`theme-gate`, `feel-gate`);
  the others carry their own.

`guides/mission-workspace-parts.md` was checked and **left alone**: its reference to "the headline
once claimed binding direction at an advisory gate" describes a real past console defect and the
field introduced to fix it. It is history, and it is still accurate as history.

## Boundaries held

- **No vault text restated.** Every rule above is cited by D-number or `spec-design-studio.md §n`.
  Where the docs give substance, it is the platform's operational procedure, not the vault's prose.
- **No sibling repo touched.** `design-studio`'s implementation of D090/D091 is its own work; nothing
  here claims it has shipped, and the console guides say so explicitly.
- **"Done" is a claim, not a verdict.** The coordinator validates and the owner approves.

## Follow-ups worth naming (not done here, not this repo's call)

- **Content reaches the console by a build-time copy.** These pages appear in the console's
  Documentation screen only after the dashboard image is rebuilt — `runbooks/rebuild-stale-service.md`.
- **`plan-gate`'s own checklist does not exist yet.** D091 ruling 4 removes the design-law checklist
  from that gate and says `design-studio` proposes the replacement items, with the vault recording
  them as a dated addendum. Until that addendum lands, `plan-gate` runs with no design-law checklist.
  The docs deliberately do not enumerate items that have not been accepted; a future doc-sync covers
  them.
- **D090 names an adjacent bug it does not fix:** a brief's `openQuestions` is frozen at the first
  content-interview dispatch, so a refreshed harvest's new gaps never become questions. `design-studio`
  will raise it separately. Not documented here, because there is no ruling to document.

standing rule. A traps-table row was added in the same voice as the existing ones: symptom is "the

## What was asked

A D081 doc-sync heads-up, explicitly not a review gate: make sure the design-mission operational docs

  It did not name the endpoint, and it knew nothing of a stage-level block.
- `workflows/design-mission.md` had no dispatch-retry semantics at all; §5's state inventory listed
  `activeDispatch` as "existing machinery, unchanged".
- A repo-wide grep for `blockedDispatch`, `dispatch/unblock`, "dead dispatch" and "self-heal" found
  nothing outside archived demand files.

So both facts in the acceptance criteria were genuinely absent, and the pre-existing §3 was actively
misleading by omission: it presented one `blocked` state where there are now two with different exits.

## What this repo decided to carry

Both facts, in both docs, split by their jobs:

- **Semantics → `workflows/design-mission.md` §2bis.** The four stages, the self-heal, the shared cap
  of three, `blockedDispatch` as a **peer of `activeDispatch`, not a variant**, the two-row exit
  table, and the fact that `dispatch/unblock` is deliberately one route rather than four and 409s at
  `system-gate`. Closes with the note that the standing invariant survives — neither advancer can
  advance a stage.
- **Procedure → `runbooks/run-a-design-mission.md` §3.0.** Written for the owner's actual question,
  "my mission looks stuck": first decide *which* thing is stuck, then read `blockedDispatch`, then
  wait or unblock. The trap that seemed most likely to burn a real session is called out twice — an
  unblock **dispatches nothing**, so "nothing happened" is the expected result, not a failed call.

Every semantic claim points at `platform-vault/spec-design-studio.md` §2 (dispatch-retry semantics)

# Fulfillment report — a mission's inputs are re-derivable in place (D087)

## What was asked

A D081 doc-sync heads-up, explicitly **not** a review gate on this repo: the design-mission workflow
docs described an owner action set that could not re-read a moved target repo without losing the
mission, so an owner whose target changed under a long-running mission would read `abort` as the only
way out. The demand left the shape of the response to this repo.

## Current state before this session

Checked first, per the demand. **Not already shipped.** `refresh-inputs` and `D087` appeared nowhere
in the repo (`grep` across all markdown returned no hits). `workflows/design-mission.md` listed
`abort` and `rewind` as the only two escapes and its §5 inventory carried no notion of an action that
moves nothing; `runbooks/run-a-design-mission.md` §3 covered only the two `blocked` states from the
previous doc-sync; `reference/decisions.md` stopped at D086.

## What was decided about shape

Three judgment calls, all this repo's own:

1. **A new numbered section rather than a bullet under `rewind`.** The whole point of D087 is that
   this is *not* a rewind and *not* a transition; filing it beside the two global transitions would
   have quietly taught the opposite. It sits as §3ter, after the gate-actions material and before
   executing.
2. **The counter-intuitive reading is stated before the mechanics.** The demand called the governance
   fact "the part worth stating plainly", and D087's own entry says the ruling is deliberately the
   opposite of the intuitive one. §3ter therefore leads with *no stage moves, no gate record is
   touched* and gives the owner-approved-a-theme reasoning, rather than burying it under the endpoint.
3. **No SVG was redrawn, and that is recorded as a decision in the text.** The demand asked that the
   diagram/state-machine note `refresh-inputs` as a non-transition. Rather than leave that as a silent
   omission a later session might "fix", §1 and §5 both say in prose that it is absent on purpose and
   that an edge would be wrong. `workflows/diagrams/design-mission-overview.svg` is unchanged.

## Every acceptance criterion, and where it landed

| Criterion | Where |
|---|---|
| The action, its payload, its stage legality, its two 409s | `workflows/design-mission.md` §3ter (blockquote); `runbooks/run-a-design-mission.md` §3bis |
| Moves no stage, touches no gate record; theme, pin and rejections survive verbatim; new information, not a reversal | §3ter, first bullet — stated before the mechanics |
| Nothing erased — superseded inputs preserved and still servable; act recorded with the owner's reason | §3ter, second and third bullets |
| Nothing is recomputed; next `POST /coverage` picks it up; added → gap, removed → gone; never auto-healed, the coverage gate is where it surfaces | §3ter consequence table + the paragraph under it; runbook §3bis closing paragraph; runbook trap row "a refresh that did nothing" |
| Not a transition — would be wrong to draw as an edge | §1 (exactly two global transitions), §5 (inventory row), and no SVG change |
| Law linked, never restated (D081) | §3ter closes on D087 + `spec-design-studio.md` §2/§4/§5; the runbook defers to §3ter rather than re-deriving |

The adjacent facts D087 is careful about are carried too: `rewind` is **not** widened to the
mechanical stages (§3ter's closing note, with the reason — rewind stays the decision-revisiting
instrument so "the mission went backward" never blurs two different causes). D069's still-open
`system-gate` rewind question was **not** touched, since D087 explicitly does not settle it.

## Not done, and why

- **No vault edit.** D087 and `spec-design-studio.md` are the vault's; every reference here is a link.
- **No sibling-repo edit.** The `dashboard` console surface for mission staleness and refresh history
  is `design-studio`'s own separately-raised demand, not this repo's, and nothing here assumes it
  exists.
- **No SVG regenerated** — deliberate, see above.
- **Not verified against a running `design-studio`.** These pages document the ruled semantics from
  D087 and the spec; the implementation is that repo's claim, recorded as such in the vault entry.

## Status

`done` is this worker's claim, not a verdict. The coordinator validates and the owner approves.

# D089 doc-sync — what a dispatched run leaves behind

## What the demand asked

A D081 one-way heads-up: D089 changes what an `agent-runner`-dispatched run leaves behind in the
repo it touched. `documentations` was to read D089 and decide what, if anything, in `workflows/`,
`runbooks/` and `reference/` needed changing. Deciding "nothing" was a valid outcome.

## State check first

Nothing had shipped for D089 before this session. `git log` showed the newest commits were the
2026-07-31 sweep-handoff fulfilment and the v0.6.2 re-pin work; a fleet grep for `clean tree`,
`uncommitted`, `supervisor`, `auto-draft` and `leaves behind` across `workflows/`, `runbooks/`,
`reference/` and `overview/` returned exactly one hit — the vault-preflight paragraph in
`runbooks/troubleshooting.md` §7 — and it described the pre-D089 behaviour. `reference/decisions.md`
stopped at D088. So this was real work, not a re-run.

## The decision: three pages change, the rest don't

D089 is narrow — the supervisor now stages and commits the two session-capture files it itself
writes, and nothing else. Two places in the corpus described the old behaviour, and one is the
D-index that has to carry every number.

**1. `workflows/brain-cycle.md`** — this is the page that documents session open → close →
`PROGRESS.md` projection, and it described only the hand-run case, where the agent that did the work
also commits its own close. Added a subsection after the D063 `Session:`-line explanation covering
the supervised close: the supervisor drafts after the worker exits, so a different actor writes those
two files, and it now commits them by name. Carried all three of the ruling's limits explicitly,
because each is a thing a reader would otherwise assume wrong — only those two files (never
`git add -A`, leftover source edits stay the worker's problem), the write boundary is narrowed rather
than lifted, and the fix is forward-only so pre-existing residue is still on disk and committing it
is the next session's normal job, not a symptom of anything.

**2. `runbooks/troubleshooting.md` §7** — the vault-write preflight tells a reader that "an
uncommitted change to a file you haven't touched means another session is live. Stop and tell the
owner." Under the pre-D089 behaviour that check had a structural false positive: every dispatched run
in a `.brain` repo ended dirty by construction, so a recently-dispatched repo tripped it without any
concurrent session. Added a paragraph naming the false positive, recording that D089 mostly closes it
forward-only, and giving the reader the discriminator — if the only modifications are those two files
and the repo was dispatched to recently, it's old residue: commit it and carry on; anything else
modified, treat as a live session and stop. Kept as a bounded exception rather than a softening of
the rule, since the underlying one-writer law (D035, narrowed by D085) is untouched.

**3. `reference/decisions.md`** — D089 added to the by-number table and to the `agent-runner &
dispatch` topic group (5 → 6), heading count 88 → 89, and the by-topic preamble's stale "same 85
rows" corrected to 89 (it had drifted three entries behind; the group itself already listed all of
them). Anchor built by the same GitHub slug rule the rest of the page uses.

`as-of` dates bumped to 2026-08-01 on all three; `brain-cycle.md`'s owning-D-number list gains D089.

## What deliberately did not change

- **`onboarding/new-agent-session.md`** — read in full for this. It tells a new session to open and
  close a `.brain` session file and to check the executioner's `errors`; it never describes dispatch
  aftermath and never tells a reader to expect a clean tree. Nothing stale.
- **`workflows/demand-lifecycle.md`, `runbooks/bootstrap-new-hexagon.md`** — both mention dispatch,
  but about *reach* and *gating* (D083/D085), not about what a run leaves behind. Untouched.
- **The guides and the mission-workspace pages** — dispatch appears there as `activeDispatch` mission
  state, unrelated to session-capture commits.
- **No restatement of D089's text anywhere.** Per this repo's one rule, the pages carry the
  operational consequence and cite `D089`; the Decision / Why / Consequences prose stays only in the
  vault.

## Not claimed

D089's own entry records the implementation as unverified at landing, per the vault's
record-ahead-of-execution charter. These pages describe the ruling as governing behaviour and do not
assert that `agent-runner` has shipped it — nor did this session check `agent-runner`'s source, which
would be another repo's business. If the implementation lands differently, the `brain-cycle.md`
subsection is what needs revisiting.

"Done" is a claim, not a verdict — the coordinator validates and the owner approves.

# Fulfillment report — D077 fifth-addendum doc sync

## What the heads-up said

D077's fifth addendum (2026-08-01) records that `launcher`'s `mark-current` override was keyed on the
repo's overall `main` HEAD, while the `isStale` verdict it overrides is decided from the component's
**build-relevant** commits (`mainHeadTime`, the last commit touching the component's Dockerfile-declared
build paths). The two halves disagreed about what counts as a change, so an override was voided by any
commit at all — and for a byte-identical rebuild that hits the Docker cache, the badge could never be
cleared again. Fixed and live-verified 2026-08-01, `launcher` commit `cb0fb56`. Overrides written before
that date carry no `buildRelevantTime` and stay keyed on `mainHead` — honoured as written, never
silently widened.

## Current state before this session

Not already shipped. Both sentences the demand names were still present and still stale:

- `runbooks/rebuild-stale-service.md:66` — "self-expires the moment either one moves"
- `runbooks/troubleshooting.md:271` — "self-expires the moment either moves"

Both pages already described the `isStale` check itself correctly (build inputs off the Dockerfile's
`COPY`/`ADD` lines, not raw HEAD) — the fifth gap is exactly that the *override* didn't match that
description, so the two pages were internally inconsistent as well as stale.

## What changed

**`runbooks/rebuild-stale-service.md` §2 ("Mark current").** The override is now described as keyed on
the component's build-relevant commit time and the image build time, with an explicit cross-reference
that "build-relevant" is the same narrowing §1 already describes for staleness — a commit that doesn't
touch the component's build inputs does not void the override. Added a blockquote recording the old
behaviour, the concrete failure shape (badge re-lights after every unrelated commit; a cache-hit
rebuild can't clear it), the fix commit, and the pre-2026-08-01 grandfathering rule. That last part is
load-bearing operationally: an owner looking at an old override needs to know it still behaves the old
way.

**`runbooks/troubleshooting.md` §"The staleness badge won't clear (or won't light)".** Same correction,
compressed to the ledger page's house density — corrected keying, the narrowing, the date/commit, and
the grandfathering, in one paragraph.

Both `as-of` dates bumped to 2026-08-02. No other page in the repo carries the claim (grepped
`self-expir` / `mark-current` / "either one moves" across the corpus — only these two hits).

## What was deliberately not changed

- **No restatement of D077.** Both pages cite the decision and the addendum by number and date; the
  reasoning that made `buildRelevantTime` the right key rather than content-hashing (the fourth
  addendum's rejected option, and why the distinction is not a technicality) stays in the vault. A
  runbook reader needs the behaviour and the grandfathering rule, not the ruling's argument.
- **The series' still-open question stays out of the runbooks.** The addendum is explicit that closing
  the fifth gap does *not* discharge `spec-launcher.md`'s standing line about rethinking the
  timestamp/tag-proxy model toward content-addressed comparison — that remains open. It is a
  fleet-wide Dockerfile question with no current operator-visible behaviour, so it belongs in the spec,
  not in a "how do I clear this badge" page. No doc claims it is settled either way.
- **No new page.** This is a two-sentence correction inside pages that already own the topic.

## Verification

Grep confirms both remaining `self-expir` occurrences are the corrected sentences. No sibling repo was
touched; no vault file was read for anything but D077's entry.
